description: Fournier's gangrene tracking cephalad along spermatic cords complicates source control and soft tissue reconstruction. We describe a 61-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes who presented with extensive scrotal necrotizing fasciitis tracking superiorly to the suprapubic region. Following wide excisional debridement, bilateral Penrose drains were passed through the spermatic cord tunnels and brought out through dependent perineal counter incisions.

title: PRAME Augments K63‐Linked Ubiquitination and Stabilization of METTL3 to Promote Lung Adenocarcinoma Metastasis
creator: Xia Yang, Xuemei Xu, Yaxuan Zhang, Jiamei Guo, Zhiyu Ye, Qiaorui Bai, Xiuqiao Yang, Shujun Liang, Xiang Dong, Xin Zhang, Jiyong Gu, Shuqin Dai, Hongchun Du, Meiwan Chen, Tianyu Tao, Hongyu Guan, Jueheng Wu, Han Tian, Junchao Cai, Mengfeng Li, Xu Li, Yi Yang
description: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in cancer including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Preferentially expressed antigen of melanoma (PRAME), a cancer‐testis antigen, displays context‐dependent functions across malignancies, but its biological role in LUAD metastasis has not been clearly defined.

title: Delayed diagnosis of congenital pulmonary airway malformation in an infant: diagnostic challenges and surgical implications
creator: Nour Srewell, Youssef Chouman, Yamama Sharief, Mohammed Baraa Meqdad, Mira Hamzeh Rafea, Omar Alsalama, Bushra Alsahan, Mohammd Abdulkader, Sawssan Ali
description: Although congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) is usually diagnosed during prenatal screening, delayed presentation may increase diagnostic uncertainty and operative complexity. We report, to our knowledge, the first case of CPAM diagnosed and surgically managed in Syria in a 4-month-old infant presenting with a 1-month history of dyspnea, fever, and poor feeding in the absence of routine prenatal screening.

title: Internal herniation through Petersen’s defect following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass presenting as subacute bilateral lower extremity edema due to IVC compression – a case report
creator: Reese Bryan, Stephanie Garcia, Zhamak Khorgami
description: A 38-year-old woman with a history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) 2 years prior presented to the bariatric clinic on multiple occasions with postprandial abdominal pain and bloating and bilateral lower extremity edema. Abdominal pain did not improve despite antiacid medication and dietary recommendations.

title: Latent Profiles of Psychological Distress and Suicidal Ideation Among Nursing Students: A Cross‐Sectional Study of Associated Factors
creator: Anshi Wang, Jingjing Wan, Qin Yang, Lijun Zhu, Liying Wen, Weiwei Chang, Yu Zhu, Yan Chen, Yuelong Jin, Yingshui Yao
description: BackgroundPsychological distress and suicidal ideation frequently co‐occur among nursing students, but their heterogeneity is often overlooked.ObjectivesTo identify latent profiles of nursing students based on psychological distress and suicidal ideation dimensions, and to explore factors associated with profile membership.MethodsA cross‐sectional survey of 1461 Chinese nursing students was conducted.

title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression after colorectal cancer treatment with chemotherapy‐induced peripheral neuropathy: A case report
creator: Kosei Esaki, Takeo Saito, Yuki Matsuda, Yueren Zhao, Hiroyuki Kimura, Masashi Ikeda, Tsuyoshi Kitajima, Nakao Iwata
description: BackgroundTreatment of depression in patients with cancer requires individualized decision‐making considering physical symptoms, drug interactions, adverse effects, treatment burden, and acceptability. We report a patient with persistent depression after colorectal cancer treatment, in whom pharmacotherapy was constrained by insufficient efficacy and tolerability, improvement with modified electroconvulsive therapy (mECT) was temporary, and reintroduction of mECT was difficult.

title: Highlights from the 59th Bürgenstock Conference on Stereochemistry 2026
creator: Giacomo E. M. Crisenza, Guanqi Qiu
description: Herein, we share an overview of the scientific highlights from speakers at the latest edition of the longstanding Bürgenstock Conference. “The following biography is intended to deal not only with the external course of my professional life; it also proposes to reveal the eroticism of scientific research: discovering – inventing – understanding.

title: Impact of the phase transition of halide perovskite on the performance of ZnO ultraviolet photoconductor
creator: Femi Igbari, Muhammad Bilal, Zhe Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite the limitations associated with the delta-phase perovskite (δ-PVK), its potential to enhance device performance and stability has recently attracted increasing interest. In this work, we investigate the influence of these properties on the performance of ZnO-based ultraviolet (UV) photoconductors by surface-modifying the ZnO active layer with a δ-PVK layer derived from the phase transition of alpha-phase triple-cation mixed-halide perovskite, (Cs0.05FA0.81MA0.14)Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3 (α-PVK), via solution processing.

title: Early Oral Gastrografin Followed by Immediate CT for Precise Leak Localization and Surgical Planning After Total Laryngectomy
creator: Seung Jo Jeong, Minsu Kwon, Yoon Se Lee, Young Ho Jung, Seung‐Ho Choi, Seung Hoon Han
description: PurposePharyngocutaneous fistula (PCF) is the most common and clinically significant complication following total laryngectomy, often leading to delayed recovery and increased morbidity. Accurate and early detection of pharyngeal leak is critical; however, conventional imaging modalities such as contrast swallow studies and computed tomography (CT) have limitations in precise anatomical localization.

title: Non-traumatic acute mediastinitis secondary to acute phlegmonous esophagitis: a rare case report
creator: Meron H Biza, Eyerusalem K Degife, Selamawit Z Tadesse, Chernet T Mengistie, Ephrem M Atsbha, Biruk T Mengistie
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute mediastinitis secondary to acute phlegmonous esophagitis (APE) is an exceptionally rare, life-threatening condition with high morbidity. We report a 75-year-old diabetic female with recent severe pneumonia who presented with pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and elevated inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography excluded embolism but revealed diffuse long-segment esophageal wall thickening with mediastinal fat stranding, aortic encasement, and pleural effusion, features consistent with APE and secondary non-traumatic mediastinitis without overt perforation.

title: The Role of Astrocytes in the Inflammatory Response in Neurodiseases
creator: Shijun Peng, Lepeng Wang, Jia Ouyang, Ruen Liu
description: Astrocytes have emerged as central regulators of neuroinflammation, extending far beyond their traditional roles as structural and metabolic support cells. In neurological disorders, astrocytes undergo reactive remodeling that encompasses morphological, transcriptional, metabolic, and functional changes. Rather than fitting into a fixed A1/A2 dichotomy, reactive astrocytes exist along a disease‐, region‐, and stage‐dependent continuum shaped by local pathology and intercellular crosstalk.

title: Stratified Therapeutic Evaluation of Presbyphonia Based on Degree of Vocal Fold Atrophy: Efficacy and Prognostic Differences of Semi‐Occluded Vocal Tract Training Across Different Stages
creator: Jieyu Lu, Wen Wu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the stratified therapeutic effects of semi‐occluded vocal tract (SOVT) training based on the degree of vocal fold atrophy and to explore response trajectories.MethodsIn this single‐center prospective cohort study, 180 patients with presbyphonia were stratified into mild, moderate, and severe groups. All participants received standardized SOVT training and were followed for 8 weeks.

title: Rare presentation of hydrocephalus occlusus caused by membranous obstruction of the foramina of Magendie and Luschka: a case report
creator: Sergio Calero Martinez, Lydia Karamani, Heike de Vries, Paul-Christian Krüger, Christian Senft, Nazeer Aboud
description: Fourth ventricle outlet obstruction is a rare cause of obstructive hydrocephalus in children. Although surgical management has been reported, the diagnostic challenges, differential considerations, and therapeutic strategies remain debated. We report a 5-year-old boy with progressive vomiting, severe headache, gait instability, and incontinence.

title: Gastric schwannoma: a case report
creator: Mohamed Tariq Haniff, Andrew Tse, Guillermo Becerril-Martinez
description: Gastric schwannomas are rare, benign mesenchymal tumours that closely mimic gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GISTs) on imaging, despite fundamentally different biological behaviour. We report a 74-year-old man with a background of proctocolectomy for rectal cancer, found incidentally to have a 5 cm exophytic gastric mass on surveillance gastroscopy.

title: Post‐Vaccination Chemosensory Dysfunction: Changes Following SARS‐CoV‐2 Vaccination in a Global Study
creator: Sachiko Koyama, Carla Mucignat‐Caretta, Maria A Klyuchnikova, Tatiana K Laktionova, Svetlana Kopishinskaia, Ilya G Kvasha, Junpeng Ye, Elena Cantone, Shima Parsa, Maria Dolors Guàrdia, Valentin Hivert, Solal Chauquet, Jingguo Chen, Giulio Centorame, Valentina Parma, Kathrin Ohla, Vera V Voznessenska
description: ObjectiveTo assess post‐vaccination changes in chemosensory function among individuals with and without COVID‐19‐related chemosensory impairment.MethodsIn this global, multilingual online survey, participants reported vaccination status, vaccine side effects, and changes in smell and taste before and after each vaccine dose. Responses were collected between May 2022 and August 2023 through convenience sampling.

title: 4D‐Flow MRI‐Derived Wall Shear Stress as a Non‐Invasive Biomarker for the Detection and Hemodynamic Characterization of Pulmonary Hypertension
creator: Ben Statton, Chlöe Armour, Kai'en Leong, Jan Sedlacik, Alaine Berry, Ning Jin, Daniel Giese, Francesco Lo Guidice, Luke Howard, Deepa Gopalan
description: Invasive right heart catheterization (RHC) remains the reference standard for diagnosing pulmonary hypertension (PH), but there is a pressing need for non‐invasive techniques to assess pulmonary hemodynamics. This study evaluates 4D‐flow MRI‐derived wall shear stress (WSS) for PH detection using the updated 2022 hemodynamic criteria, and the prediction of right ventriculo‐pulmonary arterial (RV‐PA) uncoupling to assess disease severity.

title: Identification of a Candidate IgE‐Binding Maize Protein in a Patient With Corn‐Dependent Exercise‐Induced Anaphylaxis: A Case Report
creator: Ayako Goto, Nobue Takamatsu, Tatsuya Moriyama, Yasuto Kondo, Shinichiro Nagamitsu
description: Corn‐dependent exercise‐induced anaphylaxis (food‐dependent exercise‐induced anaphylaxis [FDEIA]) is rare, and its causative allergens remain poorly defined. Here, we report a case of corn‐dependent FDEIA and investigate candidate IgE‐binding proteins using immunological and proteomic analyses. A 13‐year‐old boy with a history of buckwheat allergy developed recurrent anaphylaxis during exercise after ingesting corn‐containing foods.

title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Characterization of MRSA Colonization and Persistence in Residential Aged Care Facilities in Adelaide, Australia
creator: Belaynesh T. Asrat, Sylvia A. Sapula, Naomi L. Siderius, Jonathan J. Whittall, Anteneh Amsalu, Bradley J. Hart, Manish Kumar, Morgyn S. Warner, John Turnidge, Henrietta Venter
description: BackgroundResidential aged care facilities (RACFs) are potential reservoirs for methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with residents at increased risk due to compromised immunity, comorbidities, frequent hospital visits, and close living quarters.ObjectivesThis study is aimed at assessing MRSA prevalence in RACFs and analyzing antimicrobial resistance mechanisms both phenotypically and genotypically.

title: Tracing Hydrazine in Pharmaceuticals: Toxicological Concerns, Extraction Approaches, and Analytical Method Development
creator: Buhlebenkosi Mercy Donga, Rimadani Pratiwi, Aliya Nur Hasanah
description: Hydrazine (N2H4) is a synthetic reagent that is used in the manufacturing of various active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) such as isoniazid, hydralazine, and carbidopa. The major concerns associated with its presence in medications as a residual reagent or degradation product arise because of its ability to damage the genetic material, cause mutations, and potentially trigger cancer.

title: Evaluation of the OPTESK VR training simulator for gastric bleeding treatment
creator: Annika Köhler, Irshath Ali Syed, Jana Sophia Theile, Ioannis Kafetzis, Joel Troya, Jan-Peter Grunz, Ulrike W Denzer, Ivica Grgic, Benjamin M Walter, Rüdiger Pryss, Stavros Dimitriadis, Alexander Hann
description: BackgroundBleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract is a common and potentially life-threatening emergency that requires rapid and highly precise endoscopic intervention. As supervised hands-on training is limited and often restricted to living animal models, an immersive virtual reality (VR) simulation offers a risk-free and accessible alternative.

title: A Two‐Stage Plasma Biomarker Algorithm Reduces Amyloid PET Use and the p‐Tau217 Gray Zone
creator: Harthik Parankusham, Casey Vanderlip, Colin Birkenbihl, Eashwar Krishna, Chizobam Ugboaja, Andrew E. Budson, Brandon Frank, for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
description: ObjectivePlasma p‐Tau217 leaves 30%–50% of patients in an indeterminate “gray zone” often requiring Aβ‐PET. We developed GRAD (Gatekeeper‐Reflex for Alzheimer's Disease), a two‐stage Aβ‐positivity prediction model to improve classification while reserving Aβ‐PET for residual uncertainty.MethodsGRAD was developed in 145 cognitively impaired ADNI participants and externally validated in 1644 cognitively unimpaired A4/LEARN participants. Stage 1 used p‐Tau217 alone; probabilities between 0.

title: Recovering CDR3 sequences from RNA-seq data: a critical assessment of computational and experimental strategies
creator: Mandana AmeliMojarad, Melika AmeliMojarad
description: The adaptive immune response depends on T cell receptor (TCR) diversity to counter cancers, autoimmunity, and infections. This diversity is encoded within CDR3, which serves as a unique barcode for each T cell clone. Characterizing CDR3 sequences is essential for tracking clonal dynamics, identifying neoantigen-reactive T cells, and designing personalized immunotherapy.

title: Malocclusion and orthodontic treatment needs among individuals with down syndrome in Egypt: a multicentre cross-sectional study
creator: Hani AlSwafeeri, Nancy Bedwani, Mariam Badran, Nada Shehata, Hala Ahmed, Menna Allah Mohamed
description: BackgroundIndividuals with Down syndrome commonly present with a variety of craniofacial and dental anomalies that increase the prevalence of malocclusion and the need for orthodontic treatment. Despite this, data regarding orthodontic needs in this population in the middle east, particularly in Egypt, remain limited.

title: Targeting ubiquitin-dependent mitochondrial autophagy and apoptosis in sarcopenia: the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals
creator: Yan Zeng, Ping Wang
description: Sarcopenia is a progressive degenerative disease of skeletal muscle closely associated with aging, disuse, and chronic diseases, affecting approximately 10–16% of the global older adult population. Its core pathological basis lies in the disruption of skeletal muscle cell proteostasis and mitochondrial dysfunction.

title: Comparing the uplink performance of 3D and 2D antenna models in THz networks in the presence of joint human and wall blockages
creator: Tahniyat Aslam, Irfan Ahmed, Sundus Ali
description: Terahertz (THz) communication is considered as a key technology enabler for realizing Sixth Generation (6G) network. THz band communication offers several promising advantages, but numerous challenges are expected due to the inherent limitations of propagation at THz frequencies in the 6G network, such as path loss, interference, human and wall blockages, etc.

title: The molecular footprint of valproic acid in human hippocampal organoid
creator: Bishwa R. Pokharel, Paul P. Cook, Shaw M. Akula
description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental condition characterized by neuroinflammation, and disruption in neuronal development. Valproic acid (VPA) is a known environmental risk factor for ASD. Induced pluripotent stem cells (IPSCs IMR90-4)-derived human hippocampal organoids (hHOs) at 60 days of development were used to investigate VPA-induced changes in mRNA and microRNA (miRNA) profiles.

title: Experimental evolution of cellular miniaturization reveals a putative mechanism for cell size evolution
creator: Ana Garoña, Morgane V. Lemos, Andrea Giometto, Marco Fumasoni
description: SignificanceCell size influences nearly every aspect of cellular physiology and varies drastically among eukaryotes, yet how such diversity evolves without compromising cellular function remains unclear. Using experimental evolution in budding yeast, we selected for progressively smaller cells and identified mutations in conserved nutrient-sensing and cell-cycle pathways that enable sustained reductions in cell size with minimal fitness cost.

title: Standardizing deoxygenation studies in coral biology
creator: Wyatt C Million, Rachel Alderdice, Nicole J Dilernia, Michael Kühl, Cesar O Pacherres, Mathieu Pernice, Carly J Randall, Alexandra Skeer, David J Suggett, Christian R Voolstra, Emma F Camp
description: Deoxygenation, the global loss of biologically available oxygen (O2) from the world’s oceans, presents a pervasive and intensifying threat for reef-building corals that will require coordinated efforts to understand and manage. However, recent expansion of coral deoxygenation experimentation has produced methodological gaps, limiting collective knowledge generation.

title: A ubiquitinome and proteome dataset of the red alga Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis under cold stress
creator: Feng Qin, Xiuyu Zhang, Shuangshuang Peng, Jianxin Sun, Di Xu, Weizhou Chen, Xiaonan Zang
description: Low temperature is a major environmental factor constraining the growth and aquaculture performance of the red alga Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis, yet systematic protein-level data describing cold stress responses remain limited. Ubiquitination is a key post-translational modification involved in regulating protein stability and turnover during stress adaptation.

title: Synchronous detection method for senescence quality of damaged Korla fragrant pears during storage
creator: Jingchi Guo, Hao Niu, Yang Liu, Quan Xu, Haonan Xue, Haipeng Lan, Shengkun Dong, Yifei Gao
description: IntroductionKorla fragrant pears are highly susceptible to mechanical damage during harvest, storage, and transport, which accelerates fruit browning and senescence, leading to fruit degradation and even a complete loss of commercial value.MethodsTo enhance the utilization value of damaged pears, this study used superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, catalase (CAT) activity, peroxidase (POD) activity, superoxide anion ( O2-.

title: Misattributed biospheric carbon sink to the Three-North Program in the Taklamakan Desert may lead to an impractical policy: A commentary
creator: Tian Gao, Jiaojun Zhu, Xiao Zheng, Lining Song, Yirong Sun, Dexiong Teng, Xinhua Zhou
description: Program, TNP) is transforming hyperarid environment into a carbon sink, providing an encouraging projection for carbon sink built up through afforestation, and extrapolating it to the entire Taklamakan Desert (3). However, given extremely limited effective water to plants in the region, potential ecohydrological processes derived from nonfield data could easily misinterpreted real field cases.

title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
creator: Taewan Kim, Manuela De Franco, Miguel Dosil, Jae Taek Oh, Rajesh Bera, Marta Martos Valverde, Gaurav Kumar, Gerasimos Konstantatos
description: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY).

title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
creator: Lander Van Tricht, Matthias Huss, Harry Zekollari, Rodrigo Aguayo, Janosch Beer, Marit van Tiel, Alexandra von der Esch, Daniel Farinotti
description: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration.

title: Decrypting molecular mechanism of heat stress tolerance in rice to tackle climate change challenges through recent approaches
creator: Neeraj Kumar, Seyed Mahdi Hosseiniyan Khatibi, Deepak Sharma, Faraz Azeem, Ganesh Kumar Koutu, Jauhar Ali
description: Rice (Oryza sativa) is one of the world’s most important cereal crops, contributing to food and financial security, particularly in developing countries. High temperature due to climate change seriously threatens sustainable rice production. Rice crops are adversely affected by heat stress at the morphological, physiological, and molecular levels, resulting in reduced yield and poor grain quality.

title: Identification of candidate sex hormone-associated genes and immune infiltration characteristics in osteoarthritis based on bioinformatics analysis and machine learning
creator: Yishu Wang, Ling Zhu, Shuna Jin, Yuhan Wang, Zhaoxiang Zeng, Yunzhou Zuo, Xingliang Xiang, Xugui Li, Rongzeng Huang, Chengwu Song
description: BackgroundSex hormones play critical roles in the pathogenesis and progression of osteoarthritis (OA), yet the hormone-related molecular networks remain poorly defined. This study aimed to identify candidate sex hormone-associated genes in OA and to explore their potential functional enrichment and immune-related characteristics using bioinformatics analysis.

title: Microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric platform for selective single-cell isolation and in situ transfection
creator: Xuefeng Xu, Ziqiao Zhou, Guangyang Li, Jie Liang, Jianhui Wu, Jiaqi Lu, Fang Shen, Shengjun Wu, Zhi Ruan, Shurong Dong, Jikui Luo, Zhen Cao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Single-cell transfection technologies hold tremendous promise for precision cell and immunotherapies. However, monolithic integration of cell isolation with targeted intracellular delivery remains technically challenging, especially within complex biological matrices. Herein, we present a microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric single-cell selective isolation and sonoporative transfection platform (μC-ASSIST), which seamlessly sequences microcapillary-assisted dielectrophoresis (μC-DEP) for deterministic single-cell trapping with high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) for transient membrane poration within a unified workflow.

title: Case Report: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene heterozygous variation presenting with abdominal pain and hepatopancreatic lesions in a child
creator: Xiu Lu, Lidong Ning, Hong Zhen, Ming Liang, Yulan Han, Hongyan Wei, Lingdong Zeng, Lihong Wei, Liqin Tan
description: BackgroundCystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, leading to multi-system involvement.Case reportA 4-year-old girl presented with a 2-day history of abdominal pain. Clinical manifestations included recurrent epigastric pain and vomiting.

title: Limited efficacy of a therapeutic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody to inhibit activated CD4 T cell autoimmunity in vitro
creator: Chelsea Gootjes, Jaap Jan Zwaginga, Tatjana Nikolic, Bart O. Roep, Srinivasa Reddy Bonam, Srinivasa Reddy Bonam, Srinivasa Reddy Bonam
description: Iscalimab is a nondepleting anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody, expected to suppress immune responses by blocking the costimulation by antigen-presenting cells through CD40-CD40L ligation. This therapeutic antibody indeed inhibited proliferation of B lymphocytes and TNF production by dendritic cells and is being tested in clinical trials to treat B cell mediated autoimmune diseases.

title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
creator: Elizabeth C Heintz, Wagner S Dantas, Analisa L Taylor, Elizabeth R M Zunica, Kathryn P Belmont, Jackson M Slone, Jacob T Mey, Robbie Beyl, Bolormaa Vandanmagsar, Hailey A Parry, Peter Ajayi, Brian Glancy, Christopher L Axelrod, John P Kirwan
description: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D).

title: Perspectives of community-dwelling older adults with chronic diseases on Baduanjin practice: A qualitative study
creator: Haixu Ji, Wei Li, Jinhua Zhang, Xuyan Liu, Jing Wang, Guanglei Dong, Assoc. Prof. Phakkharawat Sittiprapaporn, Assoc. Prof. Phakkharawat Sittiprapaporn, Assoc. Prof. Phakkharawat Sittiprapaporn, Assoc. Prof. Phakkharawat Sittiprapaporn
description: BackgroundWith the accelerating aging of China’s population, Baduanjin has been promoted as a community-based exercise to enhance public health, particularly among older adults with chronic diseases. As a traditional Chinese exercise with a long history and profound cultural connotations, Baduanjin has attracted a large number of practitioners. However, the factors underlying the sustained practice of Baduanjin remain insufficiently explored.

title: Association between Internet use and adolescent behavioral development: a cross-lagged regression study
creator: Desheng Yan, Lei Qi, Yao Chen, Guangming Li
description: Promotive behavior refers to actions that facilitate individuals’ efforts to surmount obstacles and proactively pursue their goals, thereby fostering adaptive functioning and positive development. In contrast, prohibitive behavior refers to harmful or otherwise maladaptive actions that may hinder individuals’ personal growth and developmental outcomes.

title: Recurrent trigeminal neuralgia caused by an anomalous cerebellar artery arising from the persistent primitive trigeminal artery: illustrative case
creator: Hiroki Narita, Nobuyuki Watanabe, Kentaro Watanabe, Ryoto Wachi, Kohei Ishikawa, Michihiro Tanaka, Yuichi Murayama
description: BACKGROUNDPersistent primitive trigeminal artery (PTA) and its related variants—the PTA family—are rare vascular anomalies that can cause trigeminal neuralgia through atypical neurovascular compression patterns, requiring careful anatomical evaluation. The authors describe a rare case of recurrent trigeminal neuralgia caused by an anomalous cerebellar artery arising from a PTA and further complicated by a long-standing Teflon granuloma.

title: Quantitative, longitudinal measurements of response to immunotherapy for glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI in a long-term survivor treated with autologous tumor lysate–loaded dendritic cell vaccine: an illustrative case
creator: Archith Rajan, Steven Brem, Daniel Gewolb, Ajay Kumar, Laiz Laura de Godoy, Arati Desai, MacLean P Nasrallah, Timothy Lucas, Laurie A Loevner, Suyash Mohan, Sanjeev Chawla
description: BACKGROUNDNeurosurgeons are in the forefront of developing clinical trials that harness the immune system to combat glioblastoma. Autologous tumor lysate–loaded dendritic cell vaccine (DCVax-L) is a novel immunotherapy for glioblastoma. An unmet need is to develop a sensitive, specific, feasible, clinically relevant, neuroimaging biomarker that accurately reflects response to immunotherapy.

title: Comparative evaluation of ASCVD, SCORE-2, and HEARTS risk scores in Colombian adults at risk of type 2 diabetes: stratification, concordance, and associated factors
creator: Luis A. Anillo Arrieta, Yenifer Diaz Montes, Juan Jose Espitia De La Hoz, Tania Acosta-Vergara, Rafael Tuesca Molina, Victor Florez-Garcia, Jorge Acosta-Reyes, J. E. Rod, Pablo Aschner, Noël C. Barengo
description: BackgroundThe Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk Estimator (ASCVD), Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation (SCORE-2), and HEARTS risk scales are commonly used to estimate cardiovascular risk (CVR); however, their applicability may vary depending on the population context.ObjectiveThis study aims to evaluate stratification, concordance, and associated clinical and social factors across three CVR scales in Colombian adults at risk of type 2 diabetes.

title: Incorporating Data From Text Messages and Email Into Psychotherapy: Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Ipsit V Vahia, Julia Kimball, Boyu Ren, Hailey Cray, Rebecca Dickinson, Heejung Kim, Dylan X Guan, Kerry J Ressler, Sahib Khalsa
description: BackgroundAs digital communication becomes central to daily life, psychotherapy increasingly has access to patients’ electronic media data. Although digital phenotyping has been widely studied, less is known about whether incorporating personal communication data, such as text messages, improves clinical outcomes in psychotherapy.

title: Practice Effects on Repeated Self-Administered Digital Cognitive Assessments in Cognitively Intact Older Adults from the Framingham Heart Study: Longitudinal Observational Study
creator: Kieffer Christianson, Chenglin Lyu, Cody Karjadi, Sherral Devine, Ting Fang Alvin Ang, Ileana De Anda-Duran, Vijaya B Kolachalama, Honghuang Lin, Huitong Ding, Katherine A Gifford, Rhoda Au, Phillip H Hwang, Preeti Sunderaraman
description: BackgroundRemote, self-administered digital assessments provide scalable approaches for monitoring cognition in older adults. Practice effects (PEs), once viewed as measurement noise, are increasingly recognized as potential markers of cognitive decline. As disease-modifying therapies for neurodegenerative conditions emerge, longitudinal digital assessments may capture subtle cognitive changes.

title: Convergent gut microbiome adaptation and pervasive antibiotic resistome in Qinghai–Tibet Plateau passerines
creator: Shunan Shi, Jiancheng Qi, Wenxuan Peng, Xiaodong Su, Peng Chen, Shoubiao Xu, Sheng Li, Long Ma, Wenlong Wang, Ke Jiang, Zhiguo Liu, Wei Li, Haoming Xiong, Yongshun Wang
description: IntroductionThe Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, an extreme high-altitude ecosystem, presents a unique model for studying host-microbe-environment coevolution under environmental stress. However, the role of resident wildlife, particularly non-migratory passerines, as reservoirs and vectors for cross-boundary antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination remains poorly understood.MethodsHere, through metagenomic analysis of two endemic passerines (Pseudopodoces humilis and Pyrgilauda ruficollis) and their habitats.

title: Engagement and Influence of Food-Related Videos on Social Media Within the Dietary Realities of Young Adults in Jamaica and the United Kingdom: Qualitative Cross-National Study
creator: Shaniek Parks, Charlotte Albury, Jessica Renzella, Asha Kaur, Suzanne Soares-Wynter, Mike Rayner, Peter Scarborough, Kongmeng Liew
description: BackgroundThe rise of video-based social media platforms and the shift toward a video-first content strategy by social media companies have altered how people consume and engage with food-related content. However, little is known about how young adults experience, interpret, and are influenced by food-related videos on social media across different national and cultural contexts.

title: Technological Integration in Triage With AI and Machine Learning Compared With Conventional Triage and Narrative Synthesis of Telehealth for Patient Prioritization in Emergency and Acute Care Settings: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Faii O M Ashour, Waqas Sami, Intima Alrimawi, Moattar Raza Rizvi, Majeda M El-Banna, Ivan Steenstra
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundConventional triage relies on clinician judgment and limited information available at first contact. AI and machine learning (ML) may improve early risk stratification, whereas tele-triage and patient-facing tools primarily support remote assessment, access, and care routing.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of AI- and ML-assisted triage systems and summarize evidence on tele-triage, workflow, implementation, economic, and equity outcomes.MethodsComparative studies published between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025, evaluating AI-, ML-, natural language processing–, telehealth-, or digitally enhanced

title: Simulated litter input drives shifts in carbon allocation strategies within alpine meadows of the three rivers source region
creator: Weishan Lin, Kejia De, Lin Zhang, Xuemei Xiang, Tingxu Feng, Fei Li, Xijie Wei
description: To reveal the transformation in carbon allocation strategies of alpine meadows in the Three Rivers Source Region under litter input.MethodsWe conducted an experimental study on litter input in alpine meadow in Chengduo County, Qinghai Province, with the following treatments: ungrazed (F), lightly grazed (L) and moderately grazed (M).

title: A short bout of low to moderate aerobic exercise influences cognitive performance in healthy adults based on task type, timing, and individual factors
creator: Cornelia Herbert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMany young adults experience stress and poor mental health, which can negatively impact cognitive performance and overall well-being. Short aerobic exercise sessions may help enhance cognitive processing in healthy individuals, but some questions remain.Aim/methodsThis study examined how a brief 16-minute aerobic exercise session, involving cycling at low to moderate intensity, affects verbal memory, fluency, and cognitive switching before, during, or after exercise across two testing sessions—one with exercise and one without—in 19 healthy young adults (both men and women).

title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study
creator: Bin Yang, Yongfeng Fan, Xinhong Wei, Chunlei Shi, Fabian Prasser
description: BackgroundDepression is a common mental disorder that seriously affects mental health and quality of life. Traditional depression diagnosis mainly relies on clinical interviews and subjective assessments, which may lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes. Electroencephalogram (EEG)-based computer-aided diagnosis has emerged as a promising, objective approach for depression recognition.

title: The diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening in primary care: a prospective validation study
creator: Malene Krogh, Marie Ørskov, Thomas Lohne Nørgaard, Marie Germund Nielsen, Martin Bach Jensen, Morten Sig Ager Jensen, Henrik Vorum, Jette Kolding Kristensen
description: ObjectivesThis study investigated the diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening in primary care, using ophthalmologist-led screening as the reference standard.MethodsPatients with type 2 diabetes attending routine appointments at 10 primary care clinics underwent AI-assisted screening, followed by re-screening at an ophthalmology clinic.

title: Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Is Associated With Greater Cardiovascular Risk Following Lumbar Interbody Fusion
creator: Shankar S Thiru, Haseeb E Goheer, Calvin J Harris, Abdulrahman Nazif, Mina Botros, Jonathan J Carmouche
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo compare perioperative cardiovascular outcomes between patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) following transforaminal or posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF/PLIF).MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients undergoing elective TLIF or PLIF between 2011 and 2025.

title: Fgf18 marks reserve skeletal progenitors in the fibrous periosteum contributing to bone fracture repair
creator: Xing Ji, Jasmin Koehnken Sawall, Xuejun Zhang, David M. Ornitz, Fanxin Long
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SUMMARYThe periosteum, a thin membranous tissue covering the external bone surface, is a well-established source of osteogenic activity during bone growth and fracture repair. However, the molecular identity and anatomical niche of its progenitor cells remain incompletely defined.

title: Oxidative signaling thresholds shape vulnerability in the central and peripheral nervous systems
creator: Shuji Wakatsuki, Toshiyuki Araki
description: Neurodegeneration is frequently associated with oxidative stress, yet the mechanisms that convert reactive oxygen species (ROS) into irreversible degenerative signals remain incompletely understood. Neurons in the central and peripheral nervous systems often differ in their responses to injury, but these differences cannot be reduced to a simple contrast between weak and strong antioxidant capacity.

title: PAX3-FOXO1 Contacts BRD4 through Its Acetylated Intrinsically Disordered Region
creator: Olivia A. Fraser, Madeline N. Schleicher, Maya L. Pagano, Scott A. Showalter
description: Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of transcription factors are frequent sites for post-translational modifications (PTMs), which mediate regulation through diverse mechanisms including protein–protein interactions. In the fusion oncoprotein PAX3-FOXO1, which drives alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, a lysine-rich region of the FOXO1 IDR is subject to acetylation resulting in stabilization and enhanced transcriptional activity.

title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure
creator: Christiane E. Angermann, Folkert W. Asselbergs, Georg Ertl, Stefan Störk
description: Purpose of ReviewImplanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy.

title: Telehealth Usability, Engagement Patterns, and Technical Infrastructure in Managing Noncommunicable Diseases Among Health Care Professionals in Brazil, Ghana, Honduras, and the United Kingdom: Multinational Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Ken Brackstone, Roberta Lins Gonçalves, Adriana Silvina Pagano, Zilma Silveira Nogueira Reis, Seth Kwaku Afagbedzi, Lysien Ivania Zambrano, Tainá Costa Pereira Lopes, Sarah Almeida Cordeiro, Julia Macedo Nunes, Wagner Meira Jr, James Batchelor, Antonio Luiz Pinho Ribeiro
description: BackgroundNoncommunicable diseases (NCDs) account for over 70% of global deaths, with hypertension and diabetes serving as major contributors. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted traditional health care services for NCDs and highlighted telehealth as a crucial alternative. Telehealth—encompassing synchronous and asynchronous electronic communication to deliver clinical services remotely—can overcome geographical barriers and enhance patient engagement.

title: Engineering metal-organic frameworks as precision nanomedicines for myocardial infarction therapy
creator: Kaijing Liu, Yuguang Liu, Aiai Zhang, Xiaolei Han
description: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of mortality worldwide. However, current therapeutic paradigms are limited in their ability to modulate the post-infarction pathological microenvironment with spatiotemporal precision. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), an emerging class of crystalline porous coordination polymers, offer exceptional structural programmability through their ultra-high specific surface areas, tunable pore architectures, and customizable surface chemistries.

title: Skills acquisition in cavity preparation in conservative dentistry through virtual haptic simulation
creator: Sebastiana Arroyo-Bote, Catalina Bennasar-Verger, Daniela Paz-Vallejos, Jorge Dominguez-Perez, Pere Riutord-Sbert, Thais Cristina Pereira
description: IntroductionVirtual reality-based training tools have become increasingly incorporated into health education in recent years. In dentistry, three-dimensional (3D) haptic simulators are used in several undergraduate programs to support preclinical training in procedures such as caries removal, cavity preparation, coronal access, prosthodontic preparation, periodontal therapy, and surgical techniques.

title: Impact of scan duration and scatter correction on quantitative accuracy in Yttrium-90 PET/CT imaging using LAFOV and SAFOV systems: a phantom and clinical evaluation
creator: Konstantinos G. Zeimpekis, Magdalena Kulgawczuk, Carola Bregenzer, Marc Schindewolf, Christos Sachpekidis, Hasan Sari, Kalyani Pandya, Ali Afshar-Oromieh, Axel Rominger, Kuangyu Shi, Robert Seifert
description: PurposeThis study compared quantitative accuracy and image quality of post-radioembolization selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT) 90Y PET/CT using a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) and standard axial field-of-view (SAFOV) system, focusing on absolute (ABS) versus relative (RS) scatter correction. Additionally, variance modeling and logistic regression were performed to define injected-activity thresholds ensuring reliable quantification at different acquisition durations.

title: Declining centromere strength compromises meiotic chromosome segregation in aging oocytes
creator: Tom Lemonnier, Marie Dumont, Jiyeon Leem, Aysia Khan, Hossein Yazdkhasti, Vitaly Zimyanin, Ani Khutsaidze, Stefanie Redemann, Daniele Fachinetti, Binyam Mogessie
description: Lemonnier, Dumont, and colleagues show that reproductive aging is associated with weakened centromere function and altered spindle microtubule organization in mammalian oocytes. Their findings support a role for reduced CENP-A–dependent centromere function in chromosome segregation errors and highlight multiple vulnerabilities that may compromise egg quality with advancing maternal age.

title: Amyloidosis awareness and colchicine adherence in patients with familial Mediterranean fever: a cross-sectional study in an endemic region
creator: Elif Dincses-Nas, Sevilay Batibay, Tugce Bozkurt, Ender Igneci, Seda Gunay Akyol, Esen Kasapoglu
description: IntroductionFamilial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) is the most common hereditary autoinflammatory disease, and secondary amyloidosis remains its most serious complication. We aimed to investigate amyloidosis awareness, colchicine adherence and related factors among FMF patients.MethodsIn this cross-sectional single-center study, patients with FMF completed a face-to-face questionnaire assessing amyloidosis awareness using structured questions and colchicine adherence through self-reported medication use.

title: Epitope-diverse autoantibodies induce neutrophil–epithelial niches driving kidney injury in ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis
creator: Masayuki Nishide, Hiroaki Matsushita, Yumiko Mizuno, Kei Nishimura, Patrick M. Lelliott, Shoji Kawada, Takashi Fujii, Shogo Kamikawaji, Tatsuya Nonaka, Daisuke Motooka, Shoichi Metsugi, Hiroshi Shimagami, Atsuko Tsujii Miyamoto, Yasuhiro Kato, Kohei Tsujimoto, Ryuya Edahiro, Yuya Shirai, Yuji Yamamo
description: Nishide et al. identify neutrophil–epithelial niches associated with local kidney injury in ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis using single-cell–resolved spatial transcriptomics. Neutrophils in these niches show Fcγ receptor-related programs linked to epitope-diverse autoantibodies, while anti-MPO antibody combinations reproduce key pathological features in mice and engineered one-armed antibodies attenuate kidney injury in vivo. Introduction Autoantibody-driven inflammation is a fundamental mechanism underlying organ-specific autoimmune diseases.

title: Preschool attention and sleep support (PASS): protocol for a pilot feasibility randomized clinical trial
creator: Naomi O. Davis, Brian Eichner, Matthew J. Gibson, Jessica R. Lunsford-Avery
description: IntroductionAttention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) symptoms often emerge during preschool, highlighting a critical period for prevention. Preventative ADHD interventions may be most effective if they target biological mechanisms linked to core ADHD pathophysiology. Sleep dysregulation represents a potential target, yet the gold-standard behavioral intervention (behavioral parent training, BPT) focuses primarily on ameliorating daytime impairment.

title: Glymphatic system impairment in neurological disorders: potential mechanisms and therapeutic targets
creator: Nan-Nan Wang, Zhi-Jun Liu, Yong Wang, Fei Cao, Da Xu
description: The glymphatic system is a brain-wide metabolic clearance pathway, orchestrating the removal of neurotoxic wastes via glial-dependent perivascular networks. Mediated by polarized aquaporin-4 (AQP4) channels on astrocytic end-feet, this macroscopic system drives the convective exchange of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and interstitial fluid (ISF), establishing a functional coupling between the central nervous system (CNS) and the adaptive immune system.

title: GMMA as adjuvant and carrier for mucosal delivery of group A streptococcus glycoconjugate vaccine
creator: James Ozanne, Manolya Saydam, Elena Palmieri, Roberta Di Benedetto, Anjum Aktar, Martina Carducci, Luca Rovetini, Omar Rossi, H. Alexandra Shaw, Francesca Micoli, Fatme Mawas
description: Group A streptococcus (GAS) infection is usually initiated by colonization of mucosal sites such as the pharynx, followed by invasion and systemic dissemination. Development of a vaccine that can prevent colonization is enticing as it would prevent subsequent infections and all associated autoimmune sequalae such as rheumatic heart disease (RHD).

title: Perceived service quality scale for community pharmacies: tool translation of the short form and service quality exploration
creator: Norah O. Abanmy, Carl R. Schneider, Stephen R. Carter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimIn the community pharmacy sector the concept of service quality is important. Pharmacists working in these settings provide useful services that go beyond merely dispensing medications. This study aimed to translate the short Perceived Service Quality Scale (PSQS−SF) to Arabic and to use this scale to assess the determinants of service quality of community pharmacies in relation to competitively priced high quality service and loyalty intention.MethodsA pre−validated short Perceived Service Quality Scale (pSQS−A−SF) was translated from English to Arabic, validated

title: Framing a pig welfare assessment protocol suitable for smallholder settings in low-to-middle income countries
creator: Lauren Oehlers, Rebecca Doyle, Phil C Glatz, Jenny-Ann Toribio
description: Smallholder pig production in low-to-middle income countries (LMIC) can be an important contributor to the livelihoods of families including income, food, social and cultural obligations. However, to date there has been scant evaluation of welfare in smallholder pig production systems in these countries.

title: Eating attitudes among college students: the role of body shape concerns, mental health, and obesity
creator: Shromona Das, Divyansha Khajuria, Monika Kulshreshtha, Shivani Chandel
description: BackgroundBody image concerns, mental health disorders, and obesity are highly prevalent among young adults and can significantly influence eating attitudes during the college years.AimTo study the prevalence of disordered eating attitudes, body shape concerns, common mental health disorders, and obesity among college-going students, and to find out their inter-relationship.

title: Impact of prenatal pyrethroid pesticide exposure on neonatal lymphocyte subsets and apoptosis: a birth cohort study
creator: Zhiye Qi, Lili Zhang, Xia Xiao, Kun Wu, Shuqi Chen, Xiaoxiao Song, Yan Li
description: BackgroundPrenatal pyrethroid pesticides (PYRs) exposure may elevate infection diseases susceptibility of children. However, it is unclear the relationship of PYRs exposure and neonatal immune function. We explored the association of PYRs exposure during three trimesters with neonatal immunity and the roles of lymphocyte apoptosis.MethodsMaternal urinary PYRs metabolites (3PBA, 4F3PBA, cis-DBCA) were measured in each trimester.

title: Curcumin-loaded alkali-heat-treated titanium modulates macrophage inflammatory responses
creator: Andrew Cedillo, Niloufar Abedi, Sahar Vahabzadeh, Miya Kang
description: Chronic inflammation at the implant–tissue interface is a major contributor to implant failure. Therefore, enhancing the biological response of titanium (Ti) surfaces is critical for promoting early osseointegration and improving long-term implant stability. In this study, alkali-heat-treated (AHT) Ti was evaluated as a platform for the controlled delivery of curcumin (Cur), a natural anti-inflammatory compound.

title: TAR-0520, a new candidate in oncodermatology: Results of a phase 1 program in healthy volunteers
creator: Philippe Andres, Gareth Winckle, Alexandra Lamquin, Janusz Czernielewski
description: PurposeTAR-0520 gel is a new topical formulation of brimonidine tartrate designed to prevent chemotherapy-induced skin toxicities. We report here the main outcomes of the phase 1 program which included two double-blind, randomized trials in healthy volunteers (TAR006 and TAR012) and were performed to evaluate the safety, local tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics (PD) of TAR-0520 gel.

title: Therapeutic potential of combination medicinal mushrooms (NevG) in ischemic stroke: correlating motor function, cognitive recovery, and hippocampal integrity in MCAO rats
creator: Nur Athirah Azlan, Misya Afiqah Noor Tuah, Nik Nasihah Nik Ramli, Hussin Muhammad, Zolkapli Eshak, Liao Peng, Chen Bo, Yatinesh Kumari, Imran Jazuli, Che Mohd Nasril Che Mohd Nasir, Syntyche Seow Ling Sing, Cheng Poh Guat, Hafizah Abdul Hamid, Zaw Myo Hein, Muhammad Danial Che Ramli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIschemic stroke is a major neurological disorder that is characterized by cognitive decline and sensorimotor impairment. Despite the potential of therapeutic effects and anti-inflammatory properties of medicinal mushrooms, most current research focuses on single-species effects rather than combined formulations.

title: Revelations of pancreatic cancer treated by high-intensity focused ultrasound
creator: Wen Zhou, Cheng Lei, Xiaojing Xue, Hongfan Yu, Jian Li, Wenxi Li, Shizhu Li, Wei Xu, Min Li, Jing Li, Qiulan Zheng, Miao Huang, Yuxian Nie, Jin Bai, Gang Feng, Xiuni Gan, Qiuling Shi
description: BackgroundPancreatic cancer remains among the most treatment-refractory solid malignancies worldwide. High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) surgery is a treatment option with the advantage of providing cancer pain relief. However, there has been limited research addressing the trends in pancreatic cancer treatment utilizing HIFU surgery.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic atlas uncovers immune/structural lineage remodeling and fibrosis in Klebsiella pneumoniae-infected porcine lungs
creator: Wei Wang, Junhui Zhu, Sibo Zhu, Changyou Xia, Xuan Jiang, Chuntong Bao, Ziheng Li, Rining Zhu, Tong Wu, Nan Zhang, Qila Sa, Shaopeng Wei, Brendon Scicluna, Fengyang Li, Liancheng Lei, Na Li
description: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a predominant pathogen in respiratory infections, whose widespread antibiotic resistance poses severe public health risks and economic burdens. As the primary target of KP infection, the lung contains diverse immune cells, while pulmonary cellular responses to KP remain poorly understood.

title: Social inequalities in return-to-work among colorectal cancer survivors in Germany
creator: Johannes Soff, Ibrahim Demirer, Nora Tabea Sibert, Clara Breidenbach, Nicole Ernstmann, Paula Heidkamp, Lina Heier, Kati Hiltrop, Sophie Klara Schellack, Johanna Weiß, Oliver Rick, Stefan Rolf Benz, Nico Dragano, Christoph Kowalski
description: BackgroundFor working-age patients with colorectal cancer, returning to work is a key rehabilitation goal. This study examines the association between socio-economic position (SEP) and return-to-work (RTW), including competing outcomes (pension entry and death), following medical rehabilitation.MethodsGerman Pension Insurance data (2013–2022) were analysed, including 32,174 formerly employed patients (ICD-10 C18–C20) of working age undergoing oncological rehabilitation.

title: Dietary replacement of whole soybean grain with micronized defatted soybean meal in dairy cow diets: effects on intake, digestibility, ruminal parameters, and milk yield and composition
creator: Thiago Thiarles Braw André Furlan Romualdo Angelo Abraãn Lincon Picciuto Maciel, Eliane Sayuri Miyagi Okada, Euclides Reuter De Oliveira, Jefferson Rodrigues Gandra, Vera Lúcia Banys, Thaís Da Silva Fernandes, Andréa Maria de Araújo Gabriel, Claudia Andrea Lima Cardoso, Vicente Ribeiro Rocha Júnior,
description: This study aimed to evaluate effects of replacing whole soybean grain with micronized defatted soybean meal (MDSM) in diets of lactating dairy cows on performance, digestion, metabolism, and milk yield and composition. Ten primiparous Jersey cows with an initial body weight (BW) of 410 ± 9 kg and 105 ± 5 days in milk were used.

title: Imaging-Enhanced Prediction of Upper Limb Motor Function After Stroke Using Automated Segmentation and Cluster Analysis
creator: Seungwoo Cha, Wi-Sun Ryu, Bokgi Hwang, Dae Yul Kim, Seung Hak Lee
description: BackgroundStroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, and early prediction of motor outcomes is critical for guiding individualized rehabilitation strategies. Although neuroimaging offers prognostic insights, its clinical integration remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether explainable imaging-derived features can improve the prediction of upper limb motor impairment and to identify distinct recovery profiles through cluster analysis.

title: Early cardiac doppler findings and venous hemodynamic burden after combined superficial venous treatment for primary lower extremity varicose veins: an exploratory retrospective cohort study
creator: Yunkai Luo, Chenke Pan, Bin Ying, Jingjin Wu, Yanbo Lou
description: This study was designed to explore early postoperative cardiac Doppler findings, venous structural and hemodynamic burden in patients with primary lower extremity varicose veins (LEVVs) undergoing a combined superficial venous treatment pathway. A retrospective descriptive statistical analysis was performed on preoperative and postoperative one-week postoperative transthoracic echocardiographic Doppler data from 69 patients with primary LEVVs.

title: Prospective comparative assessment of liver stiffness and steatosis between iLivTouch and FibroScan
creator: Frida Nuñez-Mercado, Eva Juárez-Hernández, Raúl A Gómez-Mendoza, Martha H. Ramos-Ostos, Misael Uribe, Graciela Castro-Narro, Iván López-Méndez
description: Background:Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease currently represents the leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. FibroScan and iLivTouch are 2 devices that employ similar principles to estimate liver steatosis and fibrosis, although few studies have directly compared their results.Aim:To evaluate the concordance of 2 transient elastography devices for the estimation of liver steatosis and fibrosis.Methods:A prospective study was conducted.

title: Long-term safety and pulmonary function stabilization with nintedanib in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease, 2020–2025: a real-world retrospective study from a reference centre
creator: Stylianos Panopoulos, Vasiliki Poulia, Nikolaos Vlachogiannis, Vasiliki-Kalliopi Bournia, Maria G Tektonidou, Petros P Sfikakis
description: Randomized trials have demonstrated that nintedanib is beneficial for Systemic Sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) with an acceptable safety profile. We evaluated the long-term safety and efficacy of nintedanib in a real-world SSc-ILD cohort. Medical records of SSc patients receiving nintedanib for newly diagnosed fibrotic or progressive ILD between 2020 and 2025 in our center were retrospectively reviewed.

title: Strange attractors: purpose, synchronicity, flow, and the neurodynamics of meaning
creator: Steven Kotler, Michael Mannino, Karl Friston, Scott Kelso
description: This paper proposes a neurodynamic framework for meaningful experience, grounded in the recursive alignment of brain dynamics across time. We argue that the meaningful experiences known as “purpose”, “synchronicity”, and “flow” are not distinct phenomena, but temporal expressions of the same underlying process: metastable coherence in the brain’s attractor landscape.

title: Spring-assisted cranioplasty for sagittal synostosis: long-term clinical and patient-reported outcomes
creator: Amparo Saenz, David Dunaway, Greg James, Juling Ong, Dulanka Silva, Alessandro Borghi, Silvia Schievano, Owase Jeelani
description: PurposeSpring-assisted cranioplasty is an established technique for the correction of isolated sagittal craniosynostosis, yet data on long-term clinical durability and patient-perceived outcomes remain limited. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term surgical, aesthetic, and patient-reported outcomes following spring-assisted cranioplasty, with a particular focus on the need for secondary cranial surgery and concordance between surgeon- and parent-reported assessments.

title: Tapping into the micro-sites in multiwalled carbon nanotube sheets: nanofibers versus trunk deagglomeration for electrodes in redox flow batteries
creator: Ibrahim Mustafa, Maryam AlNahyan
description: We demonstrate an enhanced micro-site exposure capability to tap into the nanofibers as opposed to trunks consisting of Multiwalled Carbon Nanotube (MWCNT) bundles. We show this by accelerating the replenishment of the under exposed material within the active sonication zone during MWCNT sheet fabrication.

title: Beyond radiation: immunological potentials of boron neutron capture therapy
creator: Muyasha Abulimiti, Yu Sugawara, Yinuo Li, Hideyuki Sakurai, Yoshitaka Matsumoto
description: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is a targeted radiotherapeutic modality that employs boron-10 (10B) to capture thermal neutrons, thereby releasing high-linear energy transfer α-particles and lithium ions that selectively eradicate tumor cells while sparing the surrounding normal tissues. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including inhibitors of PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4, enhance antitumor immunity by alleviating immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment.

title: The impact of the 7th October war on preterm birth rates and neonatal outcomes: a retrospective comparative study from northern Israel
creator: Raghda Zidan Sweid, Adi Sharabi Nov, Hana Helfgot, Steven L. Warsof, Inbar Ben-Shachar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeMaternal psychological stress is associated with adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including preterm birth and low birthweight. Warfare represents a significant source of acute and chronic stress, yet its impact on pregnancy outcomes remains unclear.

title: 2-Aminooxazoles and 2-aminothiazoles: green regioselective synthesis and bioactivity
creator: Pankaj Popatrao Yenare, Rohini Dattatraya Patare, Kailas Khandu Sanap
description: 2-Aminooxazole and 2-aminothiazole are heterocyclic compounds that can be developed to be therapeutically significant in medicinal chemistry as they are associated with a myriad of biologically important multicentric activities such as anticancer, anti-viral, anti-bacterial, anti-fungal, and enzyme inhibition. Chemically, they have been reported to target critical enzymes such as CDKs, aurora kinases, DHPS, and proteases.

title: Comparative biochemical analysis of tea (Camellia sinensis) and coffee (Coffea arabica) extracts identifies the ethyl acetate fraction of green tea as a potential dual digestive enzyme inhibitor: an in vitro and in silico study
creator: Youmna E. El-Saied, Abdullah A. Elgazar, Fardous F. El-Senduny, Nada E. Hammouda, Omali Y. El-Khawaga, Farid A. Badria
description: Metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), have prompted interest in identifying natural products capable of modulating digestive enzymes. This study comparatively evaluated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant activity, and digestive enzyme inhibitory activities of green tea (GT), black tea (BT), and green coffee (GC) extracts.

title: Drug repurposing in KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC: a focus on resistance mechanisms and clinical strategies
creator: Anisha Jain, Rafael Rosell, Chandan Dharmashekara, Bhargav Shreevatsa, María González-Cao, Amogha Shivakumar, Shiva Prasad Kollur, Ashwini Prasad, Chandan Shivamallu, M. N. Nagendra Prasad
description: KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has transitioned from a therapeutically problematic disease to a precision-targetable cancer, anchored by the landmark approvals of sotorasib and adagrasib. Yet despite these advances, responses remain limited in duration and multiple mechanisms of rapid adaptive resistance emerge under inhibitor pressure.

title: Gut microbiome composition and cellulolytic bacteria associated with the carpenter bee Xylocopa frontalis
creator: Ana Carolina Costa Santos, Joberth Lee Corrêa, Darlan Sedinário de Lima, Aline Carla Alves Silva Andrade, Camila Nonato Junqueira, Anderson Rodrigues dos Santos, Solange Cristina Augusto, Ana Maria Bonetti, Carlos Ueira-Vieira
description: AbstractCarpenter bees of the genus Xylocopa interact extensively with woody substrates during nest construction, suggesting that associated microorganisms may contribute to the degradation of plant-derived polymers. Despite their ecological relevance, the gut microbiome and functional potential of Xylocopa species remain poorly characterized.

title: A label-free fluorescent sensor for miR-21 based on sequentially coupled CHA–HCR dual-stage amplification and synergistic signal regulation by graphene oxide and SYBR Green I
creator: Can Qiao, Zhenliang Zhang, Yidan Sang, Mengyang Hu, Yafei Dong, Luhui Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, and their sensitive and accurate detection is important for early cancer diagnosis. However, achieving sensitive miRNA detection and logic analysis while maintaining a simple workflow remains challenging. In this study, catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) and hybridization chain reaction (HCR) were sequentially coupled to construct a dual-stage enzyme-free amplification circuit and integrated with a label-free fluorescence reporting strategy based on graphene oxide and SYBR Green I for logical recognition and sensitive detection of miR-21.

title: In-hospital mortality and complications are increased in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients with myelodysplastic syndromes
creator: Aniket Vijay Rao, Aditya Sanjeevi, Daniel Jose Idoate-Domench, Diya Jayanth Kamdar, Suraj Palavilayil, Abdullah Orakzai, Himal Kharel, Muhammad Hammad Sharif, Sujay Prabath Dronamraju
description: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains the only curative therapy for patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS). Despite evidence of comparable outcomes in selected older adults, disparities in HSCT utilization persist. This study analyzes trends, outcomes, and barriers such as age and insurance status associated with HSCT in MDS.

title: Fibrinogen Alpha Chain (FGA) Associates With Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition, Stemness, and the USP–Catenin Complex in Colorectal Cancer
creator: Hao Lin, Weixu Chen, Qing Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) progression is heavily driven by epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and the acquisition of cancer stem cell (CSC) properties. Elucidating the specific molecular drivers and dynamic indicators underlying these processes is crucial for advancing CRC management.MethodsThe clinical significance and diagnostic value of fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) were evaluated using TCGA data, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and paired pre‐ and postoperative serum samples. The biological functions of FGA were assessed in HCT116 cells through Transwell and 3D spheroid formation assays.

title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification
creator: Hyunwoo Yoo, Gail L Rosen
description: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification.

title: Mobile Genetic Elements as Key Drivers of Bacterial Evolution and Adaptation in Agroecosystems
creator: Manuela Costanzo, Luciana Di Gregorio, Silvia Tabacchioni, Annamaria Bevivino, Andrea Visca
description: Mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including plasmids, transposons, integrative and conjugative elements, and phage-derived sequences, are central drivers of bacterial evolution in agroecosystems. By enabling horizontal gene transfer, MGEs allow soil- and plant-associated bacteria to rapidly acquire complex functional traits, facilitating adaptation to fluctuating environmental conditions and different agricultural management practices.

title: A Lip Mass Revealing Syphilis: A Case Report With a Review of the Literature
creator: May Ahmed Alsenani, Rana Saud Alshagroud, Emad Hadlaq, Bader Mutrik Aldawsari, Hassan Ibrahim Khormi, Abdulrahman A. Altariqi, Norah Ameen Aloushan, Abdulaziz khalid Aloshaywi, Mohammed Abdulaziz Alangari
description: BackgroundSyphilis is a chronic systemic infection caused by Treponema pallidum and is well known for its wide spectrum of clinical presentations. Oral manifestations are uncommon and often mimic benign or reactive lesions, making diagnosis challenging, particularly in the absence of overt systemic symptoms.

title: Analytic Misjudgment of Drug Safety Evidence and Causality: From the Prosecutor’s Fallacy and Simpson’s Paradox to Artificial Intelligence
creator: Tarek A. Hammad, Justine Rochon
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Drug safety assessment, particularly in the post-marketing setting, is especially vulnerable to analytic misjudgment because it relies on heterogeneous evidence streams, incomplete data, infrequent events, and decisions made under substantial uncertainty. Recurring sources of error include misinterpretation of conditional probabilities, conflation of association with causation, inappropriate denominator and comparator selection, inadequate consideration of background incidence and confounding, aggregation artifacts such as Simpson’s paradox, and overinterpretation of exploratory findings arising from multiplicity or repeated testing.

title: Advances in the Role of Chemokines in Microwave Ablation‐Based Combinatorial Immunotherapy
creator: Ruijie An, Ningning He, Wendong Gu
description: Immunotherapy enhances antitumor immunity to eliminate malignant cells and has great potential to prevent tumor recurrence and distant metastasis. In addition to direct tumor destruction, microwave ablation (MWA) remodels the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and induces antitumor immune responses, providing a strong rationale for combination with immunotherapy.

title: “I decide for myself. I’m like the boss of myself. I can cook when I want.” Prisoners’ experiences with a self-catering food system in a Norwegian low-security prison
creator: Astrid Kolderup Hervik, Stein Egil Kolderup Hervik
description: BackgroundFood is a central part of everyday life in prison, carrying meanings and values that shape identity and social relations and may have important implications for health and well-being. Previous research suggests that self-catering systems, whereby prisoners plan, shop for, and prepare their own meals, may increase opportunities for agency, participation, and health promotion.

title: AMH measurement is being overused—Are you guilty?
creator: Antti Perheentupa
description: he Nordic countries and elsewhere. AMH is secreted, not only by the granulosa cells surrounding the oocytes in small antral follicles, but also by those of preantral follicles. The circulating AMH concentration usually correlates fairly well with the antral follicle count (AFC). The number of antral follicles (2–9 mm in diameter) can be counted using transvaginal ultrasound.

title: Simultaneous Valve-in-Valve TAVR With Bioprosthetic Valve Fracture and Left Atrial Appendage Closure for Refractory Left Atrial Thrombus
creator: Ju-Hsin Chang, Chia-hao Liu, Chi-Sheuan Chin, Chia-Hao Chen, Keng-Yuan Lee, Li-Chun Wang, Ke-Wei Chen
description: BackgroundPersistent left atrial appendage thrombus complicates structural intervention when anticoagulation is limited by bleeding risk.Case SummaryA 74-year-old man with prior surgical aortic and mitral bioprostheses presented with heart failure from severe bioprosthetic aortic stenosis and persistent left atrial appendage thrombus despite 6 months of anticoagulation.

title: Progressive Enlargement of a Coronary Artery Communication With an Atrial Septal Defect Closure Device
creator: Soichiro Kobayashi, Akihiro Takasaki, Yoshito Ogihara, Tairo Kurita, Kaoru Dohi
description: A 70-year-old man underwent coronary angiography 8 years after transcatheter atrial septal defect closure. Although no coronary stenosis was observed, a progressively enlarged coronary artery communication originating from the atrial branch of the left circumflex artery and extending into the device was identified. Serial imaging demonstrated progressive enlargement and elongation of this vascular structure over time.

title: Emotion regulation and its association with subjective memory performance among undergraduate students at port said university
creator: Sama Essam Ismail, Ahmed Gamal Sharaf Eldin, Nihal Sharaf Eldin, Nesrine Saad Farrag
description: BackgroundEmotion regulation (ER), particularly through cognitive reappraisal (CR) and expressive suppression (ES), plays an important role in psychological well-being and higher-order cognitive functioning. Both ER and subjective memory performance (SMP), as measured by the Prospective and Retrospective Memory Questionnaire (PRMQ), have been proposed to draw on shared executive control resources.

title: Severe Hypertriglyceridemia Managed in a Pregnant Patient Using Nonstatin Therapies
creator: Rukmini Roy, Marie Altenberg, Shakeela Faulkner, Laura Dickens, Mary Horan, Michael Davidson, Hena Patel
description: BackgroundSevere hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) in pregnancy is associated with increased maternal-fetal morbidity. Treatment options remain limited because of fetal safety concerns.Case SummaryA 34-year-old pregnant patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus and HTG was referred to our cardio-obstetrics multidisciplinary team for management of HTG at 16 weeks of gestation.

title: Exercise promotes lipophagy and mitigates cognitive impairment in Alzheimer’s disease through downregulating microglial TMEM9
creator: Liying Zhang, Shiyin Li, Xiaomeng Ma, Shimei Cheng, Ziying Ye, Shuhua Liu, Luping Qin, Huimin Dong, Yifeng Feng, Mingyue Li, Jinghui Xu, Lei Cai, Xiquan Hu, Xiaofei He
description: BackgroundAutophagy-lysosomal dysfunction contributes to lipid droplet (LD) accumulation, which drives pathological progression in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Exercise is reported to restore autophagy-lysosomal function and attenuate cognitive impairment in AD, but its regulation of LD deposition remains unknown.Methods5×FAD transgenic mice underwent a three-month exercise intervention.

title: Retraction Note: Antitumor effect and molecular mechanism of fucoidan in NSCLC
creator: Xiaohan Chen, Li Sun, Xiaojuan Wei, Haijun Lu, Ye Tan, Zhanyi Sun, Jinju Jiang
description: m-TOR band in A549 cells (Fig. 2B); between Cyclin D1 band in A549 cells (Fig. 2A) and pm-TOR band in A549 cells (Fig. 2B); between the upper part of the A549/Fucoidan 10 mg/ml panel and lower part of the H1650/Fucoidan 10 mg/ml panel; and.

title: Recurrent Coronary Restenosis in Takayasu Arteritis
creator: Abdallah Rayyan, Aseed Mestarihi, Khanjan Shah, Matheen Khuddus
description: BackgroundCoronary involvement in Takayasu arteritis is uncommon but associated with high rates of in-stent restenosis and challenging revascularization.Case SummaryA 22-year-old woman with Takayasu arteritis and congenital antithrombin III deficiency presented with non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction due to severe ostial right coronary artery in-stent restenosis after multiple prior percutaneous interventions. Intravascular ultrasound confirmed significant neointimal hyperplasia.

title: Molecular epidemiology and emerging tet(X)-associated resistance of Elizabethkingia spp. in Taiwan, 2016–2022
creator: Yu-Tsung Huang, Cheng-Yen Kao, Han-Yueh Kuo, Li-Ting Kao, Yu-Chi Chang, Yen-Ting Liao, Li-Cheng Wu, Tzu-Ling Chen, Yu-Kai Tu, Tsung-Ying Yang
description: Elizabethkingia species are opportunistic gram-negative pathogens associated with nosocomial infections and limited therapeutic options. Longitudinal data characterizing antimicrobial resistance and molecular determinants in Taiwan remain scarce. A total of 191 non-duplicate Elizabethkingia clinical isolates were collected at the National Taiwan University Hospital between 2016 and 2022. Species identification was confirmed by 16S rRNA sequencing. Elizabethkingia anophelis predominated (81.

title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction
creator: Ingmar Brilmayer, Philip Georgis, Petra B Schumacher
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding language in real-world interaction requires methods that integrate auditory, visual, and neural signals. We present a proof-of-concept study combining mobile electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking to investigate referential selection during dyadic communication.

title: Operational comparability of ecological status assessment in Iberian transboundary rivers
creator: António Tovar Faro, João Manuel Oliveira, Gonçalo Duarte, Paulo Branco, Pedro Segurado, Teresa Ferreira
description: The European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) requires member states to assess the ecological status of surface waters using biological quality elements (BQEs). Although the WFD includes intercalibration procedures to harmonise class boundaries, differences between national assessment systems may affect the comparability of ecological status classifications, particularly in transboundary rivers.

title: Characterization of Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter calcoaceticus-baumannii complex traumatic wound isolates
creator: Ian H. Windham, Jeffrey A. Kimbrel, Olivia A. Boykin, Marina R. Wylie, Mark P. Simons, Seth A. Schobel, Michael Rouse, Eric A. Elster, Christopher J. Dente, Nicholas A. Be, Joshua Stanbro, Jennifer Huber, Meenu M. Upadhyay, Angela R. Melton-Celsa, D. Scott Merrell
description: Healing of traumatic wounds is complicated by infecting pathogens, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa and members of the Acinetobacter calcoaceticus-baumannii complex among the most common infectious agents. However, a full understanding of genotypic and phenotypic differences between circulating wound isolates is lacking. To address this, traumatic wounds were sampled at Emory University Hospital, and 24 isolates were characterized; we focused on P.

title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
creator: Yangmengfan Chen, Hao Du, Heng Sun, Xingcan Huang, Duan Wang, Xuming Chen, Jiehao Chen, Xuanjun Zhang, Liqiang Zhou, Zongke Zhou
description: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS).

title: Mosquito repellency mediated by skin commensal Bacillus species via volatile metabolite reprogramming
creator: Zhenyu Gu, Heting Gao, Hongxia Guo, Zhihua Fan, Weixian Zhang, Dan Xing, Xinyu Zhou, Haotian Yu, Teng Zhao, Jiahong Wu, Chunxiao Li
description: Individual variation in human attractiveness to mosquitoes critically influences vector-borne disease transmission, and this phenomenon arises from multiple underlying factors. This study integrated human skin microbiome profiling, non-human primate in situ intervention, and volatilomics to uncover a microbial-mediated mechanism underlying host-specific mosquito repellency. Bacillus species were identified as a microbial signature associated with reduced mosquito attraction in humans.

title: Proteomic screening identifies HNRNPA2B1 as an epigenetic repressor of Epstein-Barr virus reactivation
creator: Febri Gunawan Sugiokto, Yuxin Liu, Renfeng Li
description: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) establishes lifelong persistent infection in over 90% of the world’s population. The virus persists as an episome in the host cells during latency and periodically reactivates through transcriptional activation of the immediate-early (IE) genes. While epigenetic regulation is central to maintaining viral latency, the host factors that enforce repression at these promoters remain incompletely defined.

title: Early catastrophic posterior migration of a cervical disc replacement polyethylene insert resulting in complete spinal cord injury: illustrative case
creator: Pirooz Fereydouni, Arthur W. Cowman, Matthew J. Strok, Sultan Baz, Shahabeddin Yazdanpanah, Ryan Hoang, Michael S. Kim, Sohaib Z. Hashmi, Don Y. Park, Nitin N. Bhatia, Yu-Po Lee, Hao-Hua Wu
description: BACKGROUNDPosterior migration of a mobile-bearing cervical disc replacement (CDR) can be catastrophic.
