The authors report a single-patient case of catastrophic failure after recent trauma and implant loosening.OBSERVATIONSA 48-year-old woman had received C5–6 and C6–7 Mobi-C CDRs at an outside institution 3 weeks before presentation and had sustained a ground-level fall 8 days before presentation.

title: UV-B-induced DNA repair mechanisms and their effects on mutagenesis and culturability in Escherichia coli
creator: Sreyashi Ghosh, Jenet Narzary, Mehmet A. Orman
description: Ultraviolet-B (UV-B) radiation, intensified by ozone depletion, induces DNA damage and promotes mutagenesis, shaping evolution. While UV-induced SOS responses are well characterized in bacteria, the cellular consequences of prolonged UV-B exposure remain less clear. Prolonged UV-B exposure disrupts transcription and translation, as well as RecA-mediated SOS induction, without major changes in membrane permeability or reactive oxygen species.

title: Vertebral Rotation Discrepancy for Distal Add-on when Selecting the Touched Vertebra as the Lowest Instrumented Vertebra in Thoracic Curves of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis
creator: Hong Jin Kim, Subin Lim, Hyung Rae Lee, Jae Hyuk Yang, Seung Woo Suh
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo assess the influencing factors of the distal add-on when selecting the touched vertebra (TV) as the lowest instrumented vertebra (LIV) in thoracic idiopathic scoliosis (IS).MethodsA total of 96 thoracic IS patients who underwent deformity correction with LIV = TV were retrospectively analyzed to evaluate the distal add-on.

title: Artificial Intelligence Use Among Health Care Professionals in the United States and United Kingdom: Cross-National Survey
creator: Emre Sezgin, Jennifer Lee, Tomasz Jadczyk, Alysha J Taxter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This cross-sectional study examined AI use among 524 health care professionals in the United States and United Kingdom, focusing on current applications, access, barriers, and factors that could support adoption. AI use was common but varied across professional and national contexts, with findings highlighting the importance of evidence, organizational guidance, training, privacy safeguards, and integration into clinical workflows for responsible adoption.

title: Bridgedd, a Health Care Staff–Facing Community Resource Navigation Tool for an Urban Safety-Net Hospital: Cross-Sectional Formative Pilot Study
creator: Aravind Venkatachalam, Charles E Moore, Amaryllis Mavragani
description: BackgroundHealth care professionals in safety-net settings often rely on lengthy and inconsistently maintained community health resource lists when connecting patients with services. Bridgedd is a health care staff–facing web application designed to generate geographically and categorically filtered community resources in a unique format that makes information about each resource more accessible.

title: The association between naloxone distribution, buprenorphine treatment and retention and incident high‐risk opioid prescribing with opioid overdose death in Kentucky, Massachusetts, New York and Ohio, United States: An exploratory community‐level cohort study of data from the HEALing Communities Stu
creator: Alexander Y. Walley, Debbie M. Cheng, Nathan Vandergrift, Marc Larochelle, JaNae Holloway, Jennifer L. Brown, Redonna Chandler, Laura C. Fanucchi, Daniel J. Feaster, Patricia R. Freeman, Timothy Hunt, Michelle R. Lofwall, Hannah K. Knudsen, Edward V. Nunes, Emmanuel Oga, Douglas R. Oyler, Jeffrey H.
description: AimWe evaluated whether community‐level naloxone distribution, medication for opioid use disorder treatment and retention and incident high‐risk opioid prescribing rates were associated with opioid overdose death rates.DesignObservational cohort conducted using 2019 to 2023 community‐level data as an exploratory analysis of the HEALing (Helping to End Addiction Long‐term®) Communities Study (HCS).

title: Transcripts enriched in codons that trigger P‐site tRNA‐mediated mRNA decay possess stable mRNA
creator: Rodolfo Lopes Carneiro, Fernando Lucas Palhano
description: Synonymous codon usage significantly influences mRNA stability in yeast by guiding mRNA decay during translation. The CCR4‐NOT complex is central to this process, interacting with ribosomes when the A and E sites are unoccupied, a state that arises when a nonoptimal codon with low tRNA availability is at the A site.

title: From medicine to fields: what the 2026 nobel prize means for agricultural biotechnology
creator: Zhan-Yan Zhang, Qing-Qing Liu, B. Marambe, Barana C. Jayawardana, Ge-Fei Hao, Wen-Chao Yang
description: nnels and optogenetics. Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel first identified channelrhodopsins in unicellular green algae and characterized them as blue-light-activated, light-gated ion channels (Nagel et al. 2002, 2003). Building on these discoveries, Karl Deisseroth successfully applied channelrhodopsins to animal neurons (Aravanis et al.

title: Redirecting a Native Ene‐Reductase Toward Desaturation With Reverse Enantioselectivity
creator: Qing‐Qing Zeng, Cristina Berga, Carla Calvó‐Tusell, Marc Garcia‐Borràs, Zhen Liu
description: Chiral enones are valuable motifs in synthetic intermediates and bioactive molecules, driving significant interest in biocatalysis. Although recent enzymatic desaturation strategies for substituted cyclohexenones provide efficient and highly enantioselective synthetic routes, none offer complementary stereoselectivity. To address this gap, we introduce a stereocomplementary biocatalytic system based on an old yellow enzyme (OYE), XenA from Pseudomonas putida.

title: Macrophage interferon regulatory factor 7 aggravates the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
creator: Xuhao Ni, Qingfa Bu, Yuan Liang, Bozhou Pan, Jian Wang, Qingxiang Xu, Lei Liu, Qi Wang
description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) represents a growing clinical burden with increasing prevalence and lacking approved pharmacological therapies. Interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7) is a central mediator of type I interferon-dependent immune responses, yet the precise mechanisms by which macrophage-expressed IRF7 shapes inflammatory and metabolic events during MASH pathogenesis remain incompletely defined.

title: Leonurine Ameliorates Doxorubicin‐Induced Cardiotoxicity via STING/NF‐κB/NLRP3 Inflammasome Signaling Pathway
creator: Wang Jun, Chen Xiaoyang, Xu Jianglin, Yang Zhi, Tao Meijiao, He Jiale, Zhao Jiangfeng, Hei Xuanding, Xu Xuegong, Wang Wei, Li Chun
description: Doxorubicin‐induced cardiomyopathy (DIC) remains a dose‐limiting clinical challenge. This study reveals that cardiac vascular endothelial cells (CVECs) act as initial sensors of doxorubicin cardiotoxicity: circulating doxorubicin activates the cGAS‑STING pathway in CVECs, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome‑mediated pyroptosis and release of pathogenic extracellular vesicles that induce mitochondrial dysfunction in neighboring cardiomyocytes, establishing a self‑perpetuating injury loop.

title: Use of the IlluminOss Photodynamic Bone Stabilisation System Following Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy for Limb‐Sparing in Six Dogs With Presumptive Appendicular Osteosarcoma
creator: Emily A Pope, Vincent A Wavreille, Janis L Lapsley, Eric M Green, William C Kisseberth, Robert Rabiner, Laura E Selmic
description: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary bone tumour in dogs, with approximately 75% of cases occurring in the appendicular skeleton. Standard‐of‐care therapy consists of limb amputation followed by carboplatin chemotherapy. A minority of dogs have limb‐sparing treatments including stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) or surgery.

title: Strategies towards designing visible and near-infrared light driven molecular motors
creator: Yuyang Tu, Wojciech Danowski, Charlotte N. Stindt, Jinyu Sheng, Ben L. Feringa
description: Light is one of the most powerful and versatile stimuli for controlling molecular motion, serving as a key driving force in the development of photoresponsive molecular systems. Among these architectures, artificial molecular motors represent a unique class of molecules capable of converting light energy into chirality-controlled unidirectional rotary motion.

title: Fathers’ perceptions of factors associated with the attainment of paternity leave: a qualitative study
creator: Naoyuki Mita, Yu Par Khin, Nobutoshi Nawa, Yui Yamaoka, Takeo Fujiwara
description: BackgroundA systematic review has reported that paternal involvement is beneficial in reducing social, behavioural and psychological problems in children. However, little research has investigated factors associated with the attainment of paternity leave.ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to explore fathers’ perceptions of the factors associated with taking paternity leave.

title: What Is a Clinically Meaningful Change in Diabetes Distress? Findings for Diabetes Care and Research From the SFDT1 Cohort
creator: Dulce Canha, Jean‐Pierre Riveline, Fatima Kazanlieva, Gloria A. Aguayo, Charline Bour, Bruno Vergès, Pierre‐Yves Benhamou, Michaël Joubert, Fawaz Alzaid, Emmanuel Cosson, Guy Fagherazzi
description: AimsDiabetes distress (DD) is common and evolves heterogeneously over time. We aimed to estimate minimal clinically important differences (MCID) for the Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) scale and its sub‐dimensions and to identify predictors of worsening over 1 year in people with type 1 diabetes (PwT1D).

title: Case report: Advanced age at transplantation and pre-emptive treatment with dupilumab in DOCK8 deficiency
creator: Sophia Trombello, Andrea Jarisch, Andre Willasch, Eva Rettinger, Julia Fekadu-Siebald, Dirk Holzinger, Roland Adelmann, Peter Bader, Shahrzad Bakhtiar
description: Dedicator of cytokinesis 8 (DOCK8) deficiency is a combined immunodeficiency (CID) due to biallelic mutations in the gene encoding DOCK8. Major clinical phenomena are recurrent severe infections of the lungs and skin, atopic eczema, and predisposition to malignancy leading to a poor prognosis. Typical findings include highly elevated IgE and eosinophilia.

title: Microplastic contamination in surface water and sediments of Lake Canaçari, Central Amazon, during the dry season
creator: Gabriel dos Anjos Guimarães, Rayane Vasconcelos da Fonseca, Beatriz Rocha de Moraes, Rômulo Augusto Ando, Isreele Jussara de Azevedo Rodrigues, Gustavo Frigi Perotti, Bruno Sampaio Sant’Anna, Gustavo Yomar Hattori
description: Contamination by microplastics is an emerging environmental problem that is widely distributed across continental aquatic environments and may cause ecological impacts. This study evaluated the occurrence, concentration, and chemical and morphological characteristics of microplastics in surface waters and sediments from Lake Canaçari, comparing two areas with different land-use patterns within a floodplain system in the Central Amazon.

title: Prisoners of the Body: The Link Between Interoception and Sleep Paralysis
creator: Giuseppe Forte, Danilo Giaccari, Francesca Favieri, Maria Casagrande
description: Sleep paralysis (SP) is a REM sleep parasomnia characterized by transient motor paralysis during sleep onset or awakening. It is a terrifying experience often accompanied by vivid hallucinations. Although it is classically linked to narcolepsy, isolated SP in healthy individuals offers a valuable model to investigate the interaction between REM sleep physiology and conscious awareness.

title: Macronutrient and micronutrient requirements in sickle cell disease across age groups: a narrative review
creator: Sarbasree Bhattacharjee, Jarina Begum, Ranjitha S Shetty, Syed Irfan Ali, Gaurav Kumar Roy
description: BackgroundSickle cell disease (SCD) is a hereditary haemoglobinopathy characterised by chronic haemolysis, inflammation, oxidative stress, and increased metabolic demands. Nutritional deficiencies worsen disease severity, growth, immunity, and quality of life, but evidence on age‑specific needs is fragmented. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on macronutrient and micronutrient requirements, deficiencies, and interventions in SCD across age groups.

title: Case Report: Severe acute pancreatitis accompanied by gastric mucosal exfoliation hemorrhage: clinical alerts and novel insights
creator: Yanquan Liu, Hehui Zhang, Minjuan Zeng, Jian Luo, Yun Lai, He Huang, Qinglin Xu, Yuan Liu
description: Acute pancreatitis (AP), a condition marked by its swift progression, substantial individual discrepancies, and profound concealment, poses a formidable challenge. Within its severe form, known as severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), the disease assumes an even more prevalent status, often entwined with dire complications such as pancreatic abscess, circulatory shock, and the direst of all, multiple organ failure.

title: Healthcare costs of childhood overweight and obesity in Chile: evidence from an analysis of linked administrative records
creator: Nieves Valdés, Alejandra Abufhele, Alberto Vega, Florencia Borrescio-Higa
description: BackgroundChildhood overweight and obesity are highly prevalent in Chile, affecting over 50% of children under the age of 12, yet evidence on the healthcare costs associated with them remains limited. In this study, we quantify the association between high body mass index (BMI)-for-age and annual health expenditures among school-aged children using linked national administrative data.

title: The CaM1‐CBP60b‐MYB77 Transcriptional Cascade Regulates K+ Homeostasis and Salt Tolerance in Barley
creator: Yunfeng Xu, Haoran Sun, Lijun Liu, Qiyu Liang, Ling Shen, Ailing Han, Liangbo Fu, Fengyue Wang, Shanggeng Xie, Jiangyan Xiong, Yishan Tu, Zhengyuan Xu, Kangfeng Cai, Lingzhen Ye, Shengguan Cai, Zhong‐Hua Chen, Dezhi Wu, Guoping Zhang, Qiufang Shen
description: Soil salinity is a major abiotic stress that threatens global crop productivity. Calcium (Ca2+) is a pivotal second messenger in plant stress signalling, but how Ca2+ sensors such as calmodulin (CaM) transcriptionally control ion homeostasis and salt tolerance remains largely understood in crops.

title: mHealth for chronic disease management: effects on adherence in Ghanaian patients with diabetes and hypertension
creator: Pearl Aovare, Felix P Chilunga, Amos Laar, Nicolas Moens, Eric P Moll van Charante, Charles Agyemang
description: BackgroundMedication non-adherence remains a major barrier to effective chronic disease management, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. In Ghana, limited access to continuous care and patient engagement tools contributes to poor adherence among individuals living with type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Mobile health interventions, including smartphone applications, may offer scalable solutions to support long-term medication use and self-management.

title: Exploratory study to examine the neuroendocrinological changes in typically developing adults during a music-related participatory practice using computer software
creator: Yosuke Sugiyama, Sanae Tanaka, Aiko Komagome, Teruko Yuhi, Kazumi Furuhara, Haruhiro Higashida, Takahiro Tsuji, Mitsuru Kikuchi, Chiharu Tsuji
description: There has been a growing recognition of the benefits of participating in art practices for promoting well-being and social connection. Despite this, only a limited number of studies have assessed the neuroendocrinological changes that might contribute to these benefits. In this exploratory study, we focused on a creative activity related to music composition using digital tools.

title: Acute liver injury is triggered by dysbiosis and microbial translocation involving gut–liver axis
creator: Urmi Halder, Hamida Hamida, Khadija Kakar, Xiaoming Yang, Yin Zhong, Mitzi Nagarkatti, Prakash Nagarkatti
description: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition that can progress to chronic liver failure, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma, yet therapeutic options remain limited. Here, we investigated how hepatotoxin-induced gut–liver dysbiosis drives hepatic inflammation through microbial crosstalk. Using three murine ALI models, we assessed liver injury, intestinal barrier integrity, microbial composition along the gut–liver axis, and immune activation.

title: KASL clinical practice guidelines for management of chronic hepatitis B
creator: Won-Mook Choi, Ji Won Han, Tae Hyung Kim, Miyoung Choi, Moon Haeng Hur, Hyo Young Lee, Han Ah Lee, Byeong Geun Song, Heechul Nam, Jeong-Ju Yoo, Chang Hun Lee, Gi-Ae Kim, Hye Won Lee, Gwang Hyeon Choi, Young Eun Chon, Yun Bin Lee, Dong Hyun Sinn, Bo Hyun Kim, In Hee Kim, on behalf of the Korean Assoc
description: s B virus (HBV) in Korea has decreased to less than 3% since 2018 due to the results of national immunization and perinatal infection prevention projects, yet it shows a prevalence of 3–4% in the 40–60s age group, with a total of about 1.2 million infected individuals.

title: Alcohol use is common in older patients with fall-related fractures: a secondary analysis from a prospective cohort study using PEth as an objective assessment of consumption
creator: Cecilia ROGMARK, Linnea MALMGREN, Anna HOLMGREN, Åsa MAGNUSSON, Helmi-Sisko PYRHÖNEN
description: Background and purposeAlcohol increases the risk of falls and complications, but data on alcohol intake among trauma patients is unreliable. Excessive alcohol use can contribute to excess frailty and confusion in frail individuals and increase fall risk in otherwise robust older people. Phosphatidylethanol (PEth) is a biomarker accumulating through repeated alcohol intake, i.e., suitable for screening long-term consumption.

title: Downregulation of Trpv4 and Klf2 in brain microvessels is associated with the progression of neurovascular dysfunction and cognitive impairment in a model of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
creator: Sara MP Lambrichts, Laura van der Taelen, Irene Pastor, Peter Leenders, Nicole Bitsch, Daria Majcher, Denise Hermes, Steven J Simmonds, Marcel van Herwijnen, Rick Kamps, Ellen Weltjens, Phyllis JJ Jessen, Hellen P Steinbusch, Floor Arentz, Maximilian Wiesmann, Amanda J Kiliaan, Florian Caiment, Mart
description: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) shares major risk factors with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), including obesity, diabetes and hypertension. Yet VCI research often relies on single-stimulus models, whereas patients experience combined risk factors. We therefore assessed cerebrovascular and cognitive phenotypes in an HFpEF model and investigated underlying mechanisms.

title: Direct antiglobulin test for the prediction of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia needing an intervention: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis
creator: Vijay Kumar Krishnegowda, Viraraghavan Vadakkencherry Ramaswamy, Thangaraj Abiramalatha, Tapas Bandyopadhyay, Abdul Kareem Pullattayil S, Prakash Kannan Loganathan
description: ImportanceThe direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is commonly used as a screening test for predicting significant neonatal hyperbilirubinemia requiring intervention. However, evidence for this approach is limited.ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic utility of DAT in predicting the need for phototherapy and double volume exchange transfusion (DVET) in neonates with ABO and Rhesus (Rh) incompatibility conditions.

title: Exploring the role of alpha-tocopherol in pain and inflammation: interplay with TRPV1, PKA, and PKC pathways
creator: Sahar Jaffal, Sawsan Oran
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAlpha-tocopherol (vitamin E) is a fat-soluble antioxidant with neuroprotective properties. There is a gap in research regarding the anti-nociceptive and anti-inflammatory effects of alpha-tocopherol in different tests of nociception as well as its signaling pathways.

title: Time-aligned segmental strain as a diagnostic marker for obstructive coronary artery disease in patients with chronic chest pain
creator: Assami Rösner, Hatice Akay Caglayan, Mehran Jazbani, Semra Øztemel Sari, Pablo Marti Castellote, Didrik Kjønås, Sandro Queirós
description: BackgroundMyocardial strain curves provide valuable insights into coronary artery disease (CAD) beyond conventional peak strain measurements. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic utility of time-aligned segmental strain and strain rate (S/SR) curves to identify obstructive CAD in consecutive chest pain patients.MethodsA total of 510 chest-pain patients referred to coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were included.

title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection
creator: Mahdi Zirakchian Zadeh, Medhat M Osman
description: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach.

title: Interpreting corneal changes after PRK: Integrating biomechanics with tomographic remodeling
creator: Murat Kaşıkcı, Göksu Alaçamlı, Konuralp Yakar
description: Photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) alters corneal biomechanical and tomographic measurements, but postoperative change, an abnormal index classification, and progressive ectasia are distinct. Saif et al. reported biomechanical changes at 6 months; a separate Pentacam cohort showed tomographic changes at 1 month. Clinically and topographically normal eyes assessed approximately 25 years after PRK also had frequent abnormal classifications.

title: Segmental strain in chronic ischemic cardiomyopathy: clarifying the role of multiple-comparison adjustment and the clinical interpretation of limits of agreement
creator: Maajid Mohi Ud Din Malik, Rajesh Prasad Jayaswal
description: Khidr and colleagues recently reported an intermodality comparison of left ventricular longitudinal strain by feature-tracking cardiac magnetic resonance (FT-CMR) and 2D speckle-tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) in 55 stable patients with chronic ischemic heart disease and reduced ejection fraction. Their analysis showed a strong global longitudinal strain (GLS) correlation (r = 0.793, P < 0.

title: BMP9 induces postnatal zonal stratification of immature articular cartilage through reconfiguration of the existing collagen framework
creator: Miles Anderson-Watters, Ilyas M. Khan
description: Articular cartilage lines bones in synovial joints, and its main structural element, collagen, has an arcade-like arrangement formed from an initially random network in a process called postnatal maturation. This reshaping of the extracellular matrix is similar across all species and is critical for the lifelong strength and durability of cartilage.

title: Accuracy of transfer learning in predicting peri-implantitis onset from intraoral radiograph: A multi-center longitudinal retrospective study
creator: Muhammad H. A. Saleh, Luigi Nibali, Abdusalam E. Alrmali, Vito Carlo Alberto Caponio, Pasquale Santamaria, Francesco Fanelli, Khrystyna Zhurakivska, Hom-Lay Wang, Giuseppe Troiano
description: BackgroundThe growing application of artificial intelligence in dentistry has opened new opportunities for predicting peri-implantitis (PI) using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Transfer learning, where knowledge from a model pre-trained on a large dataset is adapted to a new, domain-specific task, may enhance performance, particularly when medical datasets are limited.

title: Efficacy and safety of ifupinostat in relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a multicenter, single-arm phase 2 study
creator: Yuankai Shi, Peng Liu, Yufu Li, Wenyu Li, Hui Zhou, Yu Yang, Jie Jin, Yuhuan Gao, Weijie Xu, Meifang Zheng, Haiyan Yang, Hongwei Xue, Zhigang Peng, Ou Bai, Fei Li, Fangfang Lv, Liling Zhang, Ning Huang, Yi Luo, Chunhong Hu, Yajing Xu, Huilai Zhang, Xiuhua Sun, Xin Li, Kaiyang Ding, Linjuan Zeng, Hai
description: Ifupinostat (BEBT-908) is a novel dual-targeted inhibitor of histone deacetylase (HDACs) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα). We evaluated the efficacy and safety of ifupinostat monotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) after at least 2 prior lines of systemic therapy. Eligible participants received intravenous ifupinostat at 22.

title: Morphological and functional characterization of respiratory muscles in male runners across different race distances: an ultrasound and physiological assessment
creator: María García-Arrabé, Rebeca Del Prado-Álvarez, Fabien Guérineau, Lucas Le Roux, Marta de la Plaza, Patricia Rico-Mena, Ángel González de la Flor
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRunning performance depends not only on aerobic capacity but also on the functional integration of the respiratory system and core musculature. However, morphological and functional adaptations of the diaphragm and abdominal muscles across different running disciplines remain insufficiently characterized.

title: Association of Prophylactic Abdominal Drain Placement With Short‐Term Postoperative Outcomes After Hepatectomy: A Nationwide Inpatient Database Study in Japan
creator: Keita Kouzu, Shotaro Aso, Yuki Hirano, Hiroki Matsui, Kensuke Yoshimura, Hiroki Kitagawa, Toru Kato, Naoki Yamane, Osahiko Hagiwara, Norikatsu Miyoshi, Satoru Matsuda, Hiroshi Maruyama, Keita Morikane, Junichi Sasaki, Hideo Yasunaga, Yuko Kitagawa, Manabu Watanabe, Hironori Tsujimoto
description: AimAlthough randomized trials have discouraged routine prophylactic abdominal drainage after uncomplicated hepatectomy, these drains are still widely used in clinical practice. This study evaluated the association between prophylactic abdominal drain placement and short‐term outcomes after hepatic resection using a nationwide inpatient database.MethodsWe identified patients who underwent initial hepatic resection for liver tumors from the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database.

title: Association between the atherogenic index of plasma trajectory and risk of cardiovascular diseases among hypertensive patients: a prospective cohort study
creator: Weiqiang Wu, Peng Fu, Zefeng Cai, Yuxian Wang, Kuangyi Wu, Hong Zheng, Guanlin Chen, Zekai Chen, Yulong Lan, Yanjuan Chen, Shouling Wu, Youren Chen
description: BackgroundCardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of global mortality, with hypertension and dyslipidemia synergistically exacerbating the atherogenic risk. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), calculated as log (triglycerides/HDL-C), reflects lipid-driven atherosclerosis; however, evidence of long-term AIP trajectory patterns and their cardiovascular implications in hypertensive populations remains scarce.MethodsThis longitudinal study included 20,013 hypertensive participants (mean age: 56.8 ± 11.

title: Flavonoids and anthocyanins in seagrasses: implications for climate change adaptation and resilience
creator: Jana Botes, Xiao Ma, Jiyang Chang, Yves Van de Peer, Dave Kenneth Berger
description: Seagrasses are a paraphyletic group of marine angiosperms and retain certain adaptations from the ancestors of all embryophytes in the transition to terrestrial environments. Among these adaptations is the production of flavonoids, versatile phenylpropanoid secondary metabolites that participate in a variety of stress responses.

title: Uncovering how selected potent bacteriocins reshape the broiler chicken gut microbiome in a PolyFermS continuous in vitro model
creator: Amal Mamjoud, Séverine Zirah, Sylvie Rebuffat, Éric Biron, Ismail Fliss
description: BackgroundBacteriocins are promising alternatives to antibiotics in poultry production, offering pathogen control with minimal disruption to gut microbiota and reduced risk of resistance dissemination. This study compared the impact of three bacteriocins—microcin J25, nisin Z, and pediocin PA-1—against bacitracin as a positive control, specifically evaluating their effects on gut microbiota composition and metabolic activity.

title: Psychosocial Correlates of Prenatal Depression and Anxiety Among Fathers from Tribal Communities in India: A Cross-sectional Study
creator: Manu Krishnan, Kimneihat Vaiphei, Pracheth Raghuveer, Prabha S Chandra
description: Background:Expectant fathers may experience psychological distress during pregnancy, yet evidence on paternal mental health among tribal populations in India remains scarce. This study assessed depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, psychological well-being, perceived social support, and their psychosocial correlates among tribal expectant fathers.Methods:A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 80 tribal expectant fathers in Attappady, India.

title: The impact of cultural origin on the psychiatric expertise in Switzerland: a focus on sexual violence illustrated by two criminal cases
creator: Marco De Pieri, Neva Suardi
description: Cultural biases and integration in novel socio-geographic contexts are relevant factors for the understanding of dynamics beneath sexual violence, and possibly play a role in modifying responsibility and perpetrators treatment. Here we offer a conceptual analysis of the relevant literature and two case study.

title: Predicting Major Amputation Rates in Diabetic Hindfoot Ulcers With Critical Infection and Ischemia: A Risk-Factor-Based Model
creator: Kyu-Il Lee, Woo-Sung Kim, Seung-Kyu Han, Kyung-Chul Moon, Sik Namgoong, Seong-Ho Jeong, Eun-Sang Dhong
description: BackgroundDiabetic hindfoot ulcers pose a substantially greater risk of progressing to major amputation than forefoot or midfoot ulcers. Patients with these ulcers often experience severe psychological distress at the prospect of major limb loss. Consequently, patients, their families, and healthcare professionals prioritize understanding the actual risk of major amputation based on the patient’s current clinical status.

title: Qualitative study identifying leadership challenges encountered in real-world scholarly projects within a faculty development program
creator: Judy Tung, Amna Aslam, Carol A. Mancuso
description: BackgroundFaculty development programs often incorporate structured pieces of academic work, i.e. action learning projects, to provide participants with experiential learning while also addressing real world problems. The Leadership in Academic Medicine Program (LAMP), a faculty development program at Weill Cornell Medicine, contains a project expectation, i.e. a capstone, that culminates in submission of a final written abstract.

title: Distinct immune signatures define hepatitis D– versus hepatitis B–associated hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Simon Glimmann, Katja Deterding, Kilian Bock, Birgit Bremer, Anke R.M. Kraft, Markus Cornberg, Heiner Wedemeyer, Bernd Heinrich, Anika Wranke
description: Background:Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Hepatitis D is the most severe form of viral hepatitis. However, the clinical, virological, and systemic inflammatory characteristics of HDV-associated HCC remain insufficiently characterized.Methods:In this single-center retrospective study, we identified 162 patients with HCC due to chronic hepatitis D (HDV-HCC; n=54) or chronic hepatitis B (HBV-HCC; n=108).

title: Enhanced liver fibrosis score is associated with cognitive performance during an 11-year follow-up period
creator: Emilia Vataja, Katri Sääksjärvi, Jenni Lehtisalo, Iris Erlund, Terhi Vihervaara, Tiia Ngandu, Seppo Koskinen, Fredrik Åberg, Antti Jula, Juha Rinne, Miikka-Juhani Honka, Laura Ekblad
description: Introduction:Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with poorer cognitive performance and greater cognitive decline. However, the liver–brain axis and the role of liver health in cognitive decline are still poorly understood. Thus, using both cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, we aimed to study how liver fibrosis score (ELF), an indicator of liver fibrosis, is associated with cognitive performance.

title: Advanced sleep disorder detection using multi-layered ensemble learning and advanced data balancing techniques
creator: Muhammad Mostafa Monowar, S. M. Nuruzzaman Nobel, Maharin Afroj, Md Abdul Hamid, Md Zia Uddin, Md Mohsin Kabir, M. F. Mridha
description: Sleep disorder detection has greatly improved with the integration of machine learning, offering enhanced accuracy and effectiveness. However, the labor-intensive nature of diagnosis still presents challenges. To address these, we propose a novel coordination model aimed at improving detection accuracy and reliability through a multi-model ensemble approach.

title: Expert Consensus on the Standardized Diagnosis, Treatment, and Management of Cancer in High‐Altitude Regions of China
creator: Yiqun Li, Feng Li, Xiaorong Bai, Yan Li, Chengyun Bai, Qiaomei Chang, Cuiping Guo, Ji Di, Qiuxia Dong, Mengting Da, Zhongcheng Li, Zhen Liu, Hongxia Liang, Yushuang Luo, Dengfeng Ren, Pengjie Yu, Rui Ma, Miaozhou Wang, Xueshan Zhao, Fuxing Zhao, Guoshuang Shen, Zhiping Feng, Hao Wang, Shengtao Zhou,
description: Cancer has become one of the major diseases threatening the health of the Chinese population. The incidence of cancer in high‐altitude regions of China is equally concerning. However, due to the unique geographical environment, population, and economic factors in high‐altitude regions, there is an urgent need for a consensus on cancer prevention and management tailored to real‐world clinical practice.

title: Effect of different long-acting reversible contraceptive methods on female sexual function: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Sha Ye, Lin Ma, Yepei Huang, Bisha Su, Yining Cao, Jian Huang, Jun Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe impact of long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) on female sexual function remains a controversial and often overlooked issue. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of three common LARC methods on female sexual function.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 90 women, divided into three groups based on their chosen contraceptive: copper-containing intrauterine device (Cu-IUD, n = 30), levonorgestrel intrauterine system (LNG-IUS, n = 30), and the etonogestrel subcutaneous implant (Implanon, n = 30). Changes in sexual frequency and partner sexual satisfaction were recorded.

title: NRS-2002–defined nutritional risk and associated factors in intensive care unit patients: a cross-sectional study
creator: Derya Bıçak Ayık, Derya Akça Doğan
description: BackgroundMalnutrition is common in intensive care units (ICUs) and is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate NRS-2002-defined nutritional risk in adult ICU patients and to examine factors associated with high nutritional risk.MethodsThis cross-sectional study was conducted in a tertiary-level ICU of a training and research hospital in Türkiye between April 2024 and May 2025.

title: TWGFD: an integrative platform for tetraploid wheat gene family analysis
creator: Qinglin Ke, Tingting Li, Yiting Su, Han Lin, You Xu, Mengxing Wang, Yihan Li, Xiaojun Nie, Licao Cui
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gene families, primarily are composed of transcription factors, comprise evolutionarily conserved orthologs derived from common ancestors, characterized by shared sequence homology, structural domains, and fundamental roles in biological processes including development, growth, and environmental adaptation. As the immediate progenitor of hexaploid bread wheat (Triticum aestivum), tetraploid wheat constitutes both a vital industrial crop and a critical genetic reservoir, harboring numerous agronomically important stress-resistance traits.

title: Association Between Preoperative Steroid Use and Short‐Term Outcomes Following Pancreaticoduodenectomy: A Nationwide Analysis Using the National Clinical Database
creator: Yoshito Tomimaru, Hideki Endo, Hiroyuki Yamamoto, Teruhide Ishigame, Hideki Ueno, Ken Shirabe, Hidetoshi Eguchi
description: BackgroundPancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) carries a high risk of postoperative complications. Although steroids are widely prescribed for various chronic diseases, the specific impact after PD remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between preoperative chronic steroid use and short‐term outcomes following PD.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used Japanese National Clinical Database data from 2019 to 2022.

title: MEL-IA: An Interoperable AI System for Multimodal Skin Lesion Classification in Hospital Settings
creator: Pablo Candela Córcoles, Alberto De Ramón Fernández, Marcelo Saval Calvo, Jose María Salinas Serrano, Diego Guijarro Peral, Daniel Ruiz Fernández
description: Skin cancer represents a growing healthcare challenge, motivating the development of AI sytems that can support lesion assessment while integrating efficiently into clinical workflows. This study presents MEL-IA (MobilE skin Lesion dIAgnosis), an interoperable AI system designed for automated skin lesion classification and full integration with hospital information systems.

title: Long-term outcomes of adjuvant proton radiotherapy (PRT) for residual pituitary adenoma (PA) in adults – a retrospective, single institute experience
creator: Fabian J. K. Allmendinger, Maximilian Deng, Sebastian Regnery, Lars Wessel, Katharina Kozyra, Felix Englert, Ricarda Wickert, Jannik Walter, Lucas Mose, Thomas Tessonnier, Sandro M. Krieg, Jürgen Debus, Laila König, Tanja Adena-Eichkorn
description: PurposePituitary adenomas (PA) are benign neoplasms treated by resection. Gross total resection is limited by extrasellar expansion in proximity to critical neurovascular structures. Residual tumor remains at risk of progression, with serious consequences such as optic compression or hormone hypersecretion. Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) offers a rescue modality for both, impeding regrowth and hormonal relapse.

title: A new putative carlavirus identified by metagenomic analysis in a wild weed in Angola
creator: Serafina Serena AMOIA, Annalisa Giampetruzzi, Luisa Flora Antònio, Aderito Tomàs Pais da Cunha, Angelantonio Minafra
description: A metagenomic analysis was performed by high-throughput sequencing (HTS) to identify viruses infecting a wild weed collected in Seles (Angola), which exhibited clear yellowing symptoms. The analysis led to the discovery of a putatively novel carlavirus, tentatively named ‘Seles weed carlavirus’.

title: Whole‐Genome Sequencing Unravels Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance Landscapes of Major Bovine Respiratory Disease Pathogens
creator: Kaiwen Yin, Shuying Liu, Yue Sun, Haiyan Dong, Kaifan Han, Wei Mao, Weiguang Zhou, Hongxia Zhao, Lipi Buch
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bovine respiratory diseases are a seasonally highly prevalent infectious condition and cause great economic losses to the farming industry. In order to expand the genomic database information of bovine respiratory disease pathogens, the raw data were assembled and genome annotated using relevant bioinformatics analysis software to clarify the strain virulence, resistance gene carriage, and evolution of bovine‐origin Pasteurella multocida, Mannheimia haemolytica, and Mycoplasma bovis.

title: Development and characterization of ivermectin nanoformulations for topical acaricidal activity against Rhipicephalus sanguineus ticks
creator: Hoda S. M. Abdel-Ghany, Sobhy Abdel-Shafy, Amany M. Mohamed, Abeer S. Hassan
description: Ticks are among the most significant ectoparasites of livestock and humans, posing serious health and economic risks. The growing resistance to conventional acaricides highlights the need for safer and more effective alternatives. This study aimed to evaluate the acaricidal efficacy of different ivermectin (IVM) nanoformulations against different developmental stages of Rhipicephalus sanguineus tick.

title: Clinically suspected central nervous system Richter transformation presenting with progressive psychiatric symptoms: A case report
creator: Tetsuro Ishida, Yusuke Sugama
description: BackgroundCentral nervous system (CNS) involvement associated with Richter transformation (RT) is a rare complication of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). Neurological manifestations are heterogeneous. To our knowledge, no previous reports have described CNS RT presenting predominantly with psychiatric and behavioral symptoms.

title: Wave energy converters as offshore wind farm guardians: a pathway to resilient ocean systems
creator: Olivia Vitale, Maha N. Haji
description: Maximizing the durability and reliability of offshore wind farms is essential for the clean energy transition. In this work, we demonstrate how wave energy converter (WEC) farms can shelter offshore wind farms from cyclic wave loading, resulting in significant reductions in wave-induced turbine fatigue damage.

title: Defining the value of circularity in beef cattle production systems
creator: Samantha J Werth, Ellen Lai, Sarah C Klopatek
description: lity forage on marginal lands while supporting carbon storage, nutrient cycling, biodiversity, and other ecosystem services often overlooked in environmental assessments. Intensive cattle feeding systems enhance circularity by upcycling substantial quantities of human‑inedible byproducts and transforming concentrated manure streams into nutrient-rich fertilizers.

title: Transformer-based coreference resolution modeling for Amharic text
creator: Lingerew Bantie Asmare
description: Coreference resolution is the task of identifying all textual expressions that refer to the same real-world entity within a document. Coreference resolution is essential for several NLP applications, including machine translation, question answering, information extraction, summarization, and dialogue systems. While substantial progress has been made in high-resource languages such as English and Arabic.

title: Applying landscape and jurisdictional approaches for nature positive outcomes in beef-producing landscapes
creator: Brodie Crouch, Hillary Fenrich, Oscar Blumetto, Sara Valencia, Josefina Eisele, Martine Maron
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstract Graphical AbstractA flow chart showing links between nature positive farmscale actions, landscape and jurisdictional approaches and nature positive outcomes. Refer to textual abstract for further detail. Landscape and jurisdictional approaches (LJAs) that bring together stakeholders within a defined geographical area offer the scale needed to address landscape-level processes affecting biodiversity and ecosystem function conservation and restoration in beef-producing regions.

title: Pulmonary dermoid cyst mimicking hydatid cyst: a case report with literature review
creator: Fahmi H Kakamad, Harem K Ahmed, Amanj K Hamad, Ari M Abdullah, Ahmed H Ahmed, Rebaz M Ali, Harun Amanj Ahmed, Mohammed Namiq Amin, Mohammed Abdullah Othman
description: Intrapulmonary dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma) is rare and may mimic common cystic lung diseases, particularly pulmonary hydatid disease. A 26-year-old woman presented with dyspnea and left-sided chest, shoulder, and neck pain. Computed tomography demonstrated a large complex cystic lesion in the left upper lobe with gas locules and associated pleural and pericardial effusions, initially suggesting a hydatid cyst.

title: Gaze dynamics of cued speech perception
creator: Annahita Sarré, Laurent Cohen
description: For many deaf people, lip-reading plays a major role in verbal communication. However, lip reading is inherently ambiguous and does not allow for a complete understanding of speech. The consequences of these limitations are significant, potentially impeding language, cognitive, and social development.

title: A novel pattern of complex bile duct injury characterized by distal ligation and proximal perforation: temporary T-tube drainage as a bridge to definitive reconstruction—a case report and literature review
creator: Mirwais Safi, Muhibullah Saifi, Nasrullah Shefayee, Hamidullah Hamid, Ehsanullah Safi, Nasratullah Nasrat, Maihan Abdullah
description: Bile duct injury (BDI) is a serious complication of cholecystectomy. We report a previously unrecognized pattern of complex BDI in a 30-year-old man who presented one week after open cholecystectomy with biliary peritonitis. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography demonstrated an abrupt common bile duct (CBD) cutoff, while magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography revealed a biloma with features suggestive of biliary peritonitis.

title: A screening pipeline to characterize stress-induced enzymes uncovers a cellular function for the poorly characterized alcohol dehydrogenase Bdh2
creator: Dunya Edilbi, Rosario Valenti, Benjamin Dubreuil, Yeynit Asraf, Yoav Peleg, Shira Albeck, Sergey Malitsky, Maxim Itkin, Maya Schuldiner
description: Cells possess intricate metabolic networks comprising hundreds of enzymes. Despite extensive research, many of these enzymes remain uncharacterized. Identifying the function of these enzymes is crucial for advancing our understanding of cellular metabolism. However, multiple enzymes are not active in standard conditions, making them challenging to study.

title: Design, synthesis, and anticancer evaluation of Biginelli-derived DHPM–amide hybrids bearing clinically inspired kinase-directed pharmacophores: EGFR docking and DFT studies
creator: Sagar P. Kothadiya, Jay B. Maheta, Darshna K. Lakhnotra, Yogesh O. Bhola, Sureshkumar B. Koradiya
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A series of twelve novel dihydropyrimidine (DHPM)–amide hybrid conjugates (6a–c, 8a–c, 10a–c, and 12a–c) were rationally designed, synthesized, and biologically evaluated as potential EGFR-targeted anticancer agents against A549 non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) cells.

title: Tysabri Observational Program (TOP): long-term safety and effectiveness of natalizumab treatment in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis over 15 years
creator: Helmut Butzkueven, Ludwig Kappos, Heinz Wiendl, Maria Trojano, Tim Spelman, Andres Greco, Zhaonan Sun, Tyler Lasky, On behalf of the TOP Investigators
description: ObjectiveThis Tysabri Observational Program (TOP) final analysis evaluated the 15-year safety and effectiveness of natalizumab treatment in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS).MethodsThis multinational, real-world observational study assessed natalizumab-associated serious adverse events, annualised relapse rates (ARRs) and disability progression/improvement in patients with RRMS.

title: Defining Alzheimer’s disease: stipulations and the ethics of diagnostic change
creator: Robin Michalon, Vincent Planche, Maël Lemoine, Lara Keuck, Nicolas Villain
description: this emerging controversy is not merely semantic, but scientifically, clinically, and politically significant. Drawing on philosophical tools and situating the current debate within a broader historical context from the reconceptualization of AD in the 1970s onwards, we explore how definitions can serve as transformative instruments, acting as strategic bets that reshape scientific fields and clinical practices.

title: Multi-omics Profiling Reveals the Effects of Xihuangcao on Hepatic Fibrosis Attenuation through Gut Microbiota and Metabolic Reprogramming
creator: Weiguo Zhao, Xueling Zhang, Lifan Xu, Mianfeng Zheng, Zhuoya Li, Yuexuan Wang, Xinxiang He, Min Hong, Huiye Zhang, Junwei Li, Lei Shi, Ying Du, Haitao Yuan, Wei Zhang, Ali Chen
description: In various chronic liver diseases, hepatic fibrosis represents a frequent pathological event. This process involves the activation of hepatic stellate cells, along with the consequent excessive deposition of extracellular matrix. Emerging evidence highlights the contribution of gut microbiota dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction to its progression, underscoring the potential of targeting the liver–gut axis.

title: Matched and Measured: An In-depth Look at the Interventional Cardiology Fellowship Match—Fellows’ Perspective
creator: Naseer A Khan, Najam U Saqib, Eva Meunier, Dean J Kereiakes, Luay Alalawi, Said Hajouli, Muhammad Saleem, Abubakar Nazir
description: BackgroundIn July 2024, the interventional cardiology (IC) fellowship match transitioned to the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) to streamline recruitment and ensure transparency. Our prior analysis explored the program directors’ (PDs) experiences, revealing positive perceptions despite initial concerns. This current study addresses a critical limitation of the previous work by incorporating the applicants’ perspective.

title: A comparative analysis of autograft choices of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction and their effects on muscle strength and joint biomechanics
creator: Wiem Issaoui, Ismail Dergaa, Hatem Ghouili, Abdelfatteh El Omri, Noomen Guelmami, Philippe Chomier, Mourad Ghrairi, Helmi Ben Saad, Wassim Moalla
description: IntroductionAnterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is crucial to restore knee stability and function after ACL injuries, especially in physically active individuals. Despite advances in surgical techniques and rehabilitation protocols, the choice of autograft has a significant impact on postoperative recovery, particularly on muscle strength and joint biomechanics.

title: Progressive Hippocampal Volume Reduction Beyond Normal Aging in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: A Longitudinal MRI Study
creator: Daichi Sone, Yoko Shigemoto, Risa Kagaya, Yukio Kimura, Hiroshi Matsuda, Noriko Sato
description: Recent neuroimaging studies have suggested that epilepsy may show progressive brain structural changes over time. However, longitudinal hippocampal volume changes in temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) have not been adequately compared with those observed in normal aging. In this study, we enrolled 46 patients with unilateral TLE and 25 healthy controls with longitudinal structural MRI scans using the same scanner.

title: Sustainable high-energy-density Li–Mn–O layered cathode via metastable synthetic kinetics
creator: Yuansheng Shi, Fushan Geng, Dilxat Muhtar, Pengfeng Jiang, Jiaqi Cao, Weixin Chen, Chunzhen Yang, Jun Qi, Wei Tong, Xueyi Lu, Bingwen Hu, Yang Sun, Xia Lu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The electrochemical stability of metastable lithium-rich layered cathodes is intrinsically governed by their synthetic history, yet the correlation between ion-exchange thermodynamics and structural evolution remains elusive. Here, using layered P3-Na0.6[Li0.2Mn0.8]O2 as a precursor, the spontaneous ion-exchange synthesis of O3-Li0.6[Li0.2Mn0.8]O2 (O3-LLM RT) at room temperature yields one of the most promising layered Li–Mn–O cathodes reported to date in LiPF6-based carbonate electrolyte at room temperature.

title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation
creator: Emily Cockle, Charles B. Malpas, Honor Coleman, Alissandra McIlroy, Joshua Laing, Martin Hunn, Matthew Gutman, Stacey Logan, Georgia‐Rose Robinson, Cecilia Harb, Catherine Meade, Wendyl D'Souza, Amy Halliday, Kristian Bulluss, Simon Vogrin, Rubina Alpitsis, Terence J. O'Brien, Genevieve Rayner, Andr
description: ObjectiveCharacterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG.MethodsConsecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia.

title: ClinAgent: AI-assisted methodology for clinical trial data processing and statistical programming
creator: Jaime Yan
description: Clinical trial statistical programming requires 12–24 full-time-equivalent months per Phase 3 study and remains a bottleneck in pharmaceutical research. Modern artificial intelligence coding agents reason capably but lack domain-specific tools: they cannot read proprietary statistical software datasets, parse analysis specifications, or generate standards-compliant code without extensive guidance.

title: Incidence and aetiology of diarrhoeal disease among children under five years in the post-rotavirus vaccine introduction era in Manhiça District, Mozambique
creator: Percina Chirinda, Llorenç Quintó, Corssino Tchavana, Augusto Messa, Arsénio Nhacolo, Sozinho Acacio, Tacilta Nhampossa, Quique Bassat, Goitom G Weldegebriel, Jacqueline E Tate, Umesh Parashar, Jason M Mwenda, Filomena Manjate, Inacio Mandomando
description: BackgroundDiarrhoea remains a major cause of death in children under five, despite the global decline in hospitalisations following the widespread introduction of rotavirus vaccines . As rotavirus-associated disease declines, it is important to identify other diarrhoea associated pathogens, although post-vaccine data remain limited in Mozambique.

title: Meeting clinicians where they are through signal-guided AI innovation
creator: Benjamin Rader, Ryan D Nagy, Heather L Nelson, Peter C Laussen, John S Brownstein
description: stitutional channels.1 2 This is not a governance issue alone; the tools clinicians independently adopt can reveal where existing systems are failing to deliver adequate clinical workflow support. We argue for signal-guided innovation: treating organic clinician behaviour as a leading indicator of where artificial intelligence (AI) can have impact.

title: When pupillometry indices disagree: does QPi add prognostic information beyond NPi?
creator: Li-Xia Xu
description: exposure. These findings support the authors’ conclusion that the two indices should not be considered interchangeable. However, an important clinical question remains: when NPi and QPi disagree, does QPi provide additional prognostic information, or does the disagreement primarily reflect differences in measurement susceptibility? The distinction matters because association with outcome and incremental clinical information are not equivalent.

title: Circannual pattern of milk crude protein and urea nitrogen and their relationship in Holstein cows in Swiss grassland-based dairy systems over a 30-year period
creator: Jedidiah Yi Lin Ong, Usman Arshad, Mutian Niu
description: Graphical AbstractSummary: The objectives of this study were to characterize circannual variations in milk crude protein (CP) and milk urea nitrogen (MUN) and to evaluate their relationship in Holstein cows managed under grassland-based dairy systems using a large national dataset. Historical milk recording data of 2.

title: Outdoor cycling competence and balance control in older adults – cross-sectional analysis of the BiPerAge trial
creator: Jana Rogler, Sebastian Krumpoch, Ellen Freiberger, Noam Margalit, Roee Zehavi, Itshak Melzer, Sharon Barak, Amir Shapiro, Dikla Judchak Amir, Shira Levi, Omri Lubovsky, Robert Kob
description: BackgroundAlthough cycling offers numerous health benefits, age-related functional decline can increase the risk of accidents. Identifying balance components linked to outdoor cycling competence could inform targeted assessment and training. We aimed to exploratorily investigate the association between outdoor cycling competence and static, dynamic, and reactive balance control in older adults.

title: The Morphological and Mechanistic Impact of an Investment Procedure on Coronary Chronic Total Occlusions
creator: Anja Øksnes, Akiko Maehara, Britt Engan, Vibeke Juliebø, Kalaivani Mahadevan, Kais Hyasat, Damien Collison, James Spratt, Ajay J Kirtane, Milada C Hagen, Svein Rotevatn, Tone Norekvål, Øyvind Bleie, Margaret B McEntegart
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDuring chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), a modification procedure is often performed after failure. Although this has been reported to improve subsequent procedural success, the anatomical impact and mechanism of benefit have never been systematically studied. The Invest-CTO study investigated whether a strategy of a planned 2-stage CTO PCI with upfront “investment” and staged “completion” procedure could improve procedural success and safety in high-risk CTO anatomy.

title: Scaling of dimensions and concentrations of plastics in two Dutch rivers
creator: Jasmijn Polinder, Frank P. L. Collas, Félix P. Leiva, Stephanie B. Oswald, Margriet M. Schoor, Wilco C. E. P. Verberk, A. Jan Hendriks
description: Plastic pollution raised great environmental concerns due to its persistence and widespread presence. To model ecological impacts, such as ingestion by wildlife, information on the abundance and dimensions of plastic particles is fundamental. Our study examined the relationships between size dimensions (length, area, circumference) of individual particles and the length of particles, their concentration, and cumulative surface area.

title: Fat matters: paraspinal muscle quality is associated with electromyographic fatigability and endurance in lumbar spinal stenosis
creator: David Koch, Corina Nüesch, Gerold Müller, Peter Stauffert, Annegret Mündermann, Alice Caimi, Dominika Ignasiak, Stefan Schären, Stephen J Ferguson, Hans-Joachim Wilke, Cordula Netzer
description: HIGHLIGHTS•Paraspinal muscle fat fraction predicted electromyographic fatigability.•Fat fraction predicted fatigability independent of age, sex, BMI and endurance.•Greater fat fraction was associated with lower trunk extension endurance.•Quantitative imaging and bilateral EMG enabled level- and side-specific assessment.•Muscle quality mattered more than quantity for electromyographic fatigability.

title: Comparable efficacy of extraoral and intraoral photobiomodulation in preventing oral mucositis during high-dose methotrexate therapy in pediatric oncology: A single-blind randomized controlled trial
creator: Isabela de Oliveira Plugge Freitas, Isabela Schuartz, Giovanna Leal Klein Renz, Rafael Zancan Mobile, Mariana Lena Sassi França, Mara Albonei Dudeque Pianovski, Laurindo Moacir Sassi, Melissa Rodrigues de Araujo
description: PurposeThis prospective randomized controlled clinical study compared intraoral (IO) and extraoral (EO) photobiomodulation (PBM) for the prevention of chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis (OM) in pediatric oncology patients.MethodsA total of 155 patients (1–18 years), receiving high-dose methotrexate (HDMTX) for leukemia, lymphoma, or osteosarcoma, were randomized to PBM-IO (n = 73) or PBM-EO (n = 82).

title: Diagnostic and operative challenge of a giant non-pancreatic intra-abdominal pseudocyst: a rare case report
creator: Om Jhaveri, Katie Scott, Joseph Galloway
description: BackgroundLarge, non-pancreatic pseudocysts are rare pathologies that present as lesions in the intra-abdominal wall or peritoneal cavity. These cases can be diagnostically difficult, particularly in situations where fine-needle aspiration yields nonspecific cytology and imaging is also often nonspecific and nondiagnostic.

title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases
creator: Claudia Maletzki, Eva Michaelis, Sae-Yeon Won, Artem Refaelian, Thomas Freitag, Thomas M Freiman, Julia Onken, David Wasilewski, Peter Vajkoczy, Jawed Nawabi, Nico Noah Martin, Annette Zimpfer, Daniel Cantré, Florian Gessler, Daniel Dubinski
description: BackgroundPerivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear.MethodsIn this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale.

title: Comprehensive chemical and bioactive investigation of Chinese peony flower: a case of valorization of by-products as a new food ingredient from Chinese herb
creator: Meng-ling Peng, Ming-Jiong Gong, Jing Zhang, Anastassiya V. Gadetskaya, Qian-Wen Liang, Pei-Wen He, Xiao-Hui Qiu, Zhi-Hai Huang, Wen Xu
description: IntroductionIn the present study, the flower of Chinese peony (CPF), major waste by-product of Chinese Herb Radix paeoniae, was comprehensively investigated for the first time.MethodsA validated UHPLC Orbitrap Mass spectrometry combined a three-levels characterization strategy were used to analyze CPF samples from four representative cultivars. The anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities were analyzed using RAW264.

title: Molecular mechanisms of NLR proteins in inflammasome activation
creator: Yichao Liu, Kexin Ji, Liman Zhang
description: Nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs) are central mediators of inflammasome signaling, activating caspase-1 to drive pyroptotic cell death and pro-inflammatory responses. Although NLR activation is generally thought to involve conformational rearrangements that oligomerize their N- or C-terminal death domains to nucleate ASC or pro-caspase-1 oligomerization, the molecular mechanisms that enable these transitions vary substantially among family members.

title: Calculation of a conversion factor for estimating the glycolytic contribution in exercise from post-exercise blood lactate concentration
creator: David W. Hill, John Michael Mihalek
description: Purpose: Often, the glycolytic contribution in a bout of heavy or severe intensity exercise is estimated by multiplying the increase in blood lactate concentration above resting levels that is engendered by the exercise (in mM) by 3.3 (or 3) mL·kg−1 per mM.

title: Author Correction: Climate heterogeneity enhances macroclimate data-driven vegetation modeling on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
creator: Yanlong Guan, Wenqing Wu, Mengxi He, Huaikai Weng, Delong Li, Xiaoxun Huang, Deliang Chen, Shungui Zhou, Eduardo Eiji Maeda

title: RET inhibition overcomes resistance to combined CDK4/6 inhibitor and endocrine therapy in ER+ breast cancer
creator: Charlotte K. Kindt, Sidse Ehmsen, Sofie Traynor, Benedetta Policastro, Nikoline Nissen, Mie K. Jakobsen, Monique F. Hundebøl, Lene E. Johansen, Martin Bak, Elsa Arbajian, Johan Staaf, Henrik J. Ditzel, Carla L. Alves
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundCombined CDK4/6 inhibitor (CDK4/6i) and endocrine therapy significantly improve the outcome of patients with advanced estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. However, resistance to this treatment and disease progression remains a major clinical challenge.

title: The digital bioeconomy: microbiomes as a stress test for global digital sequence information governance
creator: Pierre-Mathieu Pélissier, Indré Karciauskaité, Tanja Kostic, Emmanuelle Maguin, Angela Sessitsch, Kosuke Shiraishi
description: Digital sequence information governance has entered a high-stakes implementation era. The Convention on Biological Diversity’s ‘Cali Fund’ is operationalised as the financial engine of its multilateral mechanism (MLM), with similar frameworks under negotiation across other international ocean and agricultural treaties. However, because microorganisms and their functional clusters transcend national borders, traditional bilateral mechanisms are difficult to implement.

title: Writing direction and language activation affect how Arabic-English bilingual speakers map time onto space
creator: Juana Park, Christina L. Gagné, Thomas L. Spalding
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We investigated whether writing direction and language activation influence how bilingual speakers map time onto space. More specifically, we investigated how Arabic-English bilingual speakers conceived where (e.g., on the left or on the right) different time periods (e.g., past, present, future) were located, depending on whether they were tested in Arabic (a language that is written from right to left) or in English (a language that is written from left to right).

title: Implementing a professional youth mentoring program during times of crisis: lessons from the global pandemic
creator: Koren G. Hanson, A. Karryn Satchell, Martie L. Skinner, J. Mark Eddy
description: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted traditional youth mentoring practices as social distancing limited in-person interactions. This study analyzes how Friends of the Children (FOTC), a professional mentoring program, was able to maintain engagement with mentees during the pandemic. Using a sample of 112 youth (58% Black/African American) with an average age of 12.

title: Randomized controlled trials of mind–body interventions for posttraumatic stress disorder: a systematic review
creator: Josh Kaplan, Vanessa C. Somohano, Belle Zaccari, Maya E. O’Neil
description: Mind–body interventions (MBIs) include mindfulness-based interventions (MiBIs), meditation- and mantra-based interventions (MMIs), and movement-based interventions (MoBIs). These approaches have demonstrated preliminary efficacy in improving posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms. However, previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses have noted that this area of research is limited by inadequate comparator conditions, heterogeneity of measurement, and absence of objective outcome measures.

title: Multiple eccrine hidrocystomas on the bilateral forearms
creator: Kassidy Leibowitz, Candice E. Brem, Margaret S. Lee
description: Involvement of extra-facial sites, including the chest, axilla, and neck, have been reported but remain uncommon.3 We report a case of multiple eccrine hidrocystomas presenting as dermal nodules on the bilateral volar forearms in a young patient, an unusual clinical distribution for this entity.

title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
creator: Pierre Bouchet, Sébastien Brosse, Aurèle Toussaint
description: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity.

title: Author Correction: BRAHMA represses STOP1-NRT1.1 module to control plant rhizosphere alkalization and acid stress adaptation
creator: Jia Yuan Ye, Wen Hao Tian, De Rui Zhang, Qian Yi Yu, Ji Ming Xu, Wo Na Ding, Gui Xin Li, Jing Ying Yan, Chong Wei Jin, Moussa Benhamed, Shao Jian Zheng, Zhong Jie Ding

For Figs. 4c and 4d and Supplementary Fig. 14, in several cases, average values were inadvertently duplicated and pasted into cells that should have been empty due to data exclusions.

title: Predicting trail-making test performance using 7-Tesla structural cerebral MRI
creator: Gereon J Schnellbächer, Ravichandran Rajkumar, Tanja Veselinović, Shukti Ramkiran, Jana Hagen, Maria Collee, N Jon Shah, Irene Neuner, Jürgen Dammers
description: Psychopharmaceutical therapy has seen a lack of improvement in efficacy, highlighting the need for a more individualized treatment approach that optimally leverages pharmaceutical effects. To achieve this, it is necessary to identify factors that can predict psychological attributes and treatment outcomes. We hypothesize that brain morphology may serve as a predictor of performance in psychological tests.

title: Utilizing the Nursing Professional Development Model to create and sustain nursing education aimed at improving the care of patients with Parkinson’s Disease in the hospital
creator: Mary Bobek, Pamela Pascarelli, Lisa Cocoziello, Hooman Azmi
description: The Nurse Professional Development Model (NPD) has been utilized to improve quality of care for several conditions. Patients with Parkinson’s Disease (PD) are susceptible to higher risks while in the hospital. Educational efforts for this patient population are challenged by the small, disbursed number of patients as well as increased turn-over and reliance on temporary nursing staff.

title: Engineered Muscle Tissue Analysis of Irisin Protection Against Glucocorticoid- and Cancer Cachexia-Induced Muscle Wasting and Cardiotoxicity
creator: Young Hoon Son, Christina Y Sheng, Ji-Eun Jeong, Yuri Choi, Hyocheol Jung, Jihee Won, Audrey Atinsky, Junbeom Park, Jin Chul Kim, Keel Yong Lee, Young Il Park, Sung-Jin Park
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Muscle atrophy, a condition characterized by an imbalance between protein synthesis and degradation, leads to skeletal muscle wasting, exacerbating disease progression and increasing mortality rates. Exercise has been shown to counteract muscle wasting, with myokines—exercise-induced secretome proteins, and among them, irisin is known to mediate systemic benefits such as improved metabolism, reduction of oxidative stress, and promotion of tissue repair in skeletal muscle, thereby mediating beneficial effects of exercise against atrophy.

title: Abdominal functional electrical stimulation and binder to reduce orthostatic hypotension in individuals with a subacute spinal cord injury
creator: Chiettha Prajnadewie, Lynn Blecher, Keith MD McNaughton, Claire L Boswell-Ruys, Billy L Luu, Harrison T Finn, Elizabeth A Bye, Bonsan B Lee, Jane E Butler, Anne E Palermo, Euan J McCaughey
description: Study designRepeated measures comparative study.ObjectivesCompare acute effects of 4 treatment conditions: (i) abdominal binder (Binder), (ii) abdominal functional electrical stimulation (AFES), (iii) AFES and binder (AFES-Binder), and (iv) no intervention (Control), on signs of orthostatic hypotension (OH) and blood pressure (BP) maintenance in individuals with acute and subacute spinal cord injury (SCI).SettingSpinal injury inpatient ward.

title: Reply to “Methodological Concerns in ‘Prognostic Usefulness of Clinical Complete Response after PD-1 Inhibitor-Based Combination Therapy for Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma’”
creator: Da-Long Yang, Jian-Li Huang, Hong-Gui Qin, Liang Ma, Jian-Hong Zhong, on behalf of the GUIDANCE Investigators
description: we believe will strengthen the interpretation of our findings. First, in our study, all patients with chronic hepatitis B/C infection received routine oral antiviral therapy [3, 4]. As this was a retrospective analysis, we did not adjust for antiviral therapy in the multivariable models because it was uniformly administered to all eligible patients.

title: Multiply recurrent pituitary apoplexy treated nonsurgically: illustrative case
creator: Alexander P. Landry, Maíra Cristina Velho, Luma Ghalib, Daniel M. Prevedello
description: BACKGROUNDPituitary apoplexy is rare clinical entity resulting from hemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary tumor, typically presenting with headaches, endocrinopathy, and variable neurological manifestations. Recurrent apoplexy, particularly multiply recurrent cases, is exceedingly rare and associated with clinical equipoise in many cases.

title: Treating depression in Muslim communities: Meta-analysis of three trials of culturally adapted behavioural activation for Muslims (BA-M)
creator: Ghazala Mir, Robert West, Evrim Anik, Shaista Meer, Saima Dawood, Nazish Habib, Jamal Magantor, Paulette Henry, Jamal Magantor
description: Faith-sensitive depression therapies address a core aspect of cultural values but are not specifically promoted within global mental health policy. This study evaluated a culturally adapted Behavioural Activation intervention for Muslim patients (BA-M) compared with standard treatments across diverse settings.

title: Basic Bronchoscopy Competence Achieved During a One-Day Workshop for a Multidisciplinary Critical Care Team: A simulation-based study
creator: B Jayakrishnan, Saif Musabah Al-Mubaihsi, Hasan Al-Sayegh, Ahmed Zaher Al-Abri, Issa Saif AlQarshoubi, Jehan Al-Abri, Sami M Bennji
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryObjectives:Fibreoptic bronchoscopy has become a key procedure in critical care, transitioning from pulmonologists to intensivists. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a one-day simulation-based training programme in acquiring basic bronchoscopy skills.Methods:A one-day workshop was conducted at Sultan Qaboos Comprehensive Cancer Care and Research Centre, University Medical City, Muscat, Oman, in October 2024 with didactic lectures, small group skill stations, virtual bronchoscopy simulations and hands-on training using manikins and a novel, cost-effective, 3D-printed airway model.

title: AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems in Primary Care: Systematic Review of Clinical Implementation
creator: Florian Naye, Steven Ouellet, Farzaneh Yousefi, Chloé Cachinho, Frédéric Bergeron, Onil Bhattacharyya, Vess Stamenova, Maxime Sasseville
description: BackgroundAI-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSSs) can help primary care clinicians provide higher quality care amid rising case complexity and resource constraints. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness and safety in primary care practice is lacking.ObjectiveWe synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and safety of AI-CDSSs compared with usual care or non–AI-based systems in primary care settings.

title: Physiological Responses, Exercise Intensity, and Enjoyment During Ring Fit Adventure in Adults With Chronic Diseases: Single-Arm, Pre-Post Experimental Study
creator: Muhammad Jazimin Haron, Shiek Abdullah Ismail, Gilbert Tian Seng Yeo, Ivan Steenstra
description: BackgroundPhysical inactivity and insufficient muscle-strengthening exercise remain important public health concerns among adults with chronic diseases. Active video games may offer an accessible way to support exercise participation, but many may not provide sufficient exercise intensity to produce meaningful physiological responses. Ring Fit Adventure (RFA) is an active video game that combines aerobic and resistance-based exercise.

title: A preliminary study of the immunogenic response of plant-derived multi-epitopic peptide vaccine candidate of Mycoplasma gallisepticum in chickens
creator: Susithra Priyadarhni Mugunthan, Divyadharshini Venkatesan, Chandramohan Govindasamy, Dhivya Selvaraj, Harish Mani Chandra
description: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is responsible for chronic respiratory disease in avian species, characterized by symptoms like respiratory rales and coughing. Existing vaccines for MG have limited efficacy and require multiple doses. Certain MG cytoadherence proteins (GapA, CrmA, PlpA, and Hlp3) play a crucial role in the pathogen’s respiratory tract colonization and infection.

title: Effect of Alloying and Phase Segregation on the Stability of High-Entropy Alloys: A Case Study on the Dissolution of Os–Ru–Rh–Ir–Pt Nanoparticles
creator: Tatiana Priamushko, Rebecca K. Pittkowski, Maria Minichova, Attila Kormányos, Valentin Briega-Martos, Luis A. Cipriano, Nicolas Schlegel, Rasmus Rohde, Espen D. Bøjesen, Kirsten M. Ø. Jensen, Jan Rossmeisl, Matthias Arenz, Serhiy Cherevko
description: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) have emerged as a class of promising electrocatalysts for energy-conversion reactions. In addition to catalytic activity, stability under the reaction conditions is paramount for practical applications. Understanding the dissolution behavior of these multimetallic, complex nanomaterials is therefore essential.

title: Screening and surveillance of esophageal cancer by magnifying endoscopy with narrow band imaging improves the survival of hypopharyngeal cancer patients
creator: Chen-Shuan Chung, Chia-Yun Wu, Yu-Hsuan Lin, Wu-Chia Lo, Ping-Chia Cheng, Wan-Lun Hsu, Li-Jen Liao
description: IntroductionPatients with head and neck cancer may develop a second primary neoplasm (SPN) of the esophagus due to field cancerization. This study investigated the impacts of esophageal cancer screening using magnifying endoscopy with narrow-band imaging (ME-NBI) on the outcomes of hypopharyngeal cancer patients.MethodsPatients with hypopharyngeal cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2021 in a tertiary hospital were reviewed retrospectively.

title: Clinical, Economic, and System-Level Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery in Adults: Protocol for a Systematic Review
creator: Michał Bystram, Marlena Robakowska, Monika Proczko-Stepaniak, Javad Sarvestan
description: BackgroundObesity affects approximately 880 million adults worldwide and carries substantial health, economic, and social consequences. Although bariatric surgery achieves sustained weight loss and metabolic improvement, existing systematic reviews largely predate 2020 and rarely integrate clinical, economic, and system-level perspectives within a single synthesis.

title: From signal to bedside: the missing link between ECG-AI explainability and clinical trust
creator: Akinchan Bhardwaj, Ishita Vasudev, Pushkala Jayaraman
