PLOS has no evidence of any author involvement in the peer review concerns. The editor listed on the article is a PLOS Staff Editor who was not involved in the concerns, and who was unaware of the peer review issues before the article was published.

title: Sorting nexin 10 promotes triple-negative breast cancer progression through modulating cholesterol biosynthesis via stabilizing SREBP2
creator: Yinping Guo, Jiahui Li, Wenjie Zhang, Min Xia, Gaohua Liu, Xiaolin Zhong, Yan Yi, Yajun Chen, Jing Zhong
description: ObjectiveTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks effective therapeutics in clinical practice. Sorting nexin 10 (SNX10) plays essential roles in various cancers, and the role of SNX10 in TNBC remains unknown. This study investigated the role and action mechanism of SNX10 in TNBC.MethodsUsing the Kaplan–Meier Plotter database and bc-GenExMiner database to analyze the SNX10 expression and clinical significance.

title: Fertility Social Mentality Scale for Women of Childbearing Age: a scale development study
creator: Binyang Zhang, Nanyin Bu, Shiqin Xu, Zuoshan Li
description: ObjectiveTo develop a scale to measure fertility social mentality among women of childbearing age in China and to assess its psychometric properties, including reliability, validity, and measurement invariance.MethodsA total of 496, 857, 607, 632 and 362 women of childbearing age were recruited to conduct exploratory factor analysis, reliability and validity testing, and measurement invariance testing, respectively.

title: The association between perceived usefulness of AI-generated art tools and self-reported creative design performance: a parallel mediation model of artistic perception, cognitive engagement, and aesthetic judgment
creator: Zhang Guosheng, Meng Lei
description: IntroductionThe rapid expansion of AI-generated art tools has transformed creative production, yet its psychological mechanisms in shaping design outcomes remain underexplored. This study examines the associations between perceived usefulness of AI-generated art tools and self-reported creative design performance through three parallel mediating pathways: artistic perception, cognitive engagement, and aesthetic judgment.

title: First occurrence of a herrerasaurid dinosaur in a traversodontid cynodont-dominated Late Triassic fauna of southern Brazil
creator: Rodrigo Temp Müller
description: Herrerasauridae comprises the oldest large-bodied predatory dinosaurs and is currently known exclusively from the Carnian (Late Triassic) of South America. In both Argentina and Brazil, herrerasaurid occurrences have previously been restricted to rhynchosaur-dominated assemblages, with no records from younger strata characterized by the abundance of the traversodontid cynodont Exaeretodon.

title: Preoperative bladder artery embolization before transurethral resection of large bladder tumors: a propensity score–matched retrospective cohort study
creator: Chengtao Gu, Jun Li, Hao Zheng, Zilong Zhang, Hao Xu, Zhe Zhang, Gang Shen, Long Cheng
description: BackgroundTransurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) can be technically challenging in patients with large bladder tumors because intraoperative bleeding may obscure the surgical field, prolong the procedure, and hinder complete tumor resection. Preoperative bladder artery embolization may reduce tumor vascularity and facilitate subsequent TURBT; however, comparative evidence regarding its perioperative benefits and safety remains limited.

title: The modulatory effects of facial cues and familiarity in face recognition: a behavioral and eye-tracking investigation
creator: Gaoyuan Zhang, Yuye Yang, Hui Chen, Xurong Xie, Jin Huang, Xiaoxia Du
description: IntroductionFace recognition is essential for social interaction, yet the extent to which internal facial features and external facial cues contribute to identity recognition remains incompletely understood. In particular, it remains unclear how external appearance changes, such as hairstyle and hair color, influence the recognition of familiar and unfamiliar faces across perceptual and memory-based processing stages.

title: High-temperature stress response in the liver of Trachinotus ovatus: a cascade of oxidative stress, immunity, and bile acid metabolic reprogramming
creator: Ruijie Zhu, Meng Xiao, Xiaohua Huang, Dianchang Zhang, Falin Zhou, Yukai Yang, Huayang Guo, Yafei Duan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fish exhibit a high degree of susceptibility to shifts in thermal conditions within the water. The liver is central to metabolic homeostasis and immune defense, and its physiological stability is critical for fish health. The present study evaluated the hepatic physiological responses of Trachinotus ovatus following a 7-day exposure to high-temperature (HT) stress, including alterations in histology, oxidative stress, iron homeostasis, inflammation, immunity, apoptosis, and bile acid (BA) metabolism.

title: Editorial: Strategies of virus persistence
creator: Magdalena Weidner-Glunde, Michael M. Nevels, Emma Poole
description: eted therapeutic strategies aimed at disrupting tumorigenic viruses. Furthermore, the collection highlights the critical need for single-cell analysis to reveal these complex viral mechanisms, concluding with a novel, optimized method designed to accurately quantify persistent viruses as they reactivate and transition into active replication.

title: Ontogenetic shifts in the metabolomic profiles of Battus polydamas (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae: Troidini) Feeding on Aristolochia gigantea
creator: Sofia Coradini Schirmer, Thomas Christopher Rhys Williams, Jefferson Brendon Almeida dos Reis
description: Insect development involves profound physiological reorganization that can alter the assimilation and allocation of metabolites across life stages. In herbivorous insects, these processes are tightly linked to diet-derived chemical exposure, yet how metabolic organization shifts throughout ontogeny remains poorly understood.

title: A multi-composite disease activity score (NFKB1-DAS) for NFKB1 insufficiency
creator: Katharina Thoma, Pia Hassunah, Manfred Fliegauf, Gabriele Müller, Andres Caballero Garcia de Oteyza, Pavla Mrovecova, Helene Kraus, Prerana Agarwal, Maximilian Frederik Russe, Birgit Sawitzki, Lev Petrov, Katrin Vogt, Nadezhda Camacho Ordonez, Aleksandra Hirsch, Christoph B Geier, Máté Krausz, Sigun
description: NFKB1 encodes the p105/p50 NF-κB1 transcription factor. Heterozygous mutations in NFKB1 may lead to NFKB1 insufficiency affecting multiple organ systems. This study aimed to develop an NFKB1-Disease-Activity-Score (NFKB1-DAS), serving as a tool in future clinical trials. Based on published phenotypic data from 179 patients with 77 distinct NFKB1 variants, we drafted an initial score consisting of 42 parameters.

title: External validation and application of machine learning models for obesity in Chinese children and adolescents per Chinese and WHO growth standards
creator: Fangjieyi Zheng, Xiaoqian Wang, Mei Xue, Qiong Wang, Wenqian Zhang, Zhixin Zhang, Wenquan Niu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChildhood and adolescent obesity is a growing global public health challenge, underscoring the need for reliable tools to identify individuals at high risk. We aimed to develop, validate, and deploy machine learning (ML) models for predicting obesity in children and adolescents aged 3–18 years using multi-domain risk factors per Chinese and World Health Organization (WHO) growth standards, with an online tool for clinical and public health translation.MethodsWe conducted a population-based cross-sectional study.

title: Associations of cumulative exposure and dynamic trajectories of the combined atherogenic-frailty index with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study
creator: Haidi Wu, Zikai Song, Tengfei Ye, Chunhua Yang
description: BackgroundCardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) poses a growing global health burden, yet effective tools for early risk stratification remain limited. The combined impact of atherogenic dyslipidaemia and physiological frailty, captured by the atherogenic index of plasma-frailty index (AIP-FI), on CMM development is poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of cumulative exposure and longitudinal trajectories of AIP-FI with incident CMM.

title: Re-rupture is not the only failure: tendon elongation and the 6-week nonoperative protocol for Achilles tendon rupture
creator: Filippo Spiezia, Francesco Oliva, Nicola Maffulli
description: . We believe however that the data supports a narrower conclusion. The only endpoints were re-rupture requiring surgery and failed nonoperative management requiring surgery. Re-rupture is the most visible failure of a healing Achilles tendon, but not the only one.

title: Vascular dementia and vascular cognitive impairment—current treatments and future prospects
creator: Hugh S Markus
description: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) and vascular dementia (VaD) represent a substantial and growing global health burden, yet remain under-recognized and comparatively under-researched. Two broad categories are post-stroke cognitive impairment, and VCI secondary to chronic cerebrovascular disease of which the most common cause is cerebral small vessel disease (SVD).

title: The effects and mechanisms of low-carbon transition promoting air quality improvement: based on empirical evidence of low-carbon city pilot policy
creator: Chenxi Deng, Bingnan Guo
description: In the context of the “Dual Carbon” strategic goals, promoting a comprehensive green transition of the economy and society has become a national strategic priority. Using the low-carbon city pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment, this study empirically analyzes its impact on urban air quality and the underlying mechanisms.

title: Antimicrobial resistance trends among dominant pathogens in six clinical departments of the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Guangxi Medical University, 2020–2024
creator: Wentao Tang, Jieyu Yin, Zhougui Ling
description: ObjectiveA review of antibiotic resistance and pathogen detection in six key clinical departments of our hospital was conducted between 2020 and 2024. Future hospital-acquired infection prevention, control strategies, and targeted medicine administration in relevant departments can be based on this study.

title: miR2Meth: An R package for dissecting DNA methylation heterogeneity at microRNA promoters
creator: Ying Shan, Xiaoshan Rong, Andrew E Teschendorff, Zhen Yang
description: Aberrant expression of microRNAs (miRNAs) has been found in prevalent cancer types, yet the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored due to a lack of analytical tools. Studies have shown that DNA methylation (DNAm) plays a significant role in regulating miRNA expression.

title: Climate-induced vulnerability and health outcomes in urban Bangladesh: the mediating role of psychological stress
creator: Yu Xunda, Konstantin Moskalenko, Mohammad Anisur Rahaman, Natalia Taranova, Md. Rakibul Islam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundClimate change poses growing risks to urban health, particularly in low-income informal settlements where exposure to environmental hazards is frequent and adaptive capacity is limited. However, the psychosocial mechanisms linking climate exposure to health outcomes remain underexplored.ObjectiveThis study examines the relationship between climate exposure, psychological stress, and physical health outcomes, with a focus on the mediating role of stress among low-income urban populations in Dhaka, Bangladesh.MethodsA cross-sectional quantitative study was conducted using household survey data (n = 384), complemented by secondary environmental

title: All‐Inside Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction With Accurate Measurement Technique
creator: Daoliang Xu, Wei Yu, Jian Lin, Renjie Li, Zhikai Lu, Yulong Zhou, Xiaoyun Pan
description: The all‐inside anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction technique is characterized by closed bone sockets for anterior cruciate ligament graft passage and typically adopts suspensory fixation instead of screw fixation. Inaccurate determination of the intra‐articular length (IAL) of the graft is associated with an elevated risk of graft “bottoming out” and excessive length consumption of the tibial sockets.

title: Dietary Inflammation and Chronic Dizziness With Imbalance in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Nationally Representative Study
creator: Seong-Hae Jeong, Eun Ji Kim, Eunjin Kwon, Eunice Hong Lim Lee, Sukyoung Jung
description: BackgroundChronic dizziness and imbalance, which can significantly impact an individual’s quality of life and even mortality, are prevalent conditions with multifactorial etiologies, including inflammation. We examined the association between dietary inflammatory potential and chronic dizziness with imbalance.MethodsThis study included 7,562 Korean adults aged ≥ 40 years from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2019–2022.

title: Increasing and sustaining blood-borne virus screening in Spain and Portugal throughout the COVID-19 pandemic: a multi-center quality improvement intervention
creator: Inês Vaz-Pinto, Enrique Ortega, Ivan Chivite, María Butí, Juan Turnes-Vázquez, Vítor Magno-Pereira, Miguel Rocha, Jorge Garrido, Catarina Esteves-Santos, Mafalda Guimaraes, Tomás Mourão, María Martínez Roma, Vanessa Guilera, Jordi Llaneras-Artigues, Ana Barreira-Díaz, Santiago Pérez Cachafeiro, Sand
description: BackgroundAround 57,000 people in Spain and Portugal currently living with HIV or chronic hepatitis C are unaware of their infection. The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted screening efforts for these infections. We designed an intervention to increase and sustain opportunistic blood-borne virus (BBV) screening and linkage to care (SLTC) by implementing the TEST model.

title: Cattle production, water resources, and sustainability: a review of current knowledge and future directions
creator: Kevin Wagner, Susan Metzger, Brent Auvermann
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ty degradation, increasing drought severity, and low BMP adoption threaten grazing systems, but riparian protection, adaptive grazing, precision livestock technologies, and coordinated Extension–Natural Resources Conservation Service support can meaningfully improve resilience and water outcomes. Feedyards face parallel challenges, particularly nutrient‑laden runoff, high indirect water use for feed, and declining irrigation supplies, yet innovations in manure management, wastewater reuse, and low‑water forage systems offer viable pathways to reduce water demand.

title: Molecular Interplay between hypertension and dyslipidemia in cardiovascular pathogenesis: toward precision-based therapeutic strategies
creator: Boming Cao, Jingyi Pei, Ling Kong, Ying Han, Guangli Yan, Xijun Wang
description: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the foremost cause of global mortality. Hypertension and dyslipidemia, frequently coexisting, exert synergistic effects that substantially elevate CVD risk via interconnected molecular pathways. This review systematically examines the synergistic mechanisms underlying their combined contribution to CVD progression, with a focus on key pathways such as the RAAS/PPAR axis, AMPK/SIRT1 signaling, and NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

title: Interventions of Brazil's more doctors program through continuing education for Primary Health Care
creator: Laianny Krizia Maia Pereira, José Adailton da Silva, Ricardo A. de M. Valentim, Thaísa G. F. M. S. Lima, Cristine M. G. Gusmão, Marcela A. da Rocha, Marquiony M. dos Santos, Alexandre R. Caitano, Rosires M. B. de Barros, Tatyana Souza Rosendo
description: IntroductionBrazil's More Doctors Program, in its training axis, aims to improve medical training for Primary Health Care through interventions related to the reality of the territory. The research presented here analyzed the interventions implemented by Brazil's More Doctors Program physicians, members of the Family Health Continuing Education Program, and the relationship with Primary Health Care programmatic actions.

title: Swallowed dental prosthesis causing late oesophageal obstruction and tracheo-oesophageal fistula in a young patient
creator: Harish Prasanna, Daniel Boyle, David Bowrey
description: A 25-year-old man presented to the emergency department after a rugby accident having swallowed a dental plate. Initial assessment at the time of ingestion, including a chest radiograph, was unremarkable and the plate was presumed to have been expectorated. Five years later he presented with progressive dysphagia, recurrent food bolus obstruction, and haemoptysis.

title: Microbial diversity in Pyrenean ice caves: extreme cryogenic environments as analogues for extraterrestrial habitability
creator: Víctor Muñoz-Hisado, Fernando Puente-Sánchez, Miguel Bartolomé, Reyes Giménez, Eva Garcia-Lopez, Ana Moreno, Cristina Cid, Yannick Lara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pyrenean ice caves are the least studies cryogenic environments that preserve perennial ice. These caves host microbial communities adapted to extreme oligotrophy, low temperatures, and episodic water availability, making them valuable analogues for subsurface habitats on icy planetary bodies.

title: The Efferocytosis‐Driven Macrophage Polarization: A Concerto in the Tumor Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
creator: Qiuping Chen, Chunzhi Wu, Changquan Huang, Hang Zhou
description: Efferocytosis plays a critical role in maintaining tissue homeostasis and controlling inflammation. However, in the tumor microenvironment, this process is hijacked to promote immune suppression. Treatments like radiotherapy and chemotherapy lead to widespread tumor cell death, which triggers efferocytosis and drives macrophages into an immunosuppressive state, allowing the tumor to evade the immune system and resist treatment.

title: Efficacy of personalized feedback in encouraging sustainable washing behavior: evidence from a pilot study in Germany
creator: Laura Höpfl, Ivan Đula, Francisco Kiss, Rebecca Walter, Maria Wirzberger
description: IntroductionReducing household energy consumption through behavioral changes is a key strategy in addressing the emissions driving the climate crisis. Behavioral changes in affluent households toward more sustainable practices can have a significant positive impact. Prior research highlighted the role of individual values and motivational factors in shaping sustainable clusters.

title: Establishment and evaluation of a UPLC-MS/MS method for simultaneous determination of bongkrekic acid and dehydroacetic acid in rice noodles
creator: Lingguo Zhao, Ronggui Lv, Jiang Song, Xi Chen, Lei Lei, Weixian Zeng, Miaowen She, Dabing Li, Xiaxia Yu, Zhanguo Liu, Xiao Wang, Yong Liu
description: A UPLC-MS/MS method with one-step extraction and simultaneous determination of bongkrekic acid (BA) and dehydroacetic acid (DHA) in rice noodles has been established in this study for the first time. The extraction solvent consisted of a mixture of methanol, ammonia, and water.

title: Mononuclear Mg(ii) and Ca(ii) metallocarboxylates of N-phthaloyl-γ-aminobutyric acid: synthesis, characterization, ds-DNA binding, preliminary anticancer evaluation against MDA-MB-231 cells, and computational studies
creator: Naeem Abbas, Muhammad Arfan, Yasir Iqbal, Mudassir Iqbal, Naeem Ahmed, Mona G. Alharbi, Mansour K. Gatasheh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study reports the synthesis of neurotransmitter-inspired, biolabile mononuclear Mg(ii)/(NY1) and Ca(ii)/(NY2) metallocarboxylates of N-phthaloyl-γ-aminobutyric acid ligand (NPGABA), motivated by the growing relevance of metallocarboxylates in addressing essential metal-ion deficiencies. Extensive spectral (i.e. IR, UV-vis, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, AAS, and ICP-AES) and analytical (SEM, micro-analysis and thermal gravimetric analysis) techniques were used to characterize and confirm the formation of the ligand and its metal carboxylate complexes.

title: Unveiling diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for cervical cancer: biomarker discovery through proteomics approaches and exploring the role of cervical cancer stem cells
creator: Ameneh Jafari, Masoumeh Farahani, Meghdad Abdollahpour-Alitappeh, Asma Manzari-Tavakoli, Mohsen Yazdani, Mostafa Rezaei-Tavirani
description: Cervical cancer (CC) is a major global health problem and leading cause of cancer deaths among women worldwide. Early detection through screening programs has reduced mortality; however, screening compliance remains low. Identifying non-invasive biomarkers through proteomics for diagnosis and monitoring response to treatment could improve patient outcomes.

title: Cuticular wax profiling of Populus trichocarpa and P. balsamifera reveals surface similarities with underlying differences
creator: Mahbobeh Zamani-Babgohari, Huiru Peng, Armando Geraldes, Charles A. Hefer, Jessica Y. Hu, Raju Y. Soolanayakanahally, Shawn D. Mansfield, Eliana Gonzales-Vigil
description: Cuticular waxes are a mixture of hydrophobic components protecting plant tissues from the environment. Populus trichocarpa and P. balsamifera are closely-related tree species with broad North American distribution; however, variation in their cuticular wax composition across their range remained poorly understood.

title: From inertness to efficiency: immobilizing Au–Bi heterostructures on a graphite substrate to drive the hydrogen evolution reaction
creator: Kazi Hamidur Rashid, Nure Alam Siddique, Rehana Akter, Jahir Ahmed, M. Faisal, Jari S. Algethami, Farid A. Harraz, Jamal Uddin, Md Musfiqur Rahman, Nayan Ranjan Singha, Mohammad A. Hasnat
description: In this study, we fabricated Au–Bi heterostructures on a pencil graphite (GP) support to generate hydrogen from water splitting under acidic conditions. Au particles, with their electronically filled 5d band, and Bi particles, known for their strong tendency toward surface oxide formation, exhibit limited intrinsic activity toward the HER.

title: Paper integrated aptamer–CRISPR sensing enables multiplexed small-molecule sensing in a low-cost device
creator: Anindita Sen, Douglas James Bock, Tegan Foster, Rachel Fleming, Justin M. Hodgkiss
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). CRISPR/Cas12a-based diagnostics achieved attomolar sensitivity for nucleic acid detection, yet their extension to small-molecule targets remains constrained by the need for solution-phase aptasensor–CRISPR coupling and laboratory infrastructure incompatible with resource-limited settings. Here we report a Paper-integrated Aptamer–Cas12a Sensing platform (PACSense) in which the complete aptasensor–CRISPR/Cas12a signal transduction cascade is air-dried within a paper substrate, enabling a one-pot, amplification-free small-molecule detection workflow that is initiated by sample addition alone.

title: From iPSC to manufactured iNK cells using CombiCult® screening platform
creator: Marina Tarunina, Sachin Luharia, Matthew Houppermans, Giuseppe D’Agostino, Lam Lam, Michelle Gestwa, Aleksandra Habich-Crayton, Marcia Mata, Juline Guenat, Molly Tregidgo, Patrick Statham, Charlotte Lee-Reeves, Mudith Jayawardena, Simona Zingaro, Limor Zwi-Dantsis, Aishwarya Nair, Alexandru-Robert P
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAllogeneic cell-based immunotherapies generated from pluripotent stem cells show considerable promise for the treatment of oncological, autoimmune, and viral diseases, however discovery platforms for induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cell therapies do not translate well to scalable manufacturing platforms.MethodsWe applied a high-throughput combinatorial screening platform (CombiCult®) to identify novel, manufacturing-ready, feeder-free protocols for the generation of mature, functional NK cells from human iPSCs.ResultsWe validated seven CombiCult®-derived differentiation protocols for the production of highly cytotoxic, phenotypically mature iPSC-derived NK (iNK) cells, which are

title: Synthetic embryology of the human heart
creator: Maria Belen Paredes-Espinosa, Janet L. Paluh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The evolution of stem cell-based heart models from cells and tissues to organoids and assembloids and recently synthetic embryology gastruloids, is poised to revolutionize our understanding of cardiac development, congenital to adult diseases, and patient customized therapies. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) have already been integrated into transplantable patches and are in preclinical efforts to reverse fibrotic scarring from myocardial infarctions.

title: The effect of internet embeddedness on women’s non-farm employment under the power perception perspective: evidence from rural China
creator: Song Yu, Lulu Yang, Shimei Yang, Lianjun Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionFemale empowerment can promote gender equality and realize women’s comprehensive development, while the Internet has opened up an effective channel for female empowerment.MethodsGiven the relative lack of women’s rights in rural China and the rapid Internet development, this paper, based on the 2021 China Comprehensive Social Survey data, first analyses the effect of Internet embeddedness on rural women’s non-farm employment using the Probit model.

title: Recurrent TFE3‐Rearranged Renal Cell Carcinoma Responding to Pembrolizumab Plus Lenvatinib After Postoperative Pembrolizumab: A Case Report
creator: Masashi Fujimoto, Tomoyasu Sano, Yuta Sano, Satoshi Inoue, Kazuna Matsuo, Tomokazu Kimura, Shohei Ishida, Kenji Zennami, Yoshihisa Matsukawa, Shusuke Akamatsu
description: IntroductionTFE3‐rearranged renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is rare, and evidence guiding systemic therapy is limited.Case PresentationA 25‐year‐old man with gross hematuria had a left renal tumor with hilar lymph node metastasis. Robot‐assisted radical nephrectomy and hilar lymph node dissection were performed. Histology, immunohistochemistry, and fluorescence in situ hybridization confirmed TFE3‐rearranged RCC, pT3aN1.

title: Neural and autonomic regulation during brief mindfulness and relaxation interventions in clinical populations: a multimodal MEG study protocol
creator: Sabrina Diny, Fabian Schmidt, Andreas Wutz, Nathan Weisz, Thomas Probst
description: Mental disorders pose a major and growing challenge for health care systems worldwide, marked by persistent treatment gaps and limited access to psychotherapeutic care. Mind–body interventions such as mindfulness and relaxation practices are widely used in clinical contexts as low-threshold strategies to support stress regulation and psychological well-being.

title: The Immunological Consequences of Pediatric Adenotonsillectomy: Myths, Evidence, and Unsolved Questions
creator: Barbara Verro, Gaetano Ottoveggio, Simona Fiumara, Carmelo Saraniti
description: Tonsillectomy is one of the most common surgical procedures in pediatric populations, indicated primarily for recurrent tonsillitis and upper airway obstruction. Palatine tonsils represent lymphoepithelial structures crucial for local and systemic immune surveillance, with a key role in lymphocyte maturation and the production of immunoglobulins, particularly secretory IgA.

title: Opportunities, challenges, and difficulties in NMR-based metabolomics applied to neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) patient follow-up
creator: M. Schoumacher, V. Lambert, M. Campas, P. Blaise, B. Locht, M. Thys, E. Duchateau, E. Cavalier, J.-M. Rakic, A. Noël, P. de Tullio
description: IntroductionThis study applies NMR-based metabolomics to investigate neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), addressing challenges in patient management, disease progression evaluation, and treatment response assessment. A two-year follow-up of 29 nAMD patients undergoing treatment provided 231 time points for analysis.MethodsOver the two-year period, 11 males and 18 females (aged 61–92 years) were monitored, yielding 231 time points.

title: Medullary adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon mimicking appendicitis after prior appendectomy
creator: Ian L Cummings-Ruiz, Jose O Nieves-Munoz, Suheily Acevedo, Guillermo E Bolaños Avila
description: Medullary adenocarcinoma is a rare colorectal carcinoma that may be difficult to recognize when inflammation dominates the presentation. A 65-year-old woman with a remote appendectomy presented with 1 month of postprandial abdominal pain, weight loss, and constipation. Repeated computed tomography demonstrated marked pericecal inflammation and a blind-ending structure interpreted as possible appendicitis despite her surgical history.

title: Applications of functional near-infrared spectroscopy in non-drug therapy of traditional Chinese medicine: a review
creator: Shifang Fu, Fanqi Liu, Xiaoyu Zhi, Yu Wang, Yijia Liu, Hao Chen, Yanguo Wang, Mingchi Luo
description: Non-drug therapies of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), including acupuncture, massage, tai chi chuan, and Baduanjin, have emerged as widespread interventions for the treatment of various diseases in clinical practice. In recent years, preliminary studies on the mechanisms of non-drug therapies of TCM have been mostly based on functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) technology.

title: Effect of molybdenum supply on crop performance through rhizosphere soil microbial diversity and metabolite variation
creator: Muhammad Shoaib Rana, Dikhnah Alshehri, Rui-Long Wang, Muhammad Imran, Yousif Abdelrahman Yousif Abdellah, Faiz Ur Rahman, Marfat Alatawy, Hanaa Ghabban, Amany H. A. Abeed, Cheng-xiao Hu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Molybdenum (Mo) deficiency is a global problem in acidic soils, limiting plant growth, development, and nutrient availability. To address this, we carried out a field study with two treatments, i.e., Mo applied (+Mo) and without Mo (−Mo) treatment to explore the effects of Mo application on crop growth and development, microbial diversity, and metabolite variations in maize and soybean cropping systems.

title: Polyomavirus Drives Cerebellar Lesions in AIDS Monkeys With Ataxia
creator: Tian‐Zhang Song, Li‐Rong Zhang, Yun‐Mei Wang, Yan Hu, Qing Li, Ren‐Rong Tian, Liu‐Meng Yang, Si‐Dong Xiong, Dong‐Dong Wu, Yong‐Tang Zheng
description: Cognitive and motor dysfunction occurs in 30%–50% of people with HIV/AIDS. Within this clinical spectrum, HIV‐associated ataxia is an uncommon but debilitating disorder with poorly defined neuropathological mechanisms. This study investigated two rhesus macaques with chronic simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection that developed progressive ataxia, characterized by postural imbalance and nystagmus.

title: A Robust Self-Powered Triboelectric Sensor for Risk Mitigation in Seismic Scenarios: IoT Communication and Dimensional Monitoring
creator: José Sánchez del Río Sáez, Antonio Vázquez-López, Jorge Edison Pozo Benavides, Alba López Laguna, Martin Andolfi, Rafael Cascón, Francisco Santos Olalla, Sofía Paramio, Yolanda Ballesteros, Carlos Cruz, Vanesa Martínez, José Luis Jiménez, José Benito Bravo Monge, Xiang Ao, De-Yi Wang
description: Currently, there is an increasing need for low-cost detectors that can measure ground motion with high sensitivity and selectivity. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have arisen as low-cost self-powering sensing devices that can be used in multiple applications that involve vibration and motion, such as in earthquake detection.

title: Vitamin K2 ameliorates pregnancy‐ and lactation‐associated osteopenia and postpartum depression
creator: Wanqiong Yuan, Jing Hang, Jialin Jia, Jie Huang, Xuanqi Zheng, Huan Wang, Tong Wu, Hao Liu, Junxiong Zhu, Chenggui Zhang, Jinwen He, Yundi Zhang, Hong Wang, Xin Xiong, Na He, Haofan Bai, Jiamin Yan, Huijie Leng, Weili Zhu, Yingsheng Xu, Jie Shi, Chunli Song
description: Vitamin K2 (VitK2) supplementation ameliorates comorbid pregnancy‐ and lactation‐associated osteopenia (PLO) and postpartum depression (PPD). These improvements are accompanied by reduced relative abundance of Bacteroides uniformis (B. uniformis) and lower serum deoxycholic acid (DCA) levels. DCA inhibits osteoblast differentiation, promotes osteoclast differentiation, and contributes to an imbalance between hippocampal glutamatergic and GABAergic signaling. Maternal VitK2 supplementation also improves offspring cognition.

title: Valorization of Teak Leaf Agricultural Waste: Impact of Drying Technique and Production Scale on Extract Quality
creator: Natthawadee Tibkawin, Nichapa Buasumrit, Panatpong Boonnoun, Sukunya Ross, Gareth Ross, Jarupa Viyoch, Pensri Charoensit
description: This study investigates how drying technique and production scale govern the quality, structure, and functionality of teak leaf extracts derived from an abundant agricultural byproduct. Freeze-drying (FD) and spray-drying (SD) were applied at laboratory and pilot scales, and the resulting extracts were evaluated for physicochemical properties, bioactive composition, antioxidant activity, powder flowability, and thermal behavior.

title: Age and estrogen-associated reductions in hypoxic ventilatory response and chemosensitivity in female rats
creator: Jessica M. L. Grittner, Rebecca Barok, Edgar Juarez Lopez, Misha Shah, Brendan J. Dougherty
description: Respiratory function is modulated by circulating steroid hormones. In female rats, steroid hormones fluctuate across the normal estrous cycle and decline with age, similar to human menopause. To determine the influence of steroid hormones, and mimic aspects of age-related reductions in hormones, the ovariectomy model is often employed. Ovariectomy (OVX) induces an immediate and persistent decrease in steroid hormones.

title: I’ve just seen a face: further search for face pareidolia in chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)
creator: Masaki Tomonaga
description: IntroductionSeeing faces in random patterns, such as in clouds, is known as pareidolia. Two possible mechanisms can cause pareidolia: a bottom-up mechanism that automatically detects inverted triangle or top-heavy patterns, and a top-down mechanism that actively seeks out faces. Pareidolia has been reported in nonhuman animals as well.

title: Biofabricated Al2O3 nanoparticles as a recyclable heterogeneous catalyst for nicotinonitrile synthesis: antimicrobial activity, molecular docking and ADMET assessment
creator: Prakash Kokare, Ashwini More, Nilesh Pandit, Vishvanath Ghanwat, Amol Jadhav, Aniket Sawant, Chaitali Bagade, Dipak mali, Sunanda Mahanwar, Santosh Kamble
description: An efficient and environmentally benign Al2O3 nanoparticle-catalyzed protocol was developed for the synthesis of nicotinonitrile derivatives under mild reaction conditions using an ethanol–water solvent system. The Al2O3 nanoparticles were synthesized via a green approach employing Coccinia indica leaf extract and characterized by XRD, SEM, EDS, FTIR, and BET analyses.

title: Phytocanabinoids and synthetic cannabinoids: from recreational consumption to potential therapeutic use – a review
creator: Helena M. Teixeira
description: Cannabinoids are part of the most popular group of illicit substances in the Western world. The word “cannabinoid” refers to any chemical substance, regardless of structure or origin, that binds to the body’s cannabinoid receptors and that has effects similar to those produced by the Cannabis plant. Regarding their origin, cannabinoids can be classified into endocannabinoids, phytocannabinoids and synthetic cannabinoids.

title: Iron(iii) sulfate/H2O-catalysed, base-free esterification of carboxylic acids with dimethyl carbonate: the crucial role of water as a co-catalyst
creator: Yosra Ben Abdallah, Zaineb Litim, Donia Ghedira, Thierry Ollevier, Jamil Kraïem
description: An eco-friendly, base-free protocol was developed for the esterification of carboxylic acids with dimethyl carbonate (DMC), which serves as both the reagent and solvent, using an iron(iii) sulfate/H2O catalytic system. The method combines high efficiency with a broad substrate scope under mild and environmentally benign conditions.

title: Editorial: Exploring unconventional T cells and CAR-T-cells in cancer immunotherapy
creator: Laura Patrussi, Chenran Zhang
description: T) cells, and mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells, recognize non-peptide antigens, stress-associated molecules, and metabolic intermediates in an MHC-independent or non-classical MHC-restricted manner. These properties position them at the interface between innate and adaptive immunity and make them particularly attractive candidates for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.

title: Progress in immunotherapy for brain metastatic melanoma
creator: Shicheng Zheng, Zhongqiao Lin, Ruibo Zhang, Zihang Cheng, Kaixin Li, Chenkai Gu, Yu Chen, Jing Lin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Melanoma is highly aggressive, with brain metastasis being a significant contributor to poor outcomes. Immunotherapy has emerged as a crucial treatment modality for melanoma, particularly for addressing brain metastases. This review explores recent developments in immunotherapy for patients with melanoma brain metastasis, with such treatments encompassing immune checkpoint inhibitors and various immunotherapy combination approaches, such as dual immunotherapy, immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy, immunotherapy combined with targeted drugs, and immunotherapy combined with radiotherapy.

title: Current status and influencing factors of activation of older patients with chronic disease
creator: Zhu Yiran, Zhang Yan, Xing Lijun, Li Xizheng, Zhang Xinjie, Tian Yutong
description: ObjectiveWe aimed to investigate the status and influencing factors of activation of older patients with chronic disease.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study, using the general information questionnaire, Patient Activation Measure, the Chinese version of the e-Health Literacy Scale, and the Health Empowerment Scale for the Elderly with Chronic Disease.

title: Micro/nanoplastics: from synthesis to assimilation, global environmental impacts, challenges, consequences, and advanced remediation strategies
creator: Muhammad Rizwan, Amir Zada, Ghulam Murtaza, Nolubabalo Matinise, Hong Chen
description: Environmental pollution has become a hot research topic and a grave issue throughout the world. The presence of plastic and its derivatives almost everywhere and in every segment of the environment has polluted water (the marine environment), soil, and even the atmosphere. Plants, animals and microorganisms are all equally affected.

title: Biological functions and clinical efficacy of IL-5/IL-5Rα-targeted therapies across eosinophilia-associated diseases
creator: Johannes Lübke, Andreas Reiter, Juliana Schwaab
description: Interleukin-5 (IL-5) is a central regulator of eosinophil differentiation, maturation, survival, activation, and mobilization, and it contributes to eosinophil recruitment to inflamed tissues. These biological functions have made the IL-5/IL-5 receptor alpha (IL-5Rα) pathway a key therapeutic target in eosinophil-associated diseases.

title: Do VIP medical services damage efficiency? New evidence of medical institutions’ total factor productivity using Chinese panel data
creator: Yan Yang, Mingwang Cheng, Ning Chen, Ling Yuan, Zhaoxin Wang
description: This study examines the causal impact of very important person (VIP) medical services on hospital total factor productivity in Deyang, a prefectural-level city in western China, spanning the years 2015–2020. This aims to offer empirical evidence and policy recommendations for the implementation of VIP practices in the medical field.

title: Comparison of Laparoscopic-Assisted Transversus Abdominis Plane Block and Trocar-Site Local Anesthetic Infiltration After Laparoscopic Appendectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: İksan Taşdelen, Fatih Kilic, Kemal Memişoğlu, Ahmet Yalin Iscan, Bülent Kaya, Arzu Yildirim Ar
description: Background and objective: Abdominal wall blocks are increasingly used for pain control following laparoscopic appendectomy. This study aimed to compare the analgesic efficacy of a transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block performed by the surgical team under direct laparoscopic visualization with trocar-site infiltration using an equal total dose of local anesthetic (LA).

title: Burnout in residents during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Ricard Navinés, Victoria Olive, Diego Hidalgo-Mazzei, Klaus Langohr, Eduard Vieta, Rocio Martin-Santos
description: IntroductionThe high prevalence of burnout in resident physicians is expected to have increased as a result of the expansion of the pandemic. We conducted a systematic review with a meta-analysis of studies conducted during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic on burnout in residents and potential associated risk factors.

title: Optimizing the osteo-immunomodulatory balance: threshold-saturation effects of BMP-2-loaded allografts in the Masquelet’s induced membrane technique (MIMT)
creator: Junyi Li, Kehan Lv, Yunan Li, Hangyu Li, Guohao Liu, Wei Zhang, Xingyu Chen, Muguo Song, Jian Shi
description: BackgroundThe Masquelet induced membrane technique (MIMT) is an established strategy for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects (CSDs). However, the limited osteoinductivity of allografts often necessitates supplementation with bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2), whose supra-physiological doses may cause excessive inflammation. This study aimed to identify a BMP-2 concentration range that balances osteogenic efficacy with systemic safety in the MIMT setting.MethodsA 1.

title: Aging, cancer, and autophagy: connections and therapeutic perspectives
creator: Begoña Zapatería, Esperanza Arias
description: Aging and cancer are intricately linked through shared molecular processes that influence both the onset of malignancy and the progression of age-related decline. As organisms age, cellular stress, genomic instability, and an accumulation of senescent cells create a pro-inflammatory environment conducive to cancer development.

title: QuRad: Radiomics Feature Extraction for QuPath
creator: Janan Arslan, Tamara Künzle, Yeşim Güner, Agustí Alentorn
description: Radiomic features provide a quantitative description of tissue organization in histopathology images. QuPath, a widely used open-source platform for whole-slide image analysis, offers morphology, intensity, and Haralick texture measurements but no standardized radiomic feature set such as that of PyRadiomics. Researchers must therefore export data to external Python pipelines, interrupting their QuPath workflow.

title: Machine learning for the diagnosis accuracy of bipolar disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Yi Pan, Pushi Wang, Bowen Xue, Yanbin Liu, Xinhua Shen, Shiliang Wang, Xing Wang
description: BackgroundDiagnosing bipolar disorder poses a challenge in clinical practice and demands a substantial time investment. With the growing utilization of artificial intelligence in mental health, researchers are endeavoring to create AI-based diagnostic models. In this context, some researchers have sought to develop machine learning models for bipolar disorder diagnosis. Nevertheless, the accuracy of these diagnoses remains a subject of controversy.

title: Inherited bone marrow failure syndromes: phenotype as a tool for early diagnostic suspicion at a major reference center in Mexico
creator: Paula Leal-Anaya, Tamara N. Kimball, Ana Lucia Yanez-Felix, Moisés Ó. Fiesco-Roa, Benilde García-de Teresa, Angélica Monsiváis, Rocío Juárez-Velázquez, Esther Lieberman, Camilo Villarroel, Emiy Yokoyama, Liliana Fernández-Hernández, Anet Rivera-Osorio, David Sosa, Maria Magdalena Ortiz Sandoval, Nor
description: Introduction: The inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFSs) are a group of rare disorders characterized by bone marrow failure (BMF), physical abnormalities, and an increased risk of neoplasia. The National Institute of Pediatrics (INP) is a major medical institution in Mexico, where patients with BMF receive a complete approach that includes paraclinical tests.

title: Quercetin as a multifaceted neuroprotective agent against cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury: mechanisms and therapeutic potential
creator: Yinyan Wang, Haoran Sheng, Yan Zhang, Xu Guo, Enqi Wu, Yan Chen
description: Cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is a significant contributor to neurological dysfunction following ischemic stroke, involving multiple pathological mechanisms such as immune disorder, oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and apoptosis. Quercetin, a flavonoid compound widely present in fruits, vegetables, and grains, exhibits multiple biological activities including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, and anti-tumor properties, and has demonstrated significant neuroprotective effects in CIRI models.

title: Medium term health and quality of life outcomes in a cohort of children with MIS-C in Cape Town, South Africa
creator: Frank Phoya, Claire Butters, Timothy F. Spracklen, Hanna L. Kassa, Hamza van der Ross, Chris Scott, Kate Webb
description: BackgroundMultisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a disease that occurs after exposure to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Its short-term effects have been documented but little data exist on the longer term effects of MIS-C on the health and quality of life (QOL) of patients.

title: Green synthesis of copper oxide using Litchi chinensis leaf extract and nanocomposite formation with MXene for antimicrobial and antinematicidal activity
creator: Rida Zameer, Wajid Rehman, Liaqat Rasheed, Thoraya A. Farghaly, Muhammad Shakeel, Muhammed Sajid, Abdullah Y. A. Alzahrani
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to develop an eco-friendly CuO-loaded Ti3C2Tx MXene nanocomposite using Litchi chinensis leaf extract and evaluate its potential for antimicrobial and antinematicidal applications. The objective was to employ a green synthesis strategy in which the leaf extract served as a natural reducing, stabilizing, and capping agent for CuO nanoparticle formation, while Ti3C2Tx MXene was prepared from Ti3AlC2 through chemical etching.

title: Tailored Vascular Approach in Robot‐Assisted Nephroureterectomy for a Horseshoe Kidney: A Case Report
creator: Takanari Kambe, Yosuke Shimizu, Hajime Yoshida, Koken Hayashi, Shotaro Hatano, Tomoaki Okada, Kenji Mitsumori, Hiroyuki Onishi
description: IntroductionA horseshoe kidney is a rare congenital anomaly with complex vascular variations that increase surgical difficulty. Few reports have specifically addressed the vascular approaches in robot‐assisted surgery.Case PresentationA man in his 70s was diagnosed with right ureteral urothelial carcinoma in a horseshoe kidney.

title: A novel nomogram for predicting cardiometabolic diseases from modifiable risks in middle-aged adults-implication for health education
creator: Chia-Hao Chang, Ming-Shyan Lin, Yu-Chih Lin, Tung-Jung Huang, Mei-Yen Chen
description: BackgroundMiddle-aged adults often overlook critical modifiable risk factors that contribute to the emergence of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), including hypertension and diabetes. Many CMDs can be alleviated by addressing these modifiable risks. However, there has been insufficient research focused on rural adults with lower levels of health literacy in this regard.

title: Hydrophobic (deep) eutectic solvents: from characterization and modeling to rational design and applications
creator: Yuxuan Zhang, Kailong Zhang, Juan Feng, Jian Shi
description: (Deep) eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as versatile designer solvents because of their simple preparation, broad compositional flexibility, and highly tunable physicochemical properties. Hydrophobic (deep) eutectic solvents (HDESs), first reported in 2015, further extend the potential of eutectic solvents to aqueous and multiphase systems by exhibiting limited affinity toward water.

title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps-Mediated Intraplaque Angiogenesis and Microvascular Permeability Promote Rapid Plaque Progression following Myocardial Infarction
creator: Zhijun Lei, Yunfei Yin, Long Zeng, Na Yang, Ming Zhai, Yanxi Zeng, Yefei Shi, Qing Yu, Shiyu Gong, Weixia Jian, Jianhui Zhuang, Li Zhang, Wenhui Peng
description: Despite adherence to guideline-recommended therapies, survivors of myocardial infarction (MI) remain at high risk for recurrent ischemic events. This study aimed to elucidate the underlying mechanisms responsible for this residual risk. Using Mendelian randomization analysis and retrospective cohort study, we established a causal relationship between MI and plaque progression, potentially mediated by neutrophils.

title: Application of robust regression in translational neuroscience studies with non-Gaussian outcome data
creator: Michael Malek-Ahmadi, Stephen D. Ginsberg, Melissa J. Alldred, Scott E. Counts, Milos D. Ikonomovic, Eric E. Abrahamson, Sylvia E. Perez, Elliott J. Mufson
description: Linear regression is one of the most used statistical techniques in neuroscience, including the study of the neuropathology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia. However, the practical utility of this approach is often limited because dependent variables are often highly skewed and fail to meet the assumption of normality.

title: Context-dependent memory in the real world: the role of frequency and context dwell time
creator: Yura Choi, Kawon Kim, Sunwoo Moon, Geunseong Jung, Jae-Hyuk Cha, Hyungwook Yim
description: We investigated the context-dependent memory effect outside of the laboratory in order to examine whether the effect impacts everyday memory retrieval. We also examined various factors that may interact with the context-dependent memory effect such as frequency and context dwell time. In the experiment, we used a smartphone app to track participant’s GPS locations for 5 weeks.

title: Late-onset hypothalamic–pituitary dysfunction in a childhood cancer survivor treated with cranial irradiation
creator: Yuria Takamura, Reiko Inoue, Koji Takeuchi, Fukuo Kosokabe, Kota Ishizawa, Daisuke Inoue
description: Hypothalamic–pituitary dysfunction is a well-recognized late complication in childhood cancer survivors (CCSs) treated with cranial irradiation. We report a 42-year-old male with a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia diagnosed at 5 years of age and treated with chemotherapy and 26 Gray whole-brain irradiation. He presented with right upper extremity paresis due to bilateral chronic subdural hematomas.

title: Pharmacokinetics and Tissue Distribution of Fluorescently Labeled Neoagarotetraose in Mice
creator: Nan Wu, Chaocheng Wu, Yating Du, Zhuhua Chan, Runying Zeng
description: Background/Objectives: Neoagarotetraose (NA4), a marine-derived tetrasaccharide, holds promise as an anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agent; however, its oral bioavailability and systemic exposure mechanisms require elucidation. Methods: This study characterizes the biopharmaceutical profile of NA4 after oral and intravenous administration using a validated near-infrared fluorescence method based on covalent conjugation with Cy7.

title: Helping or watching it happen: how participants respond to robot failures in a turn-taking game
creator: Samantha Stedtler, Katherine Harrison, Valentina Fantasia
description: Robot failures in Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), though often stemming from technical limitations, can have severe effects on the interactional dynamics between humans and robots. Prior empirical research has led to conflicting findings on how such failures influence user perceptions and the overall success of the interaction.

title: Aging‐related morphological changes in the obturator internus and levator ani
creator: Satoru Muro, Junichi Tsuchiya, Takuya Ibara, Akimoto Nimura, Keiichi Akita
description: Pelvic floor dysfunction is a common condition in adult women. In addition to the levator ani, the obturator internus, a lateral pelvic wall muscle, has been suggested to be anatomically and mechanically associated with pelvic floor morphology. Here, we quantitatively characterized age‐related morphological changes in the obturator internus and levator ani using geometric morphometric analysis.

title: Diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma using liquid biopsy-based biomarkers: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
creator: Yutong Jiang, Shangwen Qi, Rongrong Zhang, Ruixia Zhao, Yu Fu, Yuxuan Fang, Mingyi Shao
description: IntroductionThe diagnostic performance of liquid biopsy-based biomarkers for HCC was comprehensively compared in this network meta-analysis (NMA).MethodsA thorough literature search was conducted to identify all comparative studies from January 1, 2000, to January 11, 2024. The QUADAS-2 tool was utilized to appraise the quality of studies involving diagnostic performance. R (v4.3.

title: Modeling Progressive Brain Volume Losses in Chronic Moderate Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Extensive, but Attenuating
creator: Robin E A Green, Brenda Colella, Alana Changoor, David J Mikulis, Adrienne Li, Kadeen Johns, Georges A Monette
description: ObjectiveProgressive brain atrophy has now been widely observed in the chronic stages of moderate–severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI), but there is only coarse information regarding its prevalence and magnitude, and whether rate of atrophy accelerates or attenuates across time. We examined these questions in a Canadian inception cohort from the Toronto Rehab TBI Recovery Study.

title: Case Report: Telitacicept in the treatment of cSLE-APS: novel therapeutic perspectives on autoimmune thrombotic diseases in children
creator: Jingyue Liu, Zhilang Cao, Yajun Wang, Jing Zheng
description: Thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) in Childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (cSLE) remains a therapeutic frontier. Here, we report the first case of telitacicept (a TACI-Fc fusion protein)- induced remission in cSLE related antiphospholipid syndrome (cSLE-APS), where targeted dual BAFF(B cell-activating factor)/APRIL(a proliferation-inducing ligand) inhibition resolved life-threatening infarctions and achieved sustained disease control.

title: Atrial fibrillation in stroke patients: facts, numbers and current challenges
creator: Katrin Wasser, Deborah Bochert, Johanna Rosemarie Leyhe, Marianne Hahn, Sonja Gröschel, Klaus Gröschel, Rolf Wachter
description: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading, modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke, with 20–30% of stroke patients harbouring underlying AF. Management of AF, however, differs substantially depending on clinical context. In ischaemic stroke patients with pre-known AF, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are the cornerstone of secondary prevention, with initiation timing guided by infarct severity following a risk-adapted approach.

title: Multi-omics study on the effect of moderate-intensity exercise on protein lactylation in mouse muscle tissue
creator: Jiahui Chang, Wanyu Wu, Ping Qian, Zhaoxu Lu, Xuejia He, Fang Wang, Ting Zhang
description: IntroductionThis study explores the effects of moderate-intensity exercise on protein lactylation in mouse muscle tissue metabolism.MethodsHealthy adult mice running for 6 weeks as an exercise model and sedentary mice as the control were used to perform transcriptomic, proteomic, lactylation-proteomic, and metabolomic analyses. Correlation analysis between transcriptome and proteome and between proteome and metabolome was also conducted.

title: The knowledge, attitudes and practice of nasal irrigation among patients with rhinosinusitis: a cross-sectional study
creator: Feng-ling Yang, Biao Wang, Wei Deng, Zhen-hua Jiang, Li-jun Zhang, Ni Liao, Lun-shu Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveNasal inflammatory diseases significantly impair patients' quality of life, with global prevalence varying regionally. Nasal irrigation, endorsed by international guidelines as adjunctive therapy, lacks standardized protocols and patient education, potentially compromising efficacy.

title: Current status of treatment and disease burden of a cohort of hemophilia B in China
creator: Yiwen Huang, Chuchuan Wan, Tao Guan, Xiaoyu Xi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveHemophilia B is a rare X-chromosome linked hereditary bleeding disorder. Patients require lifelong treatment and it is costly, but there is a lack of research in China on the treatment and burden for this group.

title: Community case study: an academia-industry-government partnership that monitors and predicts outbreaks in Tri-County Detroit area since 2017
creator: Irene Xagoraraki, Liang Zhao, Yabing Li, Brijen Miyani, John Norton, James Broz, Andrew Kaye, Anna Mehrotra, Anil Gosine, Scott Withington, Stacey McFarlane, Russell A. Faust
description: The Tri-County Detroit Area (TCDA) is the 12th most populous metropolitan area in the United States with over three million people. Multiple communicable diseases are endemic in the TCDA. In 2017, to explore innovative methods that may provide early warnings of outbreaks affecting populations in the TCDA, an exploratory partnership that was funded by a U.S.

title: Persistent shortfalls in government health expenditure: a decade-long analysis of Abuja 15% target attainment across 52 African countries, 2014–2023
creator: Muhammed Adeniyi Adebisi, Isaac Olushola Ogunkola, Don Eliseo Lucero-Prisno, Anas Ali Alhur, Quadri Aishat Adeola, Azeezat Fajembola, Goodness Ogeyi Odey, Nafisat Dasola Jimoh, Atunde Ahmed Olarewaju, Luke Alade, Joshua Aluga Gideon, Yusuff Adebayo Adebisi
description: BackgroundIn 2001, African governments committed through the Abuja Declaration to allocating at least 15% of annual government budgets to health. More than 2 decades later, the extent to which this commitment has been achieved consistently, rather than in isolated years, remains unclear.

title: Supramolecular Materials in Extreme Environments: Balancing Stability and Dynamics
creator: Yiwa Wang, Chao Yu, Jingnan Li, Jianfeng Cheng, Xiuming Liu, Songbao Fu
description: The development of supramolecular materials has opened up unprecedented opportunities for smart, responsive systems. Yet, their practical application in extreme environments—deep space, deep sea, polar regions, high-temperature and high-pressure reservoirs—is fundamentally challenged by the inherent trade-off between structural stability and dynamic adaptability.

title: Depression, anxiety, burnout, and substance use disorders among auto workers and COVID-19 as a stressor in Mexico
creator: Raúl A. Gutiérrez García, Abraham Sánchez Ruiz, Antonio de Jesús Serrano Carrera, Nancy Alejandra Vaca Rico, Mónica Natalia Arteaga Tovar, María Alicia Zavala Berbena, Marco Antonio Escobar Acevedo, María Abigail Paz Pérez, Kalina Isela Martínez Martínez
description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic intensified psychosocial risks, exposing vulnerabilities in labor conditions. Findings aim to inform mental health interventions and workplace policies tailored to industrial workers in post-pandemic settings.MethodsWe evaluated the prevalence of occupational stress and associated psychiatric problems, including anxiety, depression, substance use disorders, and burnout among automotive workers, examining COVID-19 as a significant stressor.

title: Adapting the ADVANCE group program for digitally-supported delivery to reduce intimate partner violence by men in substance use treatment: a feasibility study
creator: Gail Gilchrist, Sandi Dheensa, Amy Johnson, Juliet Henderson, Polly Radcliffe, Georges Dwyer, Richard Turner, Kate Thomson, Cat Papastavrou Brooks, Beverly Love, Zohra Zenasni, Cassandra Berbary, Ben Carter, Steve Parrott, Jinshuo Li, Caroline Easton, Ciara Bergman, Gene Feder, Elizabeth Gilchrist
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionCOVID-19 restrictions created barriers to “business as usual” in healthcare but also opened the door to innovation driven by necessity. This manuscript (1) describes how ADVANCE, an in-person group perpetrator program to reduce intimate partner violence (IPV) against female (ex)partners by men in substance use treatment, was adapted for digitally-supported delivery (ADVANCE-D), and (2) explores the feasibility and acceptability of delivering ADVANCE-D to men receiving substance use treatment.MethodsFirstly, the person-based approach and mHealth development framework were used to iteratively adapt ADVANCE for

title: Needs among persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers: a multi-perspective qualitative study focusing on the potential role of palliative care
creator: Kira Schmidt-Stiedenroth, Julia Salandi, Alexandra Schmidt, Balam Er Dedekarginoglu, Stefanie Paniczek, Manuela Schallenburger, Anette Scholz, Jacqueline Schwartz, Kathrin Fricke, Stefanie Keymel, Achim Mortsiefer, Martin Neukirchen, Adrian Loerbroks
description: ObjectivesTo explore needs among persons with advanced COPD and informal caregivers, and to explore how palliative care can address those needs.BackgroundCOPD is a common, progressive disease affecting lung function and represents a leading cause of death. Advanced COPD is associated with a high symptom burden and poor quality of life.

title: Automatic Tuning and Matching for NMR Probes Based on Physics-Informed Conditional Neural Processes
creator: Zhida Zhai, Zhenggang Li, Ying He, Yaohong Wang, Chenjun Zhu, Weifeng Wu, Yitong Lin, Huijun Sun
description: The NMR resonator is the sensor responsible for transmitting RF pulses and receiving detection signals, and its tuning and matching are crucial to acquiring high-sensitivity NMR signals. Automated tuning and matching (ATM) is therefore essential for rapid, accurate, and continuously efficient testing.

title: Managing two cases of twin anemia–polycythemia sequence in monochorionic twin pregnancies
creator: Yongke Zhang, Yiheng Liang, Ran Chen, Dirong Zhang, Jing Wu
description: BackgroundTwin anemia–polycythemia sequence (TAPS) is a rare monochorionic complication. In this study, we discuss the management of two cases of TAPS with different conditions.Case presentationPatient 1 was a 34-year-old multigravida in whom the fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocities (MCA-PSVs) were 0.86 multiples of the median (MoM) and 2.0 MoM at 33 weeks of gestation.

title: Emotion estimation from video footage with LSTM
creator: Samer Attrah
description: Emotion estimation is a field that has been studied for a long time, and several approaches using machine learning models exist. This article presents BlendFER-Lite, an LSTM model that uses Blendshapes from the MediaPipe library to analyze facial expressions detected from a live-streamed camera feed.

title: Introducing GABLE: Lightweight infrastructure for longitudinal experiments using Google Apps Script
creator: Ibrahim Berber, Ilke Kas, Tarun Sepuri, Brooke N. Macnamara, M. Cenk Çavuşoğlu, Amy L. Wilson-Delfosse, Elizabeth A. Krupinski, Philip J. Smith, Soumya Ray
description: Longitudinal studies are essential for understanding how behaviors, skills, and psychological states evolve over time. While online platforms have made study development easier, researchers still face major logistical challenges when managing multi-session studies, especially when coordinating large numbers of participants, session timing, reminders, and compensation.

title: DynamicFU: Contribution-Aware Dynamic Federated Unlearning for Industrial IoT
creator: Ziang Wu, Buzhen He, Zhiwei Si, Xiuheng Liao, Chunhua Su
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) increasingly relies on federated learning (FL) to enable collaborative model training without directly sharing raw traffic data across industrial sites. However, in practical IIoT deployments, clients may later request the removal of their data contributions from a trained federated model due to regulatory requirements, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), ownership transfer, or internal data-governance policies. Such practical requirements create a strong demand for federated unlearning in IIoT applications.

title: Novel phase-controlled Al2.66O3.99/iron oxide nanocomposites for rapid Cu(II) removal from acidic water
creator: Zahra Gholizadeh, Mohammed J. Al-Awady, Maryam Aliannezhadi
description: In this study, alumina/iron oxide nanocomposites are synthesized via a simple, cost-effective co-precipitation method and investigated for the removal of copper ions from acidic aqueous media. Five samples with varying iron oxide phase contents are prepared by varying the precursor molar ratios. Structural analysis confirms the coexistence of Al₂.₆₆O₃.

title: Embodiment of infinity in mathematics
creator: Omid Khatin-Zadeh, Danyal Farsani, Zahra Eskandari
description: In this article, we discuss the embodiment of infinity as one of fundamental concepts in mathematics. In contrast to the embodiment of many other mathematical concepts, the embodiment of infinity is an endless dynamic process. In embodying +∞, an object moves rightward toward a previously-set limit and passes it.

title: Effects of Citrulline Malate Supplementation on Exercise Performance: A Systematic Review and Three-Level Meta-Analysis
creator: Xuexiang Wang, Xiaohan Fan, Jindong Chang, Hansen Li, Xing Zhang, Yilin Zhang, Tianyu Song, Ping Liu, Qing Huang, Mohamed Nashrudin Bin Naharudin, Hengzhi Deng
description: Background: Citrulline malate (CM) is commonly used as an ergogenic supplement, but its effects on exercise performance and perceived exertion remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of CM supplementation, with attention paid to differences between acute and chronic protocols. Methods: Six databases were searched from inception to August 2025.

title: Development of new powdery mildew resistant lines in garden pea (Pisum sativum L.) using induced mutagenesis and validation of resistance for the er1 and er2 gene through molecular markers
creator: Akhilesh Sharma, Devinder Kumar Banyal, Vinod Janardan Dhole, Bansuli, Ranbir Singh Rana, Rajesh Kumar, Prabhat Kumar, Nimit Kumar, Srishti, Arshia Prashar, Vivek Singh, Anoushka Sharma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Powdery mildew (PM) caused by Erysiphie pisi Syd. is the most devastating disease of pea, affecting fresh pea production as well as the quality of the marketable harvest worldwide. The efforts were made to develop PM-resistant mutants of popular pea varieties “Lincoln” and “Azad P-1” through induced mutations by following gamma irradiation (300, 400, 500, and 600 Gy) and chemical mutagenesis, i.e., ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) (0.3% and 0.4%).

title: Molecular Detection Technologies for Helicobacter pylori Antibiotic Resistance: Current Status and Clinical Implications
creator: Zhenyu Wang, Jun Lin, Xuanni Zhang, Juan Yang, Yao Liu, Yuan Ji
description: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infects approximately half of the global population and is closely linked to chronic gastritis, peptic ulcers, and gastric cancer. Antibiotic resistance has become a major global health concern with marked regional variations, severely undermining empirical treatment efficacy. Resistance mechanisms primarily involve target gene mutations, efflux pump overexpression, and altered membrane permeability.

title: Anthropometry and diagnostic aware deep learning for exercise assessment
creator: Karla Miriam Reyes Leiva, Pavla Nikelova, Martin Cerny
description: BackgroundCorrect technique during strength exercises such as squats and Romanian deadlifts (RDLs) is fundamental for performance and injury prevention.ObjectiveWe introduce ADA (Anthropometry and Diagnostic Aware), a multimodal deep-learning framework that integrates IMU kinematics with anthropometric and diagnostic features to classify movement quality and predict movement related risk.

title: Author Correction: Twinned-magnesium metal negative electrodes enable reversible magnesium electrodeposition
creator: Guodong Zou, Jingli Ren, Jinming Wang, Yong Sun, Weihao Yang, Tingting Niu, Jinyu Li, Carlos Fernandez, Jean-Jacques Gaumet, Qiuming Peng
description:
d, “LCSM” originally appeared as “CLSM” and in the Fig. 5b caption, “MgCl2, MgO, and Mg0” originally appeared as “MgCl2, MgO, and MgO.” The text is amended in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

title: Correction: NRF2 signaling plays an essential role in cancer progression through the NRF2-GPX2-NOTCH3 axis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
creator: Xiaoye Jin, Xiayuan Lou, Haoxiang Qi, Chao Zheng, Bo Li, Xuerong Siwu, Ren Liu, Qiaoli Lv, An Zhao, Jian Ruan, Ming Jiang
description: an incorrect representative Transwell invasion image was inadvertently used for the sgCtrl group in Figure 2F during figure preparation. We have replaced the incorrect image in Figure 2F with the correct representative image from the original experiment, as shown below.

title: Development of a one-step multiplex RT-qPCR method for rapid detection of bovine diarrhea viruses
creator: Dequan Yang, Li Ma, Zhongping Yang, Xianchao Yang, Jian Wang, Houbin Ju, Chunguang Lu, Yonggang Weng, Heping Zhao, Haixiao Shen, Xin Li, Feifei Ge, Xiaoxu Wang, Xiujuan Wu, Meng Xiang, Guidan Feng, Congsheng Tang, Shixin Huang, Hongjin Zhao
description: IntroductionViral calf diarrhea poses a significant challenge to the cattle industry worldwide due to its high morbidity and mortality rates, leading to substantial economic losses. The clinical symptoms associated with various diarrhea pathogens often overlap, complicating accurate diagnosis; thus, there is an urgent need for rapid and precise diagnostic methods to improve prevention and treatment efforts.

title: Towards advanced motion control systems for micro-scale magnetic drillers inside viscoelastic media
creator: Emmett Z. Freeman, Pranjal Chatterjee, Tony H. Wang, Kimberly Hoang, Azadeh Ansari
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microrobotic systems have the potential to reach regions of the body with significantly less invasiveness than conventional surgical tools. However, control over clinically relevant workspaces remains challenging due to limitations in magnetic field and robotic trajectory control. Here, we present a planar eight-solenoid magnetic field generator (MFG) that enables programmable velocity and heading of a 250 × 250 × 1250 µm3 microscale driller through continuous field reorientation within a workspace of 20 × 20 × 20 cm3.

title: A fabrication-aware vectorized generative representation for topology optimization of path-defined MEMS microstructures
creator: Gong-Zeng Liu, Lin-Feng Zhao, Jie Zhang, Xiang Liu, Yi-Meng Lv, Tian-Yu Geng, Zai-Fa Zhou
description: This work proposes a vectorized generative representation for fabrication-aware heuristic topology optimization of path-defined MEMS microstructures, addressing the trade-off between topological freedom and fabrication feasibility in MEMS inverse design. Pixel-level topology descriptions provide high design freedom and often require additional constraints to suppress disconnected or fabrication-incompatible layouts.

title: Emerging novel methodologies to understand and strategically target long-lived plasma cells in vaccine design to induce durable immunity
creator: Gina Cusimano, Ryan P. Staupe, Nicole L. Sullivan
description: Long-lived plasma cells (LLPCs) are a subset of antibody secreting cells (ASCs) that reside within lymphoid tissues, including the bone marrow (BM) and gut associated lymphoid tissues (GALT), and can secrete antigen-specific antibodies for up to decades or longer. Due to these traits, LLPCs serve as a crucial mediator for durable protective immunity.

title: Spinal subependymoma mimicking an intradural extramedullary tumor: illustrative case
creator: Toshiaki Inomo, Toshiki Fukuoka, Masahito Hara, Ryuya Maejima, Risa Oishi, Koji Osuka, Tadashi Watanabe
description: BACKGROUNDSpinal subependymomas are rare, benign tumors that typically arise within the spinal cord and usually appear as intramedullary lesions on MRI. The authors report a rare case of cervical spinal subependymoma with exophytic growth that mimicked an intradural extramedullary tumor on MRI.OBSERVATIONSA 53-year-old man presented with right-sided paresthesia. MRI revealed a spinal tumor causing marked spinal cord compression.

title: Spinal intradural arachnoid cyst in an infant with motor developmental delay showing intraoperative MEP improvement: illustrative case
creator: Ayako Toda, Kenichiro Nagai, Yoshitomo Suzuki, Yuka Matsumoto, Hiroto Sasaki, Toshiaki Hayashi, Masazumi Fujii
description: BACKGROUNDSpinal intradural arachnoid cysts (SIACs) are relatively rare, but they can cause neurological symptoms. The authors report a case of an infant with an SIAC presenting with motor developmental delay, highlighting the intraoperative improvement of motor evoked potentials (MEPs).OBSERVATIONSA 14-month-old girl presented with a lower limb motor developmental delay.

title: Effects of Ferulic Acid on Meat Quality, Carcass Traits, Muscle Fiber Types, and Muscle Development in Shaziling Pigs
creator: Xiwen Zhang, Shuning Jin, Chenghuan Hu, Qi Luo, Yulian Li, Jianhua He, Yurong Zhao
description: The mechanisms by which ferulic acid (FA) improves meat quality and promotes muscle development in pigs remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of dietary FA on meat quality and muscle development in Shaziling pigs. A total of 108 pigs (30 kg ± 0.

title: Characterizing Behavioral Engagement in Smartphone Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Hilary Weingarden, Geneva K Jonathan, Susanne S Hoeppner, Sara Velazquez, Ryan J Jacoby, Jennifer L Greenberg, Oliver Harrison, Sabine Wilhelm
description: BackgroundDigital mental health interventions (DMHIs) are increasingly popular for their ability to disseminate evidence-based treatments in a scalable, accessible way. Engagement with digital treatments is critical for effectiveness but remains poorly defined and measured. Most studies rely on subjective self-reports or 1 or 2 objective metrics, overlooking the multidimensional nature of how users interact with DMHIs.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Rara Merinda Puspitasari, Zaswiza Mohamad Noor, Didik Setiawan, Norkasihan Ibrahim
description: BackgroundInsomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia.

title: Editorial: Multilevel medical security systems and big data in healthcare: trends and developments
creator: Fei Fan, Siqin Wang
description: ability, which calls for the development of multilevel medical security systems. The construction of multilevel medical security systems requires the support of a large amount of statistical data. The development of big data makes the collection and analysis of those necessary statistics possible and makes breakthroughs in health economics.

title: Early postnatal changes in thyroid-stimulating hormone and subsequent neurodevelopment in preterm infants
creator: Myoung-Jin Yoo, Yong Hun Jang, Gang-Yi Lee, Habyeong Kang, Dong Hye Ye, Woochang Hwang, Seung Yang, Hyun Ju Lee
description: IntroductionThyroid hormones are crucial for brain maturation during late gestation and early infancy. In preterm infants, immaturity of the hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid axis often leads to transient or delayed dysfunctions undetected by standard newborn screening. As these atypical thyroid patterns have been associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes, serial assessments are warranted to better characterize risk.

title: Exploring Dystrophin Expression and Mutations in the DMD and Dystrophin-Glycoprotein Complex Genes as Prognostic Factors in Leiomyosarcomas
creator: Juliana Salazar, Paula Cerdà, Alícia Artigas, Ruth Orellana, Allan González, Raúl Terés, María J. Arranz, Silvia Bagué, Caterina Fumagalli, José Antonio González, Ana Peiró, Lidia González-Quereda, María José Rodríguez, Eduard Gallardo, María Aguado, Ana Sebio
description: Molecular factors influencing prognosis in leiomyosarcomas (LMS) remain poorly understood. Given that LMS arise from smooth muscle and that the dystrophin gene (DMD) has been suggested as a tumor suppressor in this tumor type, this study investigated dystrophin expression and somatic mutations in DMD, and dystrophin–glycoprotein complex (DGC) and dysferlin (DYSF) coding genes as prognostic biomarkers in LMS.

title: Nanoscale Buried Interface Control in Silicone Hydrogels Enables a Biointerface Engineering Platform
creator: Po‐Hsiang Chen, Jia‐Hua Wang, Ching Chen, Shih‐Hsuan Fu, Rajan Deepan Chakravarthy, Hsin‐Chieh Lin
description: Engineering multifunctional biointerfaces requires quantitative understanding of how buried nanoscale coating architectures govern biological function, yet such relationships remain inaccessible because non‐destructive characterization of soft, curved interfaces is lacking. Here, we establish an integrated engineering–characterization–function platform that quantitatively resolves buried nanocoatings and directly correlates their architecture with interfacial performance.

title: Case Report: A concomitant case of eosinophilic granuloma of the spine and Fasciola hepatica infection of the liver in a young patient, and review of the literature
creator: Jinri Zhang, Haoxian Li, Yingcong Wu, Dinghao Zhang, Chuhai Xie, Long Ling, Hailan Hu, Qi Liu
description: Eosinophilic granuloma (EG) is a benign osteolytic bone lesion and is a localized form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, most commonly involving the skeletal system. EG is a rare tumor, and involvement of the spine is low. Fascioliasis is a zoonotic disease caused by Fasciola species. The concomitant occurrence of EG and Fasciola hepatica infection is very rare.

title: Dissection of the genetic basis and molecular mechanism of ovule number per ovary in oilseed rape (Brassica napus L.)
creator: Muslim Qadir, Xinyi Lin, Farhan Nabi, Kishore Kumar Ashok, Xue-Rong Zhou, Qingbin Sun, Peiman Shi, Xinfa Wang, Jiaqin Shi, Hanzhong Wang
description: Ovule number per ovary (ONPO) determines the maximum potential of seed number per fruit that is a direct component of seed yield in crops. This study aimed to dissect the genetic basis and molecular mechanism of ONPO using a newly developed doubled haploid (DH) population in oilseed rape.

title: Age- and Sex-Specific Reference Intervals for TSH, FT4, and FT3 Derived from the Turkish Multi-Center Cohort
creator: Gülce Kiren, Gizem Yılmaz Çalık, Merve Güngören, Hikmet Can Çubukçu
