description: We developed Macular, a simulation platform with a graphical interface, designed to produce in silico experiment scenarios for the retina and the primary visual system. A scenario involves generating a three-dimensional structure with interconnected layers, each layer corresponding to a type of “cell” in the retina or visual cortex.

title: A Maltese Study in Determining the Presence of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Metabolic Syndrome
creator: Jonathan Gauci, Stephanie Gauci Pullicino, Emma Caruana, Vanessa Petroni Magri, Melissa M Formosa, Anthony G Fenech, Stephen Fava, Stephen Montefort, Peter Fsadni
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionBoth Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) and Metabolic Syndrome (MetS) are pro-inflammatory states, and while the diagnosis of MetS in COPD has been extensively studied, the diagnosis of COPD in MetS is poorly studied.

title: Gut colonization and subsequent infection of neonates caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae
creator: Verónica Jiménez-Rojas, Dina Villanueva-García, Ana Luisa Miranda-Vega, Rubén Aldana-Vergara, Pamela Aguilar-Rodea, Beatriz López-Marceliano, Alfonso Reyes-López, María Dolores Alcántar-Curiel
description: The gut microbiota harbors diverse bacteria considered reservoirs for antimicrobial resistance genes. The global emergence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-PE) significantly contributes to healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). We investigated the presence of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-PEco) and ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (ESBL-PKpn) in neonatal patients’ guts.

title: Surgical Treatment of Tumor‐Induced Osteomalacia With Causative Tumors Affecting the Long Bones
creator: Shuzhong Liu, Jinyi Xing, An Song, Mingjing Zhang, Jin Jin, Xi Zhou, Yong Liu, Weibo Xia
description: BackgroundThe causative tumor for tumor‐induced osteomalacia (TIO) locating in the long bone is hidden and has diverse locations, resulting in great challenges to orthopedists. This study aimed to investigate and summarize the clinical features and surgical outcomes of TIO patients with culprit tumors involving the long bones to enhance clinical understanding and improve orthopedic surgical management of this rare disease.

title: Use of Heat for the Self-Management of Non-Specific Neck Pain: A Systematic Review
creator: Denise Wilfling, Ahmad El-Allawy, Cathleen Muche-Borowski, Thomas Kötter
description: PurposeThis systematic review aimed to summarise the evidence on the effectiveness of heat therapy for the treatment of non-specific neck pain, one of the most frequently reported musculoskeletal conditions.Materials and MethodsThis review followed established methodological guidelines for systematic reviews. A computerised literature search was conducted in Medline via PubMed in January 2025 using the key terms “neck pain” and “heat”.

title: Integrative analyses of morpho-physiological, biochemical, and transcriptomic reveal the seedling growth response of Pinus yunnanensis to nitrogen and phosphorus fertilization
creator: Junfei Xu, Xiyan Li, Shi Chen, Lin Chen, Junrong Tang, Peizhen Chen, Nianhui Cai, Yulan Xu
description: Appropriate nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) fertilization is critical for plant growth and production. Pinus yunnanensis, a silvicultural tree in southwestern China, faces economic and ecological limitations due to nutrient deficiency in the soils in its distribution areas. The slow growth of this species during the seedling stage exacerbates these problems.

title: Cell-Based Regenerative Strategies for Knee Cartilage Repair: A Scoping Review of Autologous Cartilage, Mesenchymal Stromal Cells, and Hybrid Approaches
creator: Birzhan Suiindik, Kazybek Baktybergen, Yerik Raimagambetov, Gulzhanat Korganbekova, Dina Saginova, Arman Batpen, Karlygash Suiindik
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCell-based approaches for focal knee cartilage repair include cartilage- and chondrocyte-based procedures, mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC)-based strategies, and combinations of these approaches. However, the amount and type of evidence available for these treatments differ considerably.ObjectiveTo map the clinical and preclinical evidence for cell-based regenerative strategies used for focal chondral and osteochondral defects of the knee, compare cartilage-based, MSC-based, and hybrid approaches, and identify areas where evidence remains limited.MethodsThis scoping review was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework and reported according to

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Serum Creatinine-Defined Acute Kidney Injury in Older Adults After Cardiac Surgery
creator: Yuhao Fu, Jiajie Qian, Yang Zhang, Fuhai Ji
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is a frequent and devastating postoperative complication, particularly among older adults. Accurate risk stratification and early prediction of CSA-AKI are essential for guiding preventive strategies and optimizing clinical decision-making.MethodsIn this retrospective study, data from two centers (n=623) were utilized for model training and internal validation, whereas data from a third, distinct center (n=110) were reserved for external validation. CSA-AKI was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Serum creatinine criteria.

title: METTL3-Mediated m6A Modification of lncRNA-0949 Drives Microglial Inflammation in an vitro Model of Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
creator: Xing Zeng, Xiao-Juan Luo, Zhen-Ze Zhang, Jia-Li Lu, Yi-An Zhan
description: IntroductionSepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe complication of sepsis with limited therapeutic options. Although neuroinflammation driven by microglial activation is central to SAE pathogenesis, the underlying epitranscriptional regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the role of the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 in regulating microglial inflammation using lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated HMO6 microglial cells as an in vitro SAE model.

title: A Feasible 1H‐NMR Quantification Method of Indicator Compounds in Microwave‐Processed Reynoutria multiflora Radix and Its Decoction
creator: Hao-Ze Li, Hong Nhung Phan, Zih-Hong Jhang, Guo-Fen Chen, Mei-Lin Yang, Tian-Shung Wu, Ping-Chung Kuo, Sohini Basu Roy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke is a commonly used herbal drug in traditional Chinese medicine. Prior literature has indicated that R. multiflora possesses broadband pharmacological activities. According to Taiwan Herbal Pharmacopeia (IV) and previous reports, the dominant components of R. multiflora were 2,3,5,4′‐tetrahydroxystilbene‐2‐O‐β‐D‐glucopyranoside (THSG) (1) and free anthraquinones such as emodin (2), physcion (3), and rhein (4), which played pivotal roles in the pharmacological effects of herbs.

title: From Hospital to Home: Enhancing Family Support with MIGYN (Mitra Interaktif Ginekologi), an AI-Based Discharge Planning Chatbot
creator: Ida Maryati, Ermiati Ermiati, Windy Natasya, Anisa Hasanah, Novi Irmala, Santi Susanti, Atikah Atikah, Dyana Eka Fuzi Yulianti, Khatijah Lim Abdullah
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPostoperative gynecological patients often experience challenges during the transition from hospital to home due to suboptimal discharge planning. Family involvement plays an important role in supporting postoperative recovery; however, caregiver support and education are frequently unstructured and inconsistent.ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of MIGYN (Mitra Interaktif Ginekologi), a family-based interactive chatbot, in improving family support and caregiver knowledge among postoperative gynecological patients.MethodsA quasi-experimental pre–post test study was conducted involving 34 caregivers of postoperative gynecological patients at Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung.

title: Medicaid claims alone have high sensitivity but low specificity in identifying child abuse and neglect
creator: Jessica Pac, Sherry Glied, Renata Howland, Jane Waldfogel
description: ObjectivesDecision support tools, such as predictive risk models (PRMs), may assist medical personnel identify child abuse and neglect (CAN). However, no prior work has established whether Medicaid claims alone are sufficient for accurate prediction. We developed a Medicaid claims-based PRM to predict CAN, validating against medical encounters and clinical diagnoses that precede and follow a CAN-related diagnosis code.

title: Mitochondrial transfer - a novel promising approach for the treatment of metabolic diseases
creator: Ruijing Chen, Jun Chen
description: Metabolic disorders remain a major global health concern in the 21st century, with increasing incidence and prevalence. Mitochondria play a critical role in cellular energy production, calcium homeostasis, signal transduction, and apoptosis. Under physiological conditions, mitochondrial transfer plays a crucial role in tissue homeostasis and development. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been implicated in the pathogenesis of metabolic disorders.

title: Post‐Fabrication Phase Correction of SOI 4 × 4 MMI‐Based 90° Optical Hybrids via Femtosecond‐Laser Trimming
creator: Jia Du, Xiongping Bao, Jintian Lin, Xiao Chen, Wenbing Jiang, Boyu Zhang, Yiti Xiong, Wenjun Li, Libing Zhou
description: Integrated 90° optical hybrids are essential passive components in coherent receivers, yet their quadrature accuracy and power balance are highly susceptible to fabrication‐induced deviations. Here, we demonstrate postfabrication phase trimming of silicon‐on‐insulator 4 × 4 multimode‐interference‐based 90° optical hybrids using localized femtosecond‐laser modification.

title: Stand-Alone Carboxytherapy Followed by Consolidation with Oral Hydrolyzed Marine Collagen Fragments: A Potential Sequential Bioregenerative Strategy for Hypertrophic Scars: A Case Report
creator: Nadia Fraone, Gloria Trocchi, Emanuele Bartoletti, Myriam Di Castro, Federica Lo Re, Mauro Raichi
description: IntroductionCarboxytherapy, via the Bohr effect, a denser dermal environment, and preserved fibroblast function, along with oral administration of bioactive marine collagen fragments that target fibroblasts, are regenerative strategies that could improve scar elasticity, thickness, and hydration. Their sequential combination might be an innovative approach.

title: Antiviral therapy can effectively suppress irAEs in HBV positive hepatocellular carcinoma treated with ICIs: validation based on multi machine learning
creator: Shuxian Pan, Zibing Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitors have proven efficacy against hepatitis B-virus positive hepatocellular. However, Immunotherapy-related adverse reactions are still a major challenge faced by tumor immunotherapy, so it is urgent to establish new methods to effectively predict immunotherapy-related adverse reactions.ObjectiveMulti-machine learning model were constructed to screen the risk factors for irAEs in ICIs for the treatment of HBV-related hepatocellular and build a prediction model for the occurrence of clinical IRAEs.MethodsData from 274 hepatitis B virus positive tumor patients who received PD-1 or/and CTLA4 inhibitor

title: The anti-biofilm compound 4-ethoxybenzoic acid inhibits Staphylococcus aureus virulence factor production via a putative 4EB-binding pocket in key virulence-associated proteins
creator: Caroline C. Taylor, Adonis Aviles-Gonzalez, Alexander Marchesani, Christina Kiessling, Travis Patrick, Linxin Chen, Haozhe Yao, Zixuan Li, Abbie Seward, Kuk-Jeong Chin, Eric S. Gilbert
description: There is a need for dual action anti-virulence and anti-biofilm agents that target the opportunistic pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Previous research determined that 0.8 mg/mL 4-ethoxybenzoic acid (4EB) reduced S. aureus ATCC 6538 biofilm formation by 88% relative to untreated controls with moderate inhibition of planktonic cell growth. Here we report that 4EB impacted S.

title: Same Genes, Different Wings: Wing Shape Divergence Among Castes in a Social Wasp
creator: Kayla A Murray, Sarah E Orr, Michael A D Goodisman, Emma L Gosse, Rachel Hill, Jennifer L Kovacs
description: Wings play a central role in shaping dispersal, behavior, and ecological specialization of insects. In social insects, distinct castes with specialized morphologies arise from a shared genome, raising the question of how divergence of traits, such as wings, occurs despite genetic constraints.

title: Helicobacter pylori contributes to GC progression, possibly via the MSTRG.10627.1/miR-142-5p/ADAMTS5 pathway
creator: Zhipeng Yin, Jianwei Xiang, Pengbo Guo, Nianli Zhang, Xiaoqian Lv, Yu Wang, Yi Wu, Nianhua Zhang, Gang Lv, Yinghui Zhao
description: BackgroundHelicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a class I carcinogen that induces gastric cancer (GC). The mechanisms underlying its induction of GC are not fully understood. The role of the MSTRG.10627.1/miR-142-5p/ADAMTS5 pathway induced by H. pylori in GC was investigated in this study.MethodsRNA sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to screen a regulatory pathway lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA.

title: BCL6 in T cells promotes type 1 diabetes by redirecting fates of insulin-autoreactive B lymphocytes
creator: Landon M Clark, Jack C McAninch, Dudley H McNitt, Marguerite L Padgett, Tyler W Jenkins, Lindsay E Bass, Casey M Nichols, Jeffrey C Rathmell, Rachel H Bonami
description: SummaryCurrently approved immunotherapies for type 1 diabetes (T1D) broadly target T cells and delay, but do not fully prevent, diabetes development, highlighting the need for more selective targets. Here, we show that T cell loss of the key germinal center protein, BCL6 prevents diabetes, despite the continued presence of anti-insulin B cells.

title: Knowledge, Perception, and Intention to Promote Malaria Vaccination Among Students in Southwestern Nigeria: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: James Success Odubia, Majani Edward
description: IntroductionMalaria remains a major public health burden in Nigeria, and the introduction of malaria vaccines offers a promising strategy for reducing morbidity and mortality. This study assessed knowledge, perception, and intention to promote malaria vaccination among health technology students in Southwestern Nigeria.MethodsA cross‐sectional study was conducted from November to December 2025 among 300 students using a structured questionnaire.

title: Prevalence of depression and anxiety among elderly primary care patients in Palestine
creator: Beesan Nader Maraqa, Zaher Nazzal, Suha Hamshari, Barlant Alutt, Ekram Rishmawi, Abdallah Qawasmeh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and objectivesDepression and anxiety are common mental health disorders among the elderly worldwide. In this study, we estimated the prevalence of depression and anxiety and related risk factor among elderly attending Primary Health care (PHC) centers in Palestine.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted from February to July 2021 with a sample size of 380 participants aged ≥60 attending PHC centers in West Bank, using an interviewer-administered questionnaire.

title: Mental Health, Sleep, and Physical Activity Among Young Saudi Women During Ramadan: A Comparative Cohort Study
creator: Karthick Balasubramanian, Ramya Ramasamy Sanjeevi, Mohammed M Alshehri, Shaima A Alothman
description: PurposeThis study investigated mental health outcomes of young adult women in relation to physical activity and sleep patterns before, during, and after Ramadan.Participants and MethodsA prospective repeated-measures cohort study was conducted in the Department of Physical Therapy at Jazan University, Saudi Arabia.

title: Inhibition of histone deacetylase in Arabidopsis root calli promotes de novo shoot organogenesis
creator: Qinwei Pan, Ruirui Huang, Qiong Xiao, Xuting Wu, Baoxia Jian, Yanan Xiang, Lijun Gan, Zongrang Liu, Yi Li, Tingting Gu, Huawei Liu
description: De novo organogenesis from somatic cells to the entire plant represents a remarkable biological phenomenon, but the underlying regulatory mechanism, particularly at the epigenetic level, remains obscure. In this work, we demonstrate the important role of histone deacetylases (HDACs) in shoot organogenesis.

title: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Recurrence Patterns of Olfactory Neuroblastoma: A 15‐Year Tertiary Center Case Series
creator: Mohsen Naraghi, Maryam Lotfi, Lindelwa Phakamile Mmema, Jazmin Kazravan, Amirhossein Babaei, Rong-San Jiang
description: ObjectivesOlfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) is a rare malignant tumor of the sinonasal tract with heterogeneous clinical behavior and recurrence potential. Due to its low incidence, prognostic factors and optimal treatment strategies remain incompletely defined. The objective of this study was to describe the clinicopathological characteristics, treatment approaches, and recurrence patterns of ONB over a 15‐year period at a tertiary referral center.

title: Historic and future spending estimates of maternal health and family planning in 139 low- and middle-income countries, 2000–2030: a modelling study
creator: Angela E Apeagyei, Hans Elliott, Golsum Tsakalos, Joseph L Dieleman
description: IntroductionWhile estimates of donor-provided resources for maternal health and family planning are readily available, government and household spending on these activities is limited. This study aims to generate comprehensive estimates of spending on maternal health and family planning for 139 low- and middle-income countries.

title: Thyroid-reproductive axis interplay: immunological mechanisms and implications for female reproductive health
creator: Sisi Chen, Shahid Ullah Khan, Safir Ullah Khan, Mohammed Alissa, Essam H. Ibrahim, Saleem Ahmad, Ramadan Taha, Kun Zhou
description: Thyroid dysfunction is a common endocrine disease among women of childbearing age, which seriously affects reproductive health. From an immunological perspective, this in-depth analysis clarifies the complex relationship between thyroid function and female reproduction. We studied the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis regulation by thyroid hormones through direct and indirect mechanisms, including metabolic mediators such as prolactin and leptin.

title: Managing inappropriate sexual behaviour in people with dementia
creator: Natasha E Lane, Dallas Seitz, Jennifer A Watt
description: iours, which can cause substantial distress for patients, families, and staff, but stigma and uncertainty about management can result in under-reporting. 1 Roughly 15% of reported cases occur among females.2 Not all sexual expression in people with dementia is inappropriate Appropriateness of sexual behaviours is subjective and often specific to the setting or caregiver.

title: Care-seeking among hepatocellular carcinoma patients in Uganda: health system navigation and its impact on diagnosis and survival in a prospective case-cohort study
creator: Sara K Nsibirwa, Katuku J Aizire, Fred Okuku, Emmanuel Ochola, Amir M Mohareb, Ponsiano Ocama, Gregory D Kirk
description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients are often diagnosed with advanced-stage disease. We aimed to identify care-seeking patterns, assess correlates of earlier diagnosis and determine the impact of diagnostic delay on mortality among HCC patients.MethodsCross-sectional study, enrolled (March 2015 to August 2020), HCC patients in three Ugandan tertiary care hospitals.

title: In vitro exploration of drug-induced thrombotic microangiopathies: clues of diverse endothelial activation pathways respective to interferon-β1a, ciclosporin A, and gemcitabine exposure
creator: Edouard Cubilier, Maxime Taghavi, Eric De Prez, Lucas Jacobs, Sébastien Sinaeve, Joëlle Nortier, Marie-Hélène Antoine
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pro-inflammatory and pro-thrombotic stimuli can activate endothelial cells (ECs) and predispose them to thrombotic microangiopathies (TMAs). Drug-induced TMA (DITMA) may occur in clinical practice during treatment with interferon-β1a (IFN-β1a), ciclosporin A (CsA), and gemcitabine (GEM). DITMA may also trigger the complement system and induce membrane attack complex (MAC, C5b-9) deposition in vivo, although their role and the benefit of inhibition remain unclear.

title: Enhanced photodynamic therapy through multienzyme-like MOF for cancer treatment
creator: Letian Lv, Zhao Fu, Qing You, Wei Xiao, Huayi Wang, Chen Wang, Yanlian Yang
description: Overcoming resistance to apoptosis is a major challenge in cancer therapy. Recent research has shown that manipulating mitochondria, the organelles critical for energy metabolism in tumor cells, can increase the effectiveness of photodynamic therapy and trigger apoptosis in tumor cells.

title: Spirituality and mental health – investigating the association between spiritual attitudes and psychosomatic treatment outcomes
creator: Thilo Hinterberger, Nike Walter
description: BackgroundThe relationship between spirituality and mental health has garnered attention, fostering overall well-being. Spirituality, posited as a protective factor, may enhance resilience and provide meaning, thus benefiting mental health. This study aims to identify spirituality-associated factors influencing clinical outcomes in psychosomatic inpatients and validate the Transpersonal Spirituality Inventory (TSI).

title: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis Thought to Be due to Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease Treated With Ruxolitinib: A Case Report
creator: Emily Vachon, Heena Birbal Jain, Suzanna Kitten, Nikhat Kaura
description: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a life‐threatening, systemic inflammatory syndrome. Cases without an identifiable acquired trigger are referred to as secondary HLH. In this report, we describe the case of a 24 year‐old woman whose underlying cause of HLH was particularly difficult to determine.

title: Provenance-specific responses to climatic mismatch in Betula ermanii Cham. and implications for climate adaptation
creator: Aye Myat Myat Paing, Takaki Aihara, Yoshihiko Tsumura, Mitsuru Hirota, Toshiya Yoshida, Kosuke Homma, Hajime Kobayashi, Atsuhiro Iio, Nobuhiro Tomaru, Dai Nagamatsu, Masahiro Takagi, Ikutaro Tsuyama, Yoko Hisamoto, Haruhiko Taneda, Susumu Goto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Climate change is expected to alter the growth and survival of forest trees, but the magnitude and direction of these effects remain uncertain at the intraspecific level, particularly across provenances adapted to contrasting climatic conditions. For Betula ermanii Cham., a dominant deciduous tree in cool-temperate and subalpine forests of Japan, it remains unclear how climatic mismatches between provenance origin and planting environment influence early-life performance.

title: Occupational Specific Heavy Metal Exposure: Association With Age and Anthropometric Characteristics Relative to Hypertension
creator: Godwin Chinedu Uzomba, Collins Nwafor, Chibuike Ugah, Henry Ogbodo, Chukwuka Amaku, Ken Onwe, Tamuno-Ibelema Cookey-Gam, Godwin Sunday Obaje, Ejikeme Mbajiorgu, Franco Veglio
description: The present study aimed at investigating the association between serum heavy metals, anthropometric characteristics, and hypertension among different occupations and analyzing the prediction between heavy metals, anthropometrics, and hypertension among male and female miners, artisans, laborers, and farmers. Body weight, height, and circumferences were measured via the direct standard anthropometric approach.

title: A Cost-per-Responder Analysis of Ritlecitinib vs Baricitinib in Severe Alopecia Areata
creator: Ashley S. Cha-Silva, Kate H. Zhang, Christopher N. Graham, Samantha K. Kurosky, Helen Tran, Ernest H. Law, Eingun J. Song
description: BackgroundRitlecitinib, a JAK3/TEC family kinase inhibitor, and baricitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, are approved for treating severe alopecia areata (AA).ObjectiveDevelop a cost-per-responder analysis for ritlecitinib and baricitinib for treating severe AA to estimate the budget impact based on clinical efficacy, available dosages, and pricing structure.

title: A telomere-related signature for predicting prognosis and assessing immune microenvironment in osteosarcoma
creator: Shihao Li, Lina Zhang, Haiyang Zhang
description: ObjectiveOsteosarcoma is the most common primary bone cancer with a high propensity for local invasion and metastasis. An increasing number of research studies show that telomeres play an important role in the occurrence and development of cancer. Thus, we established a telomere-related signature in osteosarcoma to comprehensively evaluate the pathogenic roles of telomeres in this disease.

title: Liquid application dosing alters the physiology of air-liquid interface (ALI) primary human bronchial epithelial cell/lung fibroblast co-cultures and in vitro testing relevant endpoints
creator: Nicholas M. Mallek, Elizabeth M. Martin, Lisa A. Dailey, Shaun D. McCullough
description: Differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cell (dpHBEC) cultures grown under air-liquid interface (ALI) conditions exhibit key features of the human respiratory tract and are thus critical for respiratory research as well as efficacy and toxicity testing of inhaled substances (e.g., consumer products, industrial chemicals, and pharmaceuticals). Many inhalable substances (e.g.

title: Hypothesis‐Generating Single‐Cell Analysis of the Endometrial Cancer Immune Microenvironment With Complementary Multiomics Evidence
creator: Xiaolan Ouyang, Xiaoli Guo, Xiaoxi Yang, Juan Wen
description: BackgroundEndometrial cancer (EC) has a heterogeneous immune microenvironment, and response‐associated biology remains incompletely characterized. We used the retained EC single‐cell dataset to describe immune‐cell states and complemented it with TCGA‐UCEC, independent gut microbiome cohorts, and RL95‐2 proof‐of‐concept experiments. All responder versus nonresponder scRNA‐seq comparisons are descriptive and hypothesis generating because only one sample was available per clinical response group.

title: Healing and trauma services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people: a scoping review
creator: Isabella Freijah, Rebekah Julian, Kelsey Madden, Kimberley A Jones, Amanda Jones, Helen Kennedy, Nina Levin, Shantai Croisdale, Catherine Chamberlain
description: ObjectiveColonisation and oppression of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have resulted in intergenerational trauma and systemic health inequities, making culturally responsive, healing-informed approaches that uphold self-determination essential. This review aimed to identify and describe healing services for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people affected by trauma, violence or abuse.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Features as Predictors of Response and Prognosis Following Neoadjuvant Therapy in Rectal Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Jinhua Deng, Sijing Cheng, Shujuan Li, Yujie Hou
description: BackgroundMRI-detected circumferential resection margin (CRM) involvement, extramural venous invasion (EMVI), and tumor deposits (TDs) are established high-risk features associated with poor prognosis in rectal cancer. These features may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from neoadjuvant therapy (NAT). However, the prognostic significance of changes in these MRI high-risk features after NAT remains unclear.

title: Animal models for investigating post‐stroke cognitive impairment: A neurovascular trafficking perspective
creator: Pratchaya Kaewkaen
description: Post‐stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major cause of long‐term disability after ischemic stroke, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely explained by infarct volume, lesion location, or conventional vascular risk factors alone. Animal models are indispensable for clarifying how ischemic injury evolves into delayed cognitive dysfunction and for determining which mechanisms are experimentally tractable, reproducible, and translationally relevant.

title: Enhancing Named Entity Recognition for immunology and immune-mediated disorders
creator: Songyue Chen, Jinshan Che, Mingming Sun, Yuhong Wang
description: IntroductionNamed Entity Recognition (NER) in the biomedical domain, particularly within immunology and immune-mediated disorders, presents unique challenges due to the presence of complex, nested, and overlapping entities. Existing NER systems often struggle with the specialized terminologies and contextual ambiguity of immunological texts, which limits their effectiveness in downstream biomedical applications.

title: Plasma IL-17A is increased in patients with critical MIS-C and associated to in-hospital mortality
creator: Emmerson C. F. de Farias, Luciana M. P. P. do Nascimento, Manoel J. C. Pavão Junior, Dalila C. A. Pavão, Ana P. S. Pinheiro, Andreza H. O. Pinheiro, Marília C. B. Alves, Kíssila M. M. M. Ferraro, Larisse F. Q. Aires, Luana G. Dias, Mayara M. M. Machado, Michaelle J. D. Serrão, Raphaella R. Gomes, Sa
description: BackgroundMultisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a rare and severe post-COVID-19 complication with multiple phenotypes.ObjectivesThe aim of this study is to study inflammatory biomarkers (cytokines and oxidative stress) in critical MIS-C patients and to observe if there is association between these biomarkers and mortality.

title: Distinct Clinicogenomic Contexts of BRAF‐Altered Gliomas and Glioneuronal Tumors: A Nationwide Real‐World Study
creator: Seiji Yamada, Tetsuya Takimoto, Sayaka Ueno, Sachiko Minamiguchi, Shigeo Ohba, Yuichi Hirose, Hideyuki Saya, Tamotsu Sudo
description: BRAF alterations occur across diverse gliomas and glioneuronal tumors, but their alteration‐specific clinicogenomic contexts in real‐world cancer genomic profiling cohorts remain incompletely characterized. We analyzed BRAF‐altered brain tumors registered in the Japanese Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics database from June 2019 to March 2026. Operational diagnostic harmonization was performed using available clinicopathological and genomic information.

title: Progressing from Simple to Multidimensional Models Towards a Biopsychosocial Framework of Addiction
creator: Paul S Regier
description: Purpose of ReviewNeuroscientific models of addiction have evolved over the past four decades from single-circuit dopamine frameworks to dual-process, tripartite, and multidimensional accounts. Despite these advances, existing models incompletely account for the lived experience of addiction and for developmental, social, and mental-health factors that contribute to heterogeneity in risk and outcome.

title: Efficacy of empagliflozin in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with or without diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Khalid I. AlHussaini
description: BackgroundEmpagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, has demonstrated potential hepatic benefits in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), particularly among those with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy of empagliflozin on hepatic and metabolic outcomes in patients with MASLD.

title: Ziziphus jujube promotes fertility and pregnancy outcomes in Rat model of uterine adhesions
creator: Fereshteh Asgharzadeh, Mahsa Attarian, Majid Khazaei, Abdulridha Mohammed Al-Asady, Saeide Mansoori, Hamideh Naimi, Moein Eskandari, Azar Khorrami, Seyedeh Elnaz Nazari, Akram Aminian, Marjaneh Farazastanian, Elaheh Eshtad, Amir Avan, Mikhail Ryzhikov, Malihe Hasanzadeh, Seyed Mahdi Hassanian
description: IntroductionThe therapeutic efficacy of oral administration of Ziziphus jujube in the context of uterine adhesion (UA) and its impact on pregnancy outcomes was investigated.MethodsIn a rat UA model, Z. jujube was evaluated for its ability to mitigate injury-induced uterine adhesion bands, uterine shortening, and enhance endometrial regeneration.

title: National trends in dual de-escalation of axillary surgery and adjuvant radiation in early-stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer
creator: Dylan S Brokaw, Leonardo Kozian, Cecilia Chang, Rebecca M Shulman, Richard J Bleicher, Alycia So, Allison A Aggon, Austin D Williams
description: PurposeDe-escalation has become standard across breast cancer management. Many early-stage HR+/HER2-negative breast cancers are eligible for both SLNB omission and accelerated partial breast irradiation (APBI). However, the oncologic safety of dual de-escalation has not been evaluated except in patients ≥ 70 years. We sought to characterize national practice patterns and factors associated with adoption of this dual de-escalation approach.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of three surgical approaches for parathyroidectomy in secondary hyperparathyroidism patients
creator: Qila Sa, Yinghui Zhou, Guangming Cheng, Boyuan Nan, Yingnan Feng, Ningyuan Zhang, Wantao Xie, Wei Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThere are three main surgical treatment options for secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT): subtotal parathyroidectomy (sPTX), total parathyroidectomy with auto-transplantation (tPTX+AT), and total parathyroidectomy (tPTX). However, a debate regarding which of these surgical methods is optimal has been ongoing.

title: Harnessing mesenchymal stromal cells for liver disease therapy: from mechanistic discoveries to clinical breakthroughs
creator: Yiting Huang, Ruogu Cheng, Guaijuan Wang, Zihan Xu, Shuping Liu, Yantong Wan, Xinjiang Hou, Jieyan Wang
description: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) demonstrate significant potential in liver tissue regeneration and disease treatment due to their unique immunomodulatory properties, multipotent differentiation capabilities, and paracrine functions. This article provides a systematic review of MSCs’ biological characteristics and mechanistic roles in liver regeneration and summarizes recent clinical advancements and future challenges.

title: Comparison of data mining algorithms and regression method for prediction of live body weight using biometric traits of non-descript indigenous chickens
creator: Joas Albino Tsenane, Thabang Sako, Madumetja Cyril Mathapo, Thobela Louis Tyasi, Obert Tada
description: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between live body weight and biometric traits, and to estimate live body weight from biometric traits of non-descript indigenous chickens. A total of 400 non-descript indigenous chickens (113 males and 287 females) were randomly selected from a multi-stage purposive sampling procedure following a cross-sectional study design.

title: Gut dysbiosis and immune dysfunction induced by chronic cola replacement of water in rats: not just a sugar problem
creator: Huijie Gao, Wanru Li, Xin Wang, Yan Ren, Xiao Li, Chao Liu
description: ObjectiveExcessive sugar-sweetened beverage consumption like cola is a worldwide public health problem. However, the effects and mechanisms of replacing water with cola (either as sugar-free cola or sugar-sweetened cola) on intestinal microbiota and overall health remain unknown, prompting this investigation.MethodsTo address this, we created a new experimental model in which cola completely replaced drinking water.

title: Epidemiology, Histopathologic Patterns, and Clinical Characteristics of Gestational Trophoblastic Diseases in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis Study
creator: Abrham Tesfaye Habteyes, Fekadeselassie Teferi Mekonen, Ashebir TufaTelila
description: BackgroundGestational trophoblastic diseases (GTDs) are rare trophoblastic disorders that contribute substantially to maternal morbidity. However, the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of GTD‐related evidence from Ethiopia remain limited and scattered. Consequently, the national burden, histopathological distribution, and clinical presentation of GTD in Ethiopia are not well defined.

title: The impact of nature‐based education on neurodivergent adolescent mental health and wellbeing: A systematic scoping review
creator: Helen Eke, Suzie Holt, Helen Dodd, Faraz Mughal, Eleanor Shaw, Abigail Emma Russell
description: BackgroundAround 10% of young people have a diagnosed neurodevelopmental condition or consider themselves neurodivergent (brain function different to that considered typical). Neurodivergent young people (NYP) utilise health services more frequently than their peers and are at increased risk of mental health problems, school absenteeism and suspension.

title: DNA Nanotechnology-Enabled Precise Regulation of Nanozymes and Their Applications
creator: Zishuo Liu, Yuanbo Zhao, Haoxiang Chen, Xin Fu, Jinyue Fan, Lingyan Lu, Zhiwen Lyu, Honghui Cai, Ziming Wang, Chao Zhang, Fan Xiao, Yao Xiao
description: Nanozymes overcome key limitations of natural enzymes, including poor environmental tolerance, high production costs, and batch-to-batch variability, with their enhanced physicochemical stability and controllable catalytic performance, thus enabling applications in biocatalysis and disease theranostics. However, their practical applications remain limited by insufficient catalytic efficiency, inadequate target specificity, and restricted programmable dynamic adaptability.

title: Global Warming and Type 2 Diabetes: Sex and Gender as Drivers in a Multidimensional Feedback Loop
creator: Massimo D'Archivio, Giulia Zanchi, Alessia Tammaro, Roberta Masella, Claudia Cataldo
description: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a determinant of metabolic health. Emerging evidence indicates that rising temperatures impair glucose homeostasis—specifically through reduced brown adipose tissue activity and increased insulin resistance—thereby exacerbating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) risk. Concurrently, food systems drive substantial greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE), with gender‐differentiated dietary patterns uniquely influencing both environmental impact and health outcomes.

title: Effect of selenium nanoparticles on the quality and fertility of short-term preserved boar semen
creator: Dipan Rudra Paul, Dibyajyoti Talukdar, Fazal Ali Ahmed, K. Lalrintluanga, Girin Kalita, T. C. Tolenkhomba, Himsikha Chakravarty, Rahul Katiyar, Gautam Khargharia, Sourabh Deori
description: This study was carried out to investigate the effect of different concentrations of selenium nanoparticles (Se-NPs) in the Beltsville Thawing Solution (BTS) extender on the semen quality and fertility of Hampshire crossbred pigs. For the study, semen was collected from four boars (10 ejaculates/boar) by the gloved hand method.

title: Geospatial Analysis of Abortion Access for U.S. Servicewomen After Dobbs
creator: Lyna Cherikh, Sreeja Puthumana, Jessica Poulson, Katerina Shvartsman, Jill Brown, Mohamed Sallam
description: Servicewomen in abortion-restricted states have a significant geographic burden to access abortion care. Abortion access within the Military Health System is uniquely dictated by federal law. Under the Hyde Amendment, abortion is a covered health service only in cases of rape or incest or when the pregnant individual's life is endangered.

title: Black‐Tailed Godwits Eat Animal and Plant Material at a Key Non‐Breeding Site at the Overlap of Two Asian Flyways
creator: Delip K Das, Naim Khandakar, Md Soab Ali, Wouter M G Vansteelant, El‐Hacen M El‐Hacen, Theunis Piersma
description: Dietary knowledge of migratory birds along their migration routes is fundamental for understanding ecological and evolutionary aspects of bird migration, how migrants select and repeatedly use specific non‐breeding areas, accumulate fuel for migration and breeding, and assess carrying capacity at key sites in the migratory network.

title: Improvement of crop production in controlled environment agriculture through breeding
creator: Krishna Bhattarai, Andrew B. Ogden, Sudeep Pandey, Germán V. Sandoya, Ainong Shi, Amol N. Nankar, Murukarthick Jayakodi, Heqiang Huo, Tao Jiang, Pasquale Tripodi, Chris Dardick
description: Controlled environment agriculture (CEA) represents one of the fastest-growing sectors of horticulture. Production in controlled environments ranges from highly controlled indoor environments with 100% artificial lighting (vertical farms or plant factories) to high-tech greenhouses with or without supplemental lighting, to simpler greenhouses and high tunnels.

title: Decoding the neural dynamics of everyday prospective remembering: a hidden Markov model approach
creator: Stefano Vicentin, Davide Buzzi Reschini, Paola Santacesaria, Lisa Toffoli, Sara Zago, Giorgio Arcara, Giorgia Cona
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionProspective memory (PM)—the ability to form, maintain, and execute delayed intentions—is essential for everyday functioning. Traditionally, PM paradigms relied on repetitive tasks and focused on transient post-stimulus activity, overlooking the sustained neural processes supporting intention maintenance.MethodsHigh-density EEG data were recorded during a naturalistic PM paradigm simulating everyday activities (preparing a meal while watching TV), comprising three conditions: naturalistic viewing, event-based PM, and time-based PM.

title: Treatment decision for recurrences in non-small cell lung cancer during or after adjuvant osimertinib: an international Delphi consensus report
creator: Myriam Mirza, Aseem Shrivastava, Cecile Matthews, Natasha Leighl, Calvin S. H. Ng, David Planchard, Sanjay Popat, Julia Rotow, Egbert F. Smit, Ross Soo, Masahiro Tsuboi, Fan Yang, Brendon Stiles, Christian Grohe, Yi-Long Wu
description: IntroductionOsimertinib is recommended by major guidelines for use in the adjuvant setting in patients with EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC following the significant improvement in disease-free survival observed in the Phase III ADAURA trials. Due to limited real-world data in the adjuvant setting, little guidance exists on how to approach potential recurrences either during or after the completion of the treatment.

title: Association Between Resident Involvement in Cesarean Delivery, Complications, and Operative Times
creator: Joseph R. Mims, Amanda A. Allshouse, Torri D. Metz
description: Resident involvement in cesarean delivery was not associated with higher rates of major maternal operative morbidity such as organ injury, reoperation, or death. Cesarean delivery is the most common major abdominal surgical procedure performed yearly in the United States, making up 32.4% of all deliveries in 2024.

title: Corn or Climate? Climate Change Facilitated, but Did Not Initiate, the Northward Range Expansion of the Green Jay in Texas
creator: Callen M Inman, Lawrence E Gilbert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Anthropogenic changes are driving global shifts in species distributions. Two highly divergent bird species, the green jay ( Cyanocorax yncas ) and the blue jay ( Cyanocitta cristata ), recently hybridized in Texas following range expansions. While the southwestern spread of the blue jay has been attributed to suburban bird‐feeding, the cause of the green jay's > 2° northward expansion over the last 70 years is less clear.

title: Removal of a Fishhook‐Shaped Foreign Body in the Bronchus and Literature Review
creator: Wan Hu, Fanrui Zeng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Foreign body aspiration, particularly involving complex metallic objects with sharp projections like fishhooks, presents a formidable therapeutic challenge, often leading to complications such as mucosal impaction and obstructive pneumonia. We report a challenging case of a metallic fishhook‐shaped foreign body deeply embedded within the distal bronchial wall, where initial attempts at retrieval using standard biopsy and foreign body forceps via flexible bronchoscopy were unsuccessful due to significant mucosal oedema and impaction.

title: Aortic arch branch-prioritized reconstruction for type A aortic dissection surgery
creator: Jianfeng Gao, Jie Yan, Yanyu Duan, Junjian Yu, Wentong Li, Zhifang Luo, Wenbo Yu, Dilin Xie, Ziyou Liu, Jianxian Xiong
description: BackgroundAcute Stanford type A aortic dissection (STAAD) is a fatal condition requiring urgent surgical intervention. Owing to the complexity of the surgical process, various complications, such as neurological disorders, are common. In this study, we prioritized the reconstruction of aortic arch branches during surgery and investigated the association between prioritizing the branches and the postoperative outcomes of patients with STAAD.

title: Persistently high prevalence of HPV16 and rising prevalence of non-16/18 HR-HPV genotypes in cervical precancer and cancer in Latvia in 2016-2024 shape the severity of cervical disease
creator: Liba Sokolovska, Karina Biserova, Arta Spridzane, Daira Krisane, Alesja Dudorova, Svetlana Gebrila, Ilvija Krasovska, Dmitry Perminov, Beatrise Orlova, Marta Petrovska, Juris Jansons, Androniks Mitildzans, Jurijs Nazarovs, Maria Isaguliants
description: BackgroundCervical cancer incidence and mortality in Latvia is one of the highest in Europe, but data on HR-HPV prevalence in cervical disease are lacking. We aimed to investigate HR-HPV prevalence in cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) and cervical dysplasia (CD), association with disease severity, and prevalence changes over time.

title: Endoscopic Retrieval of a Migrated Plastic Pigtail Stent in a Patient With Gastric Bypass Surgery Using Novel Endoscopic Cutting Device
creator: Mohammad Shahzaib Qadir, Arsalan Syed, Ridhima Kaul, Arjun Chatterjee, Jerry Dang, Hassan Siddiki
description: anatomy.1–4 We present a 52-year-old woman with previous Roux-en-Y gastric bypass who developed a gastrojejunal staple-line leak complicated by a perigastric collection, managed with a 7-Fr double-pigtail stent. During planned removal, the stent was not visualized endoscopically (Figure 1); the staple line demonstrated dense scar tissue without clear disruption.

title: FishMitoCleaner: Automated Stop Codon Processing and Quality Control of Fish Mitochondrial Protein‐Coding Sequences
creator: Shaoyu Yang, Peng Xu, Jingzhen Wang, Xiaohui Cai
description: Vertebrate mitochondrial protein‐coding genes follow a different genetic code, in which TGA encodes tryptophan and a large number of genes terminate with incomplete stop codons completed post‐transcriptionally via polyadenylation. These features are often mishandled when coding sequences (CDS) downloaded from public databases are processed with standard tools, resulting in errors in downstream codon usage and evolution.

title: The association between music therapy and mental health in Chinese university students: a moderated mediation model of self-evaluation and gender
creator: Wei Wang
description: This research examines the effects of music therapy participation on mental health among Chinese university students, focusing on the mediating role of self-evaluation and the moderating role of gender. A moderated mediation model was proposed to explain how and for whom music therapy exerts its benefits.

title: Pyoderma gangrenosum chez une femme de 26 ans
creator: Mayeesha N. Khan, Nicole Asamoah, Smitha Kacheri Pathayappura
description: rses maladies infectieuses ou vasculaires, ce qui peut compliquer le diagnostic et retarder la prise en charge. Les manifestations du pyoderma gangrenosum peuvent souvent évoquer diverses maladies infectieuses ou vasculaires, ce qui peut compliquer le diagnostic et retarder la prise en charge.

title: Unfavorable nutrient intakes in children up to school entry age: results from the nationwide German KiESEL study
creator: Leonie Burgard, Sara Jansen, Clarissa Spiegler, Anna-Kristin Brettschneider, Andrea Straßburg, Ute Alexy, Stefan Storcksdieck genannt Bonsmann, Regina Ensenauer, Thorsten Heuer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundNutrition in the first years of life is a cornerstone for child development and long-term health, yet there is a lack of current data on energy and nutrient intake among toddlers and preschoolers in Germany.ObjectiveTo analyze energy and nutrient intake in toddlers (1- to 2-year-olds) and preschoolers (3- to 5-year-olds) in Germany and compare the results with the Dietary Reference Values (DRVs) by the European Food Safety Authority.DesignDietary intake was assessed by weighed food record data (3 + 1 day) of 890

title: Diabetes Distress in Caregivers of Young Children With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
creator: Elena D. Georges, Neha Parimi, Karen Dimentstein, Elizabeth A. Brown, Risa M. Wolf
description: Introduction:The American Diabetes Association recommends screening for diabetes distress in individuals with diabetes and their caregivers. We evaluated the clinical utility of the Problem Areas in Diabetes–Parent Revised version (PAID-PR) distress screener in caregivers of young children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and examined associations between diabetes distress, demographic and clinical characteristics, and diabetes technology use.

title: Depression detection through dual-stream modeling with large language models: a fusion-based transfer learning framework integrating BERT and T5 representations
creator: Na Wang, Weijia Zhang, Raja Kamil, Ian Renner, Syed Abdul Rahman Al-Haddad, Normala Ibrahim, Zhen Zhao
description: Millions of people around the world suffer from depression. While early diagnosis is essential for timely intervention, it remains a significant challenge due to limited access to clinically diagnosed data and privacy restrictions on mental health records. These limitations hinder the training of robust AI models for depression detection.

title: Mechanisms and Applications of Conductive Biomaterials in Spinal Cord Injury Repair
creator: Bin Zhao, Zhonghan Wang, Tong Yu, Xiangran Cui, Jinbo Zhang, Quezhu Danzeng, Wenjie Wang, Yi Shen, Chenhao Ma, Yaolin Zhao, Jianhang Jiao, Minfei Wu
description: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a debilitating disorder of the central nervous system and remains a major challenge in neural regeneration and rehabilitation research. Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) has demonstrated notable efficacy in promoting neural repair and functional recovery following SCI.

title: Mass resection as a candidate treatment for uterine PEComas of uncertain malignant potential: a case report and literature review
creator: Haijuan Shi, Yan Yin, Shoujun Liang, Chuanzhong Liu, Yibao Huang, Bingfeng Lu, Liying Zhang
description: BackgroundPerivascular epithelioid cell tumours (PEComas) occurring in the uterus are rare, with surgery being the most recommended primary treatment for malignant cases. This study aims to provide clinical guidance on the clinicopathological features and appropriate treatment options for patients with uterine PEComas of uncertain malignant potential.

title: Oropharyngeal Dysphagia Assessment in Behçet Disease Using EAT‐10 and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing
creator: Emre Demirel, Emel Tahir, Ahmet Kıvanç Cengiz
description: ObjectiveTo provide a preliminary symptom‐based and standardized single‐consistency FEES screening assessment of swallowing in adults with Behçet disease using the Eating Assessment Tool‐10 (EAT‐10) and fiberoptic endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES).MethodsThis single‐center cross‐sectional observational study with prospective enrollment was conducted between September 2022 and March 2024.

title: Demographic and other correlates of non-prescription drug use among college students during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Subi Gandhi, Sidketa Fofana, Md Rafiul Islam, Tamer Oraby
description: Background and objectivesSubstance use among college students in the U.S. remains a pressing concern and may have intensified during the COVID-19 pandemic due to increased stress, uncertainty, and academic disruptions. This study investigates the relationship between non-prescription drug use and various demographic, mental health, and behavioral factors among college students during the pandemic's early stages.

title: Glioblastoma immune landscape remodeling following treatment with CD70-targeted CAR-T cells
creator: Alexandros Kourtesakis, Dennis Alexander Agardy, Clara Tejido Dierssen, Ling Hai, Dirk Carsten Frieder Hoffmann, Normann Mussnig, Ralph Sinn, Manuel Fischer, Andy Schacht, Michael Breckwoldt, Lukas Bunse, Tim Sauer, Michael Platten, Wolfgang Wick, Tobias Kessler
description: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has shown limited efficacy in glioblastoma (GB), largely because of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). We have previously demonstrated that the ligand-based mCD70-directed construct mCAR27 specifically eliminates CD70⁺ GB cells in vitro, and induces durable tumor remission with prolonged survival in a syngeneic model of orthotopic GB.

title: Female urethral diverticular carcinoma: a case report and review of the literature
creator: Dan Li, Fan Hua Meng, Xu Yang
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the etiology, clinical manifestations, treatment methods, and prognosis of urethral diverticulum cancer to enhance understanding of this disease.MethodsThis paper reports a case of urethral diverticulum cancer with “hematuria and dysuria” as the main clinical manifestations. The case is discussed in conjunction with relevant literature.

title: The Readability of British Association of Urology Society Patient Information Leaflets: Have We Done Enough for Patients to Understand?
creator: Henry St Aubyn Bilton, Peter Knapp, Gui Tran
description: IntroductionPatient Information leaflets (PILs) from the British Association of Urologists (BAUS) are commonly used to communicate to patients about surgical procedures, but previous studies have highlighted that they are too difficult for some patients to read. BAUS PILs have since been rewritten using guidelines which emphasize readability.ObjectivesTo identify if the readability of BAUS PILs has changed compared to historical versions.

title: The use of nanoparticles in the treatment of infectious diseases and cancer, dental applications and tissue regeneration: a review
creator: Ali Sobhani-Nasab, Hamid Reza Banafshe, Amir Atapour, Mahmood Khaksary Mahabady, Maryam Akbari, Abdolreza Daraei, Yaser Mansoori, Amin Moradi Hasan-Abad
description: The emergence of nanotechnology as a field of study can be traced back to the 1980s, at which point the means to artificially produce, control, and observe matter on a nanometer level was made viable. Recent advancements in technology have enabled us to extend our reach to the nanoscale, which has presented an unparalleled opportunity to directly target biomolecular interactions.

title: Associations of surgical breast cancer treatment at regional or community hospitals with patient-reported experience measures
creator: Savannah R. Gonzales, Uma Ramesh, A. James O’Malley, Gabriel A. Brooks, Tracy Onega, Erika L. Moen
description: PurposeHigh-volume hospitals deliver improved outcomes for patients with breast cancer, supporting referrals for breast cancer surgical care to high-volume regional facilities. This retrospective cohort study investigated how multidisciplinary cancer care trajectories and patient care experiences varied by surgical facility classification (regional vs. community as a proxy for high- vs. low-volume) and whether effects differed by rural-residence.

title: Contrasted modifications of IgM and IgT repertoires induced by high- and low-virulent infectious pancreatic necrosis virus strains in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss)
creator: Sofie Navelsaker Thommessen, Luc Jouneau, Rosario Castro, Vanessa Mhanna, Encarnita Mariotti-Ferrandiz, Hetron M. Munang´andu, Amr Ahmed Abdelrahim Gamil, Bertrand Collet, Pierre Boudinot, Oystein Evensen
description: IntroductionInfectious pancreatic necrosis virus (IPNV) is a significant pathogen in salmonid aquaculture, with virulence determined mainly by amino acid residues in the VP2 capsid protein.MethodsThis study investigates the modifications of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) IgM and IgT repertoire induced by two IPNV strains that differ at VP2 positions 217 and 221, specifically IPNV-TA (T217A221) and IPNV-PT (P217T221).

title: Effects of feeding a Bacillus-based probiotic to grazing Nellore bulls finished on tropical pasture
creator: Rodrigo J. Oliveira, Barbara C. Afonso, Bernardo C. Petean, Giovanna L. O. Araujo, Pedro H. C. Ribeiro, Ariany F. Toledo, Danilo Domingues Millen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Interest in probiotics as an alternative to ionophores has increased, particularly in pasture-based systems using energy supplementation. While these additives aim to improve feed efficiency and mitigate acidosis risk, probiotics may also modulate rumen function by enhancing fiber digestion. This study evaluated the effects of including a Bacillus-based probiotic in an energy supplement on intake, performance, total tract digestibility, and rumen and cecum morphometrics of finishing Nellore cattle.

title: Cavity control of multiferroic order in single-layer NiI2
creator: Chongxiao Fan, Emil Viñas Boström, Xinle Cheng, Lukas Grunwald, Zhuquan Zhang, Dante M Kennes, Dmitri N Basov, Angel Rubio
description: Controlling materials through their interactions with electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations is an emergent frontier in material engineering. Although recent experiments have demonstrated dark cavity effects for electronic material phases, like superconductivity, ferroelectricity and charge density waves, a smoking gun experiment for magnetic systems is lacking.

title: Identification and functional validation of a new gene conferring resistance to Soybean Mosaic Virus strains SC4 and SC20 in soybean
creator: Muhammad Muzzafar Raza, Huiying Jia, Muhammad Khuram Razzaq, Bowen Li, Kai Li, Junyi Gai
description: Soybean Mosaic Virus (SMV) poses a serious threat to soybean production, often resulting in considerable yield losses or complete crop failure, particularly if infection occurs during early growth stages. While several SMV resistance genes have been identified, the genetic basis of resistance to certain strains remains poorly understood.

title: Research on multi-robot collaborative operation in logistics and warehousing using A3C optimized YOLOv5-PPO model
creator: Lei Wang, Guangjun Liu
description: IntroductionIn the field of logistics warehousing robots, collaborative operation and coordinated control have always been challenging issues. Although deep learning and reinforcement learning methods have made some progress in solving these problems, however, current research still has shortcomings. In particular, research on adaptive sensing and real-time decision-making of multi-robot swarms has not yet received sufficient attention.

title: Hip Structural Analysis and Multiple Fragility Fractures: Evidence from a Large Cross-Sectional Clinical Cohort
creator: Hamzah Amin, Ajmal Elhani, Amaan Shaffi, Marwan Bukhari
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hip structural analysis parameters (HSAP) are associated with hip fracture risk, but associations with multiple fragility fracture phenotypes remain poorly characterised. We analysed 11 DXA-derived HSAP in patients referred between June 2004 and November 2019. Five mutually exclusive fracture phenotypes were defined: no fracture, single hip fracture, single non-hip fracture, multiple non-hip fractures, and multiple fractures including at least one hip fracture.

title: Microbial Pressure and Social Immunity: Bumble Bees Increase Brood Hygiene After Exposure to a Bacillus thuringiensis ‐Based Biopesticide
creator: Michelle Scheffler, Karoline Wueppenhorst, Doreen Babin, Abdulrahim T. Alkassab, Silvio Erler
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). To inhibit the spread of potential pathogens and parasites, social insects exhibit hygienic behaviour, the removal of dead or affected brood. Studies on bumble bees performing this behaviour are limited, compared to honey bees, termites, and ants. With changes in agricultural practices, bees are exposed more often to bioinsecticides, especially microorganisms, which they bring into their nests and might cause damage to brood and adult bees.

title: Lumbar Facet Joint Morphology and Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Alberto Suarez, Justin Gumbs, Michelle Schmidt, Zeena Shather, Hanna Neustadter, Dominic Lafalce, Marissa Middleton, Jaden Wise, Isabella Merem, Maohua Lin, Frank D Vrionis
description: Study DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis.ObjectivesTo evaluate the associations between lumbar facet orientation, facet tropism, and degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis (DLS), while assessing sex-specific differences in facet morphology.MethodsA PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261417450). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026.

title: Detection of slowly expanding lesions in people with multiple sclerosis using MRI: A scoping review
creator: Malo Gicquel, Anne Kerbrat, Benoit Combès
description: Slowly expanding lesions (SELs) have recently been described in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS). This pattern of slow lesion expansion, often too subtle to be identified visually, can be detected on conventional brain MRI scans and represents a candidate imaging biomarker of chronic inflammation.

title: Subcellular thiol functional group distribution in Geobacter sulfurreducens determined by Hg LIII-edge EXAFS
creator: Fanchao Meng, Ulf Skyllberg, Yangyang Li, Shusaku Hayama, Erik Björn, Yu Song
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mercury (Hg) is a global environmental concern due to its microbial conversion to methylmercury (MeHg), a potent neurotoxin that bioaccumulates in food webs and poses risks to ecosystems and human health. Thiol functional groups (RSH) play an important role in controlling Hg(II) speciation and bio-uptake in methylating bacteria, yet the spatial distribution and density of these thiols within cells remain largely unknown.

title: Enhanced bioavailability of Quercetin-loaded niosomal in situ gel for the management of Parkinson’s disease
creator: Abhishek A. Revankar, Archana S. Patil, Reshma Karishetti, Krutuja R. Chougule, Priyanka Patil, Abhijit Salokhe
description: BackgroundParkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurological disorder, characterized by motor symptoms such as tremor and rigidity due to the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. This study investigates the formulation of quercetin, a natural bioflavonoid with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, as niosomes for intranasal delivery to enhance its bioavailability and therapeutic potential for PD.

title: Endothelial anthrax toxin receptor 2 plays a protective role in liver fibrosis
creator: Xiaojuan Huang, Liyin Zhang, Wei Luo, Yu Zeng, Xiaoxue Li, Nan Yang, Wenwen Huang, Bi-Sen Ding
description: Hepatocellular carcinoma is one of the leading cancers worldwide and is a potential consequence of fibrosis. Therefore, the identification of key cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in liver fibrosis is an important goal for the development of new strategies to control liver-related diseases.

title: Sonographic Detection of a Lumbar Facet Joint Abscess with Epidural Involvement
creator: Eckehart Schöll, Anja Carolin Mair, Rainer Jürgen Litz
description: al symptoms initially mimic mechanical back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is considered the imaging modality of choice for detecting facet joint infection and associated epidural or paraspinal abscess formation (K. M. Sin et al. J Clin Imaging Sci 2024; 14: 34). However, paraspinal abscesses adjacent to the facet joints may also be detected by ultrasound.

title: The Effect of Hospital Trauma Level on Odds of Non-home Discharge from Hospital Following Dens Fracture
creator: Andrew Ni, Doha Hussien, Abhi Rashiwala, Victoria Vargas, Nasa Xu, Jason McCartney, Ralph Zachary Garza
description: IntroductionDens fractures are cervical spine injuries with high morbidity and mortality in the elderly. Many patients require discharge to rehabilitation facilities or skilled nursing care, which impacts patient recovery, healthcare system resource allocation, and prognosis. This study evaluated the effect of trauma center level designation on discharge disposition in patients with dens fractures.

title: The journey to diagnosis for patients with CIDP: results from a real-world international survey
creator: Clémence Arvin-Berod, Febe Brackx, Lucas Van de Veire, Sandra Paci, Yasmin Taylor, Jack Wright, Alejandra Pérez del Real, Jean Philippe Plançon, Richard Sperry, Chelsey Fix, Sarah Dewilde, Yusuf A. Rajabally
description: IntroductionChronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) is a rare autoimmune disorder affecting the peripheral nerves, typically characterized by muscle weakness and sensory deficits. This study seeks to describe CIDP patients’ journey to diagnosis alongside factors influencing misdiagnosis and time to diagnosis.MethodsWe analyzed demographics and diagnostic data reported by neurologists and their patients in Adelphi’s CIDP Disease Specific Programme™.

title: Beyond the binary description of sinus tracts in periprosthetic joint infection
creator: Irene K. Sigmund, Marjan Wouthuyzen-Bakker, Tristan Ferry, Ricardo Sousa, Daniel Pérez-Prieto, Alex Soriano, Volker Alt, Willem J. Metsemakers, Martin Clauss, Rihard Trebse
description: Current periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) definitions classify sinus tracts as present or absent. While this binary approach is appropriate for diagnosing PJI, it does not capture the heterogeneity of sinus tracts relevant to surgical decision-making. We propose that future studies explore a standardized characterization of sinus tract complexity to better inform surgical treatment.

title: Compensatory Fatty Acid Metabolism and Hepatic Gene Expression in African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) Fed Marine‐Ingredient‐Free Circular Diets Low in EPA and DHA
creator: Christopher Shaw, Klaus Knopf, Sven Wuertz, Koushik Roy, Radek Gebauer, Tobias Goldhammer, Viola Schöning, Wibke Kleiner, Marvin Sens, Christian Ulrichs, Werner Kloas, Ikram Belghit
description: Raw materials rich in EPA (C20:5n‐3) and DHA (C22:6n‐3) such as marine fish oils and meals are becoming increasingly scarce and valuable throughout the aquafeed industry, while human dietary intake of EPA and DHA is deficient in many parts of the world.

title: Pharmacy students’ knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 receptor agonist adverse effects in obesity management: a cross-sectional study
creator: Alaa A. Khojah, Malaz J. Gazzaz, Mohammed M. Aldurdunji, Ahmad E. Safiraldeen, Ibrahim R. Al-Qurashi, Mohammad A. Alhazmi, Ashraf N. Abdalla, Roaya S. Alqurashi, Saad M. Wali
description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are important therapeutic options for obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite their increasing use, safety concerns remain, and pharmacy students’ knowledge of their adverse effects is unclear. This study evaluated pharmacy students’ knowledge and attitudes regarding GLP-1 RA adverse effects in obesity management.

title: Acoustic stimulation and other emerging approaches to enhance sleep: design notes for the next generation of closed-loop neurostimulation technology
creator: William G. Coon, Sophie J. Nilsson, Michael T. Smith, Matthew J. Reid
description: Sleep is indispensable to human health, supporting memory consolidation, emotional regulation, immune function, and metabolic homeostasis. Despite its importance, chronic sleep disturbances are pervasive, with especially high prevalence in operational and clinical populations. This review synthesizes recent advances in sleep enhancement through closed-loop neurostimulation, focusing on systems that dynamically interact with endogenous brain rhythms to improve sleep quality and efficiency.

title: An induced pluripotent stem cell-based chemical genetic approach for studying spinal muscular atrophy
creator: Richard M. Giadone, Kristina M. Holton, Xiaoyu Hu, Ted Natoli, Sabrina Ghosh, Stanley P. Gill, Nicholas Lyons, Aravind Subramanian, Lee L. Rubin
description: IntroductionSpinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a genetic disease characterized by degeneration of spinal cord motor neurons and neuromuscular junctions. Despite recent developments in therapies for SMA, treatment efficacy largely relies on the administration of drugs early in disease progression and is impacted by underlying patient genetics.

title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and the Risk of Age-Related Macular Degeneration
creator: Athar Shadmani, Jaclyn Lekse Kovach
description: Purpose: To evaluate the association between obstructive sleep apnea and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and to characterize disease subtype distribution, age trends, and treatment patterns. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed between January 1, 2020, and July 30, 2025, of patients aged 50 or older registered in the Epic electronic health record (EHR) system at the University of Miami.

title: Comparative chloroplast genomics of Cypripedioideae: structural divergence, adaptive evolution, and phylogenomic insights
creator: Xiaoyan Zhao, Xiaoxiao Lan, Zishuo Wang, Dong Li, Wei Sun, Yunpeng Gai, Bing Liu
description: The Cypripedioideae subfamily (slipper orchids) exhibits remarkable ecological diversity, spanning temperate to tropical habitats, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its adaptive radiation remain poorly understood. Chloroplast genomes, with their critical roles in photosynthesis and conserved structure, offer a powerful system to investigate how evolutionary forces shape genomic adaptation.

title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy or chemoradiation plus consolidative chemotherapy followed by radical operation for locally advanced rectal cancer
creator: Shing Fung Lee, Pui Lam Yip, Barry Wo, Natalie Sean-Man Wong, Balamurugan A. Vellayappan, Harvey J. Mamon, Francis Ann Shing Lee
description: IntroductionLimited evidence compares short-course radiotherapy (SCRT) and long-course chemoradiotherapy (LCCRT), both of which are followed by consolidative chemotherapy before radical rectal surgery. We conducted a retrospective cohort study to assess treatment response, survival outcomes, and toxicity in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer.

title: Aqueous extract of erigeron annuus ameliorates OVA-induced atopic dermatitis-like skin lesions through modulation of Th2-mediated immune responses and MAPK signaling
creator: Yejin Ahn, Min Ji Gu, Ho-Young Park, Seol Ji Baek, Seong Un Jeong, Sang Keun Ha, Donghwan Kim
description: ContextAtopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by epidermal barrier dysfunction and dysregulated type 2 helper T cell (Th2)-mediated immune responses. Erigeron annuus (L.) Desf. is traditionally used for inflammatory conditions, but its effects on atopic dermatitis remain unclear.ObjectiveThis study evaluated the protective effects of E. annuus aqueous extract (EA) and associated mechanisms.

title: Nanoporous-based biomaterials in biomedical applications: from fundamentals and biosensing to drug delivery, wound healing, and tissue engineering
creator: Zahra Saadatidizaji, Iman Zare, Mingzhen Zhang, Shahrzad Zirak Hassan Kiadeh, Mojdeh Mirshafiei, Amin Farahani, Zahra Sadat, Hooman Aghamirza Moghim Aliabadi, Mohammad Mahdavi, Reza Eivazzadeh-Keihan, Amir Kashtiaray, Parisa Rezvani, Aisan Yahyapoor, Amirali Vaziri, Hooriehsadat Amini, Meng Yu
description: Nanoporous materials (NPMs) have emerged as powerful tools in the fields of medicine, revolutionizing diagnostics, treatment, and patient care. Their unique properties address critical challenges in healthcare. Nanoporous matrices offer abundant active sites for molecular adsorption, catalysis, and interactions with biological entities. Efficient loading of therapeutic agents and biomolecules occurs due to their expansive surface area.

title: Community implementation of a brief parent mediated intervention for toddlers with probable or confirmed autism spectrum disorder: feasibility, acceptability, and drivers of success (IE Drmic et al.)
creator: Irene Drmic, Jessica Brian, Caroline Roncadin, Chantelle Shaver, Marlene Pase, Natalie Rugajs, Kristina Tofano, Erin Dowds, Lonnie Zwaigenbaum, Isabel M. Smith, Susan E. Bryson
description: BackgroundSocial ABCs is a caregiver-mediated Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Intervention for toddlers with confirmed/suspected Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), with evidence in controlled research settings. Information is lacking on implementation in community settings. We reported on the treatment effectiveness of this program within a community setting, and the current paper describes the implementation phase of this work.

title: Machine learning models reveal microbial signatures in healthy human tissues, challenging the sterility of human organs
creator: Anargyros Skoulakis, Giorgos Skoufos, Armen Ovsepian, Artemis G. Hatzigeorgiou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe presence of microbes within healthy human internal organs still remains under question. Our study endeavors to discern microbial signatures within normal human internal tissues using data from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) consortium. Machine learning (ML) models were developed to classify each tissue type based solely on microbial profiles, with the identification of tissue-specific microbial signatures suggesting the presence of distinct microbial communities inside tissues.MethodsWe analyzed 13,871 normal RNA-seq samples from 28 tissues obtained from the GTEx consortium.

title: Assessing and Improving Access to Health and Social Care Services for Children Rendered Vulnerable by Abuse: Protocol for a Cross-Sectoral Longitudinal, Mixed Methods, Multi-Country Study Using Nationwide Data in Europe
creator: Catherine Quantin, Donna O’Leary, Yulia Shenderovich, Neha Batura, Marcella Broccia, Jonathan Cottenet, Laura Elizabeth Cowley, Troels Graesholt-Knudsen, Diogo Lamela, Kevin Lalor, Andreas Jud, Leona Hakkaart van Roijen, Peter Fallesen, George Nikolaidis, Athanasios Ntinapogias, Ulugbek Nurmatov, Si
description: Child maltreatment (CM) is a widespread and underreported public health concern with long-term health and wellbeing outcomes. In Europe, access to timely, effective support remains limited. Inadequate responses exacerbate long-term outcomes and influence life course trajectories, with substantial societal and economic costs.

title: CT ventriculographic identification and neuroendoscopic treatment of acquired hydrocephalus due to cerebral aqueduct lesions: a two-case report
creator: Kai Liu, Yuheng Feng, Shuli Wang, Yubo Zhang, Xiaoxuan Ji, Qiang Li, Xiaodong Luo
description: Hydrocephalus secondary to cerebral aqueduct lesions poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when causative lesions are occult on conventional neuroimaging. We present two pediatric cases of acquired obstructive hydrocephalus, in which routine laboratory tests were unremarkable except for mildly elevated tumor markers. Both patients exhibited acute symptoms of intracranial hypertension.

title: Case Report: Pseudotumor due to Trunnionosis in Ceramic‐on‐Ceramic THA Monoblock Acetabular Cup Disengagement
creator: M. Olivieri, R. Guarracino, D. Lup, A. Maso, E. Storni, S. Squarzoni, V. Peccerillo, P. Cimatti, D. Dallari, P. Caldora
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR) and pseudotumor formation, representing inflammatory responses to wear debris that lead to osteolytic lesions, remain major long‐term complications of total hip replacement. Hard‐bearing total hip prostheses with improved tribological properties—particularly large‐diameter head (LDH) ceramic‐on‐ceramic (CoC) bearings and preassembled cup designs—have been introduced into clinical practice to minimize wear, increase the range of motion (ROM), and reduce dislocation rates.

title: Multi-institutional evaluation comparing guidance from International Ki67 Working Group vs National Health Commission of China on immunohistochemistry-based Ki67 assessment alongside the Quantitative Dot Blot method
creator: Yin Wang, Jiarui Zou, Qinghua Cao, Guihong Dai, Panhong Fan, Xue Gong, Jinyan Jiang, Yanqing Kong, Chao Liu, Chunhui Liu, Chenjia Lu, Meiren Li, Zhiqiang Lang, Yang Lin, Yan Peng, Haiyan Shi, Yuhuan Wang, Jiu Wang, Bichen Xie, Bing Yang, Guohua Yu, Cuiping Zhang, Hengming Zhang, Luting Zhou, Zilan Z
description: PurposeRecommendations from the National Health Commission of China (NHCC) and the International Ki67 Working Group (IKWG) were issued to guide immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based Ki67 scoring for breast cancer patients in daily clinical practice. They were evaluated in this multi-institutional study alongside the results from the Quantitative Dot Blot (QDB) method.

title: A novel link between chronic inflammation and humanin regulation in children
creator: Yunhan Zhao, Outi Mäkitie, Saila Laakso, Vera Fedosova, Lars Sävendahl, Farasat Zaman
description: ObjectiveChildren with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) often suffer from poor bone growth and impaired bone health. Humanin is a cytoprotective factor expressed in bone and other tissues and we hypothesized that humanin levels are suppressed in conditions of chronic inflammation.

title: HIV Tat‐Stimulated Microglial Extracellular Vesicles Are Enriched for Ferroptosis Mediators: Role of Dysregulated Autophagy
creator: Seema Singh, Elias Horanieh, Craig L. Semerad, Palsamy Periyasamy, Susmita Sil, Shilpa Buch
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Extracellular vesicles (EVs) serve as conduits for intercellular communication, under both physiological and pathological contexts. During disease pathogenesis, microglia‐derived EVs (MEVs) play a key role in transferring pathological cargo to the recipient cells, thereby modulating their phenotype and function. The current study was aimed to explore how HIV Transactivator of transcription (Tat) protein‐mediated dysregulated autophagy/ferritinophagy contributes to the expression and release of ferroptotic mediators in Tat‐activated MEVs.

title: Attitudes towards persons with disabilities vs. personality traits of Polish students
creator: Iwona Radlińska, Marta Kożybska, Arkadiusz Prajzner, Łukasz Krzywoszański, Beata Karakiewicz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025).
