creator: Jeffrey George, Andrew J Moyal, Isha K Shah, Robert J Burkhart, Louis S Kang, Jacob G Calcei, James E Voos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose of ReviewAnterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) reliably restores anteroposterior stability; however, the rate of return to prior level of play and incidence of recurrent ACL injury have improved little over the past two decades. The purpose of this review is to describe the current state of ACLR with respect to graft selection, lateral extra-articular augmentation, rehabilitation and return to play, including the role of psychological readiness, and the specific rehabilitation protocol utilized by the senior author.Recent FindingsGraft utilization has shifted substantially.

title: FAK Mediated Coordination of Extracellular Matrix Remodeling and Cellular Mechanics Impairs Nanomedicine Delivery in Solid Tumors
creator: Tian Zhao, Hao Wu, Yujie Qin, Jingfei Zhu, Ye Huang, Wei Chen, Jiaxuan Yu, Xiang Qin, Shun Li, Junjie Li, Tingting Li, Yiyao Liu
description: Tumor extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and cell‐intrinsic mechanical properties critically limit nanoparticle (NP) delivery, yet how these multiscale biophysical cues are coordinately regulated remains unclear. Here, we identify focal adhesion kinase (FAK/PTK2) as a central mechanobiological regulator that couples ECM remodeling with cellular mechanics to control NP transport and cellular uptake.

title: Pan-cancer multi-omics analysis reveals upregulation of the POLE2 subunit of DNA polymerase epsilon and its associations with patient survival and cellular pathways beyond DNA replication
creator: Alina Krasilia, Deepali Chaudhry, Iwona J Fijalkowska, Michal Dmowski
description: DNA polymerase epsilon (Polε) is essential for high-fidelity leading-strand synthesis. It comprises a catalytic subunit, POLE, and three accessory subunits, including POLE2. In contrast to POLE, the biological functions and clinical significance of POLE2 remain unexplored. POLE2 is vital for the assembly of Polε and for interactions with the CMG helicase.

title: Preliminary Clinical Evaluation in Cross‐Sectional Imaging: A Qualitative Inquiry Into the Ethical Considerations in the Era of Artificial Intelligence
creator: Messiah N. K. Anudjo, Sharon Docherty, Theophilus N. Akudjedu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe evolving role of radiographers in Preliminary Clinical Evaluation (PCE), alongside the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiography workflows, is reshaping professional boundaries and enhancing patient care. However, this introduces ethical challenges that may impact PCE performance. This study explored the perspectives of cross‐sectional imaging radiographers on the ethical dimensions of PCE and the potential impact of AI on the future practice of PCE.MethodA descriptive qualitative inquiry employing semi‐structured interviews was conducted.

title: Awareness of Community Members in Sudan Toward Stroke in 2024
creator: Fatima Elbasri Abuelgasim Mohammed, Amna Alrasheed Abuzaid Ali, Ammar Elgadi, Ragad Magdi Mohammed Elamin Yousif, Israa Elbagir Mohamed Nassir, Ola Awad Babiker Adam, Reem Seifeldawla Taha Mohamed Osman, Igbal Izzeldin Ahmed Abuzeid, Yasir Eltayeb Elkhalifa Yousif Omer, Mohammed Alamin Mokhtar Omer,
description: BackgroundSudan ranks 27th globally in stroke‐related deaths, with an age‐adjusted death rate of 136.47 per 100,000 people. Adequate knowledge among the population, particularly during times of conflict, can improve stroke outcomes.ObjectivesTo assess the Sudanese population's knowledge toward stroke in 2024.MethodsThis cross‐sectional study was conducted from April to May 2024 among the Sudanese population who were aged more than 18 years.

title: Chronotype and Peripheral Clock Genes: Association With Frailty and Insomnia in Mexican Older Adults
creator: Citlally E. Ortiz‐Vázquez, Paola Garcia‐delaTorre, Sergio Sánchez‐García, Lorena Aguilar‐Arnal, Lucía Mendoza‐Viveros
description: ObjectivesFrailty is a geriatric syndrome associated with increased vulnerability to adverse health outcomes in older adults. Circadian rhythms regulate multiple physiological processes relevant to aging, including sleep, metabolism, and immune function; however, the relationship between circadian biology and frailty remains incompletely understood.

title: Osmium Nanoparticle Anchoring on CoFe Layered Double Hydroxides Enables High‐Valent Species Stabilization and Efficient Seawater Oxygen Evolution
creator: Xindong She, Guosheng Zhou, Kanghua Miao, Junjie Gong, Mingzhe Jiang, Xueting Zhu, Zhenzhen Wang, Shijie Shen, Wenwu Zhong
description: Direct seawater oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically hampered by chloride‐induced competitive oxidation, corrosion, and active‐site poisoning, driving the urgent need for highly active and chlorine‐tolerant electrocatalysts. Herein, a surface‐engineered electrocatalyst comprising osmium nanoparticles (Os NPs) anchored onto CoFe layered double hydroxide (Os/CoFe LDH) was prepared.

title: Climate Change is Rewriting the Hydroclimatic Operating Envelope of Mines
creator: Haoxuan Yu, Izni Zahidi, Chow Ming Fai, Jilong Pan
description: Physical climate risk in mining is framed as floods, droughts, heatwaves, and wildfires acting on assets with fixed design conditions. We argue that the deeper change is a moving hydroclimatic operating envelope: climate alters the water and heat conditions around mines, while geology, engineering, and lifecycle stage govern how those changes propagate.

title: Doggy doctorates: Early career progression outcomes for UK‐funded postgraduate canine health and welfare researchers
creator: Alison M Skipper, Rowena M A Packer, Dan G O'Neill
description: BackgroundThis quantitative study describes characteristics and career outcomes (in August 2024) of students completing research master's or PhD degrees in canine health and welfare who received not‐for‐profit funding between 2012 and 2018.MethodsHistorical canine health and welfare research funding data were used to identify research students whose subsequent career outcomes were established by visual scrutiny of public online databases.

title: Targeted Perturbation of Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism via Thermoelectric Nanoflowers for Enhanced Cuproptosis Echoed With Immunotherapy
creator: Haoyang Du, Chao Xu, Hao Wang, Bo Peng, Peng Liu, Wei Gao, Tao Ye, Xinyuan Yu, Ying Shi, Jiaxin Liu, Tiancong Zhao, Bin Sun, Piaoping Yang, Manjie Zhang
description: Cuproptosis, a novel anti‐cancer mechanism, holds significant potential for triggering sequential immunotherapy to enhance anti‐cancer efficacy. However, this cascade effect is often limited by copper efflux mechanisms mediated by the copper‐transporting ATPase (ATP7B), which reduces intracellular copper accumulation and negates cuproptosis.

title: Beta Oscillations and Pupil-Linked Arousal Regulate the Updating of Cognitive Models
creator: Charlotte R. Marshall, Mengxi Wang, Emma L. Lawrance, Nils Kolling, Jill X. O’Reilly
description: The beta rhythm (neural oscillations in the range 13–30 Hz) is associated with the control of movement. Discrete movements (such as a button press) are bounded by a premovement dip in beta power and a postmovement beta rebound, which are thought to release and terminate the action, respectively.

title: Single-cell mapping of human plasma cell fate reveals a commitment checkpoint and Cav-1β expression associated with mTORC1 machinery
creator: Gersende Caron, Fabienne Desmots, Mélanie Chabaud, Maud Lemarié, Vincent Olivier, Fabrice Chatonnet, Céline Nonn, Cassandra Jadeau, Simon Léonard, Céline Monvoisin, Kathleen Santamaria, Cédric M Blouin, Noudjoud Attaf, Tarek Gharsalli, Pierre Milpied, Christophe Lamaze, Céline Pangault, Marion Haas,
description: SummaryHuman B cell differentiation into antibody-secreting plasma cells (PCs) requires coordinated transcriptional and organelle remodeling. Using single-cell transcriptomics in an in vitro human B cell differentiation system, we identified a Day-8 commitment checkpoint separating PC, memory B cell, and germinal center-like trajectories and defined an XBP1-associated transcriptional program linked to organelle remodeling.

title: RXNMapper-v2: updated validation and evaluation on expanded chemical space
creator: Yves Grandjean, Sacha Raffaud, Annie M. Westerlund, Philippe Schwaller, Samuel Genheden, Jean-Louis Reymond
description: Atom-to-atom mapping (AAM) assigns reactant atoms to product atoms and is fundamental for reaction classification, template extraction, and synthesis planning. RXNMapper derives AAM from the attention weights of a transformer model trained by masked language modeling on unmapped reaction SMILES. However, its original model selection relied on USPTO-50K, a validation set later shown to contain erroneous mappings.

title: Recurrence of Helicobacter Pylori after Successful Eradication in Northwestern China: Rates, Risk Factors, and Resistance Profiles of Recurrence Isolates
creator: Min Niu, Xiaoming Su, Zhen Ma, Lulu Li
description: PurposeThis study aimed to investigate the recurrence rate of H. pylori after successful eradication in Ningxia, to identify independent risk factors associated with recurrence, and to characterize the antibiotic resistance profiles of isolates obtained from recurrent patients.MethodsThis study is a retrospective cohort study. A total of 891 H.

title: Internal fit of cobalt–chromium and zirconia implant abutments fabricated using different techniques: a micro–computed tomography study
creator: Pedro Molinero-Mourelle, Seyed Ali Mosaddad, Rocio Cascos-Sanchez, Margarita Chevalier del Río, Gülce Çakmak, Andrea Roccuzzo, Miguel Gómez-Polo
description: PurposeTo evaluate the internal fit at the implant-abutment interface of zirconia and cobalt–chromium abutments fabricated using different techniques by micro-computed tomography (micro-CT).MethodsTwenty screw-retained abutments were divided into 4 groups (n = 5): milled zirconia (ZrCAD), milled cobalt–chromium (Co-CrMill), laser-sintered cobalt–chromium (Co-CrLS), and cast cobalt–chromium (Co-CrCL).

title: The Paul Glaucoma Implant versus the Ahmed and Baerveldt Glaucoma Implants: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis
creator: Mohamed N Elshabrawi, Bara M Hammadeh, Ayodeji Arobo, Nader Elfar, Elsayed S Moubarak, Rami Al-Dwairi, Seren Al Beiruti, Hashem Abu Serhan
description: PurposeTo compare the efficacy and safety of the Paul Glaucoma Implant (PGI) with those of the two established glaucoma drainage devices, the Ahmed Glaucoma Valve (AGV) and the Baerveldt Glaucoma Implant (BGI).MethodsPubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar were searched.

title: Study protocol for a quasi-experimental evaluation of the whole school approach FREI DAY
creator: Dominik Röding, Ricarda Brender, Sibel Ünlü-Reske, Anna Brager, Alicia Strauß, Jacqueline Kittel, Maike Stolz, Christian Krauth, Christiane Meyer, Ulla Walter
description: BackgroundThe Sustainable Development Goals combine health, social justice, sustainability, and environmental protection. Schools offer a suitable setting for linking these goals and incorporating them into the development of children and youth. FREI DAY is a whole-school approach in German-speaking countries and at German schools abroad.

title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies SERPINE1 as a vascular endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
creator: Hongxia Su, Yuan Zhang, Jia Wang, Lei Liu, Yulin Zhao
description: Highlights•Endothelial cells are identified as key mediators of cisplatin resistance in HNSCC.•Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal SERPINE1 vascular localization.•SERPINE1 marks resistant endothelial states in HPV-negative HNSCC tumors.•High SERPINE1 expression predicts poor survival and immune suppression.•SERPINE1 may guide resistance-directed precision treatment strategies.

title: Estradiol-associated extracellular signaling in the human breast in vivo identifies mast cells as tumor-supportive stromal mediators
creator: Annelie Abrahamsson, Xingyue Wang, Wen Zhong, Charlotta Dabrosin
description: Sex steroid exposure is a major risk factor for breast cancer initiation and progression through incompletely understood mechanisms. Novel therapeutics for prevention and treatment of estrogen-dependent breast cancer are needed. Cell-cell interactions within the microenvironment contribute to breast cancer progression through extracellular signaling.

title: SIX-MONTH SUPERVISED TELEREHABILITATION COMBINING PILATES-BASED THERAPEUTIC EXERCISE AND SELF-MYOFASCIAL RELEASE IN ADULTS WITH FIBROMYALGIA: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
creator: Thomai MARANTIDOU, Evangelia I. GERMANOU, Vasiliki MANOU, Nikolaos KOUTLIANOS, Evangelos SYKARAS, Ioannis TERZIDIS
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of a 6-month supervised multicomponent telerehabilitation programme combining Pilates-based therapeutic exercise and self-myofascial release on fibromyalgia impact, sleep quality, and psychological outcomes.DesignTwo-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial.Subjects/Patients68 adults with fibromyalgia confirmed according to the 2016 ACR criteria.MethodsParticipants were randomized to a 6-month supervised home-based telerehabilitation programme (n = 35) or usual care (n = 33).

title: Development of 99mTc-cefadroxil loaded chitosan nanoparticles as a novel radiotracer for detection of septic and aseptic foci
creator: Marwa S El Refaye, Safaa B Challan, H E Ramadan, S I Khater
description: Early detection of inflammation is critical for preventing disease progression, and nuclear medicine plays a pivotal role in this context. Imaging modalities such as single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) enable the early identification of functional abnormalities through the use of targeted radiotracers that specifically localize inflammatory processes.

title: Stability and Thermophysical Properties of Silicon Carbide and Carbon Nanofibers Thermal Oil Hybrid Nanofluids
creator: Suhaib Umer Ilyas, Lim Li Shan, Nawal Noshad, Haris Naseer, Mustafa Alsaady, Aymn Abdulrahman, Anas Ahmed, Rajashekhar Pendyala
description: Hybrid Nanofluids (HNFs) have been widely investigated to improve the thermal efficiency of energy systems, thereby reducing overall energy consumption. Silicon Carbide (SiC) nanoparticles offer excellent thermal stability, and Carbon Nanofibers (CNF) provide superior phonon-mediated thermal conduction. However, their synergistic combination as HNFs remains largely unexplored.

title: An acoustic-only multivariable diagnostic model for Parkinson's disease using bowel sound acoustic signatures
creator: Sicheng Chen, Man Zhang, Surui Fang, Qi Yang, Chuyi Chen, Zhixuan Lei, Yuxia Zhu, Fen Deng, Lijuan Mo, Xi Liu, Changhong Tan, Lifen Chen
description: BackgroundEarly detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains challenging due to the lack of reliable prodromal biomarkers. Non-invasive markers of gastrointestinal dysfunction are lacking.ObjectivesTo characterize bowel sound acoustic phenotypes in PD and evaluate their potential as non-invasive diagnostic markers by developing an acoustic-based predictive model.MethodsStandardized 5-min bowel sound recordings were collected from 120 PD patients and 100 controls.

title: Charting the future: A multi-setting medical chart study of advance care planning in Parkinson's disease and atypical Parkinsonism
creator: Herma Lennaerts-Kats, Bauke W. Dijkstra, Anke Elbers, Bastiaan R. Bloem, Marieke C. Groot, Jenny T. van der Steen, Marjan J. Meinders
description: BackgroundAdvance Care Planning (ACP) enables people with progressive diseases to document and communicate future treatment preferences. For Parkinson's disease (PD) and atypical parkinsonism (AP), ACP is particularly important because of disease complexity, symptom burden, the progressive nature of the disease, and cognitive decline, yet its implementation across care settings remains unclear.

title: Unveiling Structure‐Activity Relationship With Structurally Defined and Stabilized Cu‐Based Molecular Hybrid Electrocatalysts in CO2 Electroreduction
creator: Jian‐Hao Wu, Zhi‐Mei Luo, Rong‐Jie Guo, Jia‐Wei Wang, Bingbao Mei, Fu‐Jun Niu, Lie‐Jin Guo, Gangfeng Ouyang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Deciphering the structure‐activity relationship on Cu‐based electrocatalysts is critical to rationally optimize their performances in CO2 to multicarbon (C2+) conversion, which nonetheless remains highly challenging due to their ill‐defined and electrochemically unstable structures. Herein, this study explores Cu‐based molecular hybrids with defined structures to establish structure‐activity relationships in CO2‐C2+ electrocatalysis, where a Ni(II) phthalocyanine anchored on Cu2O nanocubes via 2‐(3‐thienyl)ethoxy groups outperforms its Co(II) analog and unmodified prototype in C2+ synthesis (78.3% selectivity, 330 mA.cm−2), rivaling top catalysts.

title: Comparison of two automated PGMI-based software tools for breast positioning quality assessment in DBT screening
creator: Gisella Gennaro, Stefano Trazzi, Valentina Bordon, Vania Galli
description: ObjectiveAutomated “Perfect/Good/Moderate/Inadequate” (PGMI)-based tools have been developed to standardize breast positioning quality assessment, but their agreement remains uncertain. This study compared two automated software systems applied to the same digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) screening cohort.Materials and methodsThis retrospective study included 778 women (3,112 views). Two software tools (SW1 and SW2) independently generated PGMI classifications and quality control (QC) feature outputs.

title: Fracture and Vertebral Augmentation Utilization Following Androgen Deprivation Therapy in Men With Prostate Cancer: A Propensity Score–matched Cohort Study
creator: Taha Taka, Carson Cummings, Sarah Meng, Andrew Miner, Graydon Dietrich, David Shin, Trupti Trivedi, Rory Goodwin, William Richardson, Olumide Danisa
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectiveTo investigate the association between androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), vertebral compression fracture (VCF) incidence, and subsequent vertebral augmentation (vertebroplasty/kyphoplasty) utilization in adult men with prostate cancer.MethodsAdult men with prostate cancer were stratified by ADT exposure and matched 1:1 to non-ADT controls on demographics, comorbidities, and bone health.

title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties
creator: Nasrin Ahmadinejad, Nahid Sadighi, Rassa Ghavami Modegh, Mehran Arab Ahmadi, Mohammadhosein Akhlaghpasand, Alireza Dizaji, Amin Rezaee, Maryam Rahmani, Arvin Arian, Fahimeh Zeinalkhani, Salome Maghsudlu, Saeedeh Shokri, Niloofar Pashaeifakhri, Hossein Ghanaati, Ali Sefidmouy, Mahdi Ghaznavi, Hamed D
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate an AI-based decision-support system for mammography interpretation, assessing its impact on diagnostic performance.Materials and methodsThis retrospective study analyzed 130,838 mammograms from 35,709 patients with confirmed follow-up outcomes across multiple centers, using the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) for external validation. Representing one of the largest datasets from the Middle East, it evaluates model generalizability in underrepresented populations.

title: Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer in Reaction of Catecholamines: Experimental and Computational Approach
creator: Ana Karković Marković, Mia Jovanić, Dijana Kolezarić, Viktor Pilepić
description: Biogenic catecholamines (dopamine, noradrenaline, adrenaline) exhibit a dual role in biological systems, acting as both endogenous antioxidants and potential sources of oxidative stress. The core of their antiradical activity is the catechol moiety that enables efficient radical scavenging via hydrogen and/or electron transfer.

title: Nitrogen‐Doped Mesoporous Carbon Loaded With Zn Single Atoms as a Catalyst for the Synthesis of 2,4(5)‐Diarylimidazoles
creator: Maryam Shojaei‐Asl, Mohsen Moradian
description: Single‐atom catalysts have emerged as highly effective alternatives to conventional metal catalysts due to their uniform active sites and superior catalytic performance. Stabilizing single zinc atoms on nitrogen‐doped mesoporous carbon (NMC) enhances their stability, selectivity, electrical conductivity, and compatibility with green chemistry principles.

title: Primary Hepatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: Systematic Review and Expert Pathologist Reappraisal Using the WHO 6th Edition Framework
creator: Marcello Maestri, Ottavia Cicerone, Alessandro Gambella, Federica Grillo, Stefano La Rosa, Silvia Uccella, Alessandro Vanoli
description: Primary hepatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (PHNENs) are exceedingly rare. Published evidence often lacks adequate clinicopathological support for a primary hepatic origin and uses inconsistent historical terminology. Previous reviews have pooled well‐differentiated neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), and mixed neuroendocrine–non‐neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs), despite differences in biology, prognosis, and management.

title: Improving survival and narrowing age disparities in mantle cell lymphoma across therapeutic eras
creator: Malak Munir, John L Vaughn, Sravani Rimmalapudi, Narendranath Epperla
description: s with the incorporation of rituximab, cytarabine-based induction and autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in selected patients [3], and Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) [4]. More recently, CAR-T therapies [5] have expanded options for relapsed/refractory disease, while randomized studies have challenged the necessity of ASCT in selected patients [6, 7].

title: Association of socioeconomic factors on mental health in children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities of genetic origin
creator: Irene O Lee, Jeanne Wolstencroft, Harriet Housby, Marianne B M van den Bree, Samuel J R A Chawner, Jeremy Hall, Michael J Owen, IMAGINE ID Consortium, David H Skuse
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChildren and young people (CYP) with intellectual developmental disability (IDD) have a high prevalence of mental health and behavioural problems, which might be influenced by socioeconomical status as well as the severity of their disabilities.

title: Resolution of proximal tubular dysfunction after liver transplantation in ATP8B1 deficiency: A case report
creator: Angela Marino, Nathalie Godefroid, Catherine De Magnée, Xavier Stephenne
description: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 1 (PFIC1), caused by ATP8B1 deficiency, is a multisystem disorder with extrahepatic manifestations; however, renal involvement has rarely been described. We report a child with genetically confirmed PFIC1 who underwent living donor liver transplantation (LT) for progressive liver disease.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Enlicitide in Hypercholesterolemia: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Muhammad Farhan, Muhammad Murtaza, Muhammad Mujtaba Rasool, Farah Khan, Hammad Amjad, Kuldeep Dalpat Rai, Sheikh Muhammad Ebtehaj Ali, Ahmed Asad Raza, Muhammad Ahmad Sohail, Abedin Samadi, Furqan Hassan
description: BackgroundAtherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global mortality, with low‐density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL‐C) reduction being the cornerstone of prevention. Despite effective therapies, many high‐risk patients do not achieve recommended LDL‐C targets. Enlicitide (MK‐0616), an oral proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, offers a potential alternative to injectable PCSK9‐directed therapies.

title: Self‐Efficacy, Healthy and Sustainable Lifestyle, and Life Satisfaction: An Integrated Model Accounting for Self‐Reported Recreational Physical Activity Participation Status in Veterinary Students
creator: Sevim Güllü, Alp Emre Yıldız, Maciej Witkowski, Hasan Hüseyin Arı, Ozan Gündemir
description: BackgroundVeterinary education is characterized by intensive curricula and demanding practical training, which may constrain students’ ability to maintain health‐promoting routines and sustainable lifestyle behaviors. In such contexts, general self‐efficacy—a psychological resource related to persistence and coping—may be associated with both lifestyle patterns and overall life satisfaction.

title: Real‐World Survival Outcomes of Venetoclax Combination Therapies in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Impact of Minimal Residual Disease Status and Antifungal Prophylaxis
creator: Mariarita Sciumè, Alessandro Bosi, Alfredo Marchetti, Fabio Serpenti, Pasquale De Roberto, Sonia Fabris, Francesco Versino, Elena Tagliaferri, Francesco Passamonti, Nicola Stefano Fracchiolla
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In recent years the addition of the oral BCL2 inhibitor venetoclax to hypomethylating agents (HMAs) has emerged as the standard‐of‐care for patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are not fit for intensive chemotherapy, significantly improving survival and quality‐of‐life. Venetoclax is metabolized mainly by cytochrome P450 3A4 enzymes and serves as a P‐glycoprotein substrate, which make it largely affected by interactions with drugs.

title: A Novel Plasma Biomarker hsa_circ_0080018 Drives DLBCL Progression via M2 Polarization of Tumor‐Associated Macrophages
creator: Yanfeng Liu, Yanan Gao, Chuanli Zhao
description: Noncoding RNAs, including circular RNAs (circRNAs), have been demonstrated to play vital roles in tumorigenesis. Uncovering the functions of circRNAs in tumorigenesis and their underlying regulatory mechanisms may suggest new approaches to the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for human cancer.

title: Coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodule presented as adrenal incidentaloma
creator: Du Hee Jung, Hyunjin Kim, Seung Eun Lee
description: Adrenal hemangiomas are rare benign vascular tumors, an uncommon cause of adrenal incidentalomas. We report a patient with coexisting adrenal hemangioma and aldosterone-producing micronodules within the same adrenal gland. A 67-year-old man was referred for an incidental left adrenal mass. Noncontrast computed tomography revealed a 1.6 × 1.4 cm lesion with an unenhanced attenuation value of 40 Hounsfield units.

title: Long-term cyclic ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone syndrome with extreme fluctuations and adrenal insufficiency
creator: Soon Young Choi, Hyounjung Chin, Soyeon Yoo, Sang Ah Lee, Gwanpyo Koh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A 77-year-old woman presented with worsening glycemic control and hypokalemia and was found to have adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-dependent hypercortisolism with loss of diurnal cortisol variation and failure of suppression on low- and high-dose dexamethasone suppression tests. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral adrenal enlargement, whereas pituitary magnetic resonance imaging and chest CT failed to identify a source of ACTH secretion, leading to a diagnosis of occult ectopic ACTH syndrome.

title: Biomachining in manufacturing: mechanisms, processes, applications and future perspectives
creator: Jingyu Song, Hui Huang, Weibin Shi
description: Biomachining (BM) is an emerging bio-assisted manufacturing approach that uses microbial metabolism and bioelectrochemical reactions to remove material under mild conditions. Due to its low mechanical loading and limited thermal effects, BM has potential in low-damage microfabrication, surface functionalization, microfluidic mold fabrication, abrasive tool dressing, and functional device modification.

title: An Explainable Self‐Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant‐Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting‐State EEG
creator: Pushpamala Ramaiah, Ibtesam Nomani, Hayam Ibrahim Asfour, Mirza R Baig, Maksudjan Yuldashev, Ibrokhim Sapaev, Zein Bassam Bani Younes, Sumit Sharma, Mahesh Manchanda, Mohamad Ahmad Saleem Khasawneh, Majid S Jabir
description: BackgroundResting‐state electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non‐invasive modality for investigating depressive symptoms; however, conventional deep‐learning methods often require large labeled datasets and provide limited interpretability. We developed an Explainable Self‐Supervised Temporal Transformer Network for participant‐level classification of BDI‐defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting‐state EEG.MethodsThe framework employed masked temporal modeling for self‐supervised pretraining followed by supervised fine‐tuning.

title: Exploring Vocabularies of Motive to Optimise Patient Engagement for Drug Development
creator: Julia Frost, Widening Engagement Patient Advisory Group, Jessica Mandizha, Chantal van den Dungen, Catherine Pope
description: Patient engagement in the drug development life cycle is becoming normalised, and the return on investment is being quantified. We sought to understand what motivates biotechnology organisations to undertake patient engagement throughout the drug development life cycle, to enable us to generate theoretically and empirically grounded knowledge to optimise patient engagement.

title: CRISPR-mediated gap-based replacement enables site-specific DNA lesion insertion into long DNA and nucleosomes
creator: Youngseo Kim, Soyeong An, Jimin Choi, Moonjung Choi, Gyeongjin Lee, Kei-ichi Takata, Roopesh Anand, Kyungjae Myung, Ja Yil Lee
description: Defined DNA lesions are essential substrates for dissecting DNA repair mechanisms, yet existing approaches remain limited in positional flexibility, lesion diversity, efficiency, or compatibility with long and chromatinized DNA. Here, we present CGRID (CRISPR-mediated Gap-based Replacement for Insertion of DNA damage), a programmable strategy for site-specific installation of DNA lesions into long DNA and nucleosomes.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Green Laser Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation and Factors Associated with Surgical Failure: A Retrospective Observational Study
creator: Yoshiaki Takahashi, Shun Nakayama, Akira Imai, Junya Kitahara, Shinji Kakihara, Takao Hirano, Toshinori Murata
description: PurposeWe evaluated the 1-year outcomes of green laser endoscopic cyclophotocoagulation (ECP), a newly developed procedure approved in Japan.Patients and MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 29 eyes of 26 patients who underwent green laser ECP. Intraocular pressure (IOP), glaucoma medication burden, and laser flare were evaluated preoperatively and at 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months postoperatively.

title: Oral Upadacitinib Combined with Phototherapy for Progressive Vitiligo in 7-Year-Old Children: A Two-Case Report
creator: Yu Jiang, Zhirong Shu, Shilin Deng, Tingnan Chen, Xiaohong Lin, Jingyao Liang, Yaping Tang
description: We report two 7-year-old children with progressive vitiligo despite prior topical therapy and phototherapy; one patient had also received low-dose systemic corticosteroid therapy. Oral upadacitinib, a selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor, was initiated at 15 mg once daily in both patients in combination with phototherapy.

title: Structural and Vascular Findings in Autologous Retinal Transplantation for Macular Hole
creator: Jad Madani, Rami Madani, Timothy Mayotte, Ahmad Zeido, Tarek Alasil
description: Purpose:To describe the fluorescein angiography (FA) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) findings in autologous retinal transplantation for refractory full-thickness macular hole (FTMH).Methods:A single case was reviewed.Results:A 71-year-old Hispanic man presented with a refractory FTMH for which internal limiting membrane peel and gas tamponade had previously failed. The axial length was 23.

title: Scale‐space image analysis for mapping spotted knapweed in grassland ecosystems
creator: Shohreh Sahebi, David J. Hill
description: PremiseThis study investigates the value of scale‐space representations of spatial features for the identification and mapping of invasive plants using high‐resolution multispectral imagery. Scale‐space representations combine the two‐dimensional spatial domain with a third dimension representing spatial scale, such that features can be represented across both space and image spatial resolution.

title: Reprocessing Mass Spectra from Therapeutic Drug Monitoring to Unveil Proton Pump Inhibitor Use and Quantify Phenoconversion of Escitalopram Metabolism in CYP2C19‐Genotyped Patients
creator: Kristine Hole, Birgit M Wollmann, Julia Carolin Stingl, Espen Molden
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Escitalopram is a frequently prescribed antidepressant drug. CYP2C19 genotype is a major determinant of escitalopram metabolism and treatment outcome. However, real‐life studies show a high degree of genotype–phenotype mismatch in escitalopram metabolism. The present study aimed to identify comedication with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and quantify phenoconversion of escitalopram metabolism in CYP2C19‐genotyped patients by reprocessing high‐resolution mass spectra from therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) analyses. Patients were included from a combined TDM/pharmacogenetics (PGx) laboratory facility in Oslo, Norway.

title: Chrysanthemum Morifolium–Derived Nanovesicles Reduce Lactate‐Associated Histone Lactylation and Modulate Microglia‐Mediated Neuroinflammation in Sepsis‐Associated Encephalopathy
creator: Kaiqiang Li, Xuling Luo, Xiaoting Zhang, Chengwen He, Wei Xu, Aibo Xu, Shushan Hua, Liping Wang, Liang Ma, Ke Hao, Youmin Ying, Zhen Wang
description: Sepsis‐associated encephalopathy (SAE)—a complication of the central nervous system in patients with sepsis—markedly diminishes cognitive functions and is linked to hippocampal neuritis–induced injury. Plant exosome‐like nanovesicles can transport proteins, lipids, and molecular compounds between neural cells and the periphery, thereby modulating target cells.

title: Development of Versatile Nanoparticle System for Efficient Drug Delivery into Pulmonary Endothelium
creator: Afzaal N Mohammed, Zicheng Deng, Arnab Misra, Marcus Orzabal, Ananya Kondapally, Enhong Li, Jonathan Do, Ying‐Wei Lan, Fatemeh Kohram, Hunter Blackburn, Andreas Damianos, Tanya V Kalin, Vladimir V Kalinichenko
description: Drug delivery precisely to the pulmonary vasculature represents a formidable challenge. Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (PARDS) is an urgent public health concern accounting for high mortality and long‐term morbidity due to severe damage to lung endothelial cells (ECs). Advanced target‐specific therapeutic interventions to protect lung vasculature in PARDS are in dire need.

title: Targeting Macrophage STING O‐GlcNAcylation via Small‐Molecule Allosteric Modulation for Psoriasis Therapy
creator: Fang‐Fang Zhuo, Cheng‐Chen Hou, Wei Wang, Ya‐Xuan Zhu, Ling Li, Li‐Juan Liu, Chuan‐Jian Lu, Peng‐Fei Tu, Yang Liu, Rui‐Zhi Zhao, Ke‐Wu Zeng
description: STING undergoes distinct post‐translational modifications in autoimmune disorders, particularly in psoriasis. However, selectively targeting these disease‐associated STING modifications remains a major therapeutic challenge. Here, we show that macrophage STING O‐GlcNAcylation is a critical driver of psoriatic inflammation and identify the natural small‐molecule paeoniflorin (PF) as a selective inhibitor of STING O‐GlcNAcylation.

title: Valuing student voices: a qualitative study on fair recognition and compensation practices for student partners in mental health research
creator: Sapolnach Prompiengchai, Lexi Ewing, Emma McCann, Phuc Tran, Kristin Cleverley
description: BackgroundPost-secondary student mental health research increasingly calls for students to be engaged as equal partners, yet there is a lack of guidance on how to recognize and compensate their contributions. This study examines how student partners’ contributions to post-secondary student mental health research should be recognized through qualitative insights from diverse interest groups.

title: Epigenetics of generalized internet use disorder including data on overuse of social media: a closer look at the SLC6A4, NR3C1 and OXT genes
creator: Christian Montag, Markus Kiefer, Bernhard J. Connemann, Thomas Kammer, Simon Sanwald
description: BackgroundOnly few studies so far have investigated the molecular underpinnings of Internet Use Disorders (IUD), which can shed light on the neurochemical basis of excessive online behaviors. There are even less epigenetic studies in this research field, and longitudinal evidence is even more scarce.

title: Absence of Subliminal Body‐Image Priming Effects in Anorexia Nervosa
creator: Jana Boettner, Benjamin Mosch, Sabine Steins‐Loeber, Martin Diers
description: ObjectiveSociocultural and cognitive–neurobiological accounts suggest that automatic processing of body‐related cues may contribute to distorted body representation in anorexia nervosa (AN). This study tested whether subliminally presented body‐image cues modulate explicit evaluations of normal‐weight female bodies in women with AN compared to healthy controls (HC).

title: Re‐Thinking Electronic Circuit Design Through Emerging Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors
creator: Jens Trommer, Juan P Martinez, Yuxuan He, Giulio Galderisi, Katrin Pingen, Eduardo Sergio Oliveros‐Mata, Lisa Tellis, Cigdem Cakirlar, Christoph Beyer, Brojogopal Sapui, Joachim Knoch, Klaus Hofmann, Sandro Carrara, Eugenio Cantatore, Max C Lemme, Ian O'Connor, Akash Kumar, Andre Heinzig, Thomas Mik
description: Reconfigurable field‐effect transistors, short RFETs, are a unique class of emerging electronic devices that merge n‐type, p‐type, and ambipolar operation modes into a single element. Unlike conventional MOSFETs, the dominant carrier type in RFETs is purely defined by electrostatics and can be dynamically changed at runtime.

title: Disability after non‐cardiac surgery – patient‐centred outcomes and resource utilisation after non‐cardiac surgery (PACORUS): a prospective multicentre cohort study*
creator: Alexandra Stroda, Jan Larmann, Andrea Icks, Mark Coburn, Marc Moritz Berger, Alexander Mathes, Robert Werdehausen, Sarah Thaler, Sebastian Ziemann, Claudia Neumann, Sebastian Roth, René M'Pembele, Theresa Tenge, Celine Bußhoff, Madeleine Rallis, Giovanna Lurati Buse, the PACORUS‐D Investigators
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryIntroductionThe Standardised Endpoints in Perioperative Medicine Initiative recommends the 12‐item WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 to measure postoperative functional impairment. However, evidence describing long‐term postoperative disability, particularly at 1 year, remains limited. This study aimed to: describe disability up to 1 year after non‐cardiac, non‐neurosurgical procedures; examine associations between periprocedural risk, postoperative complications and new‐onset disability; and evaluate associations between social support, delirium, and frailty and postoperative disability.MethodsWe conducted a prospective, multicentre cohort study.

title: Estimation of glomerular filtration rate by standard renal CT imaging
creator: Kristoffer Huitfeldt Sola, Helena Genberg, Joshua Webster-Ford, Anders Ullén, Torkel B Brismar
description: ObjectivesTo develop and evaluate a method to predict glomerular filtration rate (GFR) from clinical renal CT.Materials and methodsMedical records of adult living kidney donors operated between 2013 and 2022 and patients considered for neoadjuvant cisplatin prior to cystectomy between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed.

title: Digital transformation of clinical trials with remote patient monitoring solutions
creator: Elisabeth Piault, Ramya Palacholla, Simon Pulman-Jones, Emmett Alton Sartor, Sergio Simón, Jill Bell
description: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) is becoming increasingly feasible to implement in clinical trials. A framework is presented for developing RPM digital solutions incorporating the needs and perspectives of patients and healthcare professionals, and regulatory requirements/guidance. This framework is illustrated with recent examples of RPM deployments in the context of skin toxicities and stomatitis.

title: Current status and future outlook of artificial intelligence and automation in intravenous infusion systems
creator: Islam M Ibrahim, Rahma A Elkomy, Merna A Mohamed, Fatemah A Farok, Roaa E Emam, Salma A kamel, Reham M Asem
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The combination of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and wearable biosensors is transforming healthcare by allowing continuous, real-time monitoring and more intelligent clinical decision-making. This review explores AI-driven monitoring, smart intravenous (IV) infusion automation, and wearable biosensors, and proposes Intelligent IV Automation and Smart Patient Synchronization (INFUSYNC), a conceptual framework synchronizing monitoring, automated fluid delivery, and predictive analytics.

title: Skill-guided agentic reasoning enables longitudinal synthesis of myeloma records at expert-level concordance
creator: Johannes Moll, Jannik Lübberstedt, Christoph Nuernbergk, Jacob Stroh, Luisa Mertens, Anna Purcarea, Christopher Zirn, Zeineb Benchaaben, Fabian Drexel, Hartmut Häntze, Anirudh Narayanan, Friedrich Puttkammer, Andrei Zhukov, Jacqueline Lammert, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Markus Graf, Marion Högner, Marcu
description: Patients with multiple myeloma accumulate hundreds of clinical documents over years of sequential therapy, and every treatment decision depends on synthesis across that history. Whether large language model–based systems can match expert agreement on this task, and where they fail, has not been established.

title: Small viruses reveal bidirectional evolution between HK97-fold viruses and encapsulins via procapsids
creator: Abelardo Aguilar, Ingrid Miranda Perez, Omer Nadel, Stephen Nayfach, Luis Ruiz Pestana, Anca M Segall, Forest L Rohwer, Simon Roux, Simon White, Antoni Luque
description: The HK97-fold is an ancient, conserved protein structure that assembles protein shells, forming the capsids of Duplodnaviria viruses and prokaryotic biochemical compartments called encapsulsins. It has been proposed that encapsulins evolved from HK97-fold viruses. But the higher complexity of viral capsids represents a biophysical paradox in the evolution of HK97-fold protein shells.

title: Host‐specific and deterministic microbiome assembly in major coleopteran stored‐grain pests
creator: Abrar Muhammad, Xiaoqiang Shen, Lichao Chen, Enhui Guo, Huarui Zhang, Xiaoyu Lei, Chao Sun, Jianhua Lv, Yongqi Shao
description: Dual DNA‐ and RNA‐based sequencing profiled the microbiomes of five major coleopteran stored‐grain pests and their wheat flour substrate. The microbiomes differed significantly among hosts and from flour, yet 11 core bacterial and 9 core fungal taxa were shared across hosts. RNA data revealed host‐specific active microbiota. Deterministic processes dominated community assembly, exceeding 90% in Rhyzopertha dominica and Oryzaephilus surinamensis.

title: Effects on health and antioxidant status of oral supplementation of hazelnut skin extract in dairy calves with neonatal diarrhea: a randomized clinical trial in hospitalized patients
creator: Antonio Boccardo, Martina Sannazzaro, Giulia Sala, Elisa Gazzola, Ilaria Martucci, Giulio Curone, Marta Castrica, Vincenzo Ferrulli, Claudio Forte, Rosangela Odore, Giulia Gardini, Davide Pravettoni
description: Neonatal calf diarrhea (NCD) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality in calves. Growing concern about antimicrobial resistance has spurred interest in phytotherapeutic alternatives, particularly polyphenol-rich extracts. Hazelnut skin (HS), a by-product of the confectionery sector, is a sustainable and underutilized source of polyphenols; however, its therapeutic efficacy in calves with NCD remains insufficiently investigated.

title: Irritability in Adult Depression and Anxiety: A Clinically Useful Signal Amid an Imprecise Construct
creator: Michael Uebel
description: A brief consideration of the conceptual and diagnostic tidiness of irritability associated with depression and anxiety in adults. Despite evidence for its conceptual untidiness, there are practical issues that the clinician may consider when diagnosing and treating depression or anxiety. A 34-year-old man presents to his family physician reporting poor sleep and a “short fuse.” He denies sadness.

title: Semi‐Artificial Photosynthesis Enables Light‐Driven Biomanufacturing in Non‐Photosynthetic Bacteria
creator: Jie Zheng, Anqi Tong, Wenxin Li, Meng Qiao, Yang Gu, Muhammad Sohail, Shan He, Sheng Yang, Xing Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Semiconductor biohybrid systems integrate microbial biosynthesis with semiconductor light harvesting to sustainably power energy‐intensive chemical production. Although such systems have been widely explored in photosynthetic bacteria, extending them to non‐photosynthetic biomanufacturing chassis such as Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis) remains substantially more challenging, owing to peptidoglycan‐induced nanoparticle aggregation and mass‐transfer limitations, cytotoxicity, and inefficient interfacial electron transfer from loose adsorption between inorganic semiconductors and cells. Here, we propose a non‐invasive enhancement strategy that leverages the endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S) pathway of the B.

title: Retrograde access revascularization in chronic limb threatening ischaemia
creator: Yujia Gao, Lorenzo Patrone, Neil Davies, Anthie Papadopoulou, Nick Woodward, Janice Tsui, Mark Portou, Shanka Benaragama, Conrad von Stempel
description: PurposeChronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major amputation, mortality and comorbidity that can make conventional femoral access challenging or contraindicated; in particular in patients with recent groin surgery, infection, previous aorto-bifemoral stent reconstruction, hostile groins, or unfavourable body habitus. Tibio-pedal arterial minimally invasive retrograde revascularisation (TAMI) provides an alternative access strategy.

title: Poor mental health days and depressive disorders comparing non-caregivers, informal non-cancer caregivers, and informal caregivers of cancer patients: BRFSS 2022–23
creator: Jeanne M Ward, John R Blosnich, Victoria Champion
description: PurposeInformal caregivers are increasing in number, especially those caring for cancer patients, and caregiving can affect both patient outcomes and caregiver well-being. This study sought to elucidate whether the mental health outcomes differed among informal cancer caregivers, informal non-cancer caregivers, and non-caregivers.

title: Prevalence and determinants of cesarean section delivery among Somali women: a multivariable analysis of a nationally representative survey
creator: Fatima Mohamud Ahmed
description: BackgroundCesarean section is a life-saving obstetric intervention when medically indicated, yet access remains severely limited in Somalia, where maternal morbidity and mortality are high.Objective(s)To determine the magnitude of cesarean section delivery and identify factors associated with its utilization among Somali women using nationally representative survey data.

title: Checkpoint‐Directed Glycoengineering Reprograms the Vascular Lumen for Siglec‐Mediated Immune Regulation
creator: Md Mohosin Rana, Javairia F. Rahim, Aaron P. Bernstein, Peyman Malek Mohammadi Nouri, Lyann Sim, Winnie Enns, Jenice M. Dumlao, Haiming D. Luo, Irina Chafeeva, Hong‐Ming Chen, Aizhou Wang, Jiao‐Jing Wang, Edward N. Schmidt, Zheng Jenny Zhang, Marcelo Cypel, Christopher Nguan, Matthew S. Macauley, St
description: Dysregulated immune activation at the vascular surface drives microvascular inflammation and tissue injury in many diseases, yet current therapies do not restore immune regulation at the blood‐vessel interface. Terminal sialic acids engage inhibitory Siglec receptors on circulating immune cells and function as endogenous glyco‐immune checkpoint ligands.

title: Concise ethnobotanical review and botanical pharmacognosy of turmeric rhizome (Curcuma longa L.)
creator: Roy T Upton
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ContextTurmeric (Curcuma longa L. Zingiberaceae) is a highly valued botanical medicine worldwide and has emerged as among the best-selling herbal products in North America.ObjectivePresented an ethnobotanical record of turmeric use to present a context for this edition on turmeric.MethodsInformation was primarily compiled from online sources including PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Science Direct using ‘turmeric’, ‘curcuma’, and ‘curcuma longa’ as search terms; No time limit was specified.

title: Mitochondrial Quality Control in Degenerative Musculoskeletal Diseases: Signaling Networks and Therapeutic Landscapes
creator: Haiyang Gao, Zhangrong Cheng, Xianglong Chen, Wenbo Wu, Wang Wu, Zimu Yu, Cao Yang, Yukun Zhang
description: Degenerative musculoskeletal disorders, including osteoarthritis (OA), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and osteoporosis (OP), are increasingly viewed as disorders of mitochondrial quality control (MQC) rather than passive mechanical wear. The MQC network, comprising mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy‐biogenesis coupling, and inter‐organelle communication, organizes the aging‐inflammation‐metabolism axis.

title: Enzyme‐Linked Cycloaddition Assay (ELCA) for Rapid, Ultra‐Sensitive Monitoring of Secreted Sialoglycoproteins
creator: Jon Lundstrøm, Jingmei Yang, Daniel Bojar
description: Glycosylation of proteins is central to cell signaling, immune function, and pathogen interactions, yet existing methods for monitoring glycan changes require specialized instrumentation and primarily report on membrane‐anchored, rather than secreted, glycoproteins. Here, we present the Enzyme‐Linked Cycloaddition Assay (ELCA), a click chemistry‐based platform for ultra‐sensitive detection and semi‐quantitative analysis of secreted sialoglycoproteins.

title: Monolithic fabrication of 1S1R cross-point device using single GexTe1-x material by controlling composition between memory and threshold switching
creator: Young-Min Kim, Sang-Heon Park, Jihye Lee, Sangyeop Kim, Siwon Park, Jong-Souk Yeo
description: Three-dimensional (3D) integrated one-selector one-resistor (1S1R) cross-point arrays are emerging as a leading next-generation memory technology. Achieving both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching within a single material system offers tremendous potential for simplifying fabrication. This study demonstrates that the memory and threshold switching behavior of germanium-telluride (GexTe1-x) devices can be precisely tuned by controlling their atomic ratio.

title: Experimental Evaluation and Optimisation of Sealed‐Tube Combustion Methods for Silicate Nitrogen Extraction
creator: Fawn S. M. Holland, Sami Mikhail, Kirsten W. Y. Wong, Abu Saeed Baidya, Eva E. Stüeken
description: RationaleNitrogen (N) abundance and isotopic compositions in silicate rocks are commonly measured by sealed‐tube continuous‐flow isotope ratio mass spectrometry (CF‐IRMS), but combustion protocols vary widely. It remains uncertain how the quality of data obtained from different published methods compares for differing sample types.

title: Barriers in Accessing Postpartum Mental Health Care and Coping Strategies Among Migrant and Refugee Women With Postpartum Depression
creator: Marjia Sultana, Ruheea Taskin Ruhee, Miraj Ahmed Bhuiyan, Towhid Hasan
description: BackgroundPostpartum depression (PPD) significantly impacts the well‐being of mothers and their families, with migrant and refugee women being particularly vulnerable due to unique stressors and limited access to care. Hence, this scoping review examines the specific barriers refugee and migrant women experiencing PPD face in accessing mental healthcare, as well as the diverse informal support strategies they rely on.

title: Double‐Antibody Sandwich Enzyme‐Linked Immunosorbent Assay for Detecting Feline Coronavirus Infection
creator: Bo Dong, Weijie Zou, Wenqian Hu, Hongxiao Wu, Yaqing Jing, Fuquan Xie, Shuo Zhang, Weiming Lin
description: ObjectivesDouble‐antibody sandwich enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay (DAS‐ELISA) is a simple and accurate method for detecting viral pathogens. This study established a DAS‐ELISA for the diagnosis of feline coronavirus (FCoV).MethodsIn this study, DAS‐ELISA was performed using FCoV S‐protein rabbit polyclonal and mouse monoclonal antibodies. The optimal reaction conditions were determined using the chessboard method.

title: Real‐World Metabolic Improvements in Women With and Without Polyendocrine Metabolic Syndrome via a Multidisciplinary Telehealth Care Platform
creator: Heather G. Huddleston, Rachel Blank, Nandita Sommers, Nicole Hellman, Felice Ramallo, Tiffany Pham, Karla Lindquist
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate metabolic outcomes in women with and without Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS, formerly Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS))) receiving multidisciplinary care through a women's health telehealth platform that combines physician and registered dietitian support.MethodsRetrospective cohort analysis of 919 women with BMI ≥ 25 initiating care in 2024, with ≥ 6 months follow‐up (mean 9.6 months).

title: Nudix hydrolase 15 deficiency and azathioprine toxicity in a liver transplant recipient: A case report
creator: Jenny Q. Nguyen, Natalie Rodriguez, Kimberly A. Chapman, Matthew A. Deardorff, Keith Z. Hazleton
description: Thiopurines, such as azathioprine (AZA), are among the immunosuppressants used to prevent allograft rejection. Thiopurines are metabolized by thiopurine S‐methyltransferase (TPMT) and nudix hydrolase 15 (NUDT15) enzymes, and their functions are highly influenced by genetic variation. We present a 6‐year‐old female with recurrent acute cellular rejection and steroid‐induced glaucoma due to high‐dose corticosteroid therapy.

title: Clinical, safety, and patient-reported outcomes associated with second-line and later therapies in primary biliary cholangitis: A systematic review
creator: Marco Carbone, David Jones, Oyinkan Solanke, Rikke Brandt, Taryn Krause, Darren Asquith, Alex Pashley, Sonia Shaw, Emma Worthington, Jörn M Schattenberg
description: Background:Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a rare, chronic, cholestatic disease that can result in cirrhosis, liver failure, and death. While biochemical markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and total bilirubin (TB) measure disease activity and progression, definitions of biochemical response vary.

title: Open-label extension study of leniolisib in activated PI3Kδ syndrome: Long-term efficacy and safety
creator: V. Koneti Rao, Anna Šedivá, Virgil A.S.H. Dalm, Alessandro Plebani, Catharina Schuetz, Anna Shcherbina, Antonio Trizzino, Yulia Zharankova, Alanvin Orpia, Elaine Kulm, Julia Körholz, Vassilios Lougaris, Yulia Rodina, Jason Bradt, Anurag Relan, Gulbu Uzel
description: Leniolisib, a PI3Kδ inhibitor, improves the pathophysiology of APDS. This publication demonstrates the safety and efficacy of leniolisib in patients with APDS ≥12 years of age receiving up to 7 years of treatment, illustrating a positive tolerability profile and sustained disease burden reduction.

title: Determinants of Age‐Appropriate Childhood Immunization Uptake: A Cross‐Sectional Study of Caregiver, Child, Knowledge, Access, and Attitudinal Factors
creator: Aruwa Simon Ayigu, Stephen Olaide Aremu, Adamu Ishaku Akyala, Abdillahi Abdi Barkhadle
description: BackgroundChildhood immunization is among the most cost‐effective public health strategies for reducing under‐five morbidity and mortality. However, full immunization coverage for age remains suboptimal in many low‐ and middle‐income countries due to factors related to caregivers, children, health systems, and sociocultural contexts.

title: RiboBA: a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification across diverse ribosome profiling protocols
creator: Junyu Bai, Ruolin Yang
description: By mapping ribosome-protected fragments genome-wide, ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) has uncovered extensive translation beyond conventional coding sequences, revealing non-canonical ORFs (ncORFs) with roles in diverse biological processes. However, robust ncORF identification remains challenging when Ribo-seq datasets exhibit attenuated periodicity. Protocol-induced biases during library construction is an important contributor to this loss, yet most ORF callers do not explicitly model these distortions.

title: Rare Feline Gingival Extramedullary Plasmacytoma: Clinical Application of Electrochemotherapy for Local Control
creator: Seulgi Hwang, Hayoung Ryu, Dong‐In Jung, DoHyeon Yu, Kyu‐Woan Cho, Hyeona Bae
description: Feline extramedullary plasmacytoma (EMP) is an uncommon plasma cell neoplasm typically regarded as biologically benign; however, its clinical behaviour may be heterogeneous. This case report describes an aggressive gingival EMP in a 14‐year‐old neutered male Turkish Angora cat, characterised by alveolar bone lysis and cytologically confirmed regional lymph node metastasis in the absence of systemic features consistent with multiple myeloma.

title: PRAME predicting outcome in uveal melanoma
creator: Sally Owens, Naomi Walsh, Noel Horgan, Patrick Murtagh, Katie Hanratty, Grainne Finegan, Laura Ivers, John Crown, Susan Kennedy
description: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intra‐ocular malignancy in adults and carries a high risk of metastatic disease, affecting approximately 50% of patients despite advances in local tumour control. PRAME (PReferentially expressed Antigen in MElanoma) has emerged as a marker for metastatic risk; however, evidence is largely derived from mRNA expression studies rather than routine immunohistochemistry (IHC).

title: A self‐retaining mouth prop for intraoral access during periodontal surgery in rat models: A technical note
creator: Saravanan Sampoornam Pape Reddy, Delfin Lovelina Francis, Vivek Kumar Thakur, Balaji Manohar, Shaili Pradhan, Shesh Rai
description: BackgroundRodent models are widely used in oral health research; however, maintaining stable and effective intraoral retraction in the small oral cavity is challenging. Manual retraction methods often lead to procedural instability, operator fatigue, and increased tissue trauma during rodent oral surgery.MethodsA stainless‐steel wire mouth prop incorporating helices for self‐retention and auxiliary lateral soft tissue displacement prongs was fabricated.

title: Short‐Term Outcomes of Transanal Total Mesorectal Excision for Rectal Cancer: A Multicenter Propensity Score‐Matched Analysis Comparing Patients With and Without Preoperative Neoadjuvant Therapy
creator: Takafumi Shima, Hiroki Hamamoto, Takeru Matsuda, Ichiro Takemasa, Keitaro Tanaka, Toshiki Mukai, Jun Watanabe, Sang‐Woong Lee, Seiichiro Yamamoto, Takeshi Naitoh, Akihiro Kondo, Akihiro Kondo, Akinobu Taketomi, Akiyoshi Kanazawa, Atsushi Ogura, Chikayoshi Tani, Gunpei Yoshimatsu, Hideki Endo, Hideya
description: AimTo evaluate the association between preoperative neoadjuvant therapy and short‐term outcomes of transanal total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent transanal total mesorectal excision at 26 Japanese institutions between 2012 and 2019. Patients who received neoadjuvant therapy were matched 1:1 with patients who did not. Perioperative, postoperative, and pathological outcomes were compared.

title: The Scaleup Costs, Size, and Statistics Challenge to Democratic Deliberation on Health Policy
creator: Nir Eyal
description: Current fashion supports aligning health policy with the recommendations of deliberative forums, or mini‐publics. These forums' participants are selected randomly from the general public (sometimes with overrepresentation of direct stakeholders or of underrepresented sectors). After being informed and exchanging public reasons with fellow participants under discursive rules that engage all as equals, participants vote on and sometimes rank policy recommendations.

title: Preparation for bias conversations among Black/African American, Latinx, and Asian parent‐adolescent dyads: A qualitative content analysis of observational data
creator: Frances M Lobo, Michelle Y Martin Romero, Paula Sanchez‐Hernandez, Kimberly Cang, Lisa Kiang, Stephanie Irby Coard, Gabriela Livas
description: Preparation for bias conversations may be critical in raising youth awareness of racial‐ethnic discrimination, fostering a strong racial‐ethnic identity, and teaching them how to cope or respond to racialized stressors. However, the literature relies almost exclusively on survey approaches, limiting understanding of how these conversations actually unfold in real time.

title: [Expression of Concern] Anti-metastatic effect of jolkinolide B and the mechanism of activity in breast cancer MDA-MB-231 cells
creator: Chao Sun, Hongxia Cui, Hongyan Yang, Xiaohui Du, Liling Yue, Jicheng Liu, Yu Lin
description: a panels contained an overlapping section of data, suggesting that these data had been derived from the same original source, even though the results from differently performed experiments were intended to have been portrayed. The authors have been contacted by the Editorial Office to offer an explanation for the apparently erroneous assembly of the data in Fig.

title: Cyanobacterial conversion of CO2 to bio-based diols and downstream valorization: biological basis, upgrading strategies, and applications
creator: Changou Pan, Han Chen, Mingyue Zhang, Shaoxiong He, Zhiqun Lin
description: Cyanobacteria have attracted growing interest as photosynthetic cell factories for the conversion of carbon dioxide (CO2) into renewable chemicals because they directly use solar energy and inorganic carbon under mild aqueous conditions. Recent advances in chassis development, genome engineering, carbon-partition control, and photobioreactor design have expanded the scope of cyanobacterial CO2-to-chemical biomanufacturing.

title: Socio-Demographic Inequalities in the Burden of Low Back Pain Across Development Strata: Sex-Specific, Age-Standardized Trends in Prevalence, Incidence and Disability from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, 2003–2023
creator: Mohammed M Alshehri, Mohammad Abu Shaphe, Rashid Ali Beg, Aafreen Aafreen, Shahul Hameed Pakkir Mohamed, G Shankar Ganesh, Abdur Raheem Khan, Monira I Aldhahi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLow back pain (LBP) is a leading contributor to non-fatal disability and rehabilitation needs worldwide. Monitoring trends across sociodemographic strata is important for understanding whether the disability burden is changing equitably across health systems.PurposeTo examine temporal trends and socio-demographic inequalities in the burden of LBP across Socio-demographic Index (SDI) groups from 2003 to 2023 using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates.MethodsGBD 2023 estimates for LBP prevalence, incidence and years lived with disability (YLDs) were analysed across High, High-middle, Middle, Low-middle and

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Retrospective Prediction Model for Fungal Infections in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
creator: Xiaolan Chen, Mingyan Wu, Jingjing Wang, Hongbin Jiang, Shanmei Wang
description: BackgroundPatients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are at an elevated risk of fungal infections, yet reliable tools for early risk stratification are lacking. This study aimed to analyze the risk factors associated with fungal infections in patients with COPD and to develop a predictive model.

title: Standardized Clinical Photography for Improving Dermatological Treatment Adherence (Scoping Review): Evidence Landscape and Research Gaps
creator: Naisu Cao, Yi Hu, Xiaqing Wang, Siqi Wu, Mengjie Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Treatment adherence remains suboptimal across chronic dermatological conditions, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and increased healthcare burden. Despite the established role of standardized clinical photography in clinical documentation, its specific application as an adherence-promoting intervention remains poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the literature on photographic feedback in dermatology, identify research gaps, and propose methodological recommendations for future randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

title: Ultrasound‐Triggered piRNA Delivery Using Biomimetic Phase‐Changeable Nanoparticles for Theranostics of Myocardial Infarction
creator: Yajun Zhang, Hongzhao Qi, Yanyan Yang, Feng Wang, Tiantian Han, Yanbei Lei, Xiaolu Li, Zhibin Wang, Hua Qu, Tao Yu, Pin Sun
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity, and effective strategies to prevent adverse remodeling are limited. Here, we identify piR‐1873 as a cardioprotective piRNA that is down‐regulated in MI patients, mouse models, and H2O2‐treated cardiomyocytes. Serum piR‐1873 levels correlated with MI biomarkers, suggesting its potential as a complementary biomarker, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8389. Mechanistically, piR‐1873 directly targeted Usp2 and inhibited RIP1/RIP3/MLKL‐mediated necroptosis.

title: FRIENDS – friendship-based regulation of individual emotions in networks in daily situations: An EMA study on partner–motive pairing and social outcomes in adult friendships
creator: Paula Schott, Katharina Enser, Martin Weiß
description: BackgroundInterpersonal emotion regulation depends not only on which strategy is used but on whom people turn to. Previous work suggests that individuals select regulation partners according to their perceived competence for a specific emotion. We examined whether this extends to regulatory motives, and whether partner–motive pairing is associated with better interaction outcomes, higher psychological well-being, and lower social loneliness.

title: Immediate effects of spinal manipulation, exercise therapy, and open-label placebo on lifting performance and pain in individuals with chronic non-specific back pain: a motion laboratory-based crossover randomized controlled trial
creator: Fredrik Borg, Filip Gedin, Erika Franzén, Wilhelmus Johannes Andreas Grooten
description: BackgroundChronic non-specific back pain (CBP) is a leading cause of disability worldwide and is commonly associated with limitations in movements such as lifting. Although spinal manipulation (SMT) and exercise therapy (ET) are recommended treatments for CBP, their effects on objectively measured movement performance remain insufficiently explored. Open-label placebo (OLP) has gained attention for engaging placebo-related mechanisms ethically.

title: Yoda1‐Functionalized Nanozymes Coordinate Piezo1 Activation and Mitochondrial Protection to Reprogram the Diabetic Osteoimmune Micromilieu and Promote Vascularized Bone Repair
creator: Qing‐Song Deng, Ang Wang, Ren Zhang, Xu‐Ran Li, Po‐Lin Liu, Shu‐Hang He, Zi‐Yin Han, Zhi‐Han Shen, Zhan‐Ying Wei, Chang‐Ru Zhang, Fei Wang, Helen Dawes, Jian Lu, Tong‐He Zhu, Jin‐Zhong Zhao, Shang‐Chun Guo, Shi‐Cong Tao
description: Despite advances in bone tissue engineering, repairing diabetic bone defects remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present an innovative strategy for diabetic bone regeneration, the BCPG‐MF@Y scaffold, which features diamond lattices of 3D‐printed biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP) integrating porous gelatine methacryloyl (pGelMA) hydrogels embedded with Yoda1‐functionalized manganese dioxide‐ferritin (MF@Y) biomimetic nanozymes.

title: Accounting for response styles in rating data using IRT and IRTree models: A tutorial in R with applications to self-reported metacognitive competence
creator: Thorsten Meiser, Esther Ulitzsch, Mirka Henninger
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Response styles refer to individual differences in the use of the item response format irrespective of item content. They include tendencies to favor or avoid midpoint or extreme response categories, which can distort the measurement of latent constructs. This tutorial provides an overview of IRT and IRTree models that accommodate response style factors, allowing researchers to analyze response-style effects and adjust latent-trait estimates for potential bias.

title: Development of a genetic transformation system in Echinochloa phyllopogon by particle bombardment
creator: Takahiro Gondo, Manami Sugahara, Hwan May Ng, Kentaro Yasuda, Satoshi Iwakami
description: Key MessageA stable particle bombardment-mediated transformation system was developed for Echinochloa phyllopogon, providing a platform for functional analysis of genes involved in herbicide metabolic detoxification.AbstractEchinochloa phyllopogon is a major C4 grass weed that causes serious yield losses in paddy fields and has evolved resistance to multiple herbicides.

title: Not that cloze: Sentence constraint is influenced by language and language dominance
creator: Ana Bautista, Clara D Martin
description: In the fields of language processing and prediction, cloze tests are used to establish sentence constraint norms. The validity of cloze test results depends heavily on how closely the pre-test population matches the main study population, and yet there is limited evidence on how sociolinguistic variables may influence sentence constraint.

title: Selective inhibition of IL-6 trans-signalling reveals distinct mechanisms of human classic and trans-signalling receptor-complex formation
creator: Emelie Rieneck, Jan René Haak, Kamal Asgarov, Jean-René Pallandre, Nicole Wundrack, Julia Ettich, Niloufarsadat Miri, Doreen M Floss, Jürgen Scheller, Christoph Garbers, Andy Clark, John Wijdenes, Fred Schaper, Anna Dittrich
description: The cytokine interleukin-6 orchestrates inflammation through two distinct pathways of receptor activation: anti-inflammatory classic signalling via membrane-bound interleukin-6 receptor and pro-inflammatory trans-signalling via soluble interleukin-6 receptor. Current interleukin-6-targeted therapies block both pathways, thereby disrupting essential homeostatic functions initiated by classic signalling. We here show a high-affinity, human-specific antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin-6 trans-signalling.

title: Reconfigurable acoustic tweezers based on a programmable droplet array
creator: Zhen Wang, Menglei Zhao, Kangfu Chen, Yao Lu, Haopu Wang, Zongliang Guo, Zonghao Li, Meiyi Zhou, Huiliang Cao, Kaiqiang Cao, Xiaoyi Wang, Rongxin Fu, Hang Li, Zhichao Ma, Jiafang Li, Huikai Xie, Shuailong Zhang
description: Conventional acoustic manipulation relies on either direct acoustic radiation force acting on particles or indirect methods using acoustic streaming generated by acoustic pressure fields to manipulate particles. While acoustic devices generating standing waves can create patterned arrangements of particles and cells, these methods are typically limited to producing regular arrays in static configurations.

title: Unexpected Peritoneal Loose Body Discovered During Laparoscopic Varicocelectomy: A Case Report
creator: Jad K. Alsmadi, Anas A. Al-Bdour, Ahmad F. Abuo’waida
description: Patient: Male, 22-year-old Final Diagnosis: Peritoneal loose body Symptoms: Scrotal pain Clinical Procedure: Laparoscopic surgery Specialty: Urology Objective Rare coexistence of disease or pathology BackgroundPeritoneal loose bodies (PLBs) are rare, benign intraperitoneal entities usually discovered incidentally during abdominal surgery or imaging. Their occurrence during urologic laparoscopy appears to be infrequently reported and may create intraoperative diagnostic uncertainty when encountered unexpectedly.

title: Levenberg–marquardt based ANN solution for MHD nanofluid flow and heat transportation over a thin needle with thermophoresis effects
creator: Haider Ali, Aaqib Majeed, Taoufik Saidani, Parvez Ali
description: Artificial neural network (ANN) techniques have emerged as powerful data-driven tools for their effectiveness in analysis, modeling, and simulation. These supervised learning approaches are designed to reduce the error between predicted and observed data, providing accurate approximations of complex physical systems.

title: The role of neighborhood socioeconomic environment in the association between glycemic control and the developing brain
creator: Anisha Chandra, Eustace Hsu, Shan Luo
description: Metabolic health and socioeconomic environments may jointly shape neurodevelopment during adolescence, a sensitive period of brain maturation. This cross-sectional study investigated overall and neighborhood socioeconomic deprivation moderated associations between glycemic control and brain structure in youth. Data were analyzed from 705 healthy 10–13-year-olds participating in the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study® across 21 sites in the United States.

title: Bioaccessibility of Phenolic Compounds and Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids in Whole and Ground Chia Seeds and Sprouts
creator: Flávia Oliveira Brito, Lilia Zago, Juliana Delvizio, Carolina Beres, Kim Ohanna Pimenta Inada, Vanessa Naciuk Castelo-Branco, Roberta Fontanive Miyahira
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigated the effect of grinding and germination on phenolic compounds, fatty acids, and antioxidant capacity of chia seeds after in vitro gastrointestinal digestion. After digestion, the samples ground chia (GC) and ground chia sprouts (GCS) showed the highest values of total phenolic compounds, antioxidant capacity, and fatty acids when compared to the respective whole samples, whole chia (WC), and whole chia sprout (WCS).

title: Eco-friendly synthesis and multifunctional characterization of ZrO2/Cu4O3/MnO2/CuMnO2 nanocomposite with enhanced thermal stability and antibacterial activity
creator: Adnan Alnehia, M A Ahlam, Muhammad Hadi
description: BackgroundThis study presents a simple chemical co-precipitation method for synthesizing a multifunctional ZrO2/Cu4O3/MnO2/CuMnO2 nanocomposite, utilizing distilled water as the reaction solvent and an eco-friendly medium, followed by thermal treatment at 500 °C for 2 h. This aqueous-based process allows precise control over the synthesis of a hybrid metal-oxide system, enhancing its thermal and functional properties.

title: Safety and complications of upper pole puncture in supine percutaneous nephrolithotomy
creator: Juliana Villanueva-Congote, Yi W. Li, Michal Segall, Mehmet Gokce, Silvia Proietti, Guido Giusti, Jose Ernesto Torres Garcia, Braulio Manzo, Alan Yaghoubian, Mariano Gonzalez, Leye Ajayi, Daniel A. Wollin, Brian H. Eisner
description: ObjectiveSupine percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) has gained attention as a viable alternative to the traditional/historical prone approach for the treatment of large renal stones. However, concerns remain regarding the safety and feasibility of upper calyx punctures in the supine position, particularly for upper-pole access.

title: What should be updated in the WHO guide to good prescribing?
creator: Mariëlle G Hartjes, Fleur MW Hendriksen, Michiel J Bakkum, Yoann Cazaubon, Erik M Donker, Ellen van Leeuwen, Robert Likic, Yves-Marie Pers, Tuan A Phan, Joost D Piët, Fabrizio De Ponti, Walter Raasch, Milan C Richir, Floor van Rosse, Jitka Rychlíčková, Emilio J Sanz, Markus Schwaninger, Susanna M Wa
description: PurposeOver 30 years ago, the World Health Organization (WHO) published the Guide to Good Prescribing (GGP) with its accompanying six-step model for rational prescribing. While widely used and proven effective in teaching clinical pharmacology and therapeutics (CPT), the GGP has never been revised to reflect scientific, societal, technological, and educational developments.

title: Timing of diuretic administration effects on urine volume in hospitalized patients
creator: Katie S. McCullar, Sara Abbaspour, Wei Wang, Aaron D. Aguirre, M. Brandon Westover, Elizabeth B. Klerman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Importance: Some medications have effects that depend on the time of day they are given. Current knowledge of the time-of-day effects of specific medications in hospitalized patients with cardiovascular disease is very limited. In hospitalized patients, increased medication efficiency might reduce dose (and associated side effects) and/or the length of time in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) or hospital–potentially improving patient outcomes and patient and family quality of life and reducing financial costs.

title: Early extracranial dissemination with prolonged survival in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: case study and comprehensive literature review
creator: Colin Burns, Cheng Chia Wu, Kei Suzuki, Grace Lee, Daniel Kim
description: BackgroundExtracranial metastasis of glioblastoma (GBM) is rare (0.4–2%) and associated with poor prognosis. For this report, “early extracranial dissemination” is defined as radiographically and histologically confirmed metastatic disease identified at or within one month of the index GBM diagnosis, distinguishing it from metastasis arising later in the disease course.

title: Severity-dependent and sex-biased dysregulation of A-to-I RNA editing in COVID-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target
creator: Jing-Yuan Wang, Ya-Di Zhao, Li-Ping Wang, Yu-Qing Ren, Jia-Nuo Li, Teng Wang, Hua-Kang Zhang, Feng Zhu, Jian-Huan Chen, Yun-Yun Jin
description: SARS-CoV-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID-19 severity and sex-biased disease remains unclear. We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non-COVID controls and COVID-19 patients spanning different disease severities.

title: A taxonomy of reliability indices for cluster‐level constructs measured by multiple individual‐level indicators
creator: Terrence D. Jorgensen, Suzanne Jak
description: Generalizability theory (GT) provides a variety of intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) to quantify reliability across different conditions of measurement—for example, scale and interrater reliability quantify generalization across items and raters, respectively. In a multilevel modelling (MLM) context, an ICC is often used to quantify the proportion of a subject‐level variable's variance that is attributable to cluster‐level differences (e.g.

title: Influencing factors analysis and prediction model development for ROSC in adult non-traumatic OHCA: a retrospective study based on pre-hospital emergency settings
creator: Qing Zhang, Zhixin Pang, Xiangyu Yan, Feng Tang, Shuai Li, Xiaoying Shao, Wenrui Zou, Tongyu Xing, Shengli Guo, Xiangjun Meng, Nan Hu, Xiangyan Meng, Lu Lu, Shanglun Li, Haojun Fan
description: BackgroundCardiac arrest is a major global public health problem.
