This study aimed to explore factors influencing return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and develop a prediction model for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients.MethodsWe retrospectively collected electronic medical records of adult non-traumatic OHCA patients at Tianjin Emergency Medical Center from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024.

title: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy in a neuropathologically confirmed Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease cohort
creator: Lluc Bertran, Iban Aldecoa, Arlène Sindikubwabo, Núria Vidal, Rafael Blesa, Mercè Martínez‐Corral, Carlos Nos, Verónica Santiago, Andrea González, Álex Iranzo, Christopher J Nowinski, Ann C McKee, Raquel Sánchez Valle, Laura Molina‐Porcel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a tauopathy associated with repetitive head impacts, experienced most commonly in contact sports; however, its relationship with prion diseases remains unclear. Postmortem CTE screening using phosphorylated tau staining was conducted at the Neurological Tissue Bank of Hospital Clínic‐IDIBAPS on hippocampal and frontal cortex samples from patients with neuropathologically confirmed Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease (CJD), blinded to patients' clinical histories.

title: Kinetic modelling of Chlorella spp. wastewater treatment and resource recovery in the food industry
creator: Vera Lavelli, Zhi Zhou
description: Effluents generated in the food and beverage industry typically contain elevated concentrations of organic carbon sources and inorganic nutrients, representing a significant environmental burden as global food demand continues to rise. Owing to their capacity to effectively assimilate carbon and nutrients while simultaneously generating biomass with potential valorization pathways, Chlorella spp.

title: Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR) identifies conserved translational fingerprints of M-phase
creator: Sarah B Eivers, Axelle Baumgartner, Marcio Dorn, Catherine Jessus, Juliana Silva-Bernardes, Enrico Maria Daldello
description: Entry into M-phase requires mRNA translation, but whether mitotic and meiotic divisions share a conserved translational programme and which newly synthesized proteins promote Cdk1 activation remain unclear. We developed Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR), a multi-objective network-based method that ranks mRNAs according to their proximity to a training group across heterogeneous two-condition omics datasets.

title: Prevalence and Correlates of Nomophobia and Insomnia Among Health Sciences Students: Evidence From a Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Nuha Fatima, Mohammed Waqqas, Husna Irfan Thalib, Nadeem Ikram, Sariya Khan, Samratul Fuadah, Mohammed Talha Mohammed Zubair, Zain Ul Abideen Nadeem, Mable Pereira
description: BackgroundNomophobia is a behavioral condition characterized by fear or anxiety resulting from inability to access mobile phones. Excessive smartphone use has been associated with psychological and sleep‐related disturbances. University students, particularly health sciences students, may be especially vulnerable due to academic stress and high digital exposure.

title: Patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes in refractory ascites secondary to cirrhosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Yazan Haddadin, James Ryley, Benjaman To, Vasso Anagnostopoulou, Stephen Bremner, Lucia Macken, Sumita Verma
description: Background: Refractory ascites (RA) secondary to advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD) results in poor health-related quality of life (HRQL), high symptom burden, and caregiver workload. Patient/caregiver-reported outcomes (PROs) remain uncharacterized in this cohort. This review summarises the available evidence on this topic.Methods:MEDLINE/Embase/Cochrane/PsycINFO/Web of Science/CINAHL were searched for articles that included PROs in RA secondary to ACLD.

title: Shared Governance for Effective Clinical Education in Medical Radiation Science: A Narrative Review
creator: Jacob Leonard Ago, Bismark Ofori‐Manteaw, Minh Chau, Theophilus N Akudjedu, Yobelli Jimenez, Elio Arruzza, Kelly Bentley‐Spuur
description: Medical radiation science (MRS) education operates within a rapidly evolving healthcare environment characterised by technological advancement, workforce pressures, and increasing regulatory oversight. Effective governance structures are therefore required to ensure that educational programs remain clinically relevant, compliant with accreditation standards, and responsive to students' wellbeing and patient safety imperatives.

title: Shaping public health policy in personalized prevention: the multidimensional PROPHET framework
creator: Astrid Moura Vicente, Angelica Valz Gris, Cristina Costa, Maria Luis Cardoso, Alexandra Costa, Fátima Lopes, Pragathy Kannan, Markus Perola, Roberta Pastorino, Angelo Maria Pezzullo, Stefania Boccia
description: There is currently no widely accepted framework to guide decision-making for preventive approaches using genetic and genomic technologies. In the context of the PROPHET project, we developed a multidimensional framework integrating Health Technology Assessment and Health Impact Assessment, complemented by a monitoring phase to assess the impact of policies implementing personalized prevention interventions.

title: Performance Evaluation of Dry Chemical Colorimetry for Plasma Ammonia Detection on the VITROS 350 Chemistry System
creator: Jia Liu, Lin Wang, Yue Tang, Peiran Li, Lili Zhao, Wenwen Yuan, Bo Li, Boan Li
description: ObjectivePlasma ammonia quantitation is one of the most valuable laboratory tests for assessing hepatic function. Accurate measurement is clinically imperative for the diagnosis and management of severe hepatobiliary diseases. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the analytical performance of the VITROS dry chemistry system with dry chemical colorimetry for plasma ammonia detection.

title: Clinical and patient-reported predictors of days alive and out of hospital in decompensated cirrhosis
creator: Sai Kiran Kuchana, Eric S. Orman, Kelly Mosesso, Timothy Stump, Patrick O. Monahan, Naga Chalasani, Archita P. Desai
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Days alive and out of hospital (DAOH) is a patient-centered outcome, but has not been studied in decompensated cirrhosis (DCC). We aimed to quantify DAOH and to identify clinical and patient-reported factors associated with DAOH.Methods:Using an ongoing prospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with DCC, DAOH was calculated by subtracting days hospitalized, transplanted, or deceased from 90 days post-discharge from index hospitalization.

title: A tripartite RpoS-CRP-cAMP-Cra circuit orchestrates metabolic reprogramming during stress adaptation
creator: Wenbo Chen, Yong Feng, Lin Liu, Rao Ma, Antoine Danchin, Conghui You
description: The alternative sigma factor RpoS (σS) governs stress adaptation in many bacterial clades, yet how it coordinates stress responses with metabolic demands remains poorly understood. Thus, by integrating RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and physiological and molecular assays, we redefined the RpoS regulon in Escherichia coli, expanding it to 667 genes and demonstrating that metabolic genes unexpectedly predominate over stress-response targets.

title: Structural basis of assembly-dependent activation of the MAD3–MAD4 nuclease in the Pseudomonas aeruginosa MADS defense system
creator: Jin Zhang, Zengru Li, Le Ye, Yaoyao Hou, Ke Liu, Jinrong Min
description: The methylation-associated defense system (MADS) is a bacterial antiphage immune system that cooperates with CRISPR–Cas systems to restrict phage infection. Within MADS, the MAD3–MAD4 module has been proposed to function as an ATPase–nuclease module related to the OLD nuclease family, but the molecular basis of its assembly and function remains unknown.

title: Factors Associated With Uptake of Iron Supplement During Pregnancy Among Women of Reproductive Age in Somaliland: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Awo Mohamed Kahie, Mohamed Said Hassan, Suhaib Mohamed Kahie, Abdikadir Abdillahi Husein, Asma Abdirahman
description: BackgroundAnemia in pregnancy is a severe public health problem in low‐ and middle‐income countries, yet the uptake of recommended iron supplementation remains critically low. In a post‐conflict and resource‐constrained setting like Somaliland, there is a significant evidence gap regarding the factors that determine whether pregnant women use these essential supplements.

title: Improving Post‐Fall Assessment Documentation in Older Inpatients Using a Structured Falls Proforma: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Ella V Brockwell‐Mole, Dujinthan Jayabalan, Su Kitchen, Minoti Bhagat
description: ObjectiveFalls among hospital inpatients are a major cause of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between the use of a structured Falls Proforma and the completeness of post‐fall assessment documentation in an Australian hospital.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted on patients who experienced inpatient falls between January 2022 and December 2024.

title: Dual‐Functional Membranes With Interfacial MXene/PFSA Nanoarchitectures for Low Hydrogen Permeation in Water Electrolysis and Reduced Vanadium Ion Crossover in Flow Batteries
creator: Panpan Guan, Mingjia Jiang, Yunhu Jiang, Wei Li, Yecheng Zou, Lixiao Zhang, Kaifeng Long, Ziqi Sun, Ting Liao, Hua Kun Liu, Ding Yuan, Dingsheng Wang, Shi Xue Dou, Yuhai Dou
description: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) and vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) suffer from hydrogen and vanadium ion crossover when using conventional perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes. Here we report a layer‐by‐layer MXene/PFSA membrane architecture in which MXene nanosheets are integrated into PFSA coating layers to create MXene‐regulated nanointerfaces that decouple proton conductivity from gas and ion permeation.

title: Effects of cannabidiol on risky decision-making and autonomic function in alcohol use disorder
creator: Ellen McGuire, Tristan Hurzeler, Warren Logge, Joshua Watt, Iain S McGregor, Anastasia Suraev, Paul S Haber, Kirsten C Morley
description: AimsTo examine the effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on psychophysiological responding and risky decision-making in individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD).MethodsIn a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, 18 participants with AUD completed the Columbia Card Task (CCT) following administration of CBD and placebo.

title: Mining buried plant trait data from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF): Comparison and integration with multiple plant trait databases
creator: Takuro Katori, Michio Oguro
description: PremiseDespite the availability of several plant trait databases, significant traits remain undocumented for a substantial number of species. To address this issue, the current study explored digital text from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) as an innovative source of plant trait information and evaluated its capacity to reduce existing deficiencies.

title: Temporal Trends in Janus Kinase Inhibitor (JAKi) Use Across Five European Countries: A DARWIN EU Network Study
creator: Xihang Chen, Andrei Barbulescu, George Corby, Saeed Hayati, Annika Jodicke, Toni Lehtonen, Hedvig Marie Egeland Nordeng, Alexandra Pacurariu, Gabriel Sanfélix‐Gimeno, Nhung T H Trinh, Katia Verhamme, Dina Vojinovic, Daniel Prieto‐Alhambra, Amy Shuk‐Man Lam, Edward Burn
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionJanus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) are increasingly used for autoimmune conditions despite existing safety concerns. This study aims to estimate the incidence of new JAKi use over time and characterise users in Europe to support future safety studies.MethodsThe study included individuals from five European data sources within the DARWIN EU network: FinOMOP‐HILMO (Finland; primary and secondary care), IPCI (the Netherlands; primary), IQVIA DA Germany (Germany; primary), NLHR (Norway; primary and secondary), VID (Spain; primary and secondary) from 1 January 2017.

title: Exploring a Range of Potential Factors Promoting and Constraining EF in South African Preschoolers
creator: Johanna Beukes, Caylee Cook, Steven J Howard, Gaia Scerif, Christopher F Sharpley, Robert Hart, Catherine Draper
description: BackgroundSocioeconomic disadvantage is widely associated with poorer cognitive and educational outcomes. However, emerging evidence suggests that children in low‐income contexts may demonstrate resilience in executive function (EF) development. This study examined the predictors of EF in South African preschoolers from disadvantaged communities to identify modifiable, context‐specific influences.

title: S100A9 Induces RANKL Expression in Osteocytes Utilizing IL‐6/sIL‐6R Combination and gp130 Signaling Pathways
creator: Eijiro Sakamoto, Tetsuya Yoshimoto, Rie Kido, Mikihito Kajiya, Hiromichi Yumoto
description: Calprotectin, a heterodimer of S100A8 and S100A9, is predominantly expressed in neutrophils, monocytes, and chondrocytes. Clinical studies demonstrate that elevated circulating calprotectin levels correlate with diseases followed by inflammatory bone loss, including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and periodontitis. We previously reported that S100A9 directly increased RANKL and IL‐6 expression in an osteocyte‐like cell line.

title: Medical Decision‐Making Capacity in Early‐Stage Alzheimer Patients: Comparison With Healthy Controls and Benefit of Assistive Information
creator: Dilara Aylin Felice Vossberg, Vasilija Rolfes, Heiner Fangerau, Martin Haupt
description: BackgroundEarly‐stage Alzheimer Disease (AD) may lead to restricted decision‐making capacity and without standardized instruments, there is great variability in determining patients' ability to give consent. This study aimed to assess decision‐making capacity of AD patients in comparison to a healthy control group and investigated the usefulness of visual aids.

title: Late Cross-Modal Biases in Neural Spatial Representations Revealed by EEG Decoding
creator: Zak Buhmann, Amanda K. Robinson, Jason B. Mattingley, Reuben Rideaux
description: During audiovisual perception, spatial information from vision and audition is combined, often producing biases such as the ventriloquist effect. While these interactions are well documented behaviorally, it remains unclear when cross-modal information begins to alter modality-specific spatial representations in the brain.

title: Beyond a solvent: HFIP as a game-changing medium in heterocyclic ring construction
creator: Laxman M Alakonda, Ravi Varala, Vittal Seema, Mohammed Mujahid Alam, Luigi Vaccaro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP) has emerged as one of the most powerful and versatile solvents in modern organic synthesis owing to its exceptional hydrogen-bond-donating ability, low nucleophilicity, high ionizing power, and remarkable capacity to stabilize ionic and radical intermediates. These unique physicochemical properties enable HFIP to facilitate proton transfer, activate otherwise unreactive bonds, and promote a wide range of intermolecular interactions, making it highly valuable in heterocycle synthesis.

title: Relationship Quality Among Married Indian Couples: A Narrative Review
creator: Akanksha Mendiratta, Pankaj Singh, Navin Kumar
description: BackgroundIndian marriages have traditionally been understood as fulfilling religious commitments, forming alliances between families and fostering companionship between spouses. However, relationship quality in such marriages is shaped by structural and cultural factors that Western models of marriage, which consider only the dyadic relationship, do not account for.

title: Gracilis Muscle Flap Reconstruction for Refractory Urethral Complications After Pelvic Surgery: A Report of Two Cases
creator: Akihiro Maeda, Shohei Tobu, Minika Yukimoto, Shuhei Kusano, Maki Kawasaki, Hiroaki Kakinoki, Mitsuru Noguchi
description: IntroductionIatrogenic urethral injury and rectourethral fistula are rare and challenging complications of pelvic surgery.Case PresentationCase 1 involved a 72‐year‐old man with persistent urinary leakage after primary repair of a prostatic urethral injury sustained during rectal cancer surgery following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy.

title: Factors Associated With Care Workers' Perceived Difficulty in Collaborating With Nurses on Bowel Care in Dementia Group Homes: A Nationwide Survey in Japan
creator: Yumi Fukuyama, Chie Furushima, Syoko Ito, Akiko Akiyama
description: BackgroundThis exploratory study aimed to identify factors associated with care workers' perceived difficulty in collaborating with nurses regarding bowel care in dementia group homes (GHs) in Japan.MethodsWe conducted a nationwide cross‐sectional survey from July to October 2025. Using stratified random sampling, questionnaires were mailed to 2000 of 14,202 GHs listed in national open data. Of 437 responses (21.

title: Foot‐Pedal Monitoring Camera Improves Pedal Operation During Simulated Therapeutic Endoscopy
creator: Riku Nakajima, Wataru Sano, Sachiko Shimizu, Daizen Hirata, Mineo Iwatate, Mikio Fujita, Yasushi Sano
description: ObjectivesTherapeutic endoscopic procedures often require the coordinated use of multiple foot pedals, making pedal operation challenging. We developed a foot‐pedal monitoring camera system that displays the pedal area on the endoscopic monitor, allowing operators to confirm pedal position without looking away from the procedural field. This study evaluated the effect of the system on foot‐pedal operation during simulated therapeutic endoscopy.

title: Bridging Chemical Literature and Molecular Graphs: LLM‐Augmented Enantioselectivity Prediction for Iridium‐Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Borylation
creator: Zhe Wang, Baohua Zhang, Yi Isaac Yang, Yuan Yao, Yinwu Li
description: Asymmetric C–H borylation provides direct access to enantioenriched organoboron compounds. Predictive catalyst design for this reaction class remains challenging, as stereocontrol arises from coupled interactions among catalyst, substrate, and product structures. Moreover, mechanistic knowledge is dispersed across the literature. Here we report a machine‐learning framework for predicting enantioselectivity in iridium‐catalyzed asymmetric C–H borylation that bridges molecular graphs and chemical literature.

title: Chiral Sulfide‐Catalyzed, Water‐Regulated Enantioselective Tandem Disulfuration‐Initiated Dearomative Spirocyclization/Oxa‐Michael Addition of Alkynes
creator: Li‐Miao Yang, Qing‐Yun Cai, Yu‐Xuan Huo, Xue‐Qing Gong, Hui Li, Yang Ji, Zhi‐Min Chen
description: In this work, we report for the first time an organocatalytic system for the enantioselective tandem electrophilic disulfuration/dearomative spirocyclization/oxa‐Michael addition of alkynes. The highly electrophilic saccharin‐derived disulfurating reagent, independently developed by our group, facilitates the smooth electrophilic addition of low‐reactivity alkynes. The successful achievement of high enantiocontrol was enabled using a chiral BINAM‐derived sulfide catalyst, featuring an unsymmetrical adamantylmethylamine moiety.

title: Temporally Correlated Stochastic Spiking Neural Networks Enabled by 2D Ferroelectric Synapse‐Neuron Integration
creator: Hanseo Jeon, Ui Do Ji, Sangmin Lee, Gihyeon Bhin, Chang Yong Park, Ji‐Sang Park, Byungchul Jang, Sungjoo Lee
description: Stochastic neural computation is essential for probabilistic inference and brain‐inspired information processing. However, most hardware stochastic neurons generate statistically independent spikes and fail to reproduce the temporal correlations observed in biological neurons. We demonstrate an integrated hardware synapse‐neuron consisting of a FeFET synapse and a CulnP2S6 neuron, where the neuron exhibits temporally correlated stochastic spiking.

title: Coordination‐Asymmetry‐Regulated Reconstruction of Electron‐Rich Cu Sites for pH‐Dependent Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Electrocatalysis
creator: Shih‐Ching Huang, Yu‐Ru Lin, Hsiang‐Chun Yu, Yi‐Dong Lin, Yu‐Chiao Chang, Chun‐Kuo Peng, Yu‐Chang Lin, Wen‐Wei Wu, Hao Ming Chen, Chi‐Liang Chen, Han‐Yi Chen, Yan‐Gu Lin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (e‐NO3RR) offers a promising route to valorize nitrate‐contaminated wastewater while enabling sustainable ammonia production; however, how local coordination asymmetry regulates Cu‐site evolution and reaction pathways across different pH environments remains insufficiently understood. Herein, three‐ and four‐nitrogen‐coordinated Cu single‐atom motifs, denoted as Cu─N3 and Cu─N4, are constructed as well‐defined pre‐catalyst models to elucidate how the initial Cu coordination environment directs pH‐dependent active‐site reconstruction.

title: Years-long stability of X10 expansion microscopy hydrogels
creator: Eman Abbas, Ali H Shaib, Mohamed A Hassan, Silvio O Rizzoli
description: Expansion microscopy (ExM) is developing rapidly to explore biological structures, both towards nanoscale imaging and the wider-scale analysis of cells and tissues. ExM is based on embedding samples in swellable hydrogels, which then expand to enable superior microscopy performance with conventional microscopes.

title: Stimulation-stability and preclinical bench testing of a new auditory nerve interface
creator: Taylor Stump, Stefan Strahl, Joseph Crew, Moritz Leber, Keno Hübner, Sandeep Negi, Justin Vankirk, Meredith E. Adams, Thomas Lenarz, Florian Solzbacher, Hubert H. Lim, Loren Rieth
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveCochlear implants are the flagship sensory neural prosthetic, enabling improved hearing and speech perception in >1 million patients with hearing loss. Despite over three decades of active work and innovations in cochlear implants, hearing performance for complex tasks such as speech-in-noise and music appreciation are still quite limited, putatively due to the challenge of selectively stimulating the auditory nerve with intracochlear electrodes through the bony cochlear wall.

title: CausalCellInfer: Prioritizing Cell‐Type‐Specific Disease Associations From Genetically Predicted Transcriptomes in Biobank Cohorts
creator: Liangying Yin, Yujia Shi, Ruoyu Zhang, Yong Xiang, Jinghong Qiu, Pak‐Chung Sham, Hon‐Cheong So
description: Integrating single‐cell RNA sequencing(scRNA‐seq) with the phenotypic depth of population‐scale biobanks is essential for elucidating the cellular basis of complex diseases. However, this is hindered by limited scRNA‐seq sample size and the lack of cellular resolution in biobanks. We present CausalCellInfer, a scalable computational framework bringing cellular resolution to bulk and genotype‐imputed transcriptomes.

title: CRISPR‐Scan: Cas13a Mismatch Tolerance Enabled Ultra‐Multiplexed Detection of Same‐Site Indels in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
creator: Linlin Bai, Bei Wang, Mingmin Shi, Dianwei Liu, Huimin Ji, Ting Wang, Ziwei Wang, Kaiming Guo, Xinyang Dou, Chunyan Qian, Fang Zhang, Yongming Wang, Hongju Mao, Rui Wang
description: Detection of gene mutations related to acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is crucial for its early diagnosis, personalized treatment, and recurrence monitoring. However, accurate detection of diverse mutations occurring at the same locus remains technically challenging. The CRISPR/Cas system, with its unique programmable nucleic acid recognition capabilities, provides a promising solution.

title: Real-time assessment of temperature sensitivity, pain processing, and pain behavior across the lifespan: Integrating stimulus data, contact force, and subjective ratings
creator: Heinz-Jürgen Steinhoff, Besim Prenaj, Sebastian L Kübel, Annekatrin Steinhoff
description: Assessments of temperature sensitivity and pain processing play an important role in psychological and psychiatry research, including with adolescent participants and across the lifespan. To ensure the validity and comparability of findings, experimental settings must be well tolerated and easily manageable for participants of all age groups and reliably monitored by the experimenter.

title: Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
creator: James M Stevenson, Garvit Agarwal, Sibali Debnath, Zachary K Goldsmith, Monosij Mondal, Asya Svirinovsky-Arbeli, In Won Yeu, Amy S Metlay, Yongbeom Kwon, Lakshmi Bhai, Rishabh D Guha, Eric G Keeler, John L Weber, Daniel A Steingart, Lauren E Marbella, Alexander Urban, Leif D Jacobson, Mathew D Halls
description: In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1–3.

title: Recent advances and emerging mechanisms in graphene-based materials for cartilage tissue engineering
creator: Mone’t Sawyer, David Estrada
description: Graphene-based materials offer tunable mechanical, electrical, and biochemical properties that address longstanding challenges in cartilage tissue engineering. This review synthesizes recent advances in graphene derivatives, scaffold fabrication strategies, and emerging mechanisms governing cell–graphene interactions. We evaluate how graphene enhances mechanical reinforcement, bioactivity, and matrix production across hydrogels, polymer composites, and ECM-derived scaffolds.

title: Regulation of PDH via cysteine oxidation on DLAT
creator: Fabiola Garcia-Cortizo, Tobias Weber, Hana Nůsková, Daniel Pfaff, Michael Büttner, Angela Wirth, Elisabeth Kliemank, Gernot Poschet, Marc Freichel, Thomas Fleming, Alba Sulaj, Peter Paul Nawroth, Julia Szendroedi, Aurelio A. Teleman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex is a key regulator of metabolism, controlling flux from glycolysis into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. PDH is often dysregulated in metabolic diseases and cancer. We discover here that in addition to its well characterized regulation by phosphorylation, PDH activity is also regulated via inhibitory oxidation of three cysteines of the DLAT subunit - Cys488, Cys586 and Cys618. Oxidation of these cysteines increases under oxidative stress, and is highly prevalent in mouse and human tissues.

title: Multi-omics profiling identifies triciribine as a biomarker-guided antimetabolite therapy for acute lymphoblastic leukemia
creator: Xuekang Qi, Georgios Mermelekas, Ondrej Hodek, Luay Aswad, Quentin Glaziou, Isabelle Rose Leo, Nona Struyf, Femke M Hormann, Ioannis Siavelis, Henri Colyn Bwanika, Owen F J Hovey, Martin Haraldsson, Sean G Rudd, Annika I Johansson, Tom Erkers, Katja Pokrovskaja Tamm, Janne Lehtiö, Rozbeh Jafari
description: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) exhibits molecular and metabolic heterogeneity that limits therapeutic efficacy. Although antimetabolites remain central to ALL treatment, determinants of therapeutic sensitivity and resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the activity and molecular response landscape of the purine analog triciribine (TCN) across diverse ALL models using integrated phosphoproteomics, thermal proteome profiling, and quantitative proteomics.

title: Integrating clinical and cross-cohort metagenomic features: a stable and non-invasive colorectal cancer and adenoma diagnostic model
creator: Dan Zhou, Youli Chen, Zehao Wang, Siran Zhu, Lei Zhang, Jun Song, Tao Bai, Xiaohua Hou
description: Background: Dysbiosis is associated with colorectal cancer (CRC) and adenomas (CRA). However, the robustness of diagnostic models based on microbial signatures in multiple cohorts remains unsatisfactory. Materials and Methods: In this study, we used machine learning models to screen metagenomic signatures from the respective cross-cohort datasets of CRC and CRA (selected from CuratedMetagenomicData, each disease included 4 datasets).

title: Curvature-driven passive mixing in three-dimensional conical helix micromixers
creator: İsmail Bütün, Tunahan Parlayıcı, Süleyman Çelik, Erchan Aptoula, Ali Koşar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Passive microfluidic mixing is fundamentally constrained by the dominance of laminar flow, a limitation commonly addressed using embedded obstacles or surface modifications, often at the cost of increased fabrication complexity and hydraulic resistance. Here, we introduce a conical helix micromixer (CHM) that combines circular and helical microchannel topologies into a monolithic geometry capable of passively generating progressively intensified Dean vortices through continuously varying curvature.

title: Magnetized joystick with dual-anisotropy for high-capacity wearable human-machine interactions
creator: Yuanzhe Liang, Ming Lei, Biao Qi, Yingyi Zhang, Ziyi Dai, Dan Fang, Jinbo Wu, Jianyi Luo, Bingpu Zhou
description: One of the urgent demands for flexible and wearable sensors is to achieve single-channel, less-sensor, and multi-output for effective communications. However, expansion of signal capacity on a single interface often requires sensor arrays, which significantly increases the complexity in electrode layout and multiple device design.

title: Complementing Hi-C information for 3D chromatin reconstruction by ChromStruct
creator: Claudia Caudai, Emanuele Salerno
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A multiscale method proposed elsewhere for reconstructing plausible 3D configurations of the chromatin in cell nuclei is recalled, based on the integration of contact data from Hi-C experiments and additional information coming from ChIP-seq, RNA-seq and ChIA-PET experiments. Provided that the additional data come from independent experiments, this kind of approach is supposed to leverage them to complement possibly noisy, biased or missing Hi-C records.

title: Research progress on ATP-citrate lyase and its inhibitors: a metabolic-epigenetic perspective
creator: Qinglin Liu, Hongbin Sun, Liang Dai
description: ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) is a key enzyme in cellular metabolism that catalyses the cleavage of citrate to produce acetyl coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA), thereby bridging energy metabolism and epigenetic regulation. Acetyl-CoA serves as a common substrate for de novo lipogenesis (DNL) and histone acetylation.

title: Deciphering the origin and therapeutic targets of cancer of unknown primary: a case report that illustrates the power of integrative whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing analysis
creator: Majd Al Assaad, Nara Shin, Michael Sigouros, Jyothi Manohar, Zoia Antysheva, Nikita Kotlov, Daria Kiriy, Anastasiia Nikitina, Mikhail Kleimenov, Anastasiya Tsareva, Anastasiya Makarova, Victoria Fomchenkova, Julia Dubinina, Alexandra Boyko, Nava Almog, David Wilkes, Joanna G. Escalon, Ashish Saxena,
description: Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) represents a significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, being the third to fourth leading cause of cancer death, despite advances in diagnostic tools. This article presents a successful approach using a novel genomic analysis in the evaluation and treatment of a CUP patient, leveraging whole-exome sequencing (WES) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq).

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
creator: Nicholas A. J. Graham, Cassandra E. Benkwitt, Ines D. Lange, Chris T. Perry, Eleanor R. Thomson, Lisa M. Wedding, Ruth E. Dunn, Sebastian Steibl, Courtney E. Stuart, Laura-Li Jeannot, Jennifer Appoo, Julia Rodriguez Fillol, Marleen Stuhr, Pirta Palola, Peter Carr, Jayna L. DeVore, Simon Ducatez, Ann
description: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens.

title: The value of genome-wide analysis in craniosynostosis
creator: Alexandra Topa, Anna Rohlin, André Fehr, Lovisa Lovmar, Göran Stenman, Peter Tarnow, Giovanni Maltese, Madiha Bhatti-Søfteland, Lars Kölby
description: Background: This study assessed the diagnostic yield of high-throughput sequencing methods in a cohort of craniosynostosis (CS) patients not presenting causal variants identified through previous targeted analysis. Methods: Whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing (WGS/WES) was performed in a cohort of 59 patients (from 57 families) assessed by retrospective phenotyping as having syndromic or nonsyndromic CS.

title: Optimization of chemical conditions for metabolites production by Ganoderma lucidum using response surface methodology and investigation of antimicrobial as well as anticancer activities
creator: Alireza Tajik, Hamid Reza Samadlouie, Amir Salek Farrokhi, Amir Ghasemi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Ganoderma lucidum (G. lucidum) is a medicinal mushroom that is known for its ability to produce compounds with physiological effects on human health. This research was undertaken to amplify the production of bioactive components of G. lucidum under optimal cultivation conditions, obtained in a submerged state and utilized in solid state fermentation, with the purpose of enhancing antimicrobial and anticancer activities.

title: RNA-Based Therapies for Lipoprotein(a) Reduction: Antisense Oligonucleotides, Small Interfering RNAs, and Emerging Platforms
creator: Vibhu Parcha, Vera A. Bittner
description: Purpose of ReviewLipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent, genetically determined, and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Elevated Lp(a) affects approximately 20% of the global population and is not meaningfully modified by lifestyle intervention or existing lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy.

title: A new Rogue-like Escherichia phage UDF157lw to control Escherichia coli O157:H7
creator: Yen-Te Liao, Kan-Ju Ho, Yujie Zhang, Alexandra Salvador, Vivian C. H. Wu
description: IntroductionShiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) O157:H7 is one of the notorious foodborne pathogens causing high mortality through the consumption of contaminated food items. The food safety risk from STEC pathogens could escalate when a group of bacterial cells aggregates to form a biofilm. Bacterial biofilm can diminish the effects of various antimicrobial interventions and enhance the pathogenicity of the pathogens.

title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis
creator: Amin Serradj, Gabriel Saiydoun, Costin Radu, Eric Bergoend, Antonio Fiore, Raphaelle Huguet, Pascal Lim, Cyrus Moini, Thierry Folliguet
description: BackgroundPostoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery.

title: Discovery of the biostimulant effect of asparagine and glutamine on plant growth in Arabidopsis thaliana
creator: Manon Lardos, Anne Marmagne, Nolwenn Bonadé Bottino, Quentin Caris, Bernard Béal, Fabien Chardon, Céline Masclaux-Daubresse
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Protein hydrolysates have gained interest as plant biostimulants due to their positive effects on plant performances. They are mainly composed of amino acids, but there is no evidence of the role of individual of amino acids as biostimulants. In this study we carried out in vitro experiments to monitor the development of Arabidopsis seedlings on amino acid containing media in order to analyze the biostimulant properties of the twenty individual proteinogenic amino acids.

title: “Morphological, Functional, and Molecular Progression of Blood-Brain Barrier Dysfunction in Alzheimer’s Disease”
creator: Karen León-Arcia, Humberto Martínez-Orozco, Magdalena Guerra-Crespo, Sofía Y Díaz-Miranda, Luis O Soto-Rojas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is increasingly recognized as an early pathological event in sporadic Alzheimer’s disease (AD), which represents over 95% of cases. Vascular risk factors and cerebral insulin resistance are considered potential contributors to its initiation. This review synthesizes evidence available through March 2026 on the temporal progression of morphological, functional, and molecular BBB alterations in AD patients and experimental models.

title: Targeting P2Y14R inhibits proliferation of cervical cancer cells and organoids and activates cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling pathway
creator: Rui Li, Hai-Yun Xiong, Shi-Yu Chen, Yong Tang, Wen-Bin Ma
description: Purinergic signaling has been widely recognized as a critical regulator of tumor progression, yet the role of P2Y14R in cervical cancer remains unclear. This study used the P2Y14R antagonist PPTN in in vitro cell experiments; the results showed that it significantly inhibited cell proliferation and increased LDH release.

title: Investigation of fin model using RNN intelligent computing associated to physical parameters and hybrid nanomaterials
creator: Muneeba Shahbaz, Abdelrahman H Hussein, Mohamed Arbi Khlifi, Hemn AH BARZANI, W D Mergia, Refka Ghodhbani, Sana Ullah Saqib, Adnan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The efficient thermal transport through trapezoidal fin surface remains a significant multi engineering problem because traditional fins configuration offers unsatisfactory heat transport subject to high thermal loads which limits the colling system’s thermal performance. Although, the nanoparticles have potential role in the heat mechanism across trapezoidal fin but the combined contribution of hybrid nanofluid properties, magnetic field, wetting surface and temperature dependent thermal conductivity has not been adequately presented using AI based computational paradigm.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution
creator: Florian Recker
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community.

title: The association between MGMT expression and outcome in H3 G34-mutant diffuse hemispheric glioma is robust to adjustment for pre-analytic and technical variables
creator: Qunyu Zhang, Dana Tlais, Tong Lin, Xiaoyu Li, Arzu Onar-Thomas, Jason Chiang
description: e question extends beyond DHG. Cohorts of rare pediatric brain tumors are typically retrospective and multi-institutional, span many years, and mix preservation methods, all potential sources of batch effects [3]. We analyzed RNA-seq data from 110 H3 G34-mutant DHGs, all sequenced centrally at St. Jude on the NovaSeq 6000 platform and including all RNA-sequenced tumors from our original report [9].

title: The value of luteinizing hormone basal values and sex hormone-binding globulin for early diagnosis of rapidly progressive central precocious puberty
creator: Meiyu Zhang, Jun Sun, Ying Wang, Yanhui Wu, Xiaona Li, Rong Li, Yafei Fang, Hua Bai, Peiliang Luo, Yingdi Yuan
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate the diagnostic value of luteinizing hormone (LH) basal values and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) for rapidly progressive central precocious puberty (RP-CPP).MethodsA total of 121 girls presenting with secondary sexual characteristics were selected from the Department of Pediatric Endocrinology, Lianyungang Clinical Medical College of Nanjing Medical University, from May 2021 to June 2023.

title: Leaf variegation in a barley EMS mutant is controlled by two epistatic mutations
creator: Hélène Pidon, Shobhashree Rajulareddy Nagireddy, Michael Melzer, Axel Himmelbach, Nils Stein
description: Key message We identified digenic control of leaf variegation in a barley mutant. Candidate genes, identified through whole-genome resequencing, are consistent with possible roles in chloroplast proteostasis. AbstractVariegation mutants provide valuable insights into chloroplast biogenesis. We characterized a newly identified variegated barley mutant, in which the phenotype is controlled by two epistatic recessive genes.

title: Assessment of the reliability and quality of breast cancer related videos on TikTok and Bilibili: cross-sectional study in China
creator: Hui Liu, Jialun Peng, Lu Li, Ao Deng, Xiangxin Huang, Guobin Yin, Jia Ming, Haojun Luo, Yinyin Liang
description: BackgroundAs the most common malignant tumor in the world, breast cancer also brings a huge disease burden to China. Ordinary people are increasingly inclined to use the Internet, especially video social platforms, as a source of health information. Educating the public to obtain correct information is important to reduce the incidence of breast cancer and improve the prognosis.

title: Exploring the landscape of flagellate erythema as a rare cutaneous symptom of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy: a case series-based review
creator: Aleksandra Opinc-Rosiak, Milena Kaszubska, Aleksandra Nadel, Aleksander Sztajnert, Joanna Makowska, Anna Lewandowska-Polak
description: Flagellate erythema is an exceptionally rare cutaneous manifestation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM) with poorly understood clinical significance. We report two patients who developed zebra-like flagellate erythema: one with immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM) and one with anti-Mi-2-positive cancer-associated myositis (CAM).

title: Targeting tumor-selective membrane-associated PCNA enables selective antibody–drug conjugate therapy
creator: Muhammad Abu Ahmad, Nir Miriam Ungar-Malma, Alon Naumchik, Noy Machluf-Katz, Olga Radinsky, Sarah Adi Eisdorfer, Abedallh Gara, Yosef Istoyler, Irit Alon, Daniel Sevilla-Sanchez, Kerry S. Campbell, Bar Kaufman, Moshe Elkabets, Angel Porgador
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Membrane-associated proliferating cell nuclear antigen (mPCNA) is an attractive tumor-selective antigen for antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) development. We generated a chimeric IgG1 ADC, RC14-MMAE, to exploit three key properties of mPCNA that support its use as an efficient delivery platform. First, flow-cytometric and imaging analyses show abundant mPCNA surface expression on multiple tumor cell lines and in JIMT1 xenografts, providing accessible epitopes for binding.

title: The pro-obesity role of G3BP1 through altering adipogenic differentiation in mice via the PI3K/AKT pathway
creator: Haiyan Wang, Litong Sun, Haidan Mao, Yan Mei, Jinping Ni, Liren Wang
description: As a growing but non-infectious epidemic, obesity is a common cause of several comorbidities. GTPase-activating protein SH3 domain-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) is a central regulator of stress‑granule assembly that has significant implications in metabolic disorders. This article aims to explore the functional mechanism of G3BP1 in obesity, both in vitro and in vivo.

title: Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide attenuates BMSC senescence by inhibiting NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy
creator: Xing Dai, Linhua Wang, Yu Sun, Zhuo He, Xiaolin Du, Xiaoming Lei, Shaofeng Yang, Muzhe Li
description: ContextBMSC senescence is associated with osteoporosis progression. Polygonatum sibiricum polysaccharide (PSP) shows potential anti-senescence activity, but its effects on bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) remain unclear.ObjectiveTo investigate the protective effects and molecular mechanisms of PSP against tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBH)-induced senescence in BMSCs.Materials and methodsSenescence was induced in primary rat BMSCs with TBH, followed by PSP intervention.

title: Vitamin D status and inflammatory Interleukins in women with and without polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a cross-sectional exploratory study
creator: Roba Bdeir, Nour Al-Sawalha, Hasan Rawashdeh, Ruba Malkawi, Ola Alrousan
description: BackgroundPolyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), formerly referred to as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is an intricate endocrine disorder, defined by a constellation of hormonal, metabolic, and reproductive irregularities. Vitamin D deficiency and increased levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8) have been implicated in the pathogenesis of PMOS.

title: Hybrid Molecular Imaging Using PET/CT and PET/MRI in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
creator: Yuqin Li, Min Wang, Bin Liu, Zijun Yuan, Wenbo Yang, Wenchun Yao, Yongxin Yuan
description: Hybrid molecular imaging is increasingly recognized as a valuable tool for the precision management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Driven by the treat-to-target paradigm, the noninvasive quantification of transmural inflammation and the accurate differentiation of stricture phenotypes remain key clinical challenges.

title: Environmental exposures associated with atopy in a rural community in Gwanda district, Zimbabwe: a cross-sectional study
creator: Vuyelwa Ndlovu, Moses Chimbari, Pisirai Ndarukwa, Elopy Sibanda
description: IntroductionThe increasing prevalence of allergic diseases in Zimbabwe may be attributed to changing environmental exposure patterns. In this study, we sought to identify the most influential environmental and lifestyle factors that may explain the observed atopy in a rural community in Zimbabwe.

title: Occupancy‐Guided Continuous Antipsychotic Dosing Provides a Translational Model for Evaluating Extrapyramidal Motor Liability in Mice
creator: Yosefu Arime, Kaoru Irahara, Noriaki Ohkawa
description: The therapeutic effects of antipsychotic drugs are primarily achieved through dopamine D2 receptor antagonism. However, excessive striatal D2 receptor blockade is associated with extrapyramidal side effects (EPS) in schizophrenic patients. Clinical studies indicate a therapeutic window of approximately 60%–80% striatal D2 receptor occupancy, with higher occupancy increasing the risk of EPS.

title: Surgical Success in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Patients Using Preoperative Drug‐Induced Sleep Endoscopy and Awake Endoscopy Considering Disease Severity
creator: Nafil Arimbrathodi, Arif Nambillath, Noora Alhail, Labiba Abughazzah, Waheed Rahman, Abhishek Menon, Yousef Hudaib, Majid Alabdulla
description: BackgroundObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of airway obstruction during sleep, leading to fragmented sleep and oxygen desaturation. Identifying the precise site and pattern of obstruction is essential for surgical success. Awake endoscopy with Müller's maneuver (AEMM) has long been used, but drug‐induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) offers dynamic assessment under sleep‐like conditions.

title: Fatty Acid Oxidation Disorders Detected by Newborn Screening: Clinical, Biochemical and Genetic Spectrum in a Single‐Center Cohort
creator: Elena Martín‐Hernández, Delia Barrio‐Carreras, María Martín‐Cazaña, Luis Miguel García‐Cárdaba, Carmen Martín‐Fernández, Patricia Pérez‐Mohand, Teresa Hernández Chamorro, Berta Zamora Crespo, Pedro Ruiz‐Sala, Patricia Alcaide Alonso, Pilar Quijada‐Fraile
description: Newborn screening (NBS) has significantly improved early detection and survival in fatty acid oxidation disorders (FAODs). However, the expanding phenotypic spectrum challenges prognostic stratification, and long‐term morbidity remains incompletely characterized. We conducted an observational, retrospective, single‐center study of patients with FAODs identified through NBS and followed between 2011 and 2024.

title: Identifying high-risk population segments for underweight, overweight, and obesity among reproductive-age women in sub-Saharan Africa
creator: Amare Abera Tareke, Anissa Mohammed, Amare Muche, Yeshimebet Ali
description: BackgroundDespite significant progress in addressing underweight in developing countries, the recent rise in the number of overweight and obese individuals has confirmed that the double burden of malnutrition will remain a crucial problem in the foreseeable future. Some countries that previously succeeded in reducing underweight rates are now experiencing a resurgence.

title: Research priorities and knowledge gaps in understanding hepatobiliary disease in cystic fibrosis
creator: Dominique Debray, William R. Hunt, Frank Bodewes, Sarah E. Hempstead, Daniel Peckham, Rebecca S. Petit, Alexander Philbrick, Michael Narkewicz, Zachary M. Sellers, David N. Assis, Meghana Sathe
description: to transaminase elevation, imaging abnormalities, and hepatic fibrosis. A subset of these individuals will progress to advanced CF liver disease (aCFLD), as manifested by F4 fibrosis, multilobular cirrhosis with or without portal hypertension or non-cirrhotic portal hypertension. Recently, the CF Foundation (CFF) updated guidelines for screening, monitoring, and managing CFHBI and aCFLD.

title: Molecular biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, precision therapy, and immunotherapy in cholangiocarcinoma, cHCC-CCA, and HCC
creator: Jingguo Sun, Yingjie Lu, Lu Chang, Ruiqun Gao, Ming Guan, Haoyu Ruan, Xuan Deng
description: Primary liver cancers include hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), combined hepatocellular–cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA), and rarer hepatic malignancies. Their biomarker landscapes differ substantially. HCC has many approved systemic therapies, yet most are still selected through clinical context, liver function, tumor burden, and treatment line.

title: Poor sleep quality and associated factors among HIV-positive and negative postpartum women in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: a comparative cross-sectional study
creator: Milen Mihertabe, Alehegn Bishaw Geremew, Elsa Awoke Fentie, Gidey Rtbey
description: BackgroundPoor sleep quality is common during the postpartum period due to nighttime feeding and frequent nocturnal awakenings of infants. In addition, the condition may worsen among postpartum women living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), affecting their capacity to care for their child.

title: Dose‐dependent efficacy and safety of centanafadine in patients with attention‐deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review of the latest evidence
creator: Daud Gul, Sonia Khan, Kushal Baral, Ziad Saber, Arindam Ghosh, Eemaz Nathaniel, Onuwabhagbe Daniel Omomhenle, Nathaniel Oluwakayode Oyedeji, Lana Omar Saed Alkhatib, Lina Jamal Amin Sa'doun, Austin Nwawueze, Muhammad Naveed Ullah Khan, Raouf Khan
description: Centanafadine is a multimodal norepinephrine–dopamine–serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI) that has been evaluated for the treatment of attention‐deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of centanafadine compared with placebo, with particular emphasis on dose–response patterns across different age groups.

title: Enhanced Acoustic Adhesion Enabling Agile and Small Wall‐Climbing Robot Design With Anisotropic Origami Structure
creator: Xinxian Chen, Kanglong Yuan, Ao Qin, Yikun Liu, Yusen Ma, Jun Peng
description: Small inspection robots are highly desirable for detecting damage within confined spaces. By vibrating a disk on a surface, a thin air layer with negative pressure—known as acoustic adhesion—is generated, which offers a strategy for creating compact yet strongly climbing robots. However, it is highly sensitive to disturbances.

title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of ofatumumab in multiple sclerosis: a comprehensive FAERS data analysis
creator: Hui Chen
description: BackgroundOfatumumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting CD20, is approved for the treatment of relapsing multiple sclerosis. Comprehensive real-world safety data are crucial for informing clinical practice.MethodsThe FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database was utilized to perform a disproportionality analysis, covering reports from Q3 2020 to Q2 2024, in which ofatumumab was identified as the primary suspected drug.

title: DeepLNM: A Multimodal Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Colorectal Cancer
creator: Zhengyu Zhang, Chengyu Lu, Zhen Wang, Zhijian Cen, Yangshu Zhou, Danyi Li, Qi Xie, Bingbing Li, Shujing Guo, Zhijun Gan, Er‐ran Zhu, Jinbang Li, Aihetaimu Aimaier, Rui Mao, Weihao Qiu, Chenglong Zhao, Ying Tan, Xiaolin Liu, Huiting Ma, Tiansu Geng, Peiyue Wu, Huijun Du, Yu Wang, Yueping Liu, Li Lian
description: Accurate assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for prognostic stratification and treatment selection in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet imaging and routine pathology can yield false‐negative/false‐positive results. We propose DeepLNM, a multi‐center foundation model for LNM prediction in CRC, evaluated with retrospective, external, prospective, and user study evidence.

title: Additive Manufacturing of High‐Performance Polymers for Extreme Environments
creator: Md Tofazzal Hossain, Mohammed Intishar Nur, Md Shajedul Hoque Thakur, Indranil Dey, Md Mesbahul Maruf, Md Jahid Hasan, Suryasarathi Bose, Muhammad M Rahman
description: Additive manufacturing (AM) of high‐performance polymers (HPPs) has gained significant research interest due to its potential for applications in extreme environments, including aerospace, automotive, marine, and defense sectors. Components in these applications are often subjected to prolonged exposure to high temperatures, high mechanical loads, and chemically aggressive environments.

title: Artificial Grain Boundaries Created by Freestanding Membrane Transfer Reveal Angle‐Dependent Ferroelectric Switching and Leakage in BaTiO3
creator: Shin‐Rou Yin, Yu‐Hsin Lin, Yun‐Guan Wei, Yu‐Cheng Fang, Yung‐Chi Su, Yu‐Wei Chen, Yu‐Ting Lin, Chia‐Chun Wei, Chih‐Hung Wu, Ching‐Yu Chiang, Heng‐Jui Liu, Jan‐Chi Yang, Yi‐Chun Chen, Yen‐Lin Huang
description: Grain boundaries (GBs) strongly influence polycrystalline ferroelectrics, but their discrete effects are difficult to isolate because of nanoscale heterogeneity. Here, we use freestanding membrane transfer to fabricate artificial BaTiO3 GBs with controlled, experimentally accessible in‐plane misorientation angles (ϕ). Macroscopic electrical measurements show higher coercive voltage and leakage current at the GB region than in the coherent grain region.

title: Return‐to‐Sport Assessment After Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Reconstruction Shows Substantial Variability in Objective Criteria
creator: Louis Kang, Gavin H Ward, Mario Hevesi, Kelechi R Okoroha, Daniel B F Saris, Christopher L Camp, Aaron J Krych, Adam J Tagliero
description: PurposeTo evaluate objective return‐to‐sport (RTS) outcomes and limb symmetry index (LSI) data after primary medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction (MPFLR) in patients with patellar instability.MethodsA systematic search of Scopus, PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase (2000‐2024) identified studies reporting RTS outcomes and LSI‐based performance testing in patients undergoing primary MPFLR.

title: Ambient Air Pollution Health Impacts in High‐Income Countries, Part II: A Case Study in the United Arab Emirates
creator: Tongchuan Wei, Nathan Ellermeier, Nick Kruskamp, Amal Mubarak Madhi, Latifa Juma Al Shamsi, Basema Ahmad Saddik, Jacqueline MacDonald Gibson
description: Ambient air pollution poses major global public health risks, particularly in rapidly developing regions, including the Arabian Gulf. This study estimates the disease burden attributable to anthropogenic air pollution (particulate matter [PM] and ozone) in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, for 2019–2022 and compares findings to previous estimates for 2008.

title: Noninvasive assessment of the anaerobic threshold in endurance athletes: an evidence-based narrative review of methods, validity, and field feasibility
creator: Nicola Maffulli, Johnny Padulo, Francesco Oliva
description: Introduction or BackgroundThe anaerobic threshold (AnT) marks the transition between heavy and severe exercise intensity domains and guides training prescription and performance monitoring. Criterion methods (blood lactate and gas exchange) are accurate but invasive, costly, or impractical outside laboratories, prompting the search for noninvasive surrogates. This review evaluates the validity of these estimation procedures rather than the underlying physiology.

title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry in Neurobiology: From Imaging to Proteomics
creator: Neil Taylor, João de Sousa‐Lourenço, Ivana Nikić‐Spiegel
description: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has emerged as a versatile approach for probing molecules with high selectivity and minimal perturbation. While applicable to diverse biomolecules, its use in protein studies has proven particularly powerful, especially in neurobiology, where precise molecular tools are essential.

title: Fear of COVID-19, traumatic growth, and traumatic stress symptoms: the mediating role of basic psychological needs
creator: Rafael Gargurevich, Valeria Campodónico, Lennia Matos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Although COVID-19 brought many negative psychological consequences, many people also experienced psychological growth. The present study investigated why this happened and hypothesized that self-determination theory’s (SDT’s) basic psychological needs (BPNs) may play a role in this explanation. Based on SDT, this cross-sectional study hypothesized that both the satisfaction and frustration of BPNs mediated the associations between fear of COVID-19, post-traumatic growth (PTG), and post-traumatic stress (PTS) symptoms.

title: Sandwich‐Structured Aramid Composite Papers with Heterogeneous Dielectric Layers for Integrated Corona Resistance and Thermal Conductivity
creator: Jun‐Wen Ren, Jun‐Xue Chen, Ying‐Ying Tong, Zi Wang, Jia‐Cheng Zhang, Lin Zhang, Bo Zhang, Fan Zhang, Guo‐Long Wang, Jun‐Wei Zha, Shen‐Li Jia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aramid dielectric papers are indispensable for insulation in high‐performance motors for electric vehicles, aircraft, and high‐speed rail. However, the ongoing electrification trend toward higher voltage, frequency, and power density imposes severe electrothermal stresses that conventional aramid papers cannot withstand. Their inherently low thermal conductivity leads to localized heat accumulation while poor corona resistance accelerates electrothermal aging, both compromising long‐term motor reliability.

title: On quantitizing revisited
creator: Anthony J. Onwuegbuzie
description: This article builds on the highly cited 2009 article authored by Professor Emerita Margarete Sandelowski and her colleagues by critically reevaluating the process of quantitizing—transforming qualitative data into quantitative forms—a technique that has surprisingly not proliferated in academic research, presumably due to a shortage of methodological exploration in this area.

title: The Potential of Self‐Maintainable Living Materials
creator: Mohammadsadegh Nadimifar, Tatiane Eufrásio‐da‐Silva, Lidia Maeso, Gorka Orive, Alireza Dolatshahi‐Pirouz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Engineered living materials (ELMs) are emerging as a new class of autonomous and self‐maintainable systems that integrate metabolically active organisms within structural scaffolds to create materials capable of sensing, self‐repair, adaptive response, and long‐term functional persistence. Unlike conventional smart materials, which remain externally programmed and limited in regenerative capacity, ELMs leverage the intrinsic capabilities of microorganisms, fungi, algae, and mammalian cells to support continuous environmental interaction and feedback‐regulated behavior.

title: The influence of different negative feedback on the decay of self-deception
creator: Juan Liu, Wenjun Ding, Liying Deng, Min Tan, Peipei Guan
description: IntroductionThough some studies have found the positive influences of moderate self-deception on individuals and society, there are many that have shown its negative influences on individuals and society. Long-term self-deception will have negative influences which could cause high individual losses and even social disasters.

title: Individualized Network Topography in Pre-adolescent Children and Adults Using Naturalistic Precision fMRI
creator: Shefali Rai, Kate J. Godfrey, Kirk Graff, Ryann Tansey, Daria Merrikh, Shelly Yin, Matthew Feigelis, Damion V. Demeter, Tamara Vanderwal, Deanna J. Greene, Signe Bray
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Group-averaged network definitions, commonly used in developmental functional connectivity research, limit our understanding of how network topography may change with age and can lead to inaccurate estimates of age effects on intra- and inter-network functional connectivity. Here, we collected a precision fMRI dataset from 24 parent-child pairs (children 6–8 years, 13 females; adults 33–47 years, 12 females) during passive video viewing and derived individual template-matched functional network maps from 60 min of motion-censored data per participant.

title: Context-Dependent Functional Diversity of Dorsomedial Posterior Parietal Neurons Revealed by Single-Unit FMRI Mapping during Naturalistic Viewing
creator: Xufeng Zhou, Lei Wang, Shu K. E. Tam, Michael Ortiz-Rios, Dazhi Yin, Sze Chai Kwok
description: The dorsomedial posterior parietal cortex (dmPPC) plays an important role in episodic processing by integrating sensory, cognitive, and motor information across distributed brain systems. However, how individual dmPPC neurons participate in large-scale functional organization during naturalistic experience remains poorly understood.

title: Actors influencing cancer-related fatigue and the construction of a risk prediction model in lung cancer patients
creator: Mei-Ning Zhang, Yi-Chen Zhou, Zhu Zeng, Cun-Liang Zeng, Bo-Tao Hou, Gui-Rong Wu, Qiao Jiao, Dai-Yuan Ma
description: PurposeThe paper aims to investigate the factors influencing cancer-related fatigue (CRF) in lung cancer patients and construct a CRF risk prediction model, providing effective intervention strategies for clinical medical staff.MethodsThis paper employs convenience sampling to select 400 lung cancer patients who visited a tertiary hospital in Dazhou, Sichuan Province, from January 2021 to January 2022.

title: Type D Polyorchidism as an Incidental Finding in an Adult with an Indirect Inguinal Hernia: A Case Report
creator: Tuqa Abou Alssil, Mahran Al-Ali Al-khaleel, Basel Abdulrahman, Ali Abou Alsel
description: BackgroundPolyorchidism (supernumerary testis) is an extremely rare congenital anomaly of three or more testes. Bergholz et al reported that ~65% occur on the left side, with a median patient age of 17 years.Case PresentationA 27-year-old man presented with a gradually enlarging right inguinal swelling and mild discomfort.

title: Epigenetic Regulatory Networks in Cardiac Fibrosis: Therapeutic Targets, Crosstalk, and Future Directions
creator: Yansheng Yao, Chongyu Shao, Haitong Wan
description: Cardiac fibrosis is a central driver of pathological cardiac remodeling and a critical risk factor for the progression to heart failure. Cardiac fibrosis may induce myocardial ischemia and hypoxia, impaired cardiac function, and arrhythmias, and is thereby intimately linked to escalating cardiac mortality. Epigenetic mechanisms serve as core drivers in both the initiation and malignant evolution of cardiac fibrosis.

title: Increasing prevalence of thyroid autoimmunity in childhood type 1 diabetes in the pre-COVID but not during the COVID era
creator: Vivien Herczeg, Eszter Muzslay, Diána Czipó, Lili Terkovics, Johanna Takács, Réka Garai, Fanni Kovács, Andrea Luczay, Anna Körner, Péter Tóth-Heyn
description: IntroductionStudies assessing longitudinal changes in the prevalence of autoimmune thyroiditis (AIT) among the pediatric population are limited. During the COVID-19 era, several papers proposed a rise in AIT cases. Our study aimed to analyze the prevalence of thyroid autoimmunity (TA) over a 10-year period spanning pre-pandemic and pandemic years in a population who are regularly screened for thyroid disturbances.

title: Ecological and life history traits predict urban tolerance in North American birds
creator: Rachel Elizabeth Fanelli, Frances Bonier, Paul R. Martin
description: Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology.

title: Shengxue Busui Decoction activates the PI3K/Akt and VEGF pathways, enhancing vascular function and inhibiting osteocyte apoptosis to combat steroid-induced femoral head necrosis
creator: Manting Liu, Jiexiang Ye, Runtian Wu, Dongqiang Luo, Tao Huang, Dandan Dai, Kexin Wang, Yanping Du, Junwen Ou
description: IntroductionSteroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (SONFH) is a debilitating condition with no specific treatment. Inhibiting osteocyte apoptosis may be a promising therapeutic approach. Shengxue Busui Decoction (SBD) has shown protective effects against SONFH, but its mechanisms are not fully understood.

title: Bacteriophage Therapy in Cystic Fibrosis: Emerging Strategies for Managing Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa Infections
creator: Ayona Puthenpurayil, Lauren Gordon, Joanne L Fothergill
description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the leading cause of chronic respiratory infection in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) and remains a major driver of morbidity and premature mortality. The unique environment of the CF lung promotes persistent colonisation, biofilm formation, and the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) phenotypes, severely limiting the effectiveness of conventional antibiotic therapies.

title: Enteric ChAT‐Expressing Neurons Mediate the Protective Effect of Lactobacillus plantarum in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
creator: Bing Xia, Yuwei Sun, Jialin Wang, Yike Liu, Lu Wang, Shiqi Jiang, Gaiyan Bai, Ruijing Zhang, Yu Zhang, Rongwei Kou, Danna Wang, Beita Zhao, Junjie Yi, Yu Fu, Xiaoning Liu, Xuebo Liu
description: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), yet how specific microbial components influence disease progression remains incompletely understood. Our study reveals that decreased abundance of Lactobacillus species correlates with ulcerative colitis severity in patients. Among tested strains, L.

title: A cohort study of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and the risk of hyperlipidaemia in adults
creator: Zi-yue Liu, Sha Liu, Xue Yao, Chun-yang Wang, Yunhao Song, Yan-ming Bi, Jin-Xiu Wang, Yang Li, Ta-la Shi, Wei Mi, Caiyun Chen, Zhi-Yong Hu
description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the potential association between serum 25(OH)D levels and the risk of hyperlipidemia in adults through a prospective cohort study conducted in Zhejiang Province.MethodsBaseline surveys and follow-up studies were conducted to collect and analyze follow-up data over a three-year period.

title: Fc‐Dependent Targeting of the GAS6–MERTK Axis With Monoclonal and Bispecific Antibodies Overcomes Drug Resistance Across EGFR Mutations in Exons 19, 20, and 21
creator: Suvendu Giri, Boobash Raj Selvadurai, Nitin Gupta, Arturo Simoni‐Nieves, Alessandro Genna, Moshit Lindzen, Rishita Chatterjee, Marieke Van Daele, Deepthi Ramesh Kumar, Mirie Zerbib, Roni Oren, Isabelle Sophie Meijer, Elisabeth Franziska Wippich, Yahel Avraham, Rony Dahan, Yuya Haga, Laura E. Kilpatr
description: Resistance of lung cancer to EGFR‐targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like osimertinib frequently results from secondary mutations or activation of bypass signaling pathways. Re‐analysis of clinical data unveiled elevated expression of GAS6 and its receptor MERTK in lung cancer patients developing resistance to osimertinib. This implied that the GAS6–MERTK axis could represent a therapeutic vulnerability.

title: Interface Rectification via Roll‐to‐Roll Dual‐Confinement Nanocoatings for High‐Temperature Polymer Capacitors
creator: Ning Guo, Marina Dabaghian, Jierui Zhou, Josh N. Bodin, Chong Xiang, Fei Wang, Antigoni Konstantinou, Dingxin Wei, Yifei Wang, Chao Wu, Riccardo Casalini, Bryan Huey, Priya Vashishta, Luyi Sun, Yang Cao
description: Polymer film capacitors are indispensable for energy storage and power conversion, yet their energy density and efficiency deteriorate rapidly at elevated temperatures. At temperatures relevant to wide‐bandgap semiconductor electronics (>150°C), heat‐resistant polymer films must be heavily derated to avoid premature aging due to intensive hot‐carrier injection.

title: Factors associated with the revolving door phenomenon in patients with schizophrenia: results from an acute psychiatric hospital in Romania
creator: Vlad Dionisie, Maria Gabriela Puiu, Mihnea Costin Manea, Emanuel Moisa, Ana Maria Dumitru, Leila Ibadula, Aliss Madalina Mares, Corina Ioana Varlam, Mirela Manea
description: BackgroundThe revolving door phenomenon refers to patients with frequent hospital admissions and emerged after deinstitutionalization reforms have been implemented. Schizophrenia is a severe and debilitating mental disorder and has frequently been identified as one of the most prevalent disorders among revolving door patients.

title: PDHA1 Hyperactivation‐Mediated Glucose Metabolism Reprogramming Fuels Neutrophil NETosis and Promotes Acute Lung Injury
creator: Yu‐Biao Liu, Wen‐Jing Zhong, Chen‐Yu Zhang, Meng‐Rui Chen, Nan‐Shi‐Yu Yang, Han‐Xi Sha, Yan‐Ling Qiu, Hui Chen, Jin‐Tong Yang, Li‐Ying Liang, Jian‐Bing Xiong, Shao‐Kun Liu, Cha‐Xiang Guan, Jia‐Xi Duan, Yong Zhou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, termed NETosis, is a key driver of lung tissue injury in acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ALI/ARDS). However, the precise mechanisms that trigger neutrophil NETosis remain incompletely understood. Here, we observed that neutrophils from both ALI mice and ARDS patients exhibited NETosis alongside a pronounced selective metabolic shift, characterized by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and attenuated glycolytic activity.

title: Optical Access to Dark Excitons Via Spin–Phonon Fano Interference
creator: Janina J Schindler, Katja Barthelmi, Mikhail M Glazov, Carlo Sgroi, Sven Scholz, Arne Ludwig, Andreas D Wieck, Jörg Debus
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spin‐dark excitons in semiconductor nanostructures are inherently optically silent: angular‐momentum selection rules forbid their radiative recombination, granting long lifetimes attractive for quantum information storage and excitonic condensation, but placing their energy structure and bright–dark coupling beyond standard optical spectroscopy. Established access routes rely on symmetry‐lowering perturbations, dedicated single‐emitter device fabrication, or near‐field methods, each of which perturbs the states under study or excludes ensembles.

title: Comments on “Into the future: first robotic totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass in Southeast Asia”
creator: Safa Özçelik
description: We read with great interest the report describing the first robotic totally endoscopic coronary artery bypass (TECAB) in Southeast Asia. While this achievement deserves recognition, we believe several aspects—including revascularization strategy, prolonged operative and recovery times, and the lack of intraoperative transit-time flow measurement—require further clarification to accurately interpret the clinical significance of this pioneering experience.

title: Ferula communis leaf extract: antioxidant capacity, UHPLC–MS/MS analysis, and in vivo and in silico toxicity investigations
creator: Imad Ed-Dahmani, Mohamed El Fadili, Ghizlane Nouioura, Fahd Kandsi, Yassine El Atki, Hatem A. Abuelizz, Raffaele Conte, Fatima Zahra Lafdil, Abdeslam Taleb, Abdelfattah Abdellaoui, Mustapha Taleb
description: Introduction Ferula communis has demonstrated an abundance of pharmacological and antioxidative qualities.MethodsThis study investigates the antioxidant activity of F. communis leaf aqueous extract, total polyphenol and flavonoid concentrations, and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography (UHPLC) composition and then evaluates the toxicity of the plant’s leaves in vitro and in silico.

title: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial
creator: Ahmed M. Moaz, Khaled E. Barakat, Walid Elshazly, Yasser Zaki, Amr Badawy, Bassem Kh. Hegazy, Ahmed M. Mohieldein
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDiverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak.

title: Author Correction: Versatile molecular tools enabling customizable DNA methylation editing in Arabidopsis
creator: Li He, Yao Yao, Yin You, Xiaofei Wei, Yu Ma, Wei Yuan, Zhaobo Lang, Jian-Kang Zhu
description: an autofill error. The underlying qPCR measurements were correct, but “nrpe1-6” and “nrpe1-7” were mistakenly shown as “nrpe1-4” and “nrpe1-5”, respectively, while “nrpe1-1” and “nrpe1-2” were mislabeled as “nrpe1-6” and “nrpe1-7.” The Source Data, figure and legend have been updated. In Figs.

title: Domestication of medicinal plants (Lonicera japonica Thunb.) in China: comparison of morphological, resistance and biochemical traits between wild and cultivated populations
creator: Congzhe Hou, Luyao Huang, Zhuangzhuang Li, Nan Sun, Sheng Yang, Jia Li, Zhenhua Liu
description: BackgroundMost studies on domesticated plants have focused on those utilized for sustenance purposes. This study provides valuable insights into the domestication processes of honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica Thunb.), a semi-evergreen twining vine in the Caprifoliaceae family that is important in traditional Chinese medicine for its flower buds and potential as a dietary supplement.

title: Author Correction: A microbial platform for selective biosynthesis of monoterpene esters
creator: Dianqi Yang, Hong Liang, Xuxu Li, Bowen Wang, Chenyu Zhang, Mengyao Yuan, Kang Zhou, Zhiyong Cui, Panhao Niu, Yi-Lei Zhao, Yuan Liu, Zuobing Xiao, Lianzhong Ai, Yongjin J. Zhou, Baoguo Sun, Xiaoqiang Ma
description: rminology and labeling errors. In two section titles in the Results, “monoterpenyl ester” now replaces “monoterpenoate ester”; in several instances in the Results “benzyl alcohol with benzoyl-CoA” now replaces the original “benzoyl-CoA with benzoyl-CoA”; “geranyl-CoA” has been revised to read “geranoyl-CoA” and “perillyl-CoA” to “perilloyl-CoA” in Fig. 3, the legends for Figs. 1 and 3, Supplementary Fig.

title: Spectral sensing at a glance
creator: Andreas Tittl
description: Portable biosensors are revolutionizing the way we diagnose disease and ill-health. By varying a metasurface’s geometry continuously across a chip, a recent study by H. Kim et al. reports a new sensing strategy, which reads signals from individual camera images without the need for a spectrometer. This enables the label-free detection of biomarkers in a handheld format.

title: The adductor pollicis muscle thickness is not associated with physical function, lean mass, and nutritional status in patients on maintenance hemodialysis
creator: Débora Moreira Morais, Isadora Cordeiro Trombim, Cassiana Regina de Góes, Barbara Perez Vogt
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe adductor pollicis muscle thickness (APMT) may be associated with the muscle strength in patients on hemodialysis. However, the association of APMT with other physical function assessment tests has not yet been tested. Moreover, because it is considered a good nutritional indicator and not influenced by fluid overload, the APMT may be associated with the muscle mass and nutritional status of these patients.

title: From compliance to competence: a multi-level model for AI governance in undergraduate medical education
creator: Juan José Gualda-Gea, Lourdes Estefanía Barón-Miras, Maria Jesús Bertran, Alberto L. Garcia-Basteiro, Guillermo Mena, Marta Aldea, Gemina Santana, Jaume Grau, Andrés Prat Marin, Isabel Torá-Rocamora, Antoni Trilla
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AI's fast-paced irruption in medicine and education has challenged undergraduate medical colleges, with institutions documenting policies emphasizing immediate conduct restrictions, while strategic oversight, infrastructure and evaluation remain less consistently developed. We propose a multi-level framework for AI governance in undergraduate medical education based on accountability, competence and co-responsibility across institutions, educators and students, designed to turn a fast-evolving technology from a threat into an opportunity for collective progress.

title: Clinical burden of obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in France
creator: Philippe Charron, Carla Zema, François-Emery Cotté, Eléonore Herquelot, Taryn Krause, Florent Daydé, Jean-Noël Trochu
description: BackgroundHypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) can be genetic and occurs as obstructive and non-obstructive 21 subtypes. Little is known about the clinical burden of the obstructive subtype of HCM at a national 22 level, and how it may differ by New York Heart Association (NYHA) class.

title: Serial H&E Pathology Reveals Progression‐Associated Nuclear Size Drift as a Longitudinal Digital Readout of Bladder Cancer Evolution
creator: Xing Liu, Zhen‐Duo Shi, Gong‐Cheng Wang, Jian‐Ming Wang, Ying Liu, Yi Gong, Xuan Lin, Di Wu, Shi‐Chao Zhuo, Han Han, Yi‐Bing Shi, Fan‐Lai Meng, Yu Zhang, Zhi‐Gang Jia, Cong‐Hui Han
description: Serial pathological specimens are routinely generated during bladder cancer surveillance, but their temporal information remains underused in computational pathology. This study develops a longitudinal digital pathology framework to quantify direction‐preserving nuclear morphological change within the same patient.
