creator: Ian López-Cruz, José Luis García-Giménez, Manuel Madrazo, Judit García-Guallarte, Laura Piles, Federico V. Pallardó, Arturo Artero
description: IntroductionSepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated immune response to infection, leading to organ failure. Despite its significant global burden, the underlying mechanisms of immune dysfunction in sepsis remain incompletely understood. This study explores the role of DNA methylation in white blood cells in sepsis pathogenesis.

title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
creator: Luissa Vahedi, Susan Pradhan, Sakina Zaidi, Vanessa Brizuela, Sabina Faiz Rashid, Maha El Adawy, Rana Hajjeh, Michelle Gaffey, Zulfiqar A. Bhutta
description: SummaryThis scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Eligible sources had to investigate climate change and SRHR using any study design.

title: Positive response to trastuzumab deruxtecan in a patient with HER2-mutant NSCLC after multiple lines therapy, including T-DM1: a case report
creator: Junzhu Xu, Bo He, Yunan Wang, Mengjia Wu, Yanyi Lu, Zixuan Su, Shujun Liu, Fengmin Yin, Jian-Guo Zhou, Wei Hu
description: Human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2) mutations are uncommon in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and the lack of established, effective, targeted drugs has resulted in a persistently poor prognosis. Herein, we report the case of a non-smoking, 58-year-old man diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma (cT3N0M1c, stage IVB) harboring a HER2 mutation (Y772_A775dupYVMA) and PD-L1 (-).

title: Fucoidan alleviated colitis aggravated by fiber deficiency through protecting the gut barrier, suppressing the MAPK/NF-κB pathway, and modulating gut microbiota and metabolites
creator: Weiyun Zheng, Shuangru Tang, Xiaomeng Ren, Shuang Song, Chunqing Ai
description: Insufficient dietary fiber intake has become a global public health issue, affecting the development and management of various diseases, including intestinal diseases and obesity. This study showed that dietary fiber deficiency enhanced the susceptibility of mice to colitis, which could be attributed to the disruption of the gut barrier integrity, activation of the NF-κB pathway, and oxidative stress.

title: Neoadjuvant versus adjuvant chemotherapy in luminal B-like breast cancer: a subset analysis of the CANTO study
creator: T. Gaillard, P. Cottu, O. Tredan, A.-L. Martin, C. Gaudin, A. Bertaut, C. Cheymol, C. Kaderbhai, F. Cherifi, M. Campone, M.-A. Mouret-Reynier, A. Di-Meglio, F. Reyal, A.S. Hamy-Petit, E. Laas
description: BackgroundThe benefit of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in hormone receptor (HR)-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer (BC) remains uncertain, given low pathologically documented complete response (pCR) rates and limited long-term comparative data. We compared overall survival (OS) between NAC and adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) in luminal B-like breast cancer treated in routine practice.

title: Validation of the Spanish version of the Psychological Flexibility Sports Scale (PFSS)
creator: Alejandro Garcia-Pardina, Oscar A. Belloso, Alberto Bellido-Esteban, Almudena Montalvo-Pérez, Lidia Budziszewska
description: IntroductionPsychological flexibility has been conceptualized as the capacity to relate to internal experiences, maintain focus on the present moment, thereby allowing individuals to act according to the context in pursuit of their goals and values. It is a psychological construct related to mental health, where there is an increasing body of research that highlights its importance in athletic performance.

title: Efficacy and safety of temporary selective portal vein embolization before major hepatectomy (EMBORES): a phase 2 trial
creator: Hadrien Tranchart, Sophie Maitre, Edouard Girard, Julien Ghelfi, Maximiliano Gelli, Lambros Tselikas, Maxime Barat, David Fuks, Anthony Sarran, Stéphane Benoist, Olivier Meyrignac, Ailton Sepulveda, Maxime Ronot, Maryne Pou, Mircea Chirica, Ibrahim Dagher, Christian Sengel, Christian Sengel, Antoine
description: SummaryBackgroundPortal vein embolization (PVE) is routinely used before major hepatectomy to induce hypertrophy of the future liver remnant (FLR) and reduce post-hepatectomy liver failure. Conventional PVE relies on permanent embolic agents, resulting in irreversible portal occlusion, which may be associated with complications and may limit subsequent therapeutic options in patients who do not ultimately undergo resection.

title: Prophylactic phage administration provides a time window for delayed treatment of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis in a murine bacteremia model
creator: Wei-Xiao Wang, Jiao-Yang Yu, Xiu-Zhen Chen, Shi-Yong Fu, Hui Li, Peng-Cheng Yi, Yun-Yao Ren, Shuang-Lin Gu, Jing-Han Gao, Jing Fan, Yan-Mei Sun, Jie Feng, Shi-Wei Wang, Wei Chen
description: IntroductionVancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis (VRE) poses a significant challenge in clinical settings due to its resistance to multiple antibiotics. Phage therapy offers a promising alternative to address this resistance crisis. However, critical gaps remain regarding optimal dosing, therapeutic design, and treatment timing for phage therapy targeting VRE-induced bacteremia.

title: Gut microbiota and quantitative traits divergence at different altitude of long-tailed dwarf hamsters, Cricetulus longicaudatus
creator: Yue Ren, Mengfan Tao, Xiaoliang Wang, Xinsheng Pu, Guangtong Guo, Kuiyou Chen, Bingyu Zhao, Yu Hou, Xin'gen Yang, Yumei Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To investigate the community structure and diversity of gut microflora and their function in body mass regulation, as well as the effects of various locations on gut microbiota and Cricetulus longicaudatus body mass regulation at various elevations. We examined the diversity, abundance, and community structure of the gut microbiota of long-tailed dwarf hamsters from eight regions in Shanxi province during summer using 16S rDNA sequencing technology and analyzed the relationships between these microbiota and environmental variables as well as morphological indicators.

title: Protocol for fabricating immune-regulatory bone organoids via plant-based bioinks
creator: Tianhao Wang, Gan Gao, Xiaoxu Zhang, Kaifeng Huo, Chenglong Liu, Zhen Geng, Long Bai, Hao Zhang, Han Liu, Ke Xu, Yuxiao Lai, Jianhua Wang, Yingying Jing, Chongru He, Guangchao Wang, Jiacan Su, Xiaoxiang Ren
description: SummaryBone organoids offer three-dimensional systems for studying skeletal development, disease, and regeneration. However, many existing bone organoid systems do not adequately incorporate immune-regulatory cues, despite their central role in bone repair. Their translational potential is further limited by the use of animal-derived matrices such as Matrigel, which are xenogeneic, poorly defined, and subject to batch-to-batch variation.

title: Autonomic Dysfunction as a Potential Pathophysiological Link Between Chronic Low Back Pain and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review
creator: Waqas Alauddin, Rahul Saxena, Arushi Saxena, Sayali Khairnar, Srisaisantoshini Sankaranarayanan, Brishabh R Prajesh, Fahad Shaikh, Soumya Singh
description: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a leading cause of disability worldwide and is increasingly recognized as a condition associated with systemic physiological alterations beyond musculoskeletal dysfunction. Emerging evidence suggests that autonomic nervous system dysregulation may be associated with impaired cardiovascular regulation and increased cardiovascular risk in individuals with CLBP.

title: Expression of Properdin, the positive regulator of the Complement Alternative Pathway, at the fetal-maternal interface in Preeclampsia
creator: Hadida Yasmin, Tamali Roy, Chiara Agostinis, Aishwarya Rao, Priyanka Sharma, Miriam Toffoli, Andrea Balduit, Silvia Pegoraro, Samik Bindu, Rajib Prasad, Giuseppe Ricci, Manu Vatish, Taruna Madan, Roberta Bulla, Uday Kishore
description: IntroductionAberrant complement activation can cause damage to newly formed fetal-derived structures and excessive inflammatory response at the feto-maternal interface, contributing to pregnancy-related complications, including preeclampsia (PE), which is one of the most severe pathologies in new-borns. Properdin is the only known positive regulator of the complement alternative pathway, as it stabilizes the inherently labile C3bBb complex and amplifies its activity.

title: Impact of aging on the tumor microenvironment in oral cancer: Mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives
creator: Prathibha Prasad, Ayman S. Amer, Anas Shamsi, Rashmi metgud, Khuzin Dinislam
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Oral cancer is a significant health problem worldwide, with particularly great impacts on elderly people. The aging process has a major impact on the tumor microenvironment (TME), affecting tumor initiation, progression, and the response to therapy. The present review summarizes the existing evidence regarding the effects of aging on the TME in oral cancer, the progression of oral diseases, and the implications for therapy.

title: Case Report: Refractory macrophage activation syndrome requiring high-dose anakinra, emapalumab, and etoposide therapy in early-onset systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis associated with adenoviremia
creator: Elizabeth D. Slaney, Renee Modica, Leandra Woolnough, Dina Kafisheh, Denise Heather Bell-Brunson, Melissa Elder
description: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a life-threatening condition characterized by the excessive stimulation of macrophages and T lymphocytes, provoked by infections, malignancy, and autoimmune or autoinflammatory conditions such as systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA). Clinical signs of sJIA may include high-spiking, quotidian fevers, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and a salmon-colored migratory, evanescent rash.

title: Association between the ascending aortic length and sporadic type A aortic dissection
creator: Dan Rong, Shaofan Wang, Feng Liu, Jianhan Yin, Wei Guo
description: ObjectiveThis study was performed to outline the aortic dimensions of type A aortic dissection and to investigate the association between the ascending aortic length and sporadic, non-syndromic type A aortic dissection in a Chinese population.MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, all consecutive patients diagnosed with type A aortic dissection between January 2016 and December 2020 were identified.

title: Sensor-controlled fertigation management for higher yield and quality in greenhouse hydroponic strawberries
creator: George Kerrigan Hutchinson, Lan Xuan Nguyen, Zilfina Rubio Ames, Krishna Nemali, Rhuanito Soranz Ferrarezi
description: Controlled environment agriculture (CEA) for strawberry (Fragaria x ananassa) production has experienced a growth in popularity in recent years, particularly in North America. One of the most common growing systems in CEA strawberry production is the soilless hydroponic system, which uses an inert substrate and nutrient solution to grow the plants.

title: Vulnerabilities among children of migrant rag pickers in UT Jammu and Kashmir: examining in the context of sustainable development goals 4 and 10
creator: Shabir Ahmad Najar, Wakar Amin Zargar, Bilal Ahmad Khan
description: PurposeThis study focuses on to scrutinize the experiences as well as the varying degrees of helplessness of children born into rag picking families. Within the agenda of Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education) and Goal 10 (Reducing Inequalities), this study demonstrates the systemic holes in learning and deepening cycles of dissimilarity slavery faced by children from migrant rag picking communities.

title: Add-on effects of oral tocopherol supplementation to surgical varicocelectomy on the outcome of assisted reproductive technology: a single-center pilot study report
creator: Teppei Takeshima, Takahiro Mihara, Makoto Tomita, Shinnosuke Kuroda, Yasushi Yumura, Hiroe Ueno, Mizuki Yamamoto, Mariko Murase
description: IntroductionVaricocelectomy is well known to improve the pregnancy outcome of patients with clinical varicoceles in assisted reproductive technologies as well as spontaneous conception. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the additional effects of oral antioxidant therapy after varicocelectomy on the pregnancy outcome in the assisted reproductive technology setting.MethodsThis study was a retrospective cohort study.

title: Association between Yo-yo intermittent recovery test, physiological markers of endurance performance, and buffering capacity in professional soccer players
creator: R.C.A. Ferreira, V.O. Silvino, L.V. Vilhena, M.A.P. dos Santos, D.M.L. do Prado
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIR1) is widely recognized as a reliable tool for assessing intermittent endurance and aerobic capacity in team sports athletes. This study aims to verify the association between YYIR1 and physiological markers of endurance performance in professional soccer players, as well as the relationship between metabolic buffering capacity, metabolic acidosis tolerance, and YYIR1 total distance.

title: Divergent HLA variations and heterogeneous expression but recurrent HLA loss-of- heterozygosity and common HLA-B and TAP transcriptional silencing across advanced pediatric solid cancers
creator: Wan Ching Lim, Maria Eugenia Marques Da Costa, Karine Godefroy, Eric Jacquet, Loren Gragert, Windy Rondof, Antonin Marchais, Naima Nhiri, Davide Dalfovo, Mathias Viard, Nizar Labaied, Asif M. Khan, Philippe Dessen, Alessandro Romanel, Claudia Pasqualini, Gudrun Schleiermacher, Mary Carrington, Laure
description: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is a major factor controlling cancer immunosurveillance and response to immunotherapy, yet its status in pediatric cancers remains fragmentary. We determined high-confidence HLA genotypes in 576 children, adolescents and young adults with recurrent/refractory solid tumors from the MOSCATO-01 and MAPPYACTS trials, using normal and tumor whole exome and RNA sequencing data and benchmarked algorithms.

title: Systematic analysis of the scientific quality, reliability, and educational value of Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery videos on YouTube
creator: Okay Alptekin, Betül Kalkan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SUMMARYOBJECTIVE:The aim of this study was to evaluate the scientific quality, reliability, and educational value of YouTube videos on Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery using structured assessment tools.METHODS:This cross-sectional study analyzed 20 YouTube videos on Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery identified using the keywords "Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery," "Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery hysterectomy," "vaginal natural orifice endoscopic surgery," and "transvaginal NOTES." Two obstetrics and gynecology specialists independently evaluated the videos using the Global Quality Scale, modified

title: Association of the lymphocyte-to–C-reactive protein ratio with long-term mortality in hospitalized older adults with severe dysphagia
creator: Xuejin Zhong, Dongjie Huang, Yuling Chen, Zeru Chen, Xiaomi Chen, Shuyue Zhou, Yutong Lu, Nuoyan Huang, Xiaoling Wu, Haiwei Chen, Mingdi Chen
description: BackgroundDysphagia is highly prevalent among older adults and is strongly associated with malnutrition, chronic inflammation, and multiple comorbidities, all of which contribute to increased mortality. The lymphocyte-to–C-reactive protein ratio (LCR) has recently gained attention as an immunonutritional biomarker, yet its prognostic relevance in elderly individuals with dysphagia remains unclear.

title: Encéphalite équine de l’Est (EEE) neuro-invasive chez une femme de 56 ans jusque-là en bonne santé
creator: Brian Yu Chieh Cheng, Reid Carey Gallant, Richard Xu, Dominik Mertz
description: eurs de risque de la forme neuro-invasive de l’EEE comprennent un âge inférieur à 15 ans ou supérieur à 50 ans et l’immunodépression. Les facteurs de risque de la forme neuro-invasive de l’EEE comprennent un âge inférieur à 15 ans ou supérieur à 50 ans et l’immunodépression.

title: Global progress in competitive co-evolution: a systematic comparison of alternative methods
creator: Stefano Nolfi, Paolo Pagliuca
description: The usage of broad sets of training data is paramount to evolve adaptive agents. In this respect, competitive co-evolution is a widespread technique in which the coexistence of different learning agents fosters adaptation, which in turn makes agents experience continuously varying environmental conditions.

title: A 60-year-old man with Dupuytren disease
creator: Vincent Dinh, Barbara Jemec, Kevin Cheung
description: ing (black circle) over the distal palmar crease between the fourth and fifth rays. (B) Established palmar cord (black arrow) in line with the fifth ray, causing flexion contracture of the fifth finger (different patient). What is the diagnosis? The diagnosis is Dupuytren disease, a fibroproliferative disorder of the palmar fascia.

title: Assessing daydreaming frequency and control with the Polish version of the Daydreaming Frequency Scale – validation using ecological momentary assessment
creator: Michał S. Skorupski, Izabela Krejtz, Monika Kornacka
description: Daydreaming is a prevalent type of cognitive activity, in which the content of one’s thoughts is unrelated to the current task. The Daydreaming Frequency Scale (DDFS) was the first questionnaire devised to measure the occurrence of daydreaming and remains widely used for this purpose today. We report on three studies validating the Polish version of the DDFS.

title: Prevalence and characteristics of disabilities in physicians in Canada: an analysis of Canadian Census data
creator: Michael J. Quon, Boris Kralj, Andrew Neitzel, Manish M. Sood, Arthur Sweetman, Maya A. Gibb, Daniel T. Myran
description: Background:Despite the importance of equity and accessibility with respect to the medical workforce in Canada, limited data exist on physicians with disabilities. We aimed to estimate the prevalence and types of disabilities among physicians and compare them with other occupations.Methods:We performed a population-based cross-sectional study using weighted data from the 2021 mandatory Canadian long-form Census, obtained from Statistics Canada.

title: Mucinous adenocarcinoma with peritoneal carcinomatosis presenting as acute abdomen: a case report
creator: Resul Nusretoğlu, Abdullahi Khalif Ali
description: BackgroundOvarian mucinous cystadenocarcinoma is a rare malignant epithelial tumor, accounting for approximately 10–15% of ovarian carcinomas. It typically presents with nonspecific abdominal symptoms and may reach a large size before detection. Presentation as an acute abdomen is uncommon and usually reflects advanced disease complicated by rupture or extensive peritoneal carcinomatosis.

title: A national spatial prioritisation framework for the targeted expansion of essential sickle cell disease services across health-facility catchments in Uganda
creator: George Paasi, Grace Ndeezi, Ruth Namazzi, Ezekiel Mupere, Ian Guyton Munabi, Sarah Kiguli, Richard Idro, Peter Olupot-Olupot
description: BackgroundSickle cell disease causes substantial childhood morbidity and premature mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, while access to essential services remains uneven. In Uganda, geographic variation in inherited SCD risk supports spatially targeted service planning.MethodsWe conducted a national facility-linked ecological spatial planning analysis using 280 eligible higher-level public facilities.

title: A combined approach of simulation-based “debriefing with good judgment” and case-based learning to enhance clinical thinking in Chinese residents
creator: Wenming Shao, Xin Cheng, Wanjie Gu, Yu Yan, Hiu Liu, Jialin Zhang, Li Zhang, Haiyan Yin, Mingya Zhang
description: ObjectiveClinical reasoning is a fundamental and critical competency for physicians. However, how to effectively help resident trainees to develop and enhance this ability remains a challenge for medical instructors. In this study, a teaching approach that combines simulation-based “Debriefing with Good Judgment” (DwGJ) with Case-Based Learning (CBL) was employed to improve the clinical reasoning among standardized training residents.

title: The role of interleukin-17 in inflammation-related cancers
creator: Xingru Zhang, Bangjie Li, Tian Lan, Conner Chiari, Xiaoyang Ye, Kepeng Wang, Ju Chen
description: Emerging evidence indicates a correlation between inflammation and the development and progression of cancer. Among the various inflammatory signals, interleukin-17 (IL-17) family cytokines serve as a critical link between inflammation and cancer. IL-17 is a highly versatile pro-inflammatory cytokine that plays a pivotal role in host defense, tissue repair, the pathogenesis of inflammatory diseases, and cancer progression.

title: Multi-scenario pear tree inflorescence detection based on improved YOLOv7 object detection algorithm
creator: Zhen Zhang, Xiaohui Lei, Kai Huang, Yuanhao Sun, Jin Zeng, Tao Xyu, Quanchun Yuan, Yannan Qi, Andreas Herbst, Xiaolan Lyu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Efficient and precise thinning during the orchard blossom period is a crucial factor in enhancing both fruit yield and quality. The accurate recognition of inflorescence is the cornerstone of intelligent blossom equipment. To advance the process of intelligent blossom thinning, this paper addresses the issue of suboptimal performance of current inflorescence recognition algorithms in detecting dense inflorescence at a long distance. It introduces an inflorescence recognition algorithm, YOLOv7-E, based on the YOLOv7 neural network model.

title: Population-scale reconstruction of menopause dynamics reveals a physiological cliff at the final menstrual period
creator: Glen Pridham, Yoav Hayut, Noa Lavi-Shoseyov, Michal Neeman, Noa Hovav, Yoel Toledano, Uri Alon
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Menopause reshapes female physiology, yet current understanding is limited by small longitudinal cohorts that characterize it as a gradual transition. Large-scale biomedical datasets remain underutilized because the final menstrual period (FMP) age is rarely recorded. Here we present a computational framework, inspired by astronomy, that reconstructs FMP-anchored trajectories from cross-sectional data by removing the blurring caused by variation in FMP age across individuals.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches
creator: Leeor S. Yefet, Gelareh Zadeh, Farshad Nassiri
description: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations.

title: Benefits Trafficking: human trafficking of older adults and adults with disabilities
creator: Anna Thomas, Heather Strickland
description: An emerging type of trafficking is targeting overlooked at-risk adults. Benefits Trafficking is the systematic recruitment, harboring, neglect, and financial exploitation of elder and disabled adults who receive government benefits such as Social Security, Veteran's Benefits, Medicaid, and Medicare. Traffickers often pose as kind-hearted individuals offering to provide care for at-risk adults in an in-home setting.

title: Clinical and genetic analysis of epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures caused by SLC6A1 gene variant
creator: Zhen Li, Changming Han, Hongwei Zhao
description: ObjectiveThis research intends to examine the clinical characteristics and genetic diversity of a child experiencing epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures (EMAS) attributed to a variant in the SLC6A1 gene.MethodsA male child diagnosed with EMAS underwent clinical and electroencephalographic evaluation. Peripheral blood samples were collected for DNA extraction and subsequent whole-exon gene sequencing.

title: Comparative evaluation of classical and modified Tamra Bhasma: Acute oral toxicity, antimicrobial, and antioxidant profiles
creator: Guruprasad C. Nille, Ritu Raj Patel, Himanshu Ranjan, Amaresh Kumar Singh, Meenakshi Singh, Nitesh Singh, Vijay M. Shinde, Anand Kumar Chaudhary
description: BackgroundTamra Bhasma, a traditional Ayurvedic copper-based formulation, has been used for its antimicrobial and therapeutic benefits. However, its complex preparation and the risk of toxicity when not made according to classical methods have limited its broader clinical use. Recent efforts aim to simplify its preparation and scientifically validate its safety and efficacy.

title: Optimization of kefir fermentation with plantain peel addition: effects on composition, microbial viability, and sensory quality
creator: Andrea Pissatto Peres, Cláudia Puerari, Juliana Aparecida Correia Bento, Rafael Alexandre dos Santos Martins, Yasmin Ourives Domingues, Maressa Caldeira Morzelle
description: Kefir is a fermented dairy product that can be prepared through microbial fermentation using kefir grains. These grains consist of a symbiotic community of bacteria and yeasts that influence the chemical composition, texture, and sensory characteristics of fermented milk. The incorporation of fruit by-products during fermentation has been explored as a strategy to enhance the functional quality of kefir-based beverages.

title: Targeting lipophagy and nuclear receptors in metabolic-associated fatty liver disease: insights from traditional Chinese medicine
creator: Ting Yue, Nafei Huang, Ziming Zhao, Lili Yu, Xiaoming He, Xiao Yu, Yi Zheng
description: Background: Metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) represents a globally prevalent chronic hepatic disorder hallmarked by excessive lipid accumulation within hepatocytes. This condition can progressively deteriorate to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, thereby imposing a substantial healthcare burden. Numerous laboratory studies confirm that drugs targeting the nuclear receptor (NR)-lipophagy axis exhibit preventive and therapeutic potential for MAFLD.

title: Beyond the Favorable-Risk Label: Sequential Measurable Residual Disease and KIT Variant Status in Pediatric Core-Binding Factor Acute Myeloid Leukemia
creator: Bohyun Kim
description: ing to RUNX1:RUNX1T1 and CBFB:MYH11 at the molecular level, respectively [1]. Both the 5th edition of the WHO Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumors (WHO-HAEM5) and the International Consensus Classification (ICC) classify these fusions as AML defined by specific genetic variants, enabling diagnosis based on genetic findings rather than morphology alone.

title: Long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of efgartigimod (ADAPT+): interim results from a phase 3 open-label extension study in participants with generalized myasthenia gravis
creator: James F. Howard, Vera Bril, Tuan Vu, Chafic Karam, Stojan Peric, Jan L. De Bleecker, Hiroyuki Murai, Andreas Meisel, Said R. Beydoun, Mamatha Pasnoor, Antonio Guglietta, Benjamin Van Hoorick, Sophie Steeland, Caroline T’joen, Kimiaki Utsugisawa, Jan Verschuuren, Renato Mantegazza, the ADAPT+ Study G
description: ObjectiveADAPT+ assessed the long-term safety, tolerability, and efficacy of efgartigimod in adult participants with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).MethodsADAPT+ was an open-label, single-arm, multicenter, up to 3-year extension of the pivotal phase 3 ADAPT study. Efgartigimod was administered in treatment cycles of 4 intravenous infusions (one 10 mg/kg infusion per week).

title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of surgical resection for brain metastases from lung adenocarcinoma
creator: Ming Li, Zhiying Li, Hang Zhang, Hiroaki Wakimoto, Linlin Sun, Tiantian Wang, Shengli Zhou, Liyun Zhou
description: ObjectiveThe purpose of this study was to explore the clinical characteristics, survival time and prognostic factors of patients undergoing craniotomy for brain metastases (BM) from lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD).MethodsA total of 208 patients with BM from LUAD who underwent craniotomy at the Zhengzhou University People’s Hospital, Henan province, China from March 2005 to October 2022 were included in this retrospective study.

title: The mechanism of short-chain fatty acid in hypertriglyceridemic pancreatitis
creator: Tingting Li, Fuyu Deng, Jiong Xiong, Fangqi Wu, Songxun Tang, Yijie Zhang, Qiyong Zhang, Jian Song, Yi Li, Xu Liu, Yan Tang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe incidence of hypertriglyceridemia pancreatitis (HTGP) has been rising annually with a poor prognosis, and its pathogenesis is complex. In recent years, the role of gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) has gradually attracted attention in HTGP. Therefore, the aim of this study was to investigate the characteristic alterations in gut microbiota and SCFAs and their potential clinical significance and molecular mechanisms in HTGP.Materials and methodsThis study collected feces and serum samples from 18 HTGP patients and 18 healthy volunteers.

title: Surgical cancellation and changes in postoperative level of care among high and moderate risk surgical patients in the UK
creator: Joanna K L Wong, Rosanna Sasson, Christopher Oddy, Pan-London Perioperative Audit and Research Network Committee, The REPACC Study Investigators
description: Background:The clinical and administrative pressures leading to cancellation of surgery are well established. However, it is not known whether the same factors lead to a change in patients’ planned postoperative destination and level of care.Methods:We conducted a secondary analysis of the REPACC dataset; a nationwide, retrospective, observational study examining the provision of enhanced and critical care services in the UK.

title: Tailored Amino Acid Treatment for Pediatric Patients With Mitochondrial Aminoacyl‐tRNA Synthetase Deficiencies
creator: I. J. J. Muffels, G. Kok, Z. Tang, L. S. Medeiros, F. O. Poswar, W. P. Vermeij, R. Rodenburg, K. Smit, S. K. Sukumaran, S. B. Wortmann, L. Averdunk, J. Munch, J. Pak‐lam Ho, A. M. K. Kwok, E. E. S. Nieuwenhuis, P. M. van Hasselt, I. V. D. Schwartz, C. M. A. Lubout, A. M. Bosch, K. Koop, E. M. M. Hoy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aminoacyl‐tRNA synthetases (ARSs) facilitate the loading of transfer RNAs with their cognate amino acids in the cytosol (ARS1), mitochondria (ARS2), or both (dual ARS). ARS deficiencies are clinically heterogeneous and can cause severe, occasionally fatal disease. Supplementation with cognate amino acids to prevent local amino acid depletion has shown promise in ARS1 deficiencies, but its potential in ARS2 deficiencies remains largely unexplored.

title: Lasting mesothalamic dopamine imbalance and altered exploratory behavior in rats after a mild neonatal hypoxic event
creator: Barbara Nikolic, Sara Trnski-Levak, Kristina Kosic, Matea Drlje, Ivan Banovac, Dubravka Hranilovic, Natasa Jovanov-Milosevic
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionAdversities during the perinatal period can decrease oxygen supply to the fetal brain, leading to various hypoxic brain injuries, which can compromise the regularity of brain development in different aspects. To examine the catecholaminergic contribution to the link between an early-life hypoxic insult and adolescent behavioral aberrations, we used a previously established rat model of perinatal hypoxia but altered the hypobaric to normobaric conditions.MethodsExploratory and social behavior and learning abilities were tested in 70 rats of both sexes at adolescent age.

title: EPIC-NET: EEG-based epilepsy classification and brain localization using Optuna wave-gated recurrent unit network
creator: R. Manjupriya, A. Anny Leema
description: IntroductionEpilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by abnormal brain activity, often diagnosed through visual analysis of electroencephalography (EEG) signals. However, the existing works focused only on general epilepsy and failed to focus on location-based wave detection.MethodsIn this work, a novel deep learning-based EPIC-NET is proposed for epilepsy classification and brain localization using EEG signal.

title: Factors associated with girl child marriage in Iran: a qualitative socio-ecological approach
creator: Asma Pourtaheri, Mehrsadat Mahdizadeh, Hadi Tehrani, Jamshid Jamali, Nooshin Peyman
description: IntroductionGirl child marriage is an example of a human rights violation, the unfortunate consequences of which have raised growing concerns in the health system and have become a development challenge. Therefore, this research was conducted to identify the factors driving girl child marriage based on the Socio-Ecological Model.

title: Inclusive school practices for all youth: A European Cross‐National Study of general, sexual orientation, and gender identity‐based bullying
creator: Haoran Meng, Alberto Amadori, S Henry Sherwood, Salvatore Ioverno, Stephen T Russell
description: Bullying based on sexual orientation and gender identity (SOGI‐based bullying) is prevalent across Europe. This study examined the associations among student‐level and school‐level inclusive school practices and general and SOGI‐based bullying across LGBTQ+ students and heterosexual cisgender students. Data were drawn from 13 European countries, with a final analytic sample of n = 6730.

title: LigHTS: Biomimetic Hydrogel Photo‐Fabrication for Imaging‐Based Ultra‐High‐Throughput Screening
creator: Alessandro Enrico, Sara Rigolli, Julius Zimmermann, Melissa Pezzotti, Eloisa Torchia, Moises Di Sante, Ferdinando Auricchio, Francesco S Pasqualini
description: Imaging‐based ultra‐high‐throughput screening (UHTS) in pharma and biotech still relies on 384‐ and 1536‐well plates whose rigid, flat substrates limit biological fidelity and screening efficiency. Highly biomimetic organoids and organs‐on‐chips improve relevance but at a cost that is incompatible with early screening campaigns. Photopatterned hydrogel scaffolds are potentially scalable, but current approaches lack plate‐scale reproducibility and throughput.

title: Nutrition knowledge, weight loss practices, and supplement use in senior competition climbers
creator: Edward Gibson-Smith, Ryan Storey, Marisa Michael, Mayur Ranchordas
description: IntroductionSport climbing has gained increased scientific attention, including studies investigating the dietary habits and nutritional requirements of climbers; however, significant gaps in the literature remain. An assessment of nutritional knowledge, weight loss for competition, and supplement use has not been previously reported in senior competition climbing athletes.MethodsFifty climbers (26 male, 24 female; BMI 21.6 ± 1.9; 23.7 ± 5.

title: Fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis: novel roles in joint inflammation and beyond
creator: Elpida Neofotistou-Themeli, Panagiota Goutakoli, Theodoros Chanis, Maria Semitekolou, Eirini Sevdali, Prodromos Sidiropoulos
description: High-throughput technologies in human and animal studies have revealed novel molecular and cellular pathways involved in tissue inflammation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Fibroblasts have been in the forefront of research for several decades. Subpopulations with specific phenotypic and functional properties have been characterized both in mouse models and human disease.

title: Praseodymium‐Modulated NiFe Layered Double Hydroxide with Enhanced Oxygen Evolution Activity and Extended Durability
creator: Yuanming Gao, Xuezhen Wu, Lin Zhang, Haoxiang Zhang, Xueying Feng, Yu Bai, Wei Song, Yong Zheng, Jiong Liu, Jieyu Chen, Dong Yang, Wen Ma, Shengzhong (Frank) Liu
description: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in alkaline water electrolysis suffers from sluggish kinetics and limited catalyst durability. Here, we present a praseodymium (Pr) doping strategy that simultaneously tailors the electronic structure and pore architecture of nickel–iron layered double hydroxide (NiFe‐LDH). Atomically dispersed Pr3+ expands the interlayer spacing from 0.76 to 0.

title: A systematic literature review to evaluate the cardiac and cerebrovascular outcomes of patients with Fabry disease treated with agalsidase Beta
creator: Gavin Y. Oudit, Pronabesh DasMahapatra, Nicole Lyn, Florence R. Wilson, Adekemi Adeyemi, Chae Sung Lee, Ana Crespo, Mehdi Namdar
description: BackgroundAgalsidase beta is used to treat Fabry disease (FD); however, data on cardiac and cerebrovascular outcomes with agalsidase beta treatment come from studies with limited numbers of patients.MethodsA systematic literature review of studies reporting on the efficacy and effectiveness of agalsidase beta in FD was conducted.

title: Effect of continuous theta burst stimulation on the glymphatic system, brain network and cognitive function in patients with cerebral small vessel disease
creator: Pei Dai, Hui-xian Yu, Zhao-xia Wang, Si-hao Liu, Chang-bin Liu, Guang-qing Xu
description: ObjectiveWe aim to investigate the impact of continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) on glymphatic system (GS), brain network (BN) and cognition in cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD).MethodsThis exploratory study included a small cohort of 11 patients, divided into a cTBS group (6 patients) and a sham-cTBS group (5 patients).

title: Renal stress-associated extracellular vesicle signaling linked to lysosomal cathepsin D and NEK7–NLRP3 neuroinflammation
creator: Gunhyuk Park, Ho-Ryong Yoo, Hye-Sun Lim
description: Systemic exposure to neurotoxins such as 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) affects both the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral organs; however, the contribution of peripheral organ stress to neuroinflammation remains incompletely understood. Here, we propose a peripheral-to-central signaling mechanism in which renal stress–associated extracellular vesicles (EVs) are linked to microglial inflammasome activation.

title: Psychological predictors of music performance anxiety among vocal students: a gender-based SEM analysis
creator: Ye Maoqing
description: IntroductionThis study examines how social support from parents, educators, and peers influences psychological factors—self-efficacy, self-worth, and intrinsic motivation—and how these, in turn, affect music performance anxiety (MPA) among vocal music students. It aims to identify both direct and indirect pathways through which social and psychological variables interact to shape MPA.

title: HLA-DR expression in melanoma: from misleading therapeutic target to potential immunotherapy biomarker
creator: Karim Amrane, Coline Le Meur, Benjamin Besse, Patrice Hemon, Pierre Le Noac’h, Olivier Pradier, Christian Berthou, Ronan Abgral, Arnaud Uguen
description: Since the advent of anti-PD1 immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) immunotherapy, cutaneous melanoma has undergone a true revolution with prolonged survival, as available 5-year updates for progression-free survival and overall survival demonstrate a durable clinical benefit for melanoma patients receiving ICI.

title: Dynamic physiology and transcriptomics revealed the alleviation effect of melatonin on Reaumuria trigyna under continuous alkaline salt stress
creator: Xuebo Li, Lei Wang, Heyi Wang, Rui Hao, Lunkai Gao, Hongbo Cui, Hai Wu, Xiaodong Wu, Tong Qiao, Weijie Bai, Liming Zhang
description: Introduction Reaumuria trigyna, a pivotal salt-tolerant plant species in Central Asian salt desert ecosystems, has garnered significant attention due to its resilience under harsh environmental conditions. This study investigates the response mechanisms of melatonin on the dynamic physiology and transcriptomics of Reaumuria trigyna, a critical salt-tolerant plant species in Central Asian salt desert ecosystems.

title: Evaluation of Different Methods of Haemoglobin Estimation Among Malaria‐Infected Patients
creator: Mina Ofosu, Jessica Ntiamoah, Patricia Sam Barko, Prince Elikem Torli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHaemoglobin (Hb) estimation is essential for assessing anaemia, particularly in malaria‐endemic settings. Automated Full Blood Count (FBC) analysers, cyanmethemoglobin spectrophotometry, and portable Hb meters are commonly used, but differences in analytical performance may affect measurements.MethodsThis cross‐sectional study compared Hb measurements obtained using an automated FBC analyser, the cyanmethemoglobin method, and a portable Hb meter among 100 malaria‐infected patients aged 16–65 years at Kumasi South Hospital, Ghana.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of particulate matter exposure: air pollution and hazards on human health
creator: Dulcemaría Gavito-Covarrubias, Ivonne Ramírez-Díaz, Josué Guzmán-Linares, Ilhuicamina Daniel Limón, Dulce María Manuel-Sánchez, Alejandro Molina-Herrera, Miguel Ángel Coral-García, Estela Anastasio, Arely Anaya-Hernández, Primavera López-Salazar, Gabriel Juárez-Díaz, Javier Martínez-Juárez, Julián T
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Environmental pollution nowadays has not only a direct correlation with human health changes but a direct social impact. Epidemiological studies have evidenced the increased damage to human health on a daily basis because of damage to the ecological niche. Rapid urban growth and industrialized societies importantly compromise air quality, which can be assessed by a notable accumulation of air pollutants in both the gas and the particle phases.

title: Different nitrogen uptake patterns of plant and soil microorganisms in the forest-grassland transition zone on the Loess Plateau
creator: Lina Wang, Xu Deng, Ying Zhou, Xueqi Geng, Zeling Zhang, Yakun Tang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionIt is unclear whether plants and microorganisms achieve niche complementarity by taking up different inorganic nitrogen (N) forms to alleviate N competition, particularly in N–limited regions.MethodsThis paper conducted a 15-day 15N tracer study (15NH4NO3 or 15NH4NO3) in situ to quantitatively calculate the uptake rates of plants and microorganisms in four stands (pure Hippophae rhamnoides L, pure Pinus tabuliformis Carrière, mixed H. tabuliformis, and Artemisia gmelinii Weber ex Stechm grassland) in the forest–grassland transition zone on the Loess Plateau during the growing season.

title: Continuing Professional Development—Medical Imaging
creator: Unknown
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Impact on Radiation Exposure and Multiple Imaging Testing

Brian Evans, Nicola Giannotti, Ernest Ekpo, https://doi.org/10.1002/jmrs.70097. In the studies examined, how often did doctors follow the recommended Diagnostic Imaging Pathway? 29%52%75%90% Which is a potential consequence of unnecessary imaging? Delayed diagnosis and treatmentImproved patient outcomesReduced healthcare resource useShorter hospital stays When Diagnostic Imaging Pathways are not followed, how much more likely is a patient to undergo an imaging test involving radiation?

title: The potential causes of myasthenia and fasciculations in severely ill ME/CFS patients: the role of disturbed electrophysiology
creator: Klaus J. Wirth, Jürgen M. Steinacker
description: Patients with severe myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) are bedridden and suffer from hypersensitivities to light and noise, severe orthostatic intolerance reducing cerebral blood flow, and skeletal muscle symptoms, including loss of force, fatigue, pain, fasciculations, and cramps. Because neurological investigations exclude neuronal causes of myasthenia, we hypothesize a muscular pathomechanism.

title: Photosynthetic performance and carbon metabolism in the ear organs of oats under drought stress
creator: Jiaqi Fang, Yuan Zhan, Baowen Zhao, Yan Zhao, Youjun Chen, Qingping Zhou, Hui Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Sufficiently exploiting the potential of crop photosynthesis is one of the critical ways for improving cultivation production to face global climate change. In this study, oat plants were potted with three watering treatments. The glumes, lemmas, and flag leaves were sampled on days 0, 7, and 14 after the first floret blossomed under the control (denoted as CK-0, CK-7, and CK-14), drought stress (denoted as DS-7, and DS-14) and rewatering treatments (RW-14).

title: Silver nanoparticles supported on DABCO-based ionic liquid-functionalized magnetic polystyrene for the efficient reduction of 4-nitrophenol
creator: Taraneh Abbaspour, Sakineh Asghari, Ghasem Firouzzadeh Pasha, Mahmood Tajbakhsh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The efficient conversion of nitrobenzene to aminophenols, typically achieved with metal catalysts or metal oxides, provides significant environmental benefits. In this study, a novel nanocatalyst was synthesized by immobilizing silver metal on DABCO-based ionic liquids supported on magnetic polystyrene. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized by XRD, TGA, EDS & EDS mapping, FT-IR, and ICP and subsequently evaluated as solid-phase catalysts for the reduction of 4-nitrophenol (4-NP) with excess NaBH4 using UV-vis spectroscopy, which maintained good catalytic activity after six recycling cycles.

title: CAM/TMA-DPH as a promising alternative to SYTO9/PI for cell viability assessment in bacterial biofilms
creator: Tinatini Tchatchiashvili, Mateusz Jundzill, Mike Marquet, Kamran A. Mirza, Mathias W. Pletz, Oliwia Makarewicz, Lara Thieme
description: IntroductionAccurately assessing biofilm viability is essential for evaluating both biofilm formation and the efficacy of antibacterial treatments. Traditional SYTO9 and propidium iodide (PI) live/dead staining in biofilm viability assays often ace challenges due to non-specific staining, limiting precise differentiation between live and dead cells.

title: Transcriptional response to mild therapeutic hypothermia in noise-induced cochlear injury
creator: Samantha Rincon Sabatino, Rachele Sangaletti, Anthony Griswold, W. Dalton Dietrich, Curtis S. King, Suhrud M. Rajguru
description: IntroductionPrevention or treatment for acoustic injury has been met with many translational challenges, resulting in the absence of FDA-approved interventions. Localized hypothermia following noise exposure mitigates acute cochlear injury and may serve as a potential avenue for therapeutic approaches. However, the mechanisms by which hypothermia results in therapeutic improvements are poorly understood.

title: Unbound Intrinsic Formation Clearance of 6β‐Hydroxycortisol Is a Useful Biomarker of CYP3A4 Activity during Pregnancy
creator: Aurora K Authement, Mary F Hebert, Emily E Fay, Nina Isoherranen
description: Pregnancy results in multiple physiological changes that impact drug disposition. For example, hepatic CYP3A activity and renal transporter‐mediated clearance increase in late pregnancy, but the time course of these changes across pregnancy is not known. Endogenous biomarkers offer a minimally invasive approach to characterize pharmacokinetic changes during pregnancy and postpartum.

title: Impact of dapagliflozin on metabolic phenotype, hormone levels, and fertility in female mice after prolonged high-fat diet
creator: Xiaolin Chen, Zhuoni Xiao, Na Dai, Mingxia Fan
description: IntroductionA long-term high-fat diet (HFD) cause obesity and infertility through hypothalamic inflammation and insulin resistance, leading to metabolic abnormalities and ovulation dysfunction. The sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have emerged as a treatment for type 2 diabetic patients, regulating adipose tissue metabolism, hypothalamic inflammation, and ovulation in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and type 1 diabetes: a potential game changer?
creator: Ortal Resnick, Fernando Bril, Giovanna Beauchamp
description: This mini review explores the increasing prevalence of obesity in type 1 diabetes (T1D) and the challenges patients face in achieving optimal glycemic control with current treatments. It discusses the evidence supporting the use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) as potential adjunctive therapy in T1D to reduce weight and improve insulin resistance.

title: CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer: a proof-of-concept comparison with primary-tumor radiomics
creator: Zejin Lin, Jue Wang, Hairong Chen, Qun Bao, Ming Xu, Shang Yang, Hanxiao Zhang, Guang-Zhong Yang, Peng Sun
description: ObjectiveAccurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer remains challenging using conventional CT assessment. This proof-of-concept study compared CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics with primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative prediction of LNM.Materials and methodsThis single-center retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT and surgical resection.

title: Searching for Novel COVID19 Treatments: Towards Covalent TMPRSS2 Inhibitors
creator: Marco Minneci, Barbara Farkaš, Adeyemi Rahman, Inga Nehlmeier, Amy Eichmann, Stefan Pöhlmann, Isabel Rozas
description: We present the design, synthesis and biophysical and biochemical evaluation of new guanidinium derivatives with potential as covalent inhibitors of Transmembrane Protease Serine 2 (TMPRSS2), aiming to find therapies against COVID‐19. TMPRSS2 is a key protease for SARS‐CoV‐2 entry into host cells, making it a promising drug target since blocking viral entry, viral replication is stopped.

title: Pan-cancer and experimental analyses reveal the immunotherapeutic significance of CST2 and its association with stomach adenocarcinoma proliferation and metastasis
creator: Dan Huang, Jing Li, Zhijun He, Wenjing Liang, Likun Zhong, Jun Huang, Yinteng Wu, Shijian Zhao
description: PurposeCystatin 2 (CST2) is a cysteine protease inhibitor, and recent research suggests its potential involvement in cancer development. However, its role in the occurrence, progression, and prognosis of pan-cancer has not been systematically investigated.Materials and methodsThis study comprehensively analyzes the differential expression of CST2 in pan-cancer. The expression distribution patterns of CST2 were examined using single-cell datasets.

title: Women's Ways of Coping With Chronic Widespread Pain—A Phenomenographic Study
creator: Ingrid Larsson, Katarina Aili, Stefan Bergman, Maria Andersson, Emma Haglund, Ann Bremander
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChronic widespread pain (CWP) affects around 10% of adults and is more prevalent in women. The impact of CWP on daily life varies, as do coping strategies.ObjectiveTo describe women's different ways of coping with CWP.MethodsA descriptive, qualitative phenomenographic study. Semi‐structured interviews were performed with 19 women (aged 45–67) from a population‐based cohort who did not report CWP in 1995 but reported CWP at the 2016 follow‐up assessment.

title: Immunoglobulin NGS enhance residual disease detection and prognosis in pediatric Ph+ acute lymphoblastic leukemia
creator: Lixian Chang, Jiao Chang, Beibei Zhao, Yun Gu, Yao Zou, Yumei Chen, Ye Guo, Xiaojuan Chen, Wenyu Yang, Yongjuan Duan, Tianyuan Hu, Xiaoming Liu, Min Ruan, Zefeng Lu, Shixin Lu, Xiaoxia Wang, Li Dong, Jinghua Wu, Yujiao Jia, Xiao Liu, Xiaofan Zhu, Li Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In pediatric Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ B-ALL), the clinical value of highly sensitive minimal residual disease (MRD) detection by immunoglobulin next-generation sequencing (Ig-NGS), and its role for tracking clonal evolution, remains inadequately characterized. In this study, we evaluated MRD in a cohort of pediatric Ph+ B-ALL patients using Ig-NGS in parallel with conventional methods, including flow cytometry (FCM) and BCR-ABL reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).

title: Adapting Segment Anything Model 3 for concept-driven lesion segmentation in medical images: an experimental study
creator: Guoping Xu, Jayaram K Udupa, Yubing Tong, Xin Long, Ying Zhang, Jie Deng, Weiguo Lu, You Zhang
description: Accurate segmentation of lesions is fundamental for medical image analysis. However, most existing approaches are designed for specific anatomical sites and imaging modalities, limiting their applicability in heterogeneous clinical environments. Recent vision-language foundation models have enabled concept-driven segmentation of natural images, offering a promising path toward more flexible and generalizable medical image segmentation.

title: A mediating effect of sense of coherence on the association between work-family conflict and workplace ostracism among medical staff
creator: Na Li, Huifeng Zhang, Hui Zhao, Congmin Zhang, Huinan Zhang, Fenghui Ma, Xiaojia Tang, Cuicui Wang, Jing Huang
description: BackgroundThe mental health of medical professionals has garnered increasing attention in recent years. This study aims to explore the relationships and interactions among workplace ostracism, work-family conflict, and sense of coherence (SOC) within this population.MethodsFrom January 2022 to December 2023, a survey was conducted involving 527 medical staff from three diverse hospitals.

title: Trends in the Asthma Burden Attributable to High Body Mass Index in Children Across 204 Countries and Territories, 1990–2021: An Analysis of the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study
creator: Hua Li, Hai‐Yan Chen, Dong‐Zhi Zheng, Qiu‐Yi Liu, Jia‐Bing Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High body mass index (BMI) has been identified as a significant risk factor for childhood asthma. Given the rising prevalence of childhood obesity, assessing the impact of high BMI on asthma burden trends is imperative. Utilizing Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, we estimated age‐, sex‐, geography‐, and sociodemographic index (SDI)‐stratified asthma‐related deaths and disability‐adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to high BMI in children (0–14 years old) (1990–2021).

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward leishmaniasis and one health: a cross-sectional study among medical and veterinary professionals
creator: Yasir Khan, I-Chen Lin, Sundus Khan, Mehtab Kanwal, Abdul Wajid, Aamir Khan, Fazal Noor, Ali Madi Almajwal, Chien-Chin Chen, Abdul Qadeer
description: Leishmaniasis is a significant zoonotic infection with global health implications, particularly in regions where human and animal health are closely interconnected. This cross-sectional study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of 5,074 participants regarding leishmaniasis and the One Health concept. The socio-demographic data revealed that most respondents were young (82.6%), male (82.3%), and from rural areas (50.

title: BUB1 promotes lung adenocarcinoma progression by regulating STAT3/GPX4-mediated ferroptosis
creator: Xiaocong Mo, Ying Liu, Yu Wang, Xiaofen Pan, Mengyuan Zhu, Jiehao Liao, Minling Liu, Tingwei Li, Xueying Li, Shuo Fang, Bo Wang
description: IntroductionLung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, but its therapeutic efficacy remains suboptimal. This study explores the functional role and underlying mechanism of BUB1 in LUAD.MethodsIn vitro, BUB1 knockdown (si-BUB1) in A549/H1299 cells was performed, and effects were assessed. The ferroptosis inhibitor Fer-1 was used.

title: Efficacy of Negative Pressure Suction‐Assisted Flexible Ureteroscopy for Upper Urinary Tract Calculi and Construction of a Stone‐Free Rate Prediction Model
creator: Ren‐Hui Qiu, Ding‐Sheng He, Chun‐Yu Guo, Li Dong, Guo‐Zhang Lin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study retrospectively analyzed 92 patients who underwent negative‐pressure suction sheath‐assisted flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy (observation group) and 85 patients who underwent conventional flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy (control group). Propensity score full matching and weighted analyses were used to balance covariates. Operative time, hospital stay, pain scores, hemoglobin changes, white blood cell counts, neutrophil counts, stone clearance rates, and complications were compared, and predictive models for stone clearance were constructed. The observation group achieved significantly higher stone‐free rates at 3 days (69.6% vs.

title: The assessment of marrow adiposity in type 1 diabetic rabbits through magnetic resonance spectroscopy is linked to bone resorption
creator: Wei Li, Wei Wang, Minlan Zhang, Qi Chen, Fengyi Li, Shaojun Li
description: BackgroundEnhanced marrow adiposity is frequently linked with a decline in bone density. The underlying mechanisms responsible for bone loss in diabetes are not well understood. In this investigation, we employed an alloxan-induced diabetes rabbit model to unravel the association between marrow fat content and bone resorption, utilizing magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

title: Higher Preoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging Use in Asia‐Pacific Compared With North America for Pediatric Tibial Eminence Fractures: A Systematic Review
creator: Siyuan Zhang, Jorge Hsian Ming Tay, Si Heng Sharon Tan, James Hoi Po Hui, Theodore Ganley
description: PurposeTo evaluate differences in the incidence, diagnosis, and management of pediatric tibial eminence fractures between the Asia‐Pacific region and North America.MethodsA systematic review and subjective synthesis was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses guidelines.

title: Comparative Diagnostic Performance of Three Commercial Real‐Time PCR Assays for the Detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Complex in Bronchial Washing Specimens: A Large Retrospective Study
creator: Jimyung Kim, Yumi Park
description: BackgroundMolecular assays are essential for the rapid detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC). However, head‐to‐head comparisons of widely used commercial assays remain limited. This study compared the diagnostic performance of three real‐time PCR assays—AdvanSure TB/NTM, Cobas MTB, and Xpert MTB/RIF—using bronchial washing specimens.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed molecular assay results from 3348 bronchial washing specimens obtained between January 2021 and May 2024.

title: Physicochemical Stability and Sensory Properties of Salad Dressing Formulated With Fish Oil‐in‐Water Pickering Emulsions
creator: Thang Tran, Grethe Hyldig, Betül Yesiltas, Ana C. Mendes, Ioannis S. Chronakis, Charlotte Jacobsen
description: Pickering emulsions stabilized with food‐grade particles have gained attention for food applications to deliver bioactive compounds. Fish oil, a rich source of omega‐3 PUFAs, offers numerous health benefits, but it is highly prone to lipid oxidation. While fish oil Pickering emulsions have shown potential in enhancing oxidative stability, their application in real food systems has not been explored extensively.

title: Mindfulness, mental health, and motives for eating tasty foods when not in metabolic need
creator: Katherine G. Moore, Justess D. Rice, John E. Gampher, Mary M. Boggiano
description: Habitual consumption of highly palatable foods when not in metabolic need (HPF eating) is linked to obesity. High HPF consumption is also linked to mental health disorder (MHD) symptoms. Mindfulness-based interventions are popular treatments for obesity and MHDs, but little is known about the relationship between trait mindfulness and motive-based HPF eating.

title: Defining Dysphoric Milk Ejection Reflex: using Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder as a framework for proposing preliminary diagnostic criteria
creator: Megan Howard, Teni Davoudian, Nicole H. Cirino
description: Dysphoric Milk Ejection Reflex (D-MER) is a distinct neurobiological condition characterized by negative alterations in mental state in response to milk letdown during lactation. Symptoms vary by patient and can include feelings of sadness, anxiety or agitation. Importantly, the symptoms are brief, typically lasting no more than 5 minutes.

title: Metabolomics Based Biomarkers of Green Beans Intake
creator: Rebecca Finlay, Ya Gao, Qi Sun, Frank Hu, Jayne Woodside, Xiaofei Yin, Lorraine Brennan
description: While there is considerable interest in legumes as a food source, there are no validated biomarkers for green beans (Phaseolus vulgaris, L.) intake. The objective of the current work is to identify and assess the dose–response of food intake biomarkers of green beans.

title: The influence of different forms of apple products on all-cause mortality in patients with hypertension
creator: Chuang Sun, Yingying Chen, Yue Guan, Yiming Zeng, Jie Li, Liang Chen
description: ObjectiveApple consumption has a positive effect on human health. Some studies have shown that an appropriate amount of apple intake can reduce the incidence of hypertension. However, few studies have investigated whether eating different forms of apples has the same benefits as eating whole apples.

title: The impact of different gastrointestinal reconstruction techniques on gut microbiota after gastric cancer surgery
creator: Yu Yang, Hang-Yu Zhou, Guo-Min Zhou, Jin Chen, Rui Ming, Dong Zhang, Huai-Wu Jiang
description: IntroductionGastric cancer is one of the common malignant tumors in the digestive tract, characterized by high incidence and mortality rates. This is particularly significant in China, where a large proportion of global new cases of gastric cancer and related deaths occur.

title: Baihe Zhimu Decoction ameliorates anxious depression via PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway‐mediated neuroprotection and inhibition of hippocampal neuronal apoptosis
creator: Yuanshan Han, Kexin He, Haolan Yang, Jiacheng Dai, Ronglin Chen, Yang Liu, Yuhong Wang, Lin Tang, Hongqing Zhao
description: BackgroundAnxious depression involves severe emotional dysregulation with a high risk of relapse and suicide. Although the classical Traditional Chinese Medicine formula Baihe Zhimu Decoction (BZD) is widely used for affective disorders, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.MethodsIn this study, the chemical constituents of BZD were first identified using UPLC‐Q‐TOF‐MS/MS, followed by a maximum‐dose safety evaluation.

title: Breastfeeding moderates the association between family socioeconomic status and child behavior scores
creator: Sarah E. Turner, Leslie Roos, Nathan C. Nickel, Jacqueline Pei, Sukhpreet K. Tamana, Theo J. Moraes, Stuart E. Turvey, Elinor Simons, Padmaja Subbarao, Piushkumar J. Mandhane, Meghan B. Azad
description: BackgroundChildren living in low socioeconomic status (SES) environments are more likely to develop behavior problems. Breastfeeding is one behavior that has been positively linked to mental health throughout childhood. We investigated whether breastfeeding modifies the association between low SES and behavior problems.MethodsWe studied a subset of the Canadian CHILD cohort (N = 2,342).

title: Pixel-Wise Statistical Mapping with Voltage-Sensitive Dye Imaging Reveals Differential Hippocampal Circuit Effects of Bisphenol A and Related Phenolic Analogs
creator: Yoko Tominaga, Makiko Taketoshi, Kentaro Tanemura, Takashi Tominaga
description: Exposure to environmental chemicals such as bisphenol A (BPA) may affect neural circuit function in subtle and spatially distributed ways that are difficult to attribute to a single circuit element. Here, we developed a voltage-sensitive dye (VSD) imaging analysis pipeline for acute male mouse hippocampal slices.

title: The plight of Ukrainian refugees staying in Sweden under EU:s mass refugee directive: a brief trauma-focused, participatory, online intervention as a pilot feasibility study
creator: Solvig Ekblad, Oksana Gramatik, Yuliia Suprun
description: BackgroundUkrainians staying in Sweden under the EU mass refugee directive may face challenges due to traumas caused by the invasion that started on February 24, 2022. Part of an European Social Fund (ESF) project, our study showed that a brief trauma-focused group intervention onsite helped to increase health and mental-health literacy. The intervention has not yet been adapted online.

title: Training in eight low-and middle-income countries: lessons learned from a pilot study using the WHO-TDR dissemination and implementation massive open online course
creator: Ashlin Rakhra, Cole Hooley, Meredith P. Fort, Mary Beth Weber, LeShawndra Price, Hoa L. Nguyen, Manuel Ramirez, Adamson S. Muula, Mina Hosseinipour, Kingsley Apusiga, Victor Davila-Roman, Joyce Gyamfi, Kezia Gladys Amaning Adjei, Josephine Andesia, Annette Fitzpatrick, Pascal Launois, Ana A. Baumann
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionNon-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in low-and middle- income countries (LMICs). Despite this, a lack of funding, training and mentorship for NCD investigators in LMICs exists.

title: Is it time to align adolescent diets with the Planetary Health Diet? An observational study on early cardiovascular health
creator: David Murcia-Lesmes, Emily P. Laveriano-Santos, Ramón Estruch, Marina Corrado, Camila Arancibia-Riveros, Ana María Ruiz-León, Rosa Casas, Miguel Camafort, Jesús Martínez-Gómez, Amaya de Cos-Gandoy, Patricia Bodega, Gloria Santos-Beneit, Juan M. Fernández-Alvira, Rodrigo Fernández-Jiménez, Rosa M. La
description: BackgroundAs the impact of early adoption of a sustainable plant-based diet on cardiometabolic biomarkers remains unexplored, we assessed whether they are associated with the Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) in adolescents.MethodsThis prospective study was conducted within the SI! Program for Secondary Schools trial (SI! Program) in 886 adolescents (12 years ± 0.4 at cohort entry; 49.

title: Vitamin D deficiency and oral health in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): A public health perspective
creator: Najat Alyafei
description: ObjectivesTo examine evidence regarding the relationship between vitamin D deficiency and oral health in Middle East and North Africa (MENA) populations, where vitamin D deficiency and oral diseases remain important public health challenges, emphasizing biological mechanisms, dental caries, periodontal diseases, other oral outcomes, and public health implications.

title: Down syndrome and outcomes in critically ill pediatric patients
creator: José Tantaleán Da Fieno, Rosa León Paredes, Patricia Palomo Luck, Carlos Del Águila Villar, Emiliana Rizo Patrón
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionInformation regarding children with Down syndrome (DS) in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) is limited and conflicting. We aimed to investigate the association between DS and clinical outcomes in pediatric patients admitted to the PICU at the Instituto Nacional de Salud del Niño (National Institute for Child Health, INSN for the acronym in Spanish) and to assess nutritional status within the study cohort.MethodsThis study involved the secondary analysis of a database.

title: A base-editing and auxotrophic selection platform for linking epigenetic regulators to silent biosynthetic gene clusters in Aspergillus nidulans
creator: Meng Pang, Donghui Guo, Yanling Li, Yuze Chen, Rumeng Du, Jiayang Liu, Jiahui Hu, Hang Li, Zhuofan Li, Guojun Pan, Yuan Tian, Fanglong Zhao
description: Filamentous fungi harbor numerous silent biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), representing an underexplored reservoir of natural products. Chemical inhibition of epigenetic regulators is an effective strategy for activating silent BGCs, but it often lacks specificity and cannot readily link activated clusters to their cognate regulators.

title: Prediction of hyperuricemia in people taking low-dose aspirin using a machine learning algorithm: a cross-sectional study of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
creator: Bin Zhu, Li Yang, Mingfen Wu, Qiao Wu, Kejia Liu, Yansheng Li, Wei Guo, Zhigang Zhao
description: Background: Hyperuricemia is a serious health problem related to not only gout but also cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Low-dose aspirin was reported to inhibit uric acid excretion, which leads to hyperuricemia. To decrease hyperuricemia-related CVD, this study aimed to identify the risk of hyperuricemia in people taking aspirin.

title: The impact of spousal retirement on health—an empirical analysis based on CFPS
creator: Ping Chen, Han Liang, Yufei Zhou, Guodong Zhu, Yu Peng, Jiayi Yao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionHealth impacts associated with spousal retirement vary significantly across countries and datasets, underscoring the need to examine this relationship within the Chinese context. This study aims to explore how spousal retirement affects individual health in China.MethodsUtilizing data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) for the years 2014, 2016, 2018, and 2020, this research applies a fuzzy regression discontinuity approach to assess the effects of spousal retirement on health outcomes.ResultsFindings indicate that a wife’s retirement positively impacts her husband’s mental health but

title: October 2026 obituaries
creator: Unknown
description: thology. Died Mar. 31, 2026, aged 87. https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/reuben-baumal-obituary?id=61157702 Beatty, Myles F., Oshawa, Ont.; Western University, 1975; obstetrics and gynecology. Died Jan. 26, 2026, aged 78. https://www.dignitymemorial.com/en-ca/obituaries/oshawa-on/myles-beatty-12723696 Boone, James E., London, Ont.; University of Toronto, 1951; pediatrics. Died Jan. 29, 2026, aged 98. https://lfpress.remembering.ca/obituary/james-edward-boone-1093492741 Briggs, Valerie A., Ottawa, Ont.; University of Aberdeen (Scotland), 1961; diagnostic radiology. Died Mar.

title: Psychometric evaluation of the persian version of the Social Self-Compassion Scale (SSCS): associations with Perceived Social Self-Efficacy, fear of negative evaluation, and loneliness among female undergraduate students
creator: Azadeh Taheri, Roghieh Nooripour, Mohammadreza Shabanzadeh, Hamid Barani, Alison L Rose
description: ObjectiveThe Social Self-Compassion Scale (SSCS) was developed to assess self-compassion in social and interpersonal contexts. However, the psychometric properties of the SSCS have not yet been evaluated among Iranian female undergraduate students. This study aimed to translate the SSCS into Persian and examine its psychometric properties among Iranian female undergraduate students.

title: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy improves insomnia symptoms in individuals with recurrent depression: secondary analyses from a randomized controlled trial
creator: Linn Nyjordet Evanger, Elisabeth Flo-Groeneboom, Lin Sørensen, Elisabeth Schanche
description: BackgroundEmbedded within a randomized efficacy trial, the present study aimed to investigate whether mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) for recurrent depression improved symptoms of insomnia.MethodsSixty-eight remitted participants with at least three prior episodes of depression were randomized to 8 weeks of MBCT (n = 33) or a waitlist control condition (n = 35).

title: Research progress and perspectives on the application of tyramide signal amplification-based multiplex immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence: a bibliometrics analysis
creator: Xiaotong Yu, Chen Huang, Yan Song, Chun Zhang, Debo You, XuRan Dong, DeFu Wu, Alan Keith Meeker, Hao Feng, Yuqing Wang
description: Background and aimsMultiplex immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence (mIHC/IF), which uses the tyramide signal amplification (TSA) technique, enables sequential staining of multiple targets in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples without worrying about cross-reactivity. This approach has received considerable attention from researchers over the past decades. This article aims to provide a bibliometric analysis of the research progress and perspectives on the application of TSA-based mIHC/IF.

title: Effects of music-based group exercise in patients with acquired brain injury—a randomized controlled trial
creator: Mareike Schrader, Tobias Strank, Annette Sterr, Stephan Bamborschke, Christian Dohle
description: BackgroundCognitive impairment following acquired brain injury (ABI) is common. In this study, we investigated whether music-based group exercise (MBGE) is superior to standard therapy (ST) in improving cognitive deficits. In addition, motivational aspects were investigated. The trial has been registered with the German Register for Clinical Studies (DRKS00025566).

title: Factors Associated with Sedentary Behavior in Pregnant Women: Insights from Multiple Linear Regression and Random Forest Model
creator: Lei Zeng, Rongrong Han, Jiayuan Ma, Lingling Gao
description: PurposeHigh levels of sedentary behavior (sitting for more than 6 hours a day) during pregnancy are a public health concern. Understanding the prevalence, patterns, and associated factors of sedentary behavior is important to develop targeted interventions, yet contemporary evidence remains limited.

title: An integrated framework for antimicrobial resistance: links with climate change and vulnerability
creator: Estibaliz Baroja, Inmaculada Batalla, Maria Jose Sanz, Aline Chiabai
description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has been extensively studied in clinical settings; however, research on the environmental aspects of AMR is relatively new. Recently, there has been growing interest in the relationship between climate change and AMR, yet evidence linking AMR to climate change and potential environmental transmission is very limited.

title: Computational models for predicting liver toxicity in the deep learning era
creator: Fahad Mostafa, Minjun Chen
description: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a severe adverse reaction caused by drugs and may result in acute liver failure and even death. Many efforts have centered on mitigating risks associated with potential DILI in humans. Among these, quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) was proven to be a valuable tool for early-stage hepatotoxicity screening.

title: Supporting Social Engagement in Long-Term Care Through Paired Socially Assistive Robot-Virtual Reality Activities for Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment and Apathy
creator: Miroslava Migovich, Ritam Ghosh, Nibraas Khan, Cathy A Maxwell, Paul A Newhouse, Douglas W Scharre, Alai Tan, Judith A Tate, Lorraine C Mion, Nilanjan Sarkar
description: IntroductionOlder adults living in long-term care settings, particularly those with cognitive impairment and apathy, frequently experience reduced social engagement. Socially assistive robots and virtual reality systems may help support engagement, but little is known about whether they can sustain engagement during real-world deployment while also facilitating interaction between older adults.

title: Quantitative analysis of peripapillary RNFL capillary density and thickness in patients with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy
creator: Zelie Cao, Tao Tian, Ru Liu, Jinli Peng, Guoping Kuang
description: PurposeOptical coherence tomography angiography was used to compare the changes of capillary density and thickness of the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) without diabetic retinopathy (DR) and patients with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR).

title: General practitioners’ involvement in oncological aftercare (ACTION): a study protocol for a mixed-methods study
creator: Katharina van Baal, Stephanie Stiel, Svenja Arendt, Catharina Münte, Malte Klemmt
description: BackgroundThe growing number of cancer survivors in Germany necessitates sustainable, interdisciplinary aftercare. General practitioners (GPs) are well-positioned to provide long-term, trust-based support, including early detection of recurrences and late effects. However, evidence on the level of GP involvement in oncological aftercare, on interdisciplinary aftercare models involving GPs and specialists, and on associated barriers and facilitators remains limited.

title: Additively manufactured porous scaffolds by design for treatment of bone defects
creator: Shirin Toosi, Mohammad Javad Javid-Naderi, Ali Tamayol, Mohammad Hossein Ebrahimzadeh, Sima Yaghoubian, Seyed Ali Mousavi Shaegh
description: There has been increasing attention to produce porous scaffolds that mimic human bone properties for enhancement of tissue ingrowth, regeneration, and integration. Additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, i.e., three dimensional (3D) printing, have played a substantial role in engineering porous scaffolds for clinical applications owing to their high level of design and fabrication flexibility.

title: Studies on the functionality of the TC-NER ERCC6-M1097V protein variant frequently found in Louisiana patients with PCa upon UV damage
creator: Oluwatobi Ogundepo, Arrigo De Benedetti
description: ERCC6, also known as CSB (Cockayne Syndrome B), is a key protein involved in transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair (TC-NER), a DNA repair process that removes lesions blocking RNA polymerase. ERCC6’s multifaceted roles include chromatin remodeling, transcription regulation, oxidative stress response, and coordination with other DNA repair proteins.

title: Ex-vivo right posterior sectionectomy for large-for-size mismatch in pediatric liver transplant recipients
creator: Andrea Della Penna, Steffen Hartleif, Markus Quante, Silvio Nadalin
description: PurposeLarge-for-size mismatch remains a major challenge in pediatric and small recipient liver transplantation, particularly when full-size deceased-donor grafts are allocated and conventional splitting is not feasible.MethodsWe performed a single-center retrospective analysis of seven pediatric and adolescent recipients who underwent deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) with ex-vivo right posterior sectionectomy (RPS) between 2018 and 2022.

title: Optimizing nitrogen and phosphorus application to improve soil organic carbon and alfalfa hay yield in alfalfa fields
creator: Kongqin Wei, Junwei Zhao, Yanliang Sun, Ignacio F. López, Chunhui Ma, Qianbing Zhang
description: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is the principal factor contributing to enhanced soil fertility and also functions as the major carbon sink within terrestrial ecosystems. Applying fertilizer is a crucial agricultural practice that enhances SOC and promotes crop yields. Nevertheless, the response of SOC, active organic carbon fraction and hay yield to nitrogen and phosphorus application is still unclear.

title: Discovery as public infrastructure: Renewing the social contract for science
creator: Sergio Carbajo, Asad Madni, Julia Powles
