description: Scientific capacity built over generations is being weakened by abrupt political disruption just as discovery is becoming faster, more convergent, globally networked, and more socially consequential. Restoring funding and protecting scientific institutions are urgent, but not sufficient: the postwar compact that sustained discovery before its uses were known must be renewed for 21st-century conditions and made resilient to arbitrary disruption.

title: Case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo with Lack of Transmission to Breastfeeding Infant
creator: Felicien M. Maisha, Kahatwa K. Serge, Kambale Kasonia, Zebedée Luhavo Kakule, Jayakrishnan Ajayakumar, John A. Lednicky, Andrew J. Curtis, J. Glenn Morris
description: .Disease due to Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an Orthoebolavirus species, reemerged in April 2026, in Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. A 35-year-old woman transported the body of a possible BDBV-infected patient from Bunia in Ituri Province to Goma for burial; she was accompanied by an 8-month-old breastfeeding child.

title: Differential gene expression and potential regulatory network of fatty acid biosynthesis during fruit and leaf development in yellowhorn (Xanthoceras sorbifolium), an oil-producing tree with significant deployment values
creator: Tian-Le Shi, Hai-Yao Ma, Xinrui Wang, Hui Liu, Xue-Mei Yan, Xue-Chan Tian, Zhi-Chao Li, Yu-Tao Bao, Zhao-Yang Chen, Shi-Wei Zhao, Qiuhong Xiang, Kai-Hua Jia, Shuai Nie, Wenbin Guan, Jian-Feng Mao
description: Xanthoceras sorbifolium (yellowhorn) is a woody oil plant with super stress resistance and excellent oil characteristics. The yellowhorn oil can be used as biofuel and edible oil with high nutritional and medicinal value. However, genetic studies on yellowhorn are just in the beginning, and fundamental biological questions regarding its very long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) biosynthesis pathway remain largely unknown.

title: The challenge of a late diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: co-occurring trajectories and camouflage tendencies. a case report of a young Autistic female with Avoidant Restrictive Food Intake Disorder
creator: Sara Passarini, Silvia Guerrera, Maria Picilli, Elisa Fucà, Laura Casula, Deny Menghini, Sabine Pirchio, Valeria Zanna, Giovanni Valeri, Stefano Vicari
description: IntroductionAutistic individuals may show several psychiatric co-occurrences, including Feeding and Eating Disorders (FEDs). Avoidant and Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) consists of avoidance or restriction in food intake, leading to significant weight loss, nutritional deficiencies, and marked interference with psychosocial functioning.

title: Mapping the Evidence on Vitamin D, Vitamin B12, and Folate Deficiencies and Their Potential Impact on Treatment Outcomes in Patients With Cancer in Sub-Saharan Africa: Protocol for a Scoping Review
creator: Olufunmilayo Olukemi Akapo, Olubunmi Margaret Ogbodu, Teke Apalata, Amy Schwartz
description: BackgroundMicronutrient deficiencies, particularly of vitamin D, vitamin B12, and folate, are increasingly recognized as important, yet underexplored contributors to adverse outcomes in oncology care. These micronutrients are essential for immune regulation, DNA synthesis and repair, cell proliferation, and metabolic homeostasis, all of which are frequently disrupted in patients with cancer.

title: Application of deconvolutional networks for feature interpretability in epilepsy detection
creator: Sihao Shao, Yu Zhou, Ruiheng Wu, Aiping Yang, Qiang Li
description: IntroductionScalp electroencephalography (EEG) is commonly used to assist in epilepsy detection. Even automated detection algorithms are already available to assist clinicians in reviewing EEG data, many algorithms used for seizure detection in epilepsy fail to account for the contributions of different channels. The Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) can provide the model’s interpretability but has not been applied in seizure detection.

title: The Naples prognosis score as an independent predictor of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Hao Hong, Jindan Kong, Yao Wei, Jun Jin, Xueke Liu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the predictive efficacy of the Naples prognosis score (NPS) in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) and explore its mechanistic link to renal injury, with the goal of providing a novel clinical tool for early SA-AKI risk assessment.MethodsOne-way ANOVA was applied to variables exhibiting normal distribution and homo-geneous variance. Spearman analysis was performed to assess relationships.

title: Lactobacillus johnsonii and host communication: insight into modulatory mechanisms during health and disease
creator: Llilian Arzola-Martínez, Keerthikka Ravi, Gary B. Huffnagle, Nicholas W. Lukacs, Wendy Fonseca
description: Lactobacillus johnsonii is a commensal bacterium that has been isolated from vaginal and gastrointestinal (GI) tracts of vertebrate hosts, including humans, rodents, swine, and poultry. Lactobacillus-based probiotic supplements are popular because of the health advantages they offer. Species such as L. johnsonii are particularly interesting due to their potential health-promoting properties.

title: Development of mRNA vaccines against herpes zoster
creator: Dongdong Li, Jun Luo, Junwei Wang, Lining Wang, Mengyu Zhang, Jian Shen, Xiaoyu Chu, Weian Mao, Yan Zhang, Hongwu Xin
description: Herpes zoster (HZ), caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV), remains a substantial public health burden, particularly in aging populations, due to the risk of severe complications like postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). While existing vaccines (eg. Shingrix®) have advanced prevention efficiencies, they present notable limitations, such as high reactogenicity and complex manufacturing.

title: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG mitigates bone loss induced by mechanical unloading via regulation of the gut-bone axis
creator: Xuezhi Qin, Yu-E Lian, Hanqin Tang, Xin Chai, Yuhai Gao, Yanchun Ma, Jing Guo, Hongli Wang, Yan Wang, Biaomeng Wang, Jiayu Chen, Yixuan Wang
description: BackgroundBone loss is a serious complication of mechanical unloading, such as that experienced during spaceflight or prolonged bed rest, and represents a significant clinical concern. Although the gut-bone axis has been implicated in bone homeostasis, its role under unloading conditions remains underexplored.

title: NavBLIP: a visual-language model for enhancing unmanned aerial vehicles navigation and object detection
creator: Ye Li, Li Yang, Meifang Yang, Fei Yan, Tonghua Liu, Chensi Guo, Rufeng Chen
description: IntroductionIn recent years, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have increasingly been deployed in various applications such as autonomous navigation, surveillance, and object detection. Traditional methods for UAV navigation and object detection have often relied on either handcrafted features or unimodal deep learning approaches.

title: An integrated precision medicine approach in major depressive disorder: a study protocol to create a new algorithm for the prediction of treatment response
creator: Bernhard T. Baune, Alessandra Minelli, Bernardo Carpiniello, Martina Contu, Jorge Domínguez Barragán, Chus Donlo, Ewa Ferensztajn-Rochowiak, Rosa Glaser, Britta Kelch, Paulina Kobelska, Grzegorz Kolasa, Dobrochna Kopeć, María Martínez de Lagrán Cabredo, Paolo Martini, Miguel-Angel Mayer, Valentina M
description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is the most common psychiatric disease worldwide with a huge socio-economic impact. Pharmacotherapy represents the most common option among the first-line treatment choice; however, only about one third of patients respond to the first trial and about 30% are classified as treatment-resistant depression (TRD). TRD is associated with specific clinical features and genetic/gene expression signatures.

title: TOMM5 is associated with oral cancer progression: a multi-omics analysis from single-cell atlas to in vitro validation
creator: Li Gao, Jian-Di Li, Yi-Yang Chen, Ge-Li Tan, Jian-Jia Zeng, Xi Lin, Lu Liang, Shuang Xia, Guo-Jiao Wu, Gang Chen
description: AimsTranslocase of Outer Mitochondrial Membrane 5 (TOMM5), a mitochondrial outer membrane translocase subunit implicated in tumorigenesis, remains unexplored in oral cancer. Herein, we aimed to decipher the role of TOMM5 in oral cancer.MethodsThis study comprehensively explored the expression profile, clinical significance, and functional roles of TOMM5 in oral carcinogenesis with global RNA-seq and microarray datasets.

title: Technical considerations in endovascular thrombectomy for distal vessel occlusions
creator: Amir Molaie, Nickolas Idrogo, Naoki Kaneko, May Nour, Latisha Sharma, David S Liebeskind, Gary Duckwiler, Viktor Szeder
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke due to distal vessel occlusions (DVOs) remains to be clarified. Anatomical complexities in the distal vasculature, such as tortuosity and vessel fragility, render technique selection particularly paramount during EVT.

title: Psychological safety in health professions education: insights and strategies from a global community of practice
creator: Chaoyan Dong, Lisa Altshuler, Nobutaro Ban, Lee Yuen Wong, Fatima Elbasri Abuelgasim Mohammed, Chao Tian Tang, Elizabeth Kachur
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Psychological safety is the belief that one will not be punished or humiliated for speaking up, sharing ideas, raising concerns, or making mistakes. There are various threats to psychological safety in health professions education (HPE). This commentary applies Clark’s model of psychological safety (Inclusion Safety, Learner Safety, Contributor Safety, Challenger Safety) to five different HPE settings (classroom instructions, clinical training, simulation-based training, online instructions, interprofessional education). Setting-specific threats and strategies for enhancing psychological safety are discussed.

title: Wireless bioelectronic control architectures for muscle-powered biohybrid robotic systems
creator: Hiroyuki Tetsuka, Minoru Hirano
description: Wireless bioelectronic interfaces are increasingly used to control tissue-engineered, muscle-powered biohybrid robotic systems. However, a unifying engineering framework linking device design to system-level control remains underdeveloped. Here, we formulate wireless control in biohybrid robotics as a coupled co-design problem integrating signal delivery, spatial selectivity, scalability, sensing and feedback, controller implementation, biological life support, and interface stability.

title: Neural basis for behavioral plasticity during the parental life-stage transition in mice
creator: Kazunari Miyamichi
description: Parental care plays a crucial role in the physical and mental well-being of mammalian offspring. Although sexually naïve male mice, as well as certain strains of female mice, display aggression toward pups, they exhibit heightened parental caregiving behaviors as they approach the time of anticipating their offspring.

title: The role of radiotherapy in small cell lung cancer: a new paradigm for the radiation oncologist
creator: Paolo Borghetti, Sara Ramella, Umberto Ricardi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive tumor that presents in most cases as a metastatic disease. The prognosis is poor, but the advent of immunotherapy has rekindled hopes for outcomes. Radiotherapy plays a crucial role in this oncological scenario, and there are still many open questions on the correct application of radiotherapy and its integration with chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

title: Cognitive–emotional associations between non-restorative sleep and erectile dysfunction: the role of rumination profiles and resilience
creator: Pan Gao, Yao Jiang, Zhi Cao, Fan Wu, Yukuai Ma, Peng Yang, Yexin Luo, Haozhe Shen, Yunlong Ge, Junhua Du, Xiansheng Zhang
description: IntroductionErectile dysfunction (ED) is a prevalent male health condition that substantially correlates with impaired sexual function and reduced overall quality of life. Non-restorative sleep (NRS), a prevalent subjective sleep disturbance, has recently been identified as an under-recognized factor linked to ED. Nonetheless, the psychological factors involved in the association between NRS and ED remain poorly clarified.

title: Modulation of gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids by probiotics attenuates inflammation in endometriosis
creator: Xiaoli Dong, Fang Xie, Ping Li
description: IntroductionThis study investigated whether probiotics alleviate Endometriosis (EMs)-related inflammation by modulating the gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs).MethodsAn endometriosis model was established in SD rats, which were randomly divided into a normal diet group (NCD) and a probiotic group (NCD_Pro), with four rats per group. After a 4-week dietary intervention, serum and fecal samples were collected.

title: Potential links between PCOS/PMOS and Alzheimer disease and related dementias
creator: Mina Amiri, Armita Kakavand Hamidi, Daniel L Farkas, Richard P Buyalos, Ricardo Azziz
description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome/polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PCOS/PMOS) is a common endocrine disorder with significant metabolic and reproductive implications. Increasing attention has focused on its potential long-term neurological consequences, including possible links to cognitive impairment and Alzheimer disease (AD), through overlapping biological pathways.

title: Differences between U23 and older semi-professional soccer players in perfectionism and passion: exploring determinant relationship between variables
creator: Adelaida Irene Ogallar-Blanco, Eduardo García-Mármol, Filipe Manuel Clemente, Georgian Badicu, Antonio Liñán-González, Francisco Tomás González-Fernández
description: AimAbundant studies have pointed out that perfectionism and passion are interrelated and that they both can influence performance in a variety of contexts, including sports, however, research on how these variables interact and might affect performance in team sports, such as soccer, is still scarce.

title: Functional Characterization of the P‐Type ATPases ATP13A3 and ATP13A4 as Plasma Membrane Polyamine Transporters
creator: Haruka Morimoto, Tomoya Yasujima, Mione Yamasaki, Takahiro Yamashiro, Hiroaki Yuasa
description: Polyamines are ubiquitous polycations involved in diverse cellular functions, including proliferation, differentiation, and survival. While endogenous biosynthesis can maintain the intracellular levels of polyamines, uptake becomes critical during high metabolic demand. Despite the evidence for ATP‐dependent polyamine uptake systems in the plasma membrane, their molecular characteristics remain unclear.

title: REM genes controlling phyllotaxis and yield: bridging findings from Arabidopsis thaliana to Brassica napus
creator: Carlotta C. Ferrario, Francesca Caselli, Shokhsanam Davlatboeva, Evert-Jan Blom, Arjen van Tunen, Veronica Gregis, Martin M. Kater
description: One of the main challenges in agriculture is the increasing demand to enhance plant yield per hectare. This is crucial not only for boosting food production to support a growing global population but also for minimizing land use for agricultural purposes. Seed yield is of particular importance since seeds are the primary source of carbohydrates and oil.

title: AKT Phosphorylation of FOXK2 at Ser398 Impacts Breast Cancer Cell Growth and Viability
creator: L T Carneiro, J M R C Nunes, G De Gregoriis, B S Mendonça, W M Araújo, R C Maia, E W F Lam, R S Carvalho, M A Carvalho, A D Sharrocks, G Nestal de Moraes
description: FOXK2 is a transcription factor known to mediate drug sensitivity in breast cancer. However, poor prognosis patients and drug‐resistant cells exhibit constitutively elevated levels of FOXK2 protein, which appears functionally inactive. Although emerging evidence suggests that FOXK2 is regulated by post‐translational modifications, the underlying mechanisms in breast cancer remain poorly understood.

title: CSE-8, a filamentous fungus-specific Shr3-like chaperone, facilitates endoplasmic reticulum exit of chitin synthase CHS-3 (class I) in Neurospora crassa
creator: Samantha Verónica González-Téllez, Meritxell Riquelme
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chitin is a crucial structural polysaccharide in fungal cell walls, essential for maintaining cellular plasticity and integrity. Its synthesis is orchestrated by chitin synthases (CHS), a major family of transmembrane proteins. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the cargo receptor Chs7, belonging to the Shr3-like chaperone family, plays a pivotal role in the exit of Chs3 from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and its subsequent activity in the plasma membrane (PM). However, the auxiliary machinery responsible for CHS trafficking in filamentous fungi remains poorly understood.

title: Overview of Regulatory Guidelines Related to Methods and Models for Small Populations
creator: Laurens Sluijterman, Letao Li, Kristin E. Karlsson, Vincent Damotte, Sarah Zohar, Kit Roes, Joanna IntHout
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper provides an overview of approaches and related guidelines from the EMA, FDA, and ICH that are relevant for obtaining clinical evidence for small populations to support regulatory decision making. The approaches are grouped into three categories: (1) maximizing the attainable sample size, (2) adapting the trial design to deal with a small sample size, and (3) including external information, while also examining the role of modeling.

title: Stage‐Specific Patterns of Imaging and Non‐Motor Biomarkers in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3
creator: Chun Li, Zhi‐Xian Ye, Xuan‐Yu Chen, Liang‐Liang Qiu, Zhi‐li Chen, Yu‐Sen Qiu, Wei Lin, Ru‐Ying Yuan, Xin‐Tong Yu, Chun‐Yu Huang, Xin‐Yuan Chen, Min‐Ting Lin, Jian‐Ping Hu, Wan‐Jin Chen, Ning Wang, Shao‐Bo Yao, Shi‐Rui Gan, Ying Fu
description: ObjectiveAdvancements in disease‐modifying therapies for spinocerebellar ataxia Type 3 (SCA3) underscore the need for robust biomarkers to monitor disease progression and evaluate treatment efficacy. Although motor phenotypes have been well characterized, less is known about non‐motor and imaging‐based features across different disease stages. This study aimed to characterize stage‐specific patterns of non‐motor and imaging biomarkers in SCA3.

title: A tool to address barriers in perinatal mental health screening, the PMH Connect: a perinatal mental health screening connection, education, and decision aid
creator: Sara Wagner Moyer, Jaclyn D. Nunziato, Nicole W. Karjane, Alexis I. Rivera, Katherine L. Wisner, Amy L. Salisbury, Patricia A. Kinser
description: Mental disturbances and related symptoms in the perinatal period present a challenge to patients and providers alike, particularly regarding identification and appropriate management. Perinatal Mental Health (PMH) screening occurs in clinical settings on a more regular basis thanks to guidelines recommending the use of validated screening measures used at perinatal visits.

title: Severe hypothyroidism with mixed thyrotropin receptor antibodies and diffuse thyroid uptake
creator: Senem Boz Aksoy
description: 0.37 ng/dL (4.8 pmol/L) (RR: 0.8-1.68 ng/dL; 10.3-21.6 pmol/L), and free triiodothyronine of 1.8 pg/mL (2.8 pmol/L) (RR: 2.0-4.4 pg/mL;3.1-6.8 pmol/L). Thyroid peroxidase antibody was elevated (235 IU/mL; RR, <34 IU/mL), with positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (4.42 index; RR, 0-1.3 index) and TSH receptor-blocking antibodies (5.89 IU/L; RR, 0-1.75 IU/L).

title: Primary adrenal small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma in a patient with sarcoidosis and synchronous colon adenocarcinoma
creator: Asami Sano, Tetsu Takeichi, Akio Miyamaoto, Yutaka Nishii, Teppei Yamamoto, Yukiko Kusama
description: Primary adrenal neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC), particularly the small cell subtype, is exceptionally rare. In patients with sarcoidosis, inflammatory lymphadenopathy may mimic a metastatic disease, making disease detection difficult. A 76-year-old man with sarcoidosis was referred for an enlarging left adrenal incidentaloma that had increased in size from 7 mm to 19 × 14 mm over 3 years.

title: The role of apoptosis in spinal cord injury: a bibliometric analysis from 1994 to 2023
creator: Siqiao Wang, Liming Cheng
description: BackgroundApoptosis after spinal cord injury (SCI) plays a pivotal role in the secondary injury mechanisms, which cause the ultimate neurologic insults. A better understanding of the molecular and cellular basis of apoptosis in SCI allows for improved glial and neuronal survival via the administrations of anti-apoptotic biomarkers.

title: Testing plant growth promoting microorganisms in the field - a proposal for standards
creator: Daniel Neuhoff, Günter Neumann, Markus Weinmann
description: In the European Union and worldwide there are a burgeoning markets for plant growth promoting microorganisms (PGPM) and other biological agents as soil improvers, bio-fertilizers, plant bio-stimulants, and biological control agents or bio-pesticides. Microbial agents have a major share in this development.

title: Enhancing the efficacy of traditional Mongolian alcohol-spraying bone-setting therapy for surgical neck fractures of the humerus: the effects and mechanisms of muscular origin-insertion point massage therapy
creator: Changjiang Xie, Mengte Du, Xin Wang, Huqitu Xi, Tianhu Wei
description: BackgroundHumeral surgical neck fractures (HSNF) are among the most common shoulder fractures, yet their treatment outcomes remain variable. Clinical observations suggest that combining traditional Mongolian alcohol-spraying bone-setting therapy with muscular origin-insertion point massage may accelerate fracture healing; however, the therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms require further validation.MethodsA total of patients with HSNF were randomly allocated into two groups.

title: CUE domain-containing 2 promotes diffuse large B-cell lymphoma progression via PP2A-B55β degradation and shapes macrophage-mediated immune responses
creator: Li-Jie Zeng, Wei-Xiang Lu, Yuan-Zheng Liang, Jing Yang, Jin-Yan Zhu, Liang Wang
description: CUE domain-containing 2 (CUEDC2) regulates ubiquitin-mediated protein turnover, cell-cycle progression, and inflammatory signaling, but its role in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains unclear. DLBCL is the most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and a substantial proportion of patients develop relapsed or refractory disease.

title: An X‐ray micro‐CT protocol enables non‐destructive 3D visualization of glandular architecture in archived paraffin‐embedded prostate cancer tissue
creator: Santiago Laguna‐Castro, Erna Mäkinen, Teemu Tolonen, Antti Kaipia, Jari Hyttinen
description: The prostate is organized as a complex glandular network, and prostate cancer is accompanied by architectural changes that cannot always be inferred from two‐dimensional (2D) histology. The study of these features in three dimensions (3D) in cancerous tissue is important because glandular features have shown potential value for disease characterization and risk stratification beyond that obtained from individual 2D sections.

title: The triglyceride glucose-body mass index is positively associated with higher risk of hypertension in rural southwest Chinese population: a cross sectional study
creator: Mingxue Dong, Ming Ma, LiJing Yang, Huali Xiong
description: BackgroundInsulin resistance (IR) has been shown to be associated with hypertension. The triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) has emerged as a novel surrogate marker for assessing IR. This study aimed to investigate the association between the TyG-BMI index and hypertension among adults in rural southwest China using a cross-sectional study.

title: Compound Chinese medicine (F1) improves spleen deficiency diarrhea by protecting the intestinal mucosa and regulating the intestinal flora
creator: Kang Wang, Guanzong Li, Zhi Yang, Fumei Yang, Yulin Sun, Gang Duan, Wang Sun, Ke Zhou, Jun He, Feiyan Dai
description: Compound Chinese medicine (F1) is a traditional prescription in Chinese medicine that is commonly used to treat spleen deficiency diarrhea (SDD). It has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in clinical practice. However, the precise mechanism by which it exerts its antidiarrheal effect is still unclear. This study aimed at investigating the antidiarrheal efficacy and mechanism of F1 on senna-induced secretory diarrhea (SDD).

title: MDTR: a knowledge-guided interpretable representation for quantifying liver toxicity at transcriptomic level
creator: Inyoung Sung, Sangseon Lee, Dongmin Bang, Jungseob Yi, Sunho Lee, Sun Kim
description: IntroductionDrug-induced liver injury (DILI) has been investigated at the patient level. Analysis of gene perturbation at the cellular level can help better characterize biological mechanisms of hepatotoxicity. Despite accumulating drug-induced transcriptome data such as LINCS, analyzing such transcriptome data upon drug treatment is a challenging task because the perturbation of expression is dose and time dependent.

title: Less is more: Low-strength type I interferon signaling enhances CAR T cell therapy
creator: Erting Tang, Jun Huang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ype-directed differentiation, or combination regimens.3 These strategies are powerful, but most introduce a new genetic element or a novel biologic agent and with it, a new engineering, manufacturing, and regulatory burden. In our recently published study, “Low-Strength Type I Interferon Signaling Promotes CAR T cell Treatment Efficacy,” in Cancer Immunology Research,4 we took a different approach: rather than further redesigning the CAR, we asked whether the functional state of an already FDA-approved CAR T cell product could be improved during manufacturing by

title: The diagnostic value of C-X-C motif chemokine 8 in elderly patients with bacterial upper respiratory tract infections and its correlation with prognosis
creator: Lei Yu, Youtao Hu, Jianbin Sun, Xinguang Liu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to further investigate the correlation between C-X-C motif chemokine 8‌ (CXCL8) and the prognosis of bacterial upper respiratory tract infections (BURTIs) in the elderly population (≥65 years) and to evaluate its potential as a clinical biomarker in this specific high-risk cohort.

title: The ‘Upstairs-Downstairs’ heart with complete main pulmonary artery agenesis and PDA-dependent pulmonary circulation: A rare structural intersection characterized by multi detector computed tomography
creator: Aamir M Kanji, Tariq Aziz, Lulu Fundikira, Ummehani Akberali, Lilian Salingwa, Frederick Lyimo, Mboka Jacob
description: Superior-inferior ventricular arrangement is an exceedingly rare form of congenital cardiac malposition, representing fewer than 0.1% of all congenital heart diseases, and is almost invariably associated with complex intracardiac anomalies. We report a 3-year-old male who presented with persistent cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and failure to thrive. Prospective ECG-gated CT angiography demonstrated situs solitus with levocardia.

title: Antifungal activity of eumelanin-inspired indoylenepheyleneethynylene against Cryptococcus neoformans
creator: Brittney N. Conn, Jacob A. Lieberman, Priscilla Chatman, Kaitlyn Cotton, Martha A. Essandoh, Mohammad Ebqa’ai, Toby L. Nelson, Karen L. Wozniak
description: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic fungal pathogen that causes meningitis in >152,000 immunocompromised individuals annually, leading to 112,000 yearly deaths. The four classes of existing antifungal agents target plasma membrane sterols (ergosterol), nucleic acid synthesis, and cell wall synthesis. Existing drugs are not highly effective against Cryptococcus, and antifungal drug resistance is an increasing problem.

title: Burden of diet-related chronic diseases in Chinese and Japanese adults attributable to dietary risk factors from 1990 to 2021: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
creator: Minyan Wang, Huan Ma, Chu Qin, Oscar Onayi Mandizadza, Haojie Ni, Yun Shi, Conghua Ji
description: BackgroundChronic diseases are a major cause of death, contributing significantly to the global disease burden. The growing aging population and chronic disease burden in China and Japan have a substantial impact on health outcomes. Dietary factors, as key modifiable elements, are particularly important.

title: Clinical practice guideline for female fertility preservation
creator: Ningxia Sun, Haixia Ding, Lingbo Cai, Ri-Cheng Chian, Xiaohui Deng, Yichun Guan, Lei Jin, Xiaolin La, Ge Lin, Xiufeng Ling, Zhijuan Lou, Weiying Lu, Qun Lv, Fei Ma, Xiuying Pei, Song Quan, Jianzhen Shen, Minfang Tao, Lei Wang, Xiuxia Wang, Guangwu Xiong, Jian Xu, Peng Xu, Weihai Xu, Yuanqing Yao, Xi
description: IntroductionFemale fertility preservation (FFP) has become a clinical priority because gonadotoxic therapies for cancer and benign diseases are increasingly common and may cause irreversible ovarian failure. The current clinical practice guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on fertility assessment, oocyte/embryo cryopreservation, and ovarian tissue cryopreservation and transplantation for women at risk of iatrogenic infertility.

title: Ultrafast interphase exciton funneling in alternating-cation 2D perovskites through Förster-type energy transfer
creator: Supriya Ghosh, Peiran Wang, Heinz Amenitsch, Sumea Klokic, Pavel Chabera, Christian Sternemann, Bapi Pradhan, Johan Hofkens, Tönu Pullerits
description: Efficient exciton transport is central to the development of low-dimensional semiconductors for optoelectronic applications. Layered metal halide perovskites provide a versatile platform for regulating excitonic interactions through spacer-layer engineering. Here, we demonstrate that alternating-cation-in-the-interlayer space (ACI) perovskites exhibit markedly rapid interphase exciton funneling compared with conventional Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) architectures.

title: Beyond mere respect: new perspectives on dignity for healthcare workplace learning
creator: Christiane Klinner, Amabile Borges Dario, Amani Bell, Gillian Nisbet, Merrolee Penman, Lynn V. Monrouxe
description: IntroductionAlthough dignity in workplace learning in healthcare is gathering interest, we know little about stakeholders’ conceptualizations in this area across professional groups. Dignity breaches in workplace learning are common, often with serious and long-lasting consequences for the affected. Conceptualizations shape behaviours and experiences.

title: Transcriptomic profiling reveals autophagy-associated programs and prognostic biomarkers in anoikis-resistant pancreatic cancer cells
creator: Lizhi Lin, Monika Bauden, Roland Andersson, Daniel Ansari
description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by aggressive metastatic progression and poor clinical outcomes. During metastatic dissemination, detached tumor cells must overcome anoikis, a form of apoptosis induced by loss of extracellular matrix attachment. Although anoikis resistance is considered a critical prerequisite for metastasis, the adaptive mechanisms supporting detached survival in pancreatic cancer remain incompletely understood.

title: Seaweed and yeast extracts as sustainable phytostimulant to boost secondary metabolism of apricot fruits
creator: Noemi Gatti, Moez Maghrebi, Graziella Serio, Carla Gentile, Victor V. Bunea, Ivano Vigliante, Camille Boitte, Christian Garabello, Valeria Contartese, Cinzia M. Bertea, Giuseppe Mannino
description: In our study, we investigated the effects of Expando, a commercial biostimulant derived from seaweed and yeast extracts, on the secondary metabolism of Lady cot and Orange prima apricot cultivars. Notably, treatments with or 5.0 L/ha of Expando improved fruit uniformity and harvests synchronization, providing agronomic benefits.

title: FGFR pathway inhibition enhances PD-1 blockade and modulates antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer models
creator: Zhou Shang, Changqing Jing, Jiyuan Liu, Baolin Zhang, Marta Rúbies Bedós, Irineos Papakyriacou, Yumeng Mao, Yuezhi Chen
description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated limited efficacy in microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC). The fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling pathway contributes to tumor immune evasion, yet its role in CRC remains insufficiently understood. We investigated the immunomodulatory effects of FGFR inhibition in combination with PD-1 blockade in murine CRC models.

title: Elucidating the binding mechanism of SARS-CoV-2 NSP6-TBK1 and structure-based designing of phytocompounds inhibitors for instigating the host immune response
creator: Muhammad Suleman, Iqra Ishaq, Haji Khan, Safir Ullah khan, Rehana Masood, Norah A. Albekairi, Abdulrahman Alshammari, Sergio Crovella
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SARS-CoV-2, also referred to as severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, is the virus responsible for causing COVID-19, an infectious disease that emerged in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. Among its crucial functions, NSP6 plays a vital role in evading the human immune system by directly interacting with a receptor called TANK-binding kinase (TBK1), leading to the suppression of IFNβ production.

title: Gut microbiota in dysmenorrhea: causal evidence from Mendelian randomization and microbial-targeted intervention validation
creator: Yajie Qin, Rui Ma, Lili Zhang, Xiaotian Yang, Huifang Zhou, Yanping Wang
description: BackgroundDysmenorrhea is a prevalent gynecological disorder with multifactorial pathophysiology, including prostaglandin overproduction, inflammation, and pain sensitization. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota may contribute to pain modulation, although causal relationships remain unclear.MethodsBidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed to investigate causal associations between dysmenorrhea and gut microbiota.

title: The maturation of precision medicine into pragmatic, patient‐centered care: A commentary on the 2026 EHA CLL Guidelines
creator: Stefano Molica, Talha Munir, David Allsup
description: lies in introducing a holistic framework that seamlessly harmonizes disease biology, patient profiles, clinical feasibility, and personal preferences into a unified therapeutic strategy. 1 One of the most notable conceptual advances in the 2026 EHA Guidelines is the replacement of the traditional term “watch and wait” with “active surveillance.

title: Characterization of viscerofugal neurons in human colon by retrograde tracing and multi-layer immunohistochemistry
creator: Bao Nan Chen, Adam G. Humenick, Timothy James Hibberd, Wai Ping Yew, David A. Wattchow, Phil G. Dinning, Marcello Costa, Nick J. Spencer, Simon J. H. Brookes
description: Background and AimsViscerofugal neurons (VFNs) have cell bodies in the myenteric plexus and axons that project to sympathetic prevertebral ganglia. In animals they activate sympathetic motility reflexes and may modulate glucose metabolism and feeding. We used rapid retrograde tracing from colonic nerves to identify VFNs in human colon for the first time, using ex vivo preparations with multi-layer immunohistochemistry.

title: Tour guide robot: a 5G-enabled robot museum guide
creator: Stefano Rosa, Marco Randazzo, Ettore Landini, Stefano Bernagozzi, Giancarlo Sacco, Mara Piccinino, Lorenzo Natale
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This paper presents and discusses the development and deployment of a tour guide robot as part of the 5 g-TOURS EU research project, aimed at developing applications enabled by 5G technology in different use cases. The objective is the development of an autonomous robotic application where intelligence is off-loaded to a remote machine via 5G network, so as to lift most of the computational load from the robot itself.

title: Engineering peroxygenases for pharmaceutical applications: recent advances and future perspectives
creator: Lilin Feng, Atul Kumar, Ulrich Schwaneberg, Marisa Sárria Pereira de Passos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Selective oxidation is a cornerstone process in pharmaceutical biosynthesis, as it enables the conversion of inert C–H bonds into valuable functional groups such as alcohols, ketones, epoxides, and carboxylic acids, which serve as important intermediates in drug synthesis. Peroxygenases, including unspecific peroxygenases and P450 peroxygenases, have emerged as powerful biocatalysts for enzymatic oxidation, with growing applications in metabolite synthesis, late-stage C–H functionalization, and the preparation of enantioenriched intermediates for pharmaceutical development.

title: Ligand-dependent G protein dynamics underlying opioid efficacy
creator: Jonathan C. Deutsch, Daniel Hilger, John Janetzko, Charles M. Schroeder, Steven Chu, Brian K. Kobilka, Rabindra V. Shivnaraine
description: Activation of heterotrimeric G proteins by G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) requires large-scale opening of the Gα α-helical domain (AHD) to expose the nucleotide-binding site and facilitate GDP–GTP exchange. Although orthosteric ligands are known to modulate GPCR conformation, how these effects propagate to the bound G protein remains unclear.

title: Access to context-specific lexical-semantic information during discourse tasks differentiates speakers with latent aphasia, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitively healthy adults
creator: Brielle C. Stark, Sarah Grace Dalton, Alyssa M. Lanzi
description: PurposeMild language impairments experienced by adults with neurogenic communication disorders are often difficult to detect due to the lack of sensitive traditional performance-based measures. This is problematic since many adults who have mild language deficits experience daily activity and participation limitations that are undetected and not managed.

title: The relationship between sensory processing sensitivity and medication sensitivity: brief report
creator: Jadzia Jagiellowicz, Bianca P. Acevedo, Teresa Tillmann, Arthur Aron, Elaine N. Aron
description: Sensory processing sensitivity (SPS) is a biological/temperament trait that is associated with greater awareness of and reactivity to the environment, which results in amplified responses to various stimuli, and possibly medications. We investigated the relationship between SPS and medication sensitivity in three studies.

title: A computational approach for intramural length estimation in anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery
creator: Vikram Shah, Lauren Ferrino, Dana Reaves-O’Neal, Tam T. Doan, Shagun Sachdeva, Craig G. Rusin, Dan Lior, Charles Puelz, Prakash M. Masand, Silvana Molossi
description: IntroductionAnomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery (AAOCA) is associated with sudden cardiac death. The intramural (IM) length is considered high-risk, yet radiologic measurements by computed tomography angiography (CTA) show variable agreement with measurements at surgery. We aimed to develop a semi-automatic computational method to estimate IM length in a retrospective cohort of surgical AAOCA patients.

title: miRNA-132-5p mediates a negative feedback regulation of IL-8 secretion through S100A8/A9 downregulation in neutrophil-like HL-60 cells
creator: Yang Zhou, Milène Tetsi Nomigni, Anthoula Gaigneaux, Fabrice Tolle, Helen L. Wright, Jean-Luc Bueb, Sabrina Bréchard
description: BackgroundNeutrophils are an important source of pro-inflammatory and immunomodulatory cytokines. This makes neutrophils efficient drivers of interactions with immune and non-immune cells to maintain homeostasis and modulate the inflammatory process by notably regulating the release of cytokines. Ca2+-dependent regulatory mechanism encompassing cytokine secretion by neutrophils are not still identified.

title: The influence of cell morphology on the dynamics and stability of model bacterial communities
creator: Ing Xhu Lim, Faisal Halabeya, Joshua N. Milstein, Stefan Klumpp, Tobias Bollenbach, Stefan Klumpp, Tobias Bollenbach, Stefan Klumpp, Tobias Bollenbach, Stefan Klumpp, Tobias Bollenbach
description: Understanding how structures arise in microbial communities remains an outstanding challenge in bacterial ecology. When replicating within dense and confined environments, bacterial populations may collectively self-organize as a result of mechanical interactions. We previously observed that model dual-populations of bacteria, colonizing open-ended microchannels, either quickly fixate to a single population or segregate into long-lived, coexisting populations.

title: Eye movements reflect capacity-dependent organization of working memory
creator: Qiaoli Huang, Christian F. Doeller, Lucas Smith, Lucas Smith, Lucas Smith
description: Human cognition is capacity-limited, requiring strategies to actively structure information. Eye movements offer a natural mechanism for sequential sampling, but whether such sequences reflect memory organization is unknown. We developed a working-memory task where color-frequency pairings created a latent ordinal structure to optimally reduce memory load. Across two experiments, gaze patterns spontaneously aligned with this structure.

title: Prediction of antigen-responding VHH antibodies by tracking the evolution of antibody along the time course of immunization
creator: Tomonari Matsuda, Yoko Akazawa-Ogawa, Lilian-Kaede Komaba, Norihiko Kiyose, Nobuo Miyazaki, Yusaku Mizuguchi, Tetsuo Fukuta, Yuji Ito, Yoshihisa Hagihara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Antibody maturation is the central function of the adaptive immune response. This process is driven by the repetitive selection of mutations that increase the affinity toward antigens. We hypothesized that a precise observation of this process by high-throughput sequencing along the time course of immunization will enable us to predict the antibodies reacting to the immunized antigen without any additional in vitro screening.

title: Integration of gut microbiota, Stroke Dysbiosis Index, and inflammatory biomarkers in assessing prognosis of acute ischemic stroke
creator: Weny Rinawati, Aryati Aryati, Abdulloh Machin, Stefan Kiechl, Gregor Broessner
description: BackgroundAcute ischemic stroke (AIS) is often complicated by systemic infections that worsen prognosis. Emerging evidence suggests gut microbiota dysbiosis, inflammatory biomarkers, and gut–barrier dysfunction play pivotal roles in post-stroke outcomes. This study aimed to integrate Stroke Dysbiosis Index (SDI), Microbial Dysbiosis Index (MDI), and inflammatory biomarkers to evaluate their prognostic value in AIS patients.

title: Reply to “Central hypopnea classification: bridging the gap between event identification and clinical utility”
creator: Anjali P Ahn, Atul Malhotra
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). guide clinical decision-making, and no evidence is provided to demonstrate the clinical consequences of hypopnea classification nor evidence of whether classification changes disease categorization, treatment response, or patient-centered outcomes [2]. We appreciate her highlighting the need for thresholds to define a clinically meaningful burden of central disease as well as the need for research regarding the impact of hypopnea classification on outcomes. Research in this area is lacking.

title: Post-purchase behavioral intention in medical aesthetic: the role of image, perceived value, and satisfaction
creator: Chen-Chung Ma, Tzu-Chi Ou, Chun-Mei Tsai, Tai-Hsiang Chen
description: IntroductionThe technicality and professionalism of medical aesthetics have become one of the most fashionable indicators in the world, and image is the key factor of aesthetic development. This study aims to explore the relationship between medical aesthetic image, perceived value, satisfaction and post-purchase behavioral intention.

title: The Remote Food Photography Method Is Valid for Assessing Dietary Intake of Serie A Football Players
creator: Costanza Gavioli, Florentino Huertas Olmedo, Mathieu Lacome, Rossella Dodi, Mauro Mandorino, Julien Louis
description: To ensure football players meet their nutritional demands, sport nutritionists need to accurately collect and analyse dietary intake. However, dietary assessment methods have limitations. The Remote Food Photography Method (RFPM) is a valid approach, but the validation in real‐life settings requires further investigations.

title: Deep learning and firearm wound classification: a pilot study
creator: Giuseppe Delogu, Nicola Di Fazio, Gabriele Licciardello, Paola Frati, Cristoforo Pomara, Francesco Sessa
description: IntroductionThe study on the use of deep learning in pattern recognition of gunshot wounds (GSW) represents a novelty in the field of forensic pathology. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has already revolutionized many medical specialties, applications in forensic medicine are still limited. Nevertheless, AI-based tools could be of great use in a discipline that relies heavily on visual analysis.

title: Development of an educational and monitoring mobile application for pregnant women in Nigeria
creator: Abdulhammed Opeyemi Babatunde, Adejumoke Idowu Ayede, Amalia Colangelo, Tuan Dung Nguyen, Abdullahi Tunde Aborode, Charles Umeh, Maria Paula Hernandez, Oluwaseyi Iyanuoluwa Ayede, Oluwatobiloba Oluwadunni Ayede
description: IntroductionNigeria accounts for 20% of all maternal mortality. Recently, more mobile health technology (mHealth) interventions are emerging in sub-Saharan Africa. The potential of mobile applications in maternal care has not been explored in Nigeria. This study describes the process of design, development, and testing of an educational and monitoring mobile application for pregnant women in Nigeria.

title: Integrating Nutrition and Physical Activity into the EXEMIG/01 Interdisciplinary Model for Chronic and High-Frequency Migraine
creator: Roberto Pippi, Deborah Prete, Stefano Pagano, Chiara Valenti, Simonetta Simonetti, Sandro Prati, Marco Alabiso, Giulia Settembrini, Daniela Fruttini, Paola Sarchielli
description: Background: Migraine (MIG) management guidelines support a comprehensive approach combining medication, therapeutic patient education (TPE), behavioral strategies, lifestyle changes, diet, and physical activity (PA). Objective: To present an innovative interdisciplinary outpatient model for individuals with MIG, focusing on PA, sedentary behavior, eating habits (EH), metabolic health, temporomandibular disorders, and postural dysfunctions.

title: How to Break Through the Ceiling of Scientific Progress?—Innovation Challenges and Pathways Based on the Fitness Landscape Framework
creator: Kunjie Zhu, Li Sun, Peng Du
description: Science has not hit an absolute ceiling; it is stranded on a local peak. Viewed through Wright's fitness landscape, today's evaluation and funding systems over‐select, refining work within established paradigms while suppressing the drift and recombination needed to cross fitness valleys. Restoring room for non‐consensus, curiosity‐driven and interdisciplinary research is an institutional task as much as an intellectual one.

title: Transformer-based human-motion forecasting coupled with safe reinforcement learning for telepresence robot co-navigation
creator: Heba G. Mohamed, Muhammad Nasir Khan, Fawad Naseer, Muhammad Tahir, Mohsin Jamil
description: IntroductionTelepresence robots (TPRs) must co-navigate with humans in constrained hospital environments, where safety depends on anticipating rather than merely reacting to human motion. Existing approaches rarely integrate short-horizon human-motion forecasting with safety-constrained control, which reduces robustness in dense corridors and ward bays. This study addresses this gap by evaluating an anticipatory, safety-aware co-navigation framework for TPRs.

title: The vagal rhizopathies
creator: Christopher R. Honey
description: Neurovascular compression of the tenth cranial nerve, the vagus nerve, can cause recognizable and neurosurgically treatable clinical conditions. This chapter will outline the clinical characteristics unique to vagus nerve compression and highlight both the definitive diagnostic protocol and neurosurgical treatment of these conditions. The vagus nerve has motor, sensory and autonomic components.

title: An integrated surveillance in Zhejiang Province: ecological and pathogen survey of vectors and reservoir hosts in 2024
creator: Jinna Wang, Mingyu Luo, Qinmei Liu, Tianqi Li, Zhou Guan, Zhenyu Gong, Juan Hou, Jimin Sun, Jianmin Jiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionIn this study, an integrated surveillance framework was employed to simultaneously quantify the population densities of key vectors and reservoir hosts and screen them for associated pathogens across Zhejiang Province, China.MethodsThe light trap method, larval pipette method, fly trap method, sticky trap method, trap-night method, tick-picking method, dragging method, visual inspection method, and chigger mite picking method were used for the ecological surveillance of mosquitoes, flies, cockroaches, rodents, ticks, bedbugs, and chigger mites.

title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review
creator: Félix Amiot, Karim Tazarourte, Guillaume Gorincour, Axel Benhamed
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AbstractThis narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search.

title: Effects of contrast medium injection pressure on angiographic image quality
creator: Sara A. Abosabie, Tabea Kao, Timo Alexander Auer, Dirk Schnapauff, Uli Fehrenbach, Federico Collettini, Martin Jonczyk, Willie Magnus Lüdemann, Charlie Alexander Hamm, Gero Wieners, Robin Schmidt, Emine Yaren Yilmaz, Yubei He, Bernhard Gebauer, Anne Frisch, Lynn Jeanette Savic
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rationale and objectivesTo evaluate if higher contrast medium injection pressure can improve image quality of digital subtraction angiography (DSA) in liver-directed interventions.Materials and methodsProspective single-center study including twelve patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (n = 11) or liver metastases (n = 1) undergoing intra-arterial therapies to systematically compare DSA image quality (primary endpoint) and radiation exposure (secondary endpoint) using two microcatheters with maximum application pressures 750 (“C750”) and 1,200 PSI (“C1200”).

title: Sister haplotypes and recombination disequilibrium: a new approach to identify associations of haplotypes with complex diseases
creator: Shun-Yao Liao, Yuan-De Tan
description: Haplotype-based association analysis has several advantages over single-SNP association analysis. However, to date all haplotype-disease associations have not excluded recombination interference among multiple loci and hence some results might be confounded by recombination interference. Association of sister haplotypes with a complex disease, based on recombination disequilibrium (RD) was presented.

title: Investigating endogenous pain modulation through pupillometry: can pupil size reflect offset analgesia?
creator: Anna Leonhartsberger, Iwanka Iwanojko, Joëlle Katharina Metzger, Florin Allmendinger, Michèle Hubli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Supplemental Digital Content is Available in the Text.Pupillometry might capture offset analgesia–like effects in healthy participants, providing a complementary physiological marker of endogenous pain modulation and potential tool to detect dysfunction in chronic pain.

title: Breaking barriers: enhancing cancer detection in younger patients by overcoming diagnostic bias in primary care
creator: Waseem Jerjes, Daniel Harding
description: ly diagnosis of cancer is critical for effective treatment and improved prognostic outcomes, making the recognition and mitigation of diagnostic biases an essential component of primary care practice. Cancer incidence and mortality in adults under 50 years of age has been rising globally in the decades since 1990, especially in more highly-developed countries (2).

title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review
creator: Samah Hassan, Kenneth J. Faber, Joy C. MacDermid
description: Supplemental Digital Content is Available in the Text.Shoulder pain requires an effective triage model. This review underscores the need for a paradigm shift in shoulder pain triage that recognizes referral management as a multifactorial decision-making process. 1. Introduction Shoulder pain is the leading cause of work absenteeism55 affecting 1 in 3 adults at some point during their lifetime.

title: Mortality rates from asbestos-related diseases in Italy during the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Lucia Fazzo, Enrico Grande, Amerigo Zona, Giada Minelli, Roberta Crialesi, Ivano Iavarone, Francesco Grippo
description: Background and aimPatients with interstitial lung diseases, including asbestosis, showed high susceptibility to the SARS-CoV-2 virus and a high risk of severe COVID-19 symptoms. Italy, highly impacted by asbestos-related diseases, in 2020 was among the European countries with the highest number of COVID-19 cases.

title: Are Asymmetry-Focused Training Interventions More Effective than General Programs in Reducing Interlimb Asymmetries and Improving Athletic Performance? A Systematic Review
creator: Antonio Martos-Arregui, Iago Rojas-Cepero, Xing Zhang, Amador García-Ramos, Francisco Javier Rojas-Ruiz, Mar Cepero-González
description: BackgroundInterlimb asymmetries (ILA) have been associated with an increased risk of injury and decreased athletic performance. However, despite the growing number of training interventions targeting ILA, their comparative effectiveness relative to general strength and conditioning approaches has not yet been systematically reviewed.

title: Effectiveness rehabilitative therapy and Pridinol Mesylate in low back pain
creator: Lorenza Lauricella, Noemi Calabrese, Dalila Scaturro, Domenico Migliorino, Michele Vecchio, Giulia Letizia Mauro
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSpondylarthritis is a degenerative disease involving the intervertebral disc, vertebral bodies, and adjacent soft tissues. Treatment aims to slow disease progression and manage symptoms through an interdisciplinary approach. It can be conservative and rarely chirurgic.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a rehabilitation combined with Pridinol Mesylate in the treatment of Spondylarthritis in elderly patients in terms of pain resolution, improving disability, and quality of life.Materials and methodsWe conducted a retrospective study on patients with Spondylarthritis.

title: Evolving role of proton therapy in contemporary oncology
creator: Emily S Lebow, Helen A Shih
description: Proton therapy offers a distinct physical advantage over photon radiotherapy through the Bragg peak dose concentration in target with both lower integral dose and finite path length, and sharper penumbra as compared to photons, collectively reducing radiation exposure to surrounding normal tissues and potentially improving the therapeutic ratio.

title: CoviWall, a whole-virion-inactivated B.1.617.2 vaccine candidate, induces potent humoral and Th1 cell response in mice and protects against B.1.617.2 strain challenge in Syrian hamsters
creator: Jyotsna Dandotiya, Neeta Adhikari, Manas Ranjan Tripathy, Kamini Jakhar, Sudipta Sonar, Dibya Ranjan Pati, Vibhu Kanchan, Varsha S. Prasad, Jitendra Kumar, Nitesh K. Senapati, Arti Bharmoria, Neeraj Rani, Monika Lakhanpal, CS. Patil, Nishan Singh, Lovely Khan, Lavit Jambu, Naveen K. Jain, Syed Khali
description: Rapid development of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccines and antiviral drugs have significantly reduced morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although most of the vaccines were developed initially with the ancestral Wuhan antigen, here, we report the development and immunological efficacy of a whole-virion–inactivated vaccine candidate (CoviWall) to combat the deadly B.1.617.2 (Delta strain) infection.

title: A data driven approach for soft tissue biomarker identification linked to Chiari-like malformation and syringomyelia
creator: Jake Cumber, Emma Scales-Theobald, Clare Rusbridge, Kevin Wells
description: Canine Chiari-like malformation (CM) is a neuroanatomical condition associated with conformational change of the cranium, craniocervical junction and neuroparenchyma, resulting in pain (Chiari associated pain or CM-P) and the development of syringomyelia (SM). The associated neuro-disability in affected individuals compromises quality of life.

title: Dietary supplementation with Epimedium contributes to the improvement of hormone levels, gut microbiota, and serum metabolite composition in the Chinese forest musk deer (Moschus berezovskii)
creator: Shan Xie, Qinlin Yang, Zaixiang Ying, Mingcheng Cai, Wenqiao Fan, Hanyu Gao, Xiaolan Feng, Yongjiang Wu
description: The Chinese forest musk deer (Moschus berezovskii) is a small ruminant animal with special economic value. It is listed as a National Level I key protected species in China. However, these animals are prone to stress responses in captive environments.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Systemic Immunomodulatory Therapies for Non‐Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review With Pairwise and Network Meta‐Analyses
creator: Kai‐Yang Chen, Hoi‐Chun Chan, Chi‐Ming Chan
description: IntroductionNon‐infectious uveitis (NIU) is a chronic immune‐mediated ocular inflammatory disease that may cause irreversible visual impairment. The comparative efficacy and safety of systemic immunomodulatory therapies, including conventional agents and biologics, remain incompletely defined. This systematic review and network meta‐analysis evaluated systemic immunosuppressive therapies for NIU.

title: DEmiRNA-mRNA regulatory network reveals miR‐122-5p as a regulatory factor of arginine metabolism in necrotizing enterocolitis
creator: Zhili Ding, Ting Guo, Qiang Tang, Yaqiang Hong, Zhibao Lv, Li Lu, Wenjun Zhuang
description: ObjectiveNecrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a gastrointestinal emergency with relatively high morbidity and mortality in neonates. The role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in NEC is not yet entirely clear. This study aimed to explore the mechanism of miR-122-5p in NEC.MethodsDifferentially expressed (DE) miRNAs were sequenced in control and NEC mice.

title: Analysis of behavioral sequences in social interactions of autistic children: a latent class model based on structured play observation
creator: YiWen Chen
description: ObjectiveThis study addresses the unclear dynamic mechanisms underlying social interactions in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by constructing a structured play observation framework.MethodsBy combining latent class analysis (LCA) and temporal analysis techniques, this study systematically analyzed the heterogeneous characteristics of social behavioral sequences.

title: Intermittent theta‐burst stimulation versus sham stimulation for suicidal ideation and psychiatric symptoms in depressive disorders: A systematic review and meta‐analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Muhammad Bilal, Muskan Kumari, Syeda Zainab Farooq, Fatima Sajjad, Meerab Sana Ullah, Muhammad Akif, Sana Iftikhar, Muhammad Nabeel Saddique, Mohammad Jalal Nazari
description: Suicidal ideation, depressive symptoms, anxiety, and sleep disturbance remain difficult to manage in psychiatric populations, and intermittent theta‐burst stimulation (iTBS) has emerged as an accelerated, non‐invasive neuromodulation strategy for these outcomes. This meta‐analysis compares iTBS versus sham–iTBS across suicidal ideation, depression severity, anxiety severity, and sleep quality to guide clinical decision‐making.

title: From genetic risk to early detection - clinical outcomes of a person-centered screening program for women with a high genetic risk of breast cancer
creator: Ke Zhou, Caroline Abadie, Louise Crivelli, Euriell Fortin, Martine Bellanger, Charlotte Huet
description: BackgroundThere is little evidence on breast cancer (BC) diagnosed in women with a high genetic risk, before and after their inclusion in a long-term risk management program based on genetic risk assessment. We analyzed clinical outcomes in women enrolled in the Phare Grand Ouest (PGO) program.

title: Conventional and complementary alternative medicine therapies for renal anemia: a literature review
creator: Ching-Ming Lu, Yuan-Hsuan Hsu, I-Hsin Lin, Ko-Lin Kuo, Jian-Fu Liao, Hui-Fen Huang, Ping-Hsun Lu
description: Renal anemia stems mainly from chronic inflammation with elevated hepcidin levels, iron deficiency, and reduced red blood cell lifespan. Inadequate erythropoietin (EPO) production, worsened kidney function, leads to symptoms such as low energy, fatigue, and impaired physical function, significantly affecting patients’ quality of life.

title: Case Report: Primary cutaneous apocrine carcinoma mimicking breast carcinoma - a rare diagnostic challenge
creator: Masih Kameh Khosh, Tobias Hirsch, Hans-Joachim Schulze, Cornelius Kuhnen, Sascha Wellenbrock
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundA 60-year-old male patient presented to a senological clinic with a left axillary tumor. The histomorphological characteristics were ambiguous, initially pointing to apocrine carcinoma of mammary origin. This suspicion led to a delay in establishing the correct diagnosis.

title: Data-Driven Virus Discovery with Virushunter and Virusgatherer
creator: Liubov Chuprikova, Li Chuin Chong, Sergej Ruff, Stefan Seitz, Chris Lauber
description: We present Virushunter and Virusgatherer, a bipartite computational workflow for discovering viral genomes from unprocessed next-generation sequencing data. Virushunter conducts a profile Hidden Markov Model-based sequence homology search for viral hallmark protein-coding sequence reads to construct microcontigs, which are used as seeds for targeted viral genome assembly by Virusgatherer.

title: 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase C677T gene polymorphism as a risk factor for premature coronary artery disease in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
creator: Nisreen O. Mohammed, Ibtisam A. Ali, Bahaelddin K. Elamin, Bakri Osman Saeed
description: BackgroundAfrica, like the rest of the world, is experiencing an increasing prevalence of diabetes mellitus. Diabetes increases the risk for coronary artery disease (CAD) by fourfold compared to people without diabetes. C677T polymorphism in methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) and hyperhomocysteinemia were reported by many studies as risk factors for CAD among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

title: Comment on Higher Post‐Operative L‐Thyroxine Dosage Needed After Right Compared to Left‐Lobe Hemithyroidectomy
creator: Nayab Ikram, Madeeha Amir
description: ated with higher postoperative levothyroxine requirement. Unlike other studies focusing on patient‐related factors, this study also considers surgical site and we commend the authors for this contribution. We would like to raise points that deserve further consideration. First, postoperative TSH was higher following right‐sided surgery than left‐sided surgery (1.70 vs. 1.40 μIU/mL, p = 0.

title: Intersubject variability in a comprehensive numerical assessment of operator electromagnetic exposure to TMS
creator: S. D’Agostino, M. Colella, R. Falsaperla, M. Liberti, F. Apollonio
description: IntroductionTranscranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is increasingly used in clinical and research settings, often requiring the operator to remain in close proximity to the stimulation coil. While regulatory guidelines exist for patient safety, the workplace exposure assessment, particularly its dependence on operator anatomy, remains limited.

title: The impact of artistic sports on academic self-efficacy
creator: Yanyan Tian, Haiqing Wang
description: IntroductionArtistic sports have a more positive impact on adolescents on the basis of basic sports. This study delves into the beneficial effects of Artistic sports compared to basic sports in enhancing academic self-efficacy in college students, and investigates the mediating roles of mindfulness, social anxiety, and academic procrastination in this process.

title: Exploring medical food supplementation as an adjunct strategy for microbiota restoration and seizure reduction in CDKL5 deficiency disorder
creator: Elisa Borghi, Matteo Domenico Marsiglia, Francesca Triva, Emerenziana Ottaviano, Ilaria Viganò, Miriam Nella Savini, Valentino Costabile, Aglaia Vignoli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesCDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy characterized by early‐onset, treatment‐resistant seizures and severe neurodevelopmental impairment. Increasing evidence suggests that alterations in the gut–brain axis may contribute to disease pathophysiology, raising interest in microbiota‐targeted interventions.

title: High resolution and contrast 7 tesla MR brain imaging of the neonate
creator: Philippa Bridgen, Raphael Tomi-Tricot, Alena Uus, Daniel Cromb, Megan Quirke, Jennifer Almalbis, Beya Bonse, Miguel De la Fuente Botella, Alessandra Maggioni, Pierluigi Di Cio, Paul Cawley, Chiara Casella, Ayse Sila Dokumaci, Alice R. Thomson, Jucha Willers Moore, Devi Bridglal, Joao Saravia, Thomas
description: IntroductionUltra-high field MR imaging offers marked gains in signal-to-noise ratio, spatial resolution, and contrast which translate to improved pathological and anatomical sensitivity. These benefits are particularly relevant for the neonatal brain which is rapidly developing and sensitive to injury. However, experience of imaging neonates at 7T has been limited due to regulatory, safety, and practical considerations.

title: MONDE·T: A database and interactive webserver for non‐standard amino acids and peptide components in the PDB
creator: Alex Waldherr, Gesa L. Freimann, Andrei N. Lupas
description: Non‐standard amino acids (ncAAs) together with synthetic additions (like caps and linkers) are of wide interest for protein design and pharmaceutical optimization, as they can improve physicochemical properties and possibly reshape protein structure. Their inclusion in experimental structures has not been explored systematically. It remains elusive which components are those most impactful for protein design.

title: Belongingness and loneliness in higher education: a meta-analysis of pre- and post-pandemic trends
creator: Gulsah Dost
description: IntroductionThis meta-analysis seeks to explore how the complex relationship between loneliness and belongingness in higher education students can be explained by a set of pre- and post-COVID-19 pandemic dynamics.MethodsA meta-analysis including 56 studies and involving a total of 30,062 participants was conducted, and the review explores direct relations and moderation through age, education, and country.

title: Unusual paraneoplastic thrombocytosis in small bowel neuroendocrine tumor responding to 177Lu-DOTATATE
creator: Eve Piekarski, Anne-Ségolène Cottereau, Romain Coriat, Lise Willems, Lucas Bouys, Florence Tenenbaum
description: Neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are often associated with paraneoplastic features including carcinoid syndrome in up to 30% to 40% of cases. However, paraneoplastic thrombocytosis is a rare NET-associated condition. We report the case of a 59-year-old woman referred for significant and unexplained weight loss. Biological evaluation revealed thrombocytosis (900 × 109/L).

title: Splicing and expression dynamics of SR genes in hot pepper (Capsicum annuum): regulatory diversity and conservation under stress
creator: Lin Li, Yueqin Zhang, Rui Zhang, Xiangtao Cen, Yongxiang Huang, Hanqiao Hu, Xingyu Jiang, Yu Ling
description: In this study, we identified and characterized 23 genes encoding serine/arginine-rich (SR) protein in hot pepper (Capsicum annuum), named CaSR here. These CaSR proteins are grouped into seven subfamilies. Phylogenetic analysis revealed a high degree of similarity between CaSRs and their homologous proteins in other plants.

title: The impact of social participation on activities of daily living in older adults with knee osteoarthritis: the chain mediating effects of sleep quality and multidimensional frailty
creator: Huiqiong Tu, Tingting Zhao, Lan Chen, Yanyan Ling, Yelin Zhang, Jianling Wei, Xiaomeng Liang, Li Zhou, Yushi Liu
description: IntroductionThis study aimed to investigate the associations among social participation, sleep quality, multidimensional frailty, and activities of daily living (ADL) in older adults with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), and to further evaluate whether sleep quality and frailty jointly mediate these relationships.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 288 older adults with KOA recruited via convenience sampling.

title: High-accuracy prediction of colorectal cancer chemotherapy efficacy using machine learning applied to gene expression data
creator: Soukaina Amniouel, Mohsin Saleet Jafri
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: FOLFOX and FOLFIRI chemotherapy are considered standard first-line treatment options for colorectal cancer (CRC). However, the criteria for selecting the appropriate treatments have not been thoroughly analyzed. Methods: A newly developed machine learning model was applied on several gene expression data from the public repository GEO database to identify molecular signatures predictive of efficacy of 5-FU based combination chemotherapy (FOLFOX and FOLFIRI) in patients with CRC.

title: Rethinking Postmigration HIV Vulnerability Through Migrant Networks and Whiteness: Race‐Conscious Conversations With Newly Arrived Asian‐Born Gay Migrants in Australia
creator: Satrio Nindyo Istiko, Allyson Mutch, Judith A. Dean, Lisa Fitzgerald
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Migrants do not only acquire HIV in their home countries; a significant proportion acquire HIV postmigration. Newly arrived Asian‐born gay migrants in Australia have been identified as having low HIV risk but still being vulnerable to HIV. In this paper, we qualitatively examine their postmigration HIV vulnerability embedded within migrant networks, drawing from race‐conscious conversations with 11 newly arrived Asian‐born gay migrants in Queensland.

title: Editorial: Aquatic photosynthetic organisms under global change
creator: Justine Marchand, Benoît Schoefs
description: anisms, including phototrophs. Their diversity is also great with anoxygenic and oxygenic bacteria, and unicellular and multicellular eukaryotes, including some flowering plants. For example, the number of identified alga species lies in the range of 40–60,000 (Guiry, 2024), a number that increases annually (e.g., Schoefs et al., 2020; Morin et al., 2025).

title: Development and application of an amplified luminescent proximity homogeneous assay-linked immunosorbent assay for the accurate quantification of kidney injury molecule-1
creator: Yulin Fu, Danqin Sun, Yuan Qin, Tianyu Zheng, Zixuan Zhou, Xiumei Zhou, Xueqin Zhao, Yan Xu, Biao Huang
description: Background: Kidney injury molecule-1 (Kim-1), a specific marker of kidney injury, is usually not expressed in normal kidneys or at very low levels but is highly expressed in injured renal tubular epithelial cells until the damaged cells recover completely. Therefore, we aimed to develop an efficient and highly sensitive assay to accurately quantify Kim-1 levels in human serum and urine.

title: A Clinical Study of Decellularized Tissue Engineering Hyaline Cartilage Graft (dLhCG) for Articular Cartilage Repair
creator: Zhen Zhang, Gong Cheng, Wenyong Fei, Qiuzhen Liang, Liang Zhang, Kegui Liu, Jihang Dai, Bo Cong, Xu Hu, Zhonglian Wu, Jialu Zhang, Jinlan Cui, Hang Yao, Dong‐An Wang, Jingcheng Wang, Tao Sun, Jiang Zheng
description: Current clinical approaches for knee cartilage repair are often limited by hypertrophy and fibrosis in the regenerated tissues. A decellularized tissue‐engineered hyaline cartilage graft (dLhCG), composed of a type II collagen‐based extracellular matrix, has been developed to overcome this limitation. Extensive preclinical studies have demonstrated the ability of dLhCG to achieve hyaline cartilage repair and maintain a stable hyaline phenotype.

title: CircACVR2A(2–4) regulates stem cell pluripotency by uncoupling CDK-activating kinase functions
creator: Stuart Webb, Vanessa M Conn, Eljo Yvette van Battum, Kirsty Kirk, Ashleigh B Geiger, Suman Singh, Marta Gabryelska, Michael J Roach, Shashikanth Marri, He Lin, Ryan Liu, Jordyn Binelli, John Toubia, Jenne Tran, Alex D Colella, Thomas Colunga, Michael Kulik, Cedric Bardy, Lachlan Jolly, R Jeroen Past
description: Differentiation of stem cells is driven by tightly coordinated transcriptional programs, yet the contribution of circular RNAs (circRNAs) to lineage specification remains poorly defined. Here, we profiled circRNA and messenger RNA expression during differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into five germ layer–derived lineages.

title: Double-base deletions and signatures associated with platinum adducts in metastatic cancer
creator: Marcel Smid, Lotte van Leeuwen, Saskia M Wilting, John W M Martens
description: Platinum compounds preferably create intrastrand G-G adducts to halt replication in cancer cells. When successfully bypassed, resulting somatic variants end up in the genome. Unexpectedly, current double-base substitution signatures associated with platinum lack a GG component, and we hypothesized that deletion was missing from the possible solutions to circumvent a double-base lesion.

title: Fast, flexible gene cluster family delineation with IGUA
creator: Martin Larralde, Josefin Blom, Hadrien Gourlé, Hale-Seda Radoykova, Lucas Paoli, Georg Zeller, Laura M Carroll
description: Prokaryotic genomes harbor a variety of functional elements encoded as contiguous multi-gene clusters. To identify homologous gene clusters, computational tools that account for multi-gene architectures are needed to group gene clusters into Gene Cluster Families (GCFs). However, existing GCF delineation methods do not scale well to large datasets and are often limited to certain subclasses of gene clusters.

title: M2 macrophage infiltration drives tumor progression and identifies a multigene prognostic signature in esophageal cancer
creator: Guangxia Wei, Chunlin Ye, Yunhe Huang, Zan Luo, Bin Xu, Junyu Li
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to elucidate the mechanistic role of M2 tumor-associated macrophages in esophageal cancer (EC) progression and to construct an M2 macrophage–related gene signature for prognostic prediction.MethodsIntegrated analyses of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and bulk RNA-seq data of EC were performed. scRNA-seq data were processed with Seurat and annotated using SingleR. Immune infiltration was evaluated through ssGSEA and CIBERSORT.

title: Validation of the digital health literacy assessment among the university students in China
creator: Limei Nie, Jiajia Zhao, Lutong Pan, Mingli Pang, Jieru Wang, Yue Zhou, Rui Chen, Hui Liu, Xixing Xu, Baochen Su, Fanlei Kong
description: PurposeWith the development of the internet, digital health literacy (DHL) has become increasingly important for managing health. Consequently, various digital health literacy scales have been created for different groups. The purpose of this study was to verify the reliability and validity of the simplified Chinese version of the Digital Health Literacy Assessment (DHLA) scale among university students in China.

title: The ubiquitin–proteasome system and proteostasis in the cochlea and sensorineural hearing disorders
creator: Yiming Zhong, Bing Kong, Jinju Xu, Weiyi Huang, Yi Pan, Yuenan Liu, Mingliang Xiang, Bin Ye, Yilin Shen
description: The ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS) is the major machinery for intracellular protein degradation, playing an indispensable role in maintaining proteostasis across all tissues. Sensorineural hearing loss affects billions of people worldwide and is characterized by the irreversible degeneration of cochlear hair cells and spiral ganglion neurons. However, effective treatments remain unavailable.

title: Personality and help-seeking for psychological distress: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Anna Szücs, Rachel Hui Xin Lam, Wymann Shao Wen Tang, Lifan Zhou, Monica Lazarus, Andrea B. Maier, Jose M. Valderas
description: IntroductionThe effective management of depression, anxiety, and other forms of psychological distress depends on individuals’ readiness to seek and accept help for their mental suffering. Understanding which personality traits relate to help-seeking can help better tailor mental healthcare to individual needs. However, findings regarding associations of personality traits with help-seeking have been inconsistent.

title: Investigation Into the Effectiveness of Community Water Fluoridation and Dental Caries Experience in 4‐Year‐Old Aotearoa New Zealand Children: A National Repeated Cross‐Sectional Study From 2010 to 2022
creator: Tim Chambers, Philip J. Schluter, Frank Dean, Matt Hobbs, Jonathan Broadbent
description: ObjectivesTo provide contemporary national evidence on the effectiveness of community water fluoridation (CWF) for the prevention of early childhood caries (ECC) among 4‐year‐old children in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), and to examine potential effect modification by ethnicity and other sociodemographic characteristics.MethodsA national repeated cross‐sectional study was conducted using routinely collected B4 School Check data (2010–2022).

title: Interleukin-15 and innate effector cells as predictors of outcome in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation
creator: Marie Warny, Sisse Rye Ostrowski, Søren Lykke Petersen, Lone Smidstrup Friis, Brian Thomas Kornblit, Niels Smedegaard Andersen, Ida Schjødt, Margit Hørup Larsen, Janne Amstrup Møller, Eva Kannik Haastrup, Henrik Sengeløv, Lia Minculescu
description: IntroductionImmune reconstitution is a critical parameter in successful hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) and involves different cell types and a microenvironment including cytokines. Natural killer (NK) cells and γδ T cells are known to repopulate early after HCT and are proposed to have the intriguing capacity of mediating graft-versus-leukemia (GVL) effects without accompanying graft-versus-host-disease (GVHD).
