title: Leader’s Machiavellianism and employees’ counterproductive work behavior: testing a moderated mediation model
creator: Han Cai, Le Wang, Xiu Jin
description: Counterproductive work behavior wastes organizational resources and significantly damages organizational development. The importance of employees’ counterproductive work behaviors in organizations is becoming increasingly obvious. This is directly related to the sustainable development and survival of organizations. This study believes that employee’s behavior is closely related to leadership style.

title: Schizophrenia-associated glycoprotein Adamtsl3 regulates perineuronal net formation, maintenance, and adult cortical plasticity
creator: Teresa M L Cramer, Saad B Hannan, Lucie Petre, Mark F Bear, Takao K Hensch, Shiva K Tyagarajan
description: Perineuronal nets (PNNs) regulate the maturation of parvalbumin-positive (PV+) interneurons during postnatal critical periods and continue to support their function thereafter. Their disruption is implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, yet key endogenous PNN regulators remain unknown. Here, we identify the schizophrenia-associated glycoprotein Adamtsl3 as a PV+ cell-autonomous regulator of PNN integrity.

title: Infrared spectroscopy with statistical analysis and machine learning for cancer risk assessment in inflammatory bowel disease patients
creator: Eric Kumi-Barimah, Raneem Toman, Animesh Jha, Sharib Ali, Venkataraman Subramanian
description: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergo regular colonoscopic surveillance due to their elevated risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC). However, current clinical, endoscopic and histopathological risk stratification methods can be limited in sensitivity and objectivity, highlighting the need for complementary molecular approaches.

title: Performance prediction equation for the Valencia Marathon based on time and pacing in the half marathon
creator: Fran Oficial-Casado, Jose Ignacio Priego-Quesada, Pedro Pérez-Soriano
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionAlthough pacing is a variable that affects marathon running performance, there is a lack of studies that assessed whether it can improve performance prediction. The aim was to calculate a linear regression model with data such as the half marathon race time, age category, sex and pacing range (difference between the maximum and minimum relative speed of the half marathon) to predict the marathon time.

title: A dosimetric comparison of non-coplanar volumetric modulated arc therapy and non-coplanar fixed field intensity modulated radiation therapy in hippocampus-avoidance whole-brain radiation therapy with a simultaneous integrated boost for brain metastases
creator: Huaqu Zeng, MinZhi Zhong, Zongyou Chen, Shukui Tang, Zunbei Wen
description: ObjectiveThe aim of this study was to investigate the dosimetric differences between non-coplanar volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) and non-coplanar fixed-field intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) in hippocampus-avoidance whole-brain radiation therapy with a simultaneous integrated boost (HA-WBRT+SIB) for brain metastases using the Monaco treatment planning system (TPS).MethodA total of 22 patients with brain metastases were retrospectively enrolled.

title: The emerging role of subchondral bone homeostasis in osteoarthritis
creator: Antonia Donat, Weixin Xie, Assil-Ramin Alimy, Anke Baranowsky, Tim Rolvien, Johannes Keller
description: The treatment of progressive articular cartilage degeneration and consequent joint deterioration, also known as osteoarthritis (OA), remains a major challenge in musculoskeletal medicine. The subchondral bone has become a key area of research, as early alterations in bone remodelling and structure may precede cartilage degeneration and contribute to disease initiation and progression.

title: Potential molecular links between triclosan exposure and osteoarthritis: An integrative systems toxicology study
creator: Xijie Tang, Haijia Xu, Xiangzhong Liu, Yi Yang, Zhanghua Li
description: SummaryOsteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. Triclosan (TCS), a commonly used antimicrobial compound, has been linked to oxidative and immune disturbances; however, its molecular relevance to OA remains to be elucidated.

title: How to achieve low-carbon development in China: spatial spillover of education on carbon intensity
creator: Congying Ma, Hongchao Wu
description: IntroductionWith the looming global warming crisis, the question of how to achieve carbon neutrality is becoming an important issue confronting many countries. Although the spatial studies have indicated that education can spatially reduce the carbon intensity, they have ignored the transmission mechanism and dynamic interrelationship between education and carbon intensity.

title: A triple-masked, two-center, randomized parallel clinical trial to assess the superiority of eight weeks of grape seed flour supplementation against placebo for weight loss attenuation during perioperative period in patients with cachexia associated with colorectal cancer: a study protocol
creator: Felipe Aguiar Pupo Seabra Malta, Daniela Caetano Gonçalves
description: BackgroundProgressive, involuntary weight and lean mass loss in cancer are linked to cachexia, a prevalent syndrome in gastrointestinal malignancies that impacts quality of life, survival and postoperative complications. Its pathophysiology is complex and believed to involve proinflammatory cytokine-mediated systemic inflammation resulting from tumor-host interaction, oxidative stress, abnormal metabolism and neuroendocrine changes.

title: Quantitative systems pharmacology modeling of class I–III BRAF-mutant NSCLC enables subgroup treatment analysis and combination therapy design
creator: Jingjing Hu, Qi Rao, Zichun Li, Geli Li, Zhenle Bi, Danyi Wen, Chen Zhao, Guohua Zhou
description: SummaryBRAF-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) comprises three functional classes (I–III) with distinct driving mechanisms, yet effective therapies for classes II and III remain limited. To address this, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model that mechanistically recapitulates signaling networks and drug responses across all three classes, integrating multiscale preclinical-to-clinical datasets.

title: Outcomes of Simultaneous Three- or Four-Horizontal Muscle Surgery for Very Large-Angle Convergence Insufficiency-Type and Basic-Type Exotropia
creator: Ayaka Yagasaki, Teiji Yagasaki, Kazuo Ichikawa
description: PurposeWe investigated the outcomes of simultaneous three- or four-horizontal muscle surgery for very large-angle exotropia (> 60 prism diopters [Δ]).Subjects and MethodsThis retrospective study included 24 patients (16 with convergence insufficiency-type and 8 with basic-type exotropia). The deviation angle was measured using the alternate prism and cover test, and stereopsis was evaluated.

title: Commentary: Is obesity associated with taste alterations? a systematic review
creator: Marco Alessandrini, Alessandra Vezzoli, Simona Mrakic-Sposta, Sandro Malacrida, Alessandro Micarelli
description: ring the burdening of the obesity outbreak (2) and the works pointed to reduce the epidemic have almost failed (3). Emerging results highlighted that the taste system – together with the smell – could be engaged in diverse metabolic processes (for example appetite control and energy homeostasis) possibly influencing body weight and health (4, 5).

title: How to Interpret Needle EMG Study
creator: Gabriela Figueiredo Pucci, Jonathan Minkis, Marcus V. Pinto, Aaron S. Zelikovich
description: is the study of the motor unit action potentials (muscle contracted). Step 3 involves identification of patterns and localization, with the conjunction with NCS (Figure 2). Step 4 is the identification of the time course to better characterize the abnormalities previously seen.

title: Multi-omics approaches to studying gastrointestinal microbiome in the context of precision medicine and machine learning
creator: Jingyue Wu, Stephanie S. Singleton, Urnisha Bhuiyan, Lori Krammer, Raja Mazumder
description: The human gastrointestinal (gut) microbiome plays a critical role in maintaining host health and has been increasingly recognized as an important factor in precision medicine. High-throughput sequencing technologies have revolutionized -omics data generation, facilitating the characterization of the human gut microbiome with exceptional resolution.

title: RNA thermometers as temperature-dependent tools for enhanced recombinant protein production in precision fermentation
creator: Christina Peternell, Philipp Noll, Marius Henkel
description: BackgroundPrecision fermentation is a key technology for the future sustainable production of food proteins, bulk ingredients, and high-value recombinant products. However, process efficiency is often limited by the coupling of biomass formation and recombinant protein synthesis, leading to substantial carbon losses into non-recyclable biomass.

title: Comment on “EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation”
creator: Alessandra Tedeschi, Raul Cordoba, Alessandra Ferrajoli, George Follows, Anna Maria Frustaci, Anne Sophie Michallet, Talha Munir, Susan O'Brien, John F Seymour, Tait Shanafelt, Clemens Martin Wendtner, Pier Luigi Zinzani, Stephan Stilgenbauer
description: ransformation have recently been published in HemaSphere, following the previous versions developed under the auspices of the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO). 1 The authors have made a substantial effort to comprehensively outline the management of CLL, encompassing diagnosis, active surveillance, supportive care, and treatment.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing and AlphaFold 3 insights into cytokine signaling and its role in uveal melanoma
creator: Hongyan Sun, Cunzi Li, Zuhui Pu, Ying Lu, Zijing Wu, Lan Zhou, Hongzhan Lin, Yumo Wang, Tao Zi, Lisha Mou, Ming-ming Yang
description: BackgroundUveal melanoma (UVM) is a form of eye cancer with a poor prognosis, particularly in metastatic patients. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular heterogeneity within UVM and identify prognostic biomarkers.MethodsWe performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on primary and metastatic UVM samples.

title: Loop closure detection of visual SLAM based on variational autoencoder
creator: Shibin Song, Fengjie Yu, Xiaojie Jiang, Jie Zhu, Weihao Cheng, Xiao Fang
description: Loop closure detection is an important module for simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Correct detection of loops can reduce the cumulative drift in positioning. Because traditional detection methods rely on handicraft features, false positive detections can occur when the environment changes, resulting in incorrect estimates and an inability to obtain accurate maps.

title: Structural basis of an endoplasmic reticulum EMC:Spf1 insertase–dislocase complex
creator: Carolin J. Klose, J. Rajan Prabu, Emma J. Fenech, Bastian Bräuning, Ida Baydar, Barbara Steigenberger, Susanne von Gronau, Sivan Arad, Christine R. Langlois, Maya Schuldiner, Brenda A. Schulman, Matthias J. Feige
description: Most eukaryotic membrane proteins are inserted into the membrane at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This essential process relies on molecular quality control machineries to prevent mistargeting and incorrect structure formation. Here, we show that the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) forms an evolutionarily conserved supercomplex with the P5A-ATPase Spf1/ATP13A1.

title: Research progress of vascularization strategies of tissue-engineered bone
creator: Nanning Lv, Zhangzhe Zhou, Mingzhuang Hou, Lihui Hong, Hongye Li, Zhonglai Qian, Xuzhu Gao, Mingming Liu
description: The bone defect caused by fracture, bone tumor, infection, and other causes is not only a problematic point in clinical treatment but also one of the hot issues in current research. The development of bone tissue engineering provides a new way to repair bone defects. Many animal experimental and rising clinical application studies have shown their excellent application prospects.

title: Transcriptome-wide identification of the WUSCHEL-related homeobox transcription factors and their expression patterns underlying drought and salt stress in Populus euphratica
creator: Boniface Ndayambaza, Jianhua Si, Xin Zhao, Yingxue Zhao, Dongmeng Zhou, Bing Jia, Zijin Liu, Xue Bai, Boyang Wang
description: Drought and salinity are major abiotic stresses that severely affect plant growth and the productivity of woody plants. The WUSCHEL-related homeobox (WOX) transcription factors are central to the regulation of plant development and plant stress responses, yet their roles in the stress-resilient desert tree Populus euphratica remain unexplored.

title: Computed Tomographic Features Associated with Pulmonary Melioidosis versus Pulmonary Tuberculosis in Diabetic Patients: A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study
creator: Nitin Gupta, Chiranjay Mukhopadhyay, Tirlangi Praveen Kumar, Kavita Salian, Priya P. S., Sundeep Malla, Rahul Magazine, Steven Van Den Broucke, Erika Vlieghe, Emmanuel Bottieau
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). .Pulmonary melioidosis is frequently mistaken for pulmonary tuberculosis because of overlapping clinical and radiological features, often delaying appropriate treatment. We conducted a retrospective comparative cohort study at a tertiary care center in southern India between January 2018 and August 2025 to compare chest computed tomography (CT) features of microbiologically confirmed melioidosis and tuberculosis in diabetic adults who underwent CT within 30 days of symptom onset. A total of 151 patients were included: 46 with melioidosis and 105 with tuberculosis.

title: Genome-wide identification of TPS and TPP genes in cultivated peanut (Arachis hypogaea) and functional characterization of AhTPS9 in response to cold stress
creator: Chao Zhong, Zehua He, Yu Liu, Zhao Li, Xiaoguang Wang, Chunji Jiang, Shuli Kang, Xibo Liu, Shuli Zhao, Jing Wang, He Zhang, Xinhua Zhao, Haiqiu Yu
description: IntroductionTrehalose is vital for plant metabolism, growth, and stress resilience, relying on Trehalose-6-phosphate synthase (TPS) and Trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase (TPP) genes. Research on these genes in cultivated peanuts (Arachis hypogaea) is limited.MethodsThis study employed bioinformatics to identify and analyze AhTPS and AhTPP genes in cultivated peanuts, with subsequent experimental validation of AhTPS9’s role in cold tolerance.

title: Swine influenza A replicon particle and live attenuated influenza virus vaccines induce differential systemic and mucosal antibody and T cell responses
creator: Meghan Wymore Brand, Bryan S. Kaplan, Carine K. Souza, Jayne E. Wiarda, J. Brian Kimble, Bailey Arruda, Daniel R. Perez, Amy L. Baker
description: Influenza A virus (IAV) in swine is a significant economic concern, and there is a critical need to improve vaccine efficacy. Commercial and experimental vaccine platforms are effective against homologous infection but may not reliably provide protection against drifted or heterologous viruses.

title: Life-Threatening Ventricular Tachycardia and Transient Brugada-Like Electrocardiographic Abnormalities Caused by Severe Hyperkalemia Due to Urinary Retention in a 55-Year-Old Man
creator: Yoshiyasu Aizawa, Tomoko S. Kato, Akio Kawamura
description: Patient: Male, 55-year-old Final Diagnosis: Acute kidney injury • hyperkalemia • urinary retention • ventricular tachycardia Symptoms: Diaphoresis • dyspnea • palpitations Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Cardiology Objective: Unusual clinical course BackgroundHyperkalemia is a potentially fatal electrolyte disturbance that typically manifests as progressive conduction abnormalities, bradyarrhythmias, and sine-wave electrocardiographic changes.

title: Nurturing positive mental health and wellbeing in educational settings – the PRICES model
creator: Tyralynn Frazier, Sebrina L. Doyle Fosco
description: This article presents a comprehensive framework for the implementation of social and emotional learning (SEL) programs as a means of health promotion in educational settings, to positively impact student, school, and adult mental health and wellbeing across education. It emphasizes the profound impact of education on life trajectories and success definitions.

title: Family factors associated with dental caries among 5-year-old preschool children
creator: Giovanna Torqueto Castilho, Marília Narducci Pessoa, Caroline Correa de Oliveira, Letícia Santos Alves de Melo, Elaine Pereira Silva Tagliaferro, Vanessa Pardi
description: BackgroundAlthough dental caries is largely preventable, it remains highly prevalent among children.AimEvaluate family factors associated with the prevalence of dental caries in 5-year-old children.DesignThis cross-sectional study recruited 5-year-old children from public preschools in Araraquara, São Paulo, Brazil. Data on sociodemographic factors, family routines, and oral health practices were gathered via a self-administered questionnaire completed independently by caregivers.

title: Automated thigh muscle segmentation using foundation models: validation and impact of segmentation quality
creator: Katharina Ziegeler, Gabrielle Hoyer, Felix Liu, Virginie Kreutzinger, Zehra Akkaya, Gabby B Joseph, John A Lynch, Valentina Pedoia, Sharmila Majumdar, Thomas M Link
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis study aimed to validate a segmentation pipeline for the extraction of volumetric thigh muscle data, investigate the influence of demographics on segmentation performance, and investigate the influence of low-quality segmentations on quantitative performance and downstream metrics.Materials and methodsManual thigh muscle segmentations on axial T1-weighted spin echo thigh images of 364 (106 training and validation; 258 testing) participants of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) were used.

title: Multidimensional analysis of conventional and electronic cigarette consumption among students
creator: Carmen Maria Țîru, Claudiu Coman, Costel Marian Dalban, Vlad Bătrânu-Pințea, Mihail Anton, Vasile Gherheș, Daniel-Rareș Obadă, Adrian Otovescu
description: IntroductionCigarette consumption among university students remains a complex public health issue, encompassing both conventional and electronic products. This study investigates the multidimensional aspects of cigarette use among young adults, with a particular focus on psychosocial, perceptual, and behavioral determinants influencing nicotine consumption.MethodsA quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed.

title: Reproducibility and diagnostic performance of ADC for assessing response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multi-ROI comparison analysis from the phase-Ib NABUCCO trial
creator: Joyce Greidanus, Carlotta Bernabei, Kalina Chupetvloska, Georgios Agrotis, Laura S. Mertens, Bas W. G. van Rhijn, Henk G. van der Poel, Michiel S. van der Heijden, Regina G. H. Beets-Tan, Andrea Delli Pizzi, Thierry N. Boellaard, Stefano Trebeschi
description: ObjectiveMRI is increasingly used to assess treatment response in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but only qualitatively. This study evaluates the reproducibility and predictive value of quantitative apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), thought to be a non-invasive surrogate for tumor cell density, in patients with MIBC receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy.

title: Multitarget Drug Design for Cardiovascular Disease: Bridging Chemistry and Medicine
creator: Gyuzel Y. Mitronova, Vladimir N. Belov, Constanze Schmidt, Stephan E. Lehnart
description: This review provides an overview of recent advances in the development of multitarget drugs (MTDs) for cardiac diseases, with a particular focus on emerging molecular scaffolds and their pharmacological properties. We discuss the fundamental principles of cardiac polypharmacology and multitarget drug design, highlighting key compound classes, such as 1,4‐benzothiazepines, 1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs), and polyphenol derivatives.

title: The Anomalously High Boiling Point of Water Revisited
creator: Lucas de Azevedo Santos, Siebe Lekanne Deprez, F Matthias Bickelhaupt, Célia Fonseca Guerra
description: Typically, boiling points increase with molecular weight because dispersion forces strengthen. However, H2O deviates from this trend, exhibiting a higher boiling point than its heavier group‐16 analogs. This anomaly is traditionally attributed to water’s larger dipole moment, which is thought to promote stronger electrostatic intermolecular hydrogen bonds. Yet, this textbook explanation lacks quantitative support.

title: Magnet Recognition, Leadership Responsiveness, and Nurse Moral Distress: A Multilevel Mediation Analysis
creator: Hyunmin Yu, Daniel McNeish, Celsea Tibbitt, Christin Iroegbu, Matthew D. McHugh
description: PurposeMoral distress is a pervasive challenge in nursing and has been associated with burnout, job dissatisfaction, and turnover. Although Magnet Recognition has been associated with more favorable nursing practice environments and nurse outcomes, little is known about the association between Magnet status and nurses' experiences of moral distress or the role of leadership responsiveness in this association.

title: Clinical, epidemiological, and drug resistance insights into HIV-positive patients in Meizhou, China
creator: Xianhui Liu, Sandip Patil, Xuemin Guo, Feiqiu Wen, Xianyan Zhang, Zhixiong Zhong, Xinlu Wang
description: The acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) epidemic, resulting from human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, exhibits distinct regional characteristics. This study undertakes a retrospective analysis of the epidemiological and clinical features of 195 HIV-positive cases in Meizhou, China, from May 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019. Western blotting (WB) confirmed and assessed these cases.

title: Liraglutide Dose Affordability and Durability in Real‐World Obesity Care
creator: Azhar Zafar, Carina Scarlata
description: ch 3.0 mg cited medication cost. Affordability is therefore a system‐level determinant of dose attainment, treatment continuity and real‐world effectiveness. Obesity care must consider whether a sustainable dose can be achieved and maintained, not simply whether treatment is effective at the target dose. Cost‐limited dosing risks inequitable treatment intensity based on ability to pay rather than clinical need.

title: Coulomb force-guided deep reinforcement learning for effective and explainable robotic motion planning
creator: Sirui Song, Trevor Bihl, Jundong Liu
description: Training mobile robots through digital twins with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has gained increasing attention to ensure efficient and safe navigation in complex environments. In this paper, we propose a novel physics-inspired DRL framework that achieves both effective and explainable motion planning. We represent the robot, destination, and obstacles as electrical charges and model their interactions using Coulomb forces.

title: Health and care workforce-driven transformations can improve workforce stability and strengthen health system resilience
creator: Ellen Kuhlmann, Gabriela Lotta, André Beja, Viola Burau, Olga Gershuni, Zuzana Kotherová, Klaas Stek, Marius-Ionuț Ungureanu, Tiago Correia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). strategy is still lacking in most European countries. In this situation, workforce-driven stability and resilience may emerge bottom-up. However, these capacities are not well understood by health policy. Instead, health and care workers are mostly perceived as critical infrastructure and as a cost factor for health systems, obscuring the view of both the needs of individual health workers and their active role in health systems.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists for the management of diabetic peripheral neuropathy
creator: Chunyan Liu, Tianqiang Wu, Na Ren
description: Diabetes mellitus is a prevalent chronic disease characterized by hyperglycemia. Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is one of the complications of diabetes mellitus and is caused by neuron injury induced by hyperglycemic circumstances. The incidence of DPN varies among different countries and regions, ranging from nearly 20% to over 70%.

title: Pathogenesis and signaling pathways related to iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer
creator: Simeng Zhao, Yuejia Zhao, Yongfu Zhao, Guangzhi Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Thyroid cancer is the most common malignant neoplasm within the endocrine system and the field of head and neck surgery. Although the majority of thyroid cancers, more than 90%, are well-differentiated thyroid carcinomas with a favourable prognosis, the escalating incidence of this disease has contributed to an increasing number of patients with a propensity for recurrent disease, rapid disease progression, and poor or no response to conventional treatments.

title: Racial Discrimination, School Climate, and Black Adolescents' Internalizing and Externalizing Behaviors: A Longitudinal Moderation
creator: E Cole Green, Jia Yan, Jasmine N Coleman, Elizabeth I Johnson
description: Using data from Black adolescents in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study (n = 1,316), we examined the moderating effect of school climate on the relationship between racial discrimination and later internalizing and externalizing behaviors during adolescence (M age = 12.00; SD = 0.65).

title: Zika virus infection disturbs development of human muscle progenitor cells
creator: Cássia Rocha, Daniella Arêas Mendes-da-Cruz, Elisa Negroni, Vincent Mouly, Ieda Pereira Ribeiro, Myrna Cristina Bonaldo, Wilson Savino, Vinicius Cotta-de-Almeida, Dumith Chequer Bou-Habib, Ingo Riederer
description: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection has emerged as a global public health emergency due to its expansion capacity and ability to cause neurological and congenital diseases. Muscle cells are targets for ZIKV, and myalgia and muscle disorders are frequently related symptoms during infection.

title: Development and validation of a clinical prediction model of fertilization failure during routine IVF cycles
creator: Liu Xingnan, Zhang Na
description: PurposeThis study aims to create and validate a clinical model that predict the probability of fertilization failure in routine in-vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles.MethodsThis study employed a retrospective methodology, gathering data from 1770 couples that used reproductive center’s of the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University standard IVF fertilization between June 2015 and June 2023.

title: Identification and functional characterization of the RPP13 gene family in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) for disease resistance
creator: Baoqi Yuan, Chuang Li, Qingfeng Wang, Qi Yao, Xiaowei Guo, Yuhang Zhang, Zhongwei Wang
description: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), as the world’s fourth largest food crop, plays a crucial role in ensuring food security through its disease resistance. The RPP13 gene family is known to play a pivotal role in plant disease resistance responses; however, its specific functions in potato remain unclear.

title: The Use of Cannabidiol in Cutaneous Wound Healing: A Systematic Review
creator: João Henrique Ferreira França, Renale Beserra de Melo Freitas, Geovanne Lucas Rodrigues Rosendo, Mariana Pereira Carvalho, Glicia Maria de Oliveira, Júlio César Claudino dos Santos, Fernanda das Chagas Angelo Mendes Tenorio, Jaiurte Gomes Martins da Silva
description: Cutaneous wounds represent a significant health problem due to their high prevalence, functional impact, and effects on quality of life. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non‐psychoactive compound derived from Cannabis sativa , has been investigated for its anti‐inflammatory, antioxidant, and regenerative properties, suggesting potential therapeutic applications in wound healing.

title: Enhancing particle swarm optimization based on optical computing mechanism: application to dyslexia detection
creator: Nermine Mahmoud, Mohamed Abd Elaziz, Abdelghani Dahou, Mohammad Ghatasheh, Ibrahim A. Fares, Mohammed Azmi Al-Betar, Ahmed A. Ewees
description: IntroductionThis study presents a modified version of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) using an all-optical computational update mechanism. The primary innovation and objective of this collaboration aimed to leverage the inherent properties of coherent optical systems, including specialized complex-domain computation and nonlinear light-matter interactions, to enhance the exploration and exploitation of the search space process for particles.

title: Portfolio management based on value distribution reinforcement learning algorithm
creator: Yan Yang, Tian Wang, Yiding Fu, Jingna Huang, Dong Zhou
description: IntroductionIn the face of high uncertainty and complexity in financial markets, achieving portfolio return maximization while effectively controlling risk remains a critical challenge.MethodsWe propose a novel portfolio management framework based on the value distribution maximum entropy actor-critic (VD-MEAC) reinforcement learning algorithm. We establish a framework where the agent’s actions represent portfolio weight adjustments and stock factors serve as state observations.

title: A Single Exercise Session Elicits a Transient Kynurenine Metabolic Signature in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
creator: Marcus Vinicius dos Santos Rangel, Gabriela Andrade Paz, Maria das Graças C Souza, Marie Kupjetz, Tiffany Y Wences Chirino, Philipp Zimmer, Paulo Farinatti, Juliana Pereira Borges
description: Tryptophan (TRP) is primarily metabolized via the kynurenine (KYN) pathway, which plays a central role in energy homeostasis, as well as immune, inflammatory, and neurobiological regulation. Although a single exercise session may modulate this pathway, the magnitude and consistency of these responses remain unclear. Therefore, this meta‐analysis aimed to synthesize acute exercise–induced changes in KYN pathway metabolites.

title: Dietary change revealed in kitchen refuse pits from the ancient floors of Housepit 54, K'etxelknáz (Bridge River Site), British Columbia
creator: Anna Marie Prentiss, Ashley Hampton, Jeannie Larmon, Megan Denis, Thomas A. Foor, Haley O'Brien, Nathan Goodale, Matthew J. Walsh, Alysha Edwards, Joshua Jack, Ethan Ryan
description: IntroductionDietary change in traditional fishing and foraging societies has been examined from standpoints of resource accessibility, population demands, and social needs. Typically, scholars focus on singular models to explain diet choice including those from optimal foraging theory, socio-ecology, and political and historical ecology.

title: What contributes to the long-term implementation of an evidence-based early childhood intervention: a qualitative study from Germany
creator: Marie Lisanne Schepan, Tanja Jungmann, Sören Kliem, Carolin Siegert, Malte Sandner, Tilman Brand
description: BackgroundRigorous research trials have demonstrated that early childhood interventions can reach socially disadvantaged families and can have a lasting impact on the healthy development of their children. However, little is known about the internal and contextual factors that contribute to the long-term implementation of such interventions. In this study, we investigated the development of the home visiting program Pro Kind.

title: A mouse model of immunosuppression facilitates oral Candida albicans biofilms, bacterial dysbiosis and dissemination of infection
creator: Raja Veerapandian, Anuja Paudyal, Sarah M. Schneider, Sonny T. M. Lee, Govindsamy Vediyappan
description: Opportunistic pathogens are a major threat to people, especially those with impaired immune systems. Two of the most important microbes in this category are the fungus Candida albicans and Gram-positive bacteria of the genus Enterococcus, which share overlapping niches in the oral cavity, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts. title: Diagnostic challenge of pulmonary embolism during testosterone replacement therapy for primary hypogonadism
creator: Hamza El Hadi, Silke Dorothea Hölscher, Jonel Trebicka, Elena Vorona
description: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is widely used in the management of male hypogonadism to restore physiological androgen levels and improve related symptoms. Although generally considered safe under appropriate monitoring, its association with pulmonary embolism (PE) remains controversial. We report a case of a 50-year-old man who independently and progressively shortened testosterone injection intervals due to recurrent hypogonadal symptoms.

title: Association of reproductive factors with acute myocardial infarction in young women: A VIRGO and NHANES case-control study
creator: Weilai Dong, Huanhuan Yang, Mitsuaki Sawano, Shu-Xia Li, Xiao Xu, Karthik Murugiah, Harlan M. Krumholz, Yuan Lu
description: ObjectiveYoung women with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) often present with distinct risk profiles compared with older women and men, but the role of reproductive factors remains poorly understood. This study examines associations of reproductive factors with AMI in young women.MethodsWe conducted a case-control study of 1561 women aged 18–55 years with AMI from VIRGO and age-matched controls from NHANES.

title: When anorexia nervosa conceals Cushing syndrome: a diagnostic pitfall in hypercortisolemia
creator: Miao Yunn Lim, Serena Chong, Kerry-Lee Milner
description: A 37-year-old woman presented with severe hypertension, mood changes, and weight loss (body mass index 14.6 kg/m2). She exhibited restrictive eating behaviors consistent with anorexia nervosa, alongside biochemical hypercortisolemia with serum cortisol 43.6 µg/dL (1204 nmol/L; reference range: 6.2-18.1 µg/dL; 170-500 nmol/L), 24-hour urinary free cortisol 430.3 µg/24 hours (1187 nmol/24 hours; reference range: <60.

title: The atherogenic index of plasma is associated with an increased risk of diabetes in non-obese adults: a cohort study
creator: Jun Cao, Zhaohai Su, Jiangyong Yang, Bilong Zhang, Rengui Jiang, Weiling Lu, Zhenhua Huang, Zheng Xie
description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the relationship between the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and diabetes risk in Chinese non-obese adults. This is important because the incidence of diabetes is significant in non-obese populations, and evidence regarding this association is limited.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study with 82,977 Chinese non-obese adults.

title: Development, refinement, and validation of an equine musculoskeletal pain scale
creator: Ulrike Auer, Zsofia Kelemen, Claus Vogl, Stephanie von Ritgen, Rabea Haddad, Laura Torres Borda, Christopher Gabmaier, John Breteler, Florien Jenner
description: Musculoskeletal disease is a common cause of chronic pain that is often overlooked and inadequately treated, impacting the quality of life of humans and horses alike. Lameness due to musculoskeletal pain is prevalent in horses, but the perception of pain by owners is low compared with veterinary diagnosis.

title: Ultra-early follow-up computed tomography detects hematoma expansion in intracerebral hemorrhage with high accuracy
creator: Jawed Nawabi, Kira Koch, Andrea Dell’Orco, Andrea Morotti, Georg Bohner, Michael Scheel, Eugen Schwabauer, Joachim E. Weber, Kersten Villringer, Justus F. Kleine, Mike P. Wattjes, Horst Urbach, Heinrich Audebert, Frieder Schlunk
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ve so far failed to prove a convincing therapeutic effect (1–3). One major reason may be that the diagnostic accuracy of imaging-based predictors of HE used to select treatment-eligible patients is limited (4). Therefore, there is an unmet medical need for a diagnostic tool capable of identifying patients at high risk for further hematoma enlargement, to guide both RCTs and clinical treatment in the future.

title: Pharmacological treatment of idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis
creator: Adrianna Niksińska, Robert Kruszewski, Witold Tłustochowicz
description: Idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis (IRF) is a rare disease characterized by inflammatory infiltration around the aorta, which can lead to clinical symptoms and complications, the most common of which is ureteral obstruction, potentially resulting in secondary renal failure.A search of medical databases was conducted to compile a review article summarizing the immunosuppressive treatment options for IRF.

title: Real-world treatment utilization in adults with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy in the United States
creator: Cécile Blein, Chafic Karam, Clémence Arvin-Berod, Deborah Gelinas, Sergio Barrera-Sierra, Hashmath Ulla T. A. Syed, Charlotte Ward, Amit Goyal, Jeffrey Guptill
description: BackgroundManagement of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) is challenged by heterogeneity in severity, comorbidities, potential adverse effects, and treatment accessibility. This study aimed to elucidate treatment utilization among patients with CIDP in the United States (US) to identify potential unmet needs.MethodsAdult patients with CIDP were identified using Komodo Health’s Healthcare Map™ (January 2016–December 2020).

title: Exploring perceived barriers to palliative and end of life care provision in South-West England: bringing together the perspectives of professionals, patients, and families
creator: Gary Hodge, Gina Kallis, Tomasina M. Oh, Hannah Wheat, Susie Pearce
description: IntroductionPalliative and End of Life care (PEoLC) in the United Kingdom (UK) is increasingly being reported as inadequate. This is occurring amidst a wider backdrop of health and social care systems facing unprecedented pressure, particularly as they recover from the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Improved stacking ensemble learning based on feature selection to accurately predict warfarin dose
creator: Mingyuan Wang, Yiyi Qian, Yaodong Yang, Haobin Chen, Wei-Feng Rao
description: BackgroundWith the rapid development of artificial intelligence, prediction of warfarin dose via machine learning has received more and more attention. Since the dose prediction involve both linear and nonlinear problems, traditional machine learning algorithms are ineffective to solve such problems at one time.

title: Social determinants of health associated with newly documented opioid‐related postpartum readmissions
creator: India Perez‐Urbano, Timothy Wen, Yongmei Huang, Alexander Friedman
description: ObjectivePeripartum opioid‐related mortality has increased in recent years, and social determinants of health (SDOH) are associated with adverse maternal outcomes. We sought to identify risk factors (including SDOH risk factors) for 180‐day postpartum readmissions related to opioid use among individuals without a documented diagnosis of opioid use at delivery.

title: ZBP1 specifically binds pre-formed Z-RNA, limiting its potential pool of nucleic acid ligands compared to ADAR1
creator: Jeffrey B Krall, Lily G Beck, Parker J Nichols, Robb Welty, Quentin Vicens, Morkos A Henen, Beat Vögeli
description: ZBP1 senses foreign nucleic acids in the unusual, left-handed Z-conformation via binding through its Zα1 and Zα2 domains and initiates cell death pathways that enable viral clearance. dsDNA and dsRNA can adopt Z-conformations; however, both typically require chemical modifications or protein binding to induce Z-form conversion and stabilization.

title: Unveiling the role of SYNGR4 in breast cancer development: a novel target for immunotherapy
creator: Jie Ma, Hongtao Wang, Zhengwei Gui, Yuanrong Yang
description: IntroductionSYNGR4 is considered to be one of the causative genes for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, but its role in breast cancer development has not been revealed.MethodsThe expression of SYNGR4 in a variety of malignancies including breast cancer was analyzed using Genotype Tissue Expression (GTEx) and the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases and verified by specimens collected from our center.

title: PXL: a nucleic acid-binding module of the promyelocytic leukemia protein
creator: Daniel Fairchild, Irina V Semenova, Dane Geddes-Buehre, Yunfeng Li, Renata Szczepaniak, Sandra K Weller, Bing Hao, Irina Bezsonova
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The promyelocytic leukemia protein (PML) is a stress-response factor that assembles into PML nuclear bodies, dynamic subnuclear compartments involved in tumor suppression and antiviral defense. The most abundant isoform, PML-1, has been linked to transcriptional regulation, genome stability, and antiviral responses, yet the molecular basis of these functions remains unclear and is generally attributed to proteins associated with PML nuclear bodies. Here, we report that PML-1 itself harbors a previously structurally uncharacterized nucleic acid-binding domain.

title: PeHVA22 gene family in passion fruit (Passiflora edulis): initial characterization and expression profiling diversity
creator: Zhimin Hou, Jianxiang Liang, Xinkai Cai, Jingting Lin, Xiaomei Wang, Ruoyu Liu, Lin Lu, Gaifeng Chai, Chang An, Shengzhen Chen, Yuan Qin, Ping Zheng
description: Passion fruit, an economically valuable fruit crop, is highly vulnerable to adverse climate conditions. The HVA22 genes, recognized as abscisic acid (ABA) and stress-inducible, play vital roles in stress response and growth regulation in diverse eukaryotic organisms. Here, six HVA22 genes were firstly identified in passion fruit genome and all predicted to be localized within the endoplasmic reticulum.

title: Machine vision-enabled OD600 measurement and mass spectrometric determination of metabolites of microbial cell-containing microfluidic droplets in real-time
creator: G. Thomas Knecht, Maxwell J. Unger, Alison R. H. Narayan, Robert T. Kennedy
description: Droplet microfluidics has become a versatile tool for high-throughput phenotypic analysis of cells, employed in enzyme engineering, drug screening, and antibiotic assays. An important metric in such bioanalyses is the optical density (OD600) of the culture, but current methods for measuring OD600 within cultured droplets are limited. Herein, we present a machine-vision method for the measurement of OD600 between 0.

title: Exploring coronary microvascular dysfunction from functional impairment and structural damage
creator: Wei Wen, Yiqing Zhang, Genlin Jia, Yi Chi
description: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a syndrome characterized by myocardial ischemia resulting from structural and/or functional impairments of the coronary microvasculature, which includes pre-arterioles, arterioles, and capillaries. It has taken center stage in cardiovascular research due to its established role in triggering heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

title: A pilot randomized controlled trial of the ABCs of SLEEPING mHealth intervention for parents of school-aged children with insomnia symptoms
creator: Anastasija Jemcov, Penny Violet Corkum, Isabel M. Smith, Sean P. Mackinnon
description: IntroductionSleep is important for overall functioning; thus, parents should have access to effective sleep intervention for their children's insomnia. Mobile health interventions (mHealth) are increasingly popular partly due to their accessibility. Currently, no evidence-based sleep intervention apps are available for parents and their school-age children. Our research team developed the ABCs of SLEEPING intervention to address this gap.

title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction
creator: Ghulam Musaddaq, Labibah Ehsan, Yano Yoga, Joshua Castillo, Linda Marriott, Nicholas R. Leslie, Deborah Williamson, Thomas Tran, Chuan Kok Lim, Maïwenn Kersaudy-Kerhoas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Timely and accurate nucleic acid extraction is a critical bottleneck in point-of-care (POC) molecular diagnostics, particularly for low-abundance cell-free nucleic acids (DNA, RNA, miRNA) in plasma. We present a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device for power-free, pipette-free, nucleic acid extraction. The prototype device integrates finger-actuated valves, pump and blister reagent storage, enabling a complete, intuitive, “sample-to-eluate” workflow, including lysis, binding, washing and elution via manual actuation in approximately 35 minutes.

title: Cynaroside ameliorates TNBS-induced colitis by inhibiting intestinal epithelial cell apoptosis via the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway
creator: Ju Huang, Jing Li, Zhijun Geng, Lixia Yin, Minzhu Niu, Qingqing Li, Xinyue Liu, Xinke Cheng, Xiaofeng Zhang, Xue Song, Yueyue Wang, Lian Wang, Lugen Zuo, Jianguo Hu
description: Background and aimsPatients with Crohn’s disease (CD) exhibit excessive apoptosis of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs), which contributes to damage to the intestinal barrier structure and function, thereby playing a role in the progression of colitis. Preventing IEC apoptosis and protecting the intestinal barrier are critical to alleviating colitis.

title: EZ-SPOTs: a simple, low-cost, high-throughput liquid handling platform applied to antimicrobial susceptibility testing of clinical isolates
creator: Jon Albo, Shenghao Tan, Joee D. Denis, Rebecca Franklin-Guild, Samira Shiri, Kelsi M. Sandoz, Nate J. Cira
description: High-performance liquid handling is essential for a wide range of experiments. Previously, we introduced the Surface Patterned Omniphobic Tiles (SPOTs) platform, which enables manipulation of hundreds to thousands of independent experiments without costly equipment or excessive consumable expenses. However, the SPOTs platform uses a custom coating that requires a chemical synthesis step.

title: Clinical efficacy of electroacupuncture on pelvic floor function in women with stress urinary incontinence: a randomized sham-controlled trial protocol
creator: Shuren Ming, Jiaxin Yang, Bingli Chen, Juanjuan Li, Wenguang Hou, Yuelai Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStress urinary incontinence (SUI) is a prevalent condition among adult women, significantly impairing quality of life. Patients with SUI often exhibit abnormal pelvic floor muscle function, which can be comprehensively assessed using surface electromyography (sEMG) and transperineal ultrasound (TPUS). Electroacupuncture (EA) is an effective treatment for SUI, and multiple studies have confirmed its clinical efficacy; however, objective evidence regarding its impact on pelvic floor muscle function remains limited.

title: Heightened expression of type I interferon signaling genes in CD4+ T cells from acutely HIV-1–infected women is associated with lower viral loads
creator: Elina El-Badry, Luxiao Chen, Khader Ghneim, Ziyi Li, Kelsie Brooks, Jake Rhodes, Rafick Sekaly, William Kilembe, Susan Allen, Hao Wu, Eric Hunter
description: Sex differences play a role in the pathogenesis of a number of viral diseases. In HIV-1, several studies have reported that chronically infected women have significantly lower plasma viremia than men, although the exact mechanism by which this occurs has yet to be identified.

title: Reverse Dorr Classification of Lateral Knee Radiographs: A Qualitative Assessment of Bone Quality in Total Knee Arthroplasty
creator: Matthew A Beilfuss, Micah MacAskill, Kyle R Wagner, Diane C Krueger, Sam Mosiman, Brian T Nickel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe Dorr classification is the standard radiographic method for assessing proximal femur bone quality and guiding implant selection in total hip arthroplasty (THA); however, a similar method has not been established for total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Previous studies have demonstrated that radiographic parameters of the distal femur, specifically the ratio of the inner vs outer cortical diameter on lateral knee radiographs, are associated with bone mineral density.

title: Vision-language models for zero-shot weed detection and visual reasoning in UAV-based precision agriculture
creator: Muhammad Fahad Nasir, Mobeen Ur Rehman, Irfan Hussain
description: Weeds remain a major constraint to row-crop productivity, yet current deep learning approaches for UAV imagery often require extensive annotation, generalize poorly across fields, and provide limited interpretability. We investigate whether modern vision–language models (VLMs) can address these gaps in a zero-shot setting. Using drone images from soybean fields with ground-truth weed boxes, we evaluate six commercial VLMs, ChatGPT-4.

title: Mucin-producing urothelial-type adenocarcinoma of the prostate with a gene mutation characteristic of intestinal adenocarcinoma: case report and literature review
creator: Ao Yu, Hongbo Su, Peiling Yu, Siqi Cai, Shuaixian Mu, Jinhui Yu, Qianting Lu, Yuan Miao, Ailin Li
description: We report an elderly male with mucin-producing urothelial-type adenocarcinoma of the prostate (MPUAP) and oligometastatic lung involvement, initially diagnosed as benign prostatic hyperplasia and treated with transurethral plasma resection of the prostate (TURP). Postoperative pathology indicated mucinous adenocarcinoma, with immunohistochemistry positive for CK7, CK20, and CDX-2. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) identified genetic alterations similar to those found in intestinal adenocarcinoma.

title: A dual recombinant strategy to quantify PreS1 antibody in hepatitis B patients with genotype B or C virus by ELISA
creator: Yumin Li, Xiaoyu Wen, Jing Zhan, Tingting Cao, Xiumei Chi, Huanyi Cheng, Qingrui Huang, Wenyi Zhang, Junqi Niu, Huan Du, Zhenning Liu
description: SummaryElevated levels of anti-preS1 antibodies in patients correlate with faster hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, since preS1 is vital for viral entry. However, accurate quantification of preS1 antibodies is hindered by the variation of HBV genotypes. Herein, a quantitative preS1 antibody assay was developed for Chinese patients with predominant HBV genotypes B and C.

title: Case report: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease: unveiling a case of recurrent fever and enlarged cervical lymph nodes in a young female patient with a literature review of the immune mechanism
creator: Jia-Li Yu, Zhen Li, Bo Zhang, Ya-Nan Huang, Tian-Yu Zhao
description: The inflammatory response to viral infection is an important component of the antiviral response, a process that involves the activation and proliferation of CD8+ T, CD4+ T, and dendritic cells; thus, viral infection disrupts the immune homeostasis of the organism, leading to an increased release of inflammatory factors.

title: Response to “Interpreting bone turnover responses and treatment persistence with once-weekly teriparatide”
creator: Jiemei Gu, Qi Zhao, Xin Zhang, Zhenlin Zhang
description: d persistence, statistical methodology, and the characterization of fracture benefit. We address each in turn below, supplementing with additional background not fully elaborated in the original manuscript. Regarding bone turnover markers: monitoring and interpretation Dr. Li and colleagues note that the Week 12 P1NP in our study increased only 0.

title: “It's a good idea, but…”: a qualitative evaluation of the GoldiCare intervention in Norwegian home care services
creator: Heike Fischer, Fredrik Klæboe Lohne, Marius Steiro Fimland, Skender Elez Redzovic
description: BackgroundAddressing high levels of physical strain among Norwegian home care workers is crucial if home care services are to continue to provide cost-effective and high-quality health care for people in their homes. Excessive physical demands may contribute to poor long-term musculoskeletal health and high sick leave rates among home care workers.

title: YOLO-LitchiVar: a lightweight and high-precision detection model for fine-grained litchi variety identification
creator: Bing Xu, Xianjun Wu, Xueping Su, Wende Ke
description: Pengju Ren, Shanghai Maritime University, ChinaLitchi is a popular subtropical fruit with approximately 100 known varieties worldwide. Traditional post-harvest litchi variety classification primarily relies on manual identification, which suffers from low efficiency, strong subjectivity, and a lack of standardized systems.

title: Mechanochemical synthesis using hypervalent iodine reagents
creator: Nasser Amri, John A Murphy
description: Mechanochemical activation offers a powerful means of expanding the reactivity of hypervalent iodine reagents while advancing solvent-free synthetic methodologies. This review surveys the evolution of iodine(III) and iodine(V) chemistry in the solid state, from foundational solvent-free oxidations to mechanochemical approaches that enable efficient heterocycle construction, C–H functionalization, cascade dioxygenation, fluoroiodane-mediated fluorocyclization, and redox-initiated polymerization.

title: The establishment of dynamic microexpression training tool
creator: Jianxin Zhang, Ning Cai, Lihan Xu, Jinghua Liu, Yichen Li, Xiaodan Wang, Ming Yin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The existing microexpression training tool METT only trains the static microexpression recognition ability under neutral background, but does not train the dynamic microexpression recognition ability under expression backgrounds. Therefore, in the current study, the dynamic microexpression recognition ability test DMERT was used as pretest and posttest, the METT recognition techniques were guided and trained, and the dynamic microexpression training tool DMETT was established as a training tool for dynamic microexpression recognition ability. The experiment was conducted in 3 stages (pretest vs.

title: Synergistic Inhibition of Spinal TRPV1 Signaling by Combined Eye Acupuncture and Electroacupuncture Alleviates Inflammatory Pain in a Rat Model of Knee Osteoarthritis
creator: Shan Chen, Yinyan He, Bin Que, Zhipeng Liang, Xin Chen, Sheng Li, Rong Zhou
description: BackgroundChronic pain caused by knee osteoarthritis (KOA) remains inadequately managed by safe, non-pharmacological therapies. Although acupuncture is recommended for KOA pain by clinical guidelines, the efficacy of single-modality acupuncture remains modest, and the synergistic mechanisms of combining different acupuncture modalities are poorly understood.

title: Case report: The first case of concurrent breast myeloid sarcoma and borderline phyllodes tumor with malignant features
creator: Li Chun, Zhen Zeng, Qianyu Guo, Yangjun He
description: BackgroundMyeloid sarcoma (MS) is a rare hematological malignancy characterized by the formation of a solid mass of myeloblasts outside the bone marrow, such as in the lymph nodes, skin, or bone. MS may arise de novo or concurrently with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN), or myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS).

title: Gut-kidney-brain axis and daytime sleepiness in Parkinson's disease and chronic kidney disease: an expert narrative review
creator: Shanshan Yang, Canmin Zhu, Shihong Xiong, Xinyue Wang, Ke Cheng, Yuxin Wang, Na Gong
description: BackgroundExcessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is a debilitating comorbidity in over 80% of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Evidence implicates dysregulation of the gut-kidney-brain axis as a may contribute of EDS pathogenesis, though detailed mechanistic insights remain limited.

title: Best practices for engaging lived experience experts in dialogues about climate change and mental health: lessons learned from a global effort
creator: Britt Wray, Ans Vercammen, Lian Zeitz, Sacha Wright, Vashti-Eve Burrows, Jeannie Yamazaki, Suhailah Jasmin Ali, Kyle Hill, Jemaima Tiatia-Siau, Kezang Wangmo, John Jamir Benzon Aruta, Gail Co, Renzo R. Guinto, Emma L. Lawrance
description: The Connecting Climate Minds global initiative sought to advance research and action at the intersection of climate change and mental health by centering the voices of people with lived experience. Through a series of regional and thematic dialogues, Connecting Climate Minds engaged nearly 1,200 participants across seven global regions, including Indigenous communities, smallholder farmers and fisher peoples, and youth.

title: Summary of the best evidence that cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia improves sleep quality in patients with chronic insomnia
creator: Panpan Yan, Siyu Feng, Miaomiao Ma, Bo Li, Jie Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimTo evaluate and summarize the best available evidence regarding the efficacy of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) in improving sleep quality in patients with chronic insomnia and to provide structured, evidence-based recommendations for clinical nursing practice.DesignThis evidence summary was conducted using the PIPOST model from the Center for Evidence-Based Nursing at Fudan University, which guided the development of structured evidence-based questions.MethodsA systematic search was performed across multiple databases and guideline repositories for literature published from inception to December 10, 2024.

title: Combining genotyping approaches improves resolution for association mapping: a case study in tropical maize under water stress conditions
creator: Fernanda Carla Ferreira de Pontes, Ingrid Pinheiro Machado, Maria Valnice de Souza Silveira, Antônio Lucas Aguiar Lobo, Felipe Sabadin, Roberto Fritsche-Neto, Júlio César DoVale
description: Genome-wide Association Studies (GWAS) identify genome variations related to specific phenotypes using Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) markers. Genotyping platforms like SNP-Array or sequencing-based techniques (GBS) can genotype samples with many SNPs. These approaches may bias tropical maize analyses due to reliance on the temperate line B73 as the reference genome.

title: University of Patanjali as a Centre of Excellence in Yoga Education
creator: Rudra B. Bhandari, Sadhvi Devpriya
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). that aims to carry out quality teaching, learning, research, and advocacy on Yoga, Ayurveda, Vedic wisdom, and culture to produce professionally competent, personally developed, and socially empathetic youths dedicated to promoting Indian Knowledge System (IKS).

title: Cyberinfrastructure for machine learning applications in agriculture: experiences, analysis, and vision
creator: Lucas Waltz, Sushma Katari, Chaeun Hong, Adit Anup, Julian Colbert, Anirudh Potlapally, Taylor Dill, Canaan Porter, John Engle, Christopher Stewart, Hari Subramoni, Scott Shearer, Raghu Machiraju, Osler Ortez, Laura Lindsey, Arnab Nandi, Sami Khanal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionAdvancements in machine learning (ML) algorithms that make predictions from data without being explicitly programmed and the increased computational speeds of graphics processing units (GPUs) over the last decade have led to remarkable progress in the capabilities of ML. In many fields, including agriculture, this progress has outpaced the availability of sufficiently diverse and high-quality datasets, which now serve as a limiting factor.

title: Unraveling the mechanisms of intervertebral disc degeneration: an exploration of the p38 MAPK signaling pathway
creator: Xingmin Zhang, Zilin Zhang, Xiaosong Zou, Yongjie Wang, Jinwei Qi, Song Han, Jingguo Xin, Zhi Zheng, Lin Wei, Tianhui Zhang, Shaokun Zhang
description: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration (IDD) is a worldwide spinal degenerative disease. Low back pain (LBP) is frequently caused by a variety of conditions brought on by IDD, including IVD herniation and spinal stenosis, etc. These conditions bring substantial physical and psychological pressure and economic burden to patients.

title: Validation of the Korean version of the Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale
creator: Jiseon Jang, Taeyoung Lee, Aram Im, Myungji Ha, Jinyoung Oh, Ki Beom Park, Dong Hyuck Kim, Hyo Shin Kang
description: BackgroundThe use of prescription opioids has risen dramatically in South Korea in recent years; however, there is no standardized Korean-language instrument to assess opioid withdrawal. The Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS) is a widely used clinician-rated measure for assessing the severity of opioid withdrawal. We aimed to validate the Korean version of the COWS (K-COWS) among patients receiving opioid therapy.

title: Ayurvedic approaches to scorpion stings: Historical insights, modern scientific perspectives and challenges
creator: Susmita Nath, Naba K. Hazarika, Ashis K. Mukherjee
description: Scorpion stings are medical emergencies that require immediate attention and are frequently overlooked. Commercial antivenom available only in India is for a single species of venomous scorpion, with significant limitations. Additionally, access to antivenom therapy is limited in rural areas. Examining the ancient Indian traditional medicine, Ayurveda, reveals insights into the underlying mechanisms of scorpion envenomation and potential treatments.

title: Leveraging AI-driven nudge theory to enhance hand hygiene compliance: paving the path for future infection control
creator: Samiksha Bhattacharjee, Sudip Bhattacharya
description: Hand hygiene is critical for preventing infections, yet maintaining compliance remains challenging across healthcare, schools, and communities. Despite strong evidence, lapses occur due to cognitive barriers, understaffing, limited resources, and antimicrobial resistance. Behavioral science highlights factors like time constraints and cognitive biases affecting adherence, with compliance rates as low as 40%.

title: Acid-responsive nanoparticles with microneedles for anti‑inflammatory sonodynamic therapy of gouty arthritis
creator: Jiaqi Weng, Lili Feng, Binghui Xie, Linxiao Liu, Shulin Shen, Xuechao Chen, Liting Wang, Yueyue Xie, Jianhua Yao, Laurent David, Qinying Yan
description: The pathological microenvironment of acute gouty arthritis (AGA) features local tissue acidification and the release of a storm of pro-inflammatory cytokines. To address this dual challenge, we engineered an acid-responsive curcumin-loaded nanoparticles microneedle system (Cur-PNPs@MN) that delivers curcumin with pH-triggered release and anti-inflammatory activity.

title: Deep learning-based multimodality classification of chronic mild traumatic brain injury using resting-state functional MRI and PET imaging
creator: Faezeh Vedaei, Najmeh Mashhadi, Mahdi Alizadeh, George Zabrecky, Daniel Monti, Nancy Wintering, Emily Navarreto, Chloe Hriso, Andrew B. Newberg, Feroze B. Mohamed
description: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a public health concern. The present study aimed to develop an automatic classifier to distinguish between patients with chronic mTBI (n = 83) and healthy controls (HCs) (n = 40). Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging were acquired from the subjects.

title: Esports physical exercise/performance matrix 1.0 country factsheets: results and analyses from Serbia
creator: Xuanyu Zhou, Yuwen Hu, Radenko M. Matic, Stevo Popovic
description: The Serbian Country Factsheets on Physical Exercise and Performance for Esports Players provide a foundational assessment of nine physical exercise and performance indicators tailored to esports athletes. This study utilizes Serbia’s Esports Physical Exercise/Performance Matrix 1.0 framework, integrating recent peer-reviewed studies and nationally representative secondary data to evaluate these indicators.

title: Analysis of material reliability features of plasma material interactions
creator: Alper Pahsa
description: This work presents a statistical methodology for evaluating material surface degradation and reliability based on roughness measurements obtained from Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM). Surface roughness metrics were employed to evaluate and model aluminum specimens exposed to helium plasma via a Weibull reliability method.

title: A new name for an old problem—Colletotrichum cigarro is the cause of St John’s wilt of Hypericum perforatum
creator: Lana-Sophie Kreth, Ulrike Damm, Monika Götz
description: A major problem for St John’s wort (Hypericum perforatum) is St John’s wilt, which can lead to reduced crop yields and even complete crop losses. In the past, the pathogen was referred to as Colletotrichum gloeosporioides or occasionally as Colletotrichum cf. gloeosporioides based on morphology. Although a strain from this host had been re-identified as C.

title: Impact of deep learning image reconstruction on CT radiomics reproducibility in patients with pulmonary nodules
creator: Huiyuan Zhu, Tingle Wei, Luna Wang, Lin Zhu, Qunhui Chen, Guangyu Tao, Linlin Sun, Xiwen Sun, Zike Huang, Hong Yu
description: ObjectiveEnsuring CT feature reproducibility across imaging protocols and reconstruction algorithms is essential for the generalizability of radiomics applications. This study aimed to evaluate the reproducibility of CT radiomic features in pulmonary nodules using deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) compared with conventional reconstruction techniques under different radiation doses.Materials and methodsWe included 94 patients between March and June 2023.

title: Novel insights into the isolation of extracellular vesicles by anion exchange chromatography
creator: Leon F. Koch, Tatjana Best, Elena Wüstenhagen, Klaus Adrian, Oliver Rammo, Meike J. Saul
description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane structures enclosed by a lipid bilayer that are released into the extracellular space by all types of cells. EVs are involved in many physiological processes by transporting biologically active substances. Interest in EVs for diagnostic biomarker research and therapeutic drug delivery applications has increased in recent years.

title: Cell:cell adhesion in sweet cherry fruit primarily due to pectins
creator: Elsa Culemann, Christine Schumann, Andreas Winkler, Simon Sitzenstock, Moritz Knoche
description: Rain cracking limits the production of sweet cherries wherever they are grown. Cracking occurs by the separation of neighboring cells along their cell walls (by cell:cell separation). The objectives were to identify the cell wall components involved in cell:cell adhesion using immunolabeling and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and digestion assays employing pectinases, hemicellulases, and a cellulase.

title: RAPID perfusion CT in acute ischemic stroke: an educational pictorial review of common patterns, pearls, and pitfalls
creator: Andrea Buoso, Caterina Bernetti, Michele Tondo, Ilenia Barbalace, Teresa Giannarelli, Michele Pillitteri, Andrea Romano, Alessandro Bozzao, Bruno Beomonte Zobel, Carlo A. Mallio
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rapid processing of Perfusion and Diffusion (RAPID) software for CT perfusion (CTP) is a valuable tool for the evaluation of acute ischemic stroke and therapeutic decision-making in extended therapeutic windows. However, automated maps should not be interpreted in isolation. A structured, pattern-based approach, integrating qualitative visual assessment with automated quantitative output and clinical information to refine therapeutic selection, remains essential to mitigate pitfalls and optimize patient care.

title: Thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (CCL17) as a clinical biomarker in atopic dermatitis: significance and limitations in the new treatment era
creator: Yoko Kataoka
description: Thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC; CCL17) is a T-helper-2 chemokine that reflects atopic dermatitis (AD) disease activity. Since 2008, serum TARC levels have been commercially measured in Japan, and clinical experience has shown the usefulness of TARC. The fallacy that eczema is always visible often hinders successful treatment, when there is subclinical inflammation which is inferable from the TARC level.

title: Honneth’s dialectical shortcoming: understanding Honneth’s problem with power
creator: Matthew Rutherford
description: Within contemporary critical theory, Axel Honneth’s recognition paradigm continues to exert significant influence. Honneth adopts an empathetically positive view of recognition, that it is always freedom-enhancing. But recently, there is a trend toward a more complex and ambivalent understanding of recognition. Critics highlight Honneth’s inattentiveness to deeper power relations which can use recognition as a tool for domination.

title: DepITCM: an audio-visual method for detecting depression
creator: Lishan Zhang, Zhenhua Liu, Yumei Wan, Yunli Fan, Diancai Chen, Qingxiang Wang, Kaihong Zhang, Yunshao Zheng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionDepression is a prevalent mental disorder, and early screening and treatment are crucial for detecting depression. However, there are still some limitations in the currently proposed deep models based on audio-video data, for example, it is difficult to effectively extract and select useful multimodal information and features from audio-video data, and very few studies have been able to focus on three dimensions of information: time, channel, and space at the same time in depression detection.

title: Health beliefs and attitudes toward Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination in Portugal: a study using a mixed-method approach
creator: Ana João Santos, Irina Kislaya, Carlos Matias-Dias, Ausenda Machado
description: IntroductionVaccination is one of the most effective population strategies to prevent infectious diseases and mitigate pandemics, and it is important to understand vaccine uptake determinants since vaccine hesitancy has been increasing for the past few decades. The Health Belief Model (HBM) has been widely used for understanding vaccination behavior.

title: Mechanotransduction through oxidative stress upregulates circLyst to drive vascular remodeling in hypertensive humans and rodents
creator: Juanjuan Tan, Weiyi Hu, Li Shen, Biyang Luo, Huajin Liu, Feng Li, Hui Qin, Yuanwang Yu, Haifang Wang, Jing Dong, Qi Zhang, Hong Zhang, Fan Lv, Yingxin Qi, Kai Wang, Yi Yang, Zhiqiang Yan, Kai Huang
description: Aberrant cyclic stretch serves as a critical driver of vascular remodeling in hypertension, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here, we studied the role of a novel circRNA, termed circ_2465 (circLyst), in vascular remodeling in both human and rodent samples under high cyclic stretch.

title: Venetoclax combined with olverembatinib and prednisone as a frontline therapeutic strategy for Philadelphia chromosome-positive mixed-phenotype acute leukemia
creator: Xia Li, Yile Zhou, Xiangjie Lin, Hongyan Tong, Jie Jin, Huafeng Wang
description: Mixed-phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL) is a rare hematological malignancy with poor prognosis, for which there are currently no standardized therapeutic guidelines. Preclinical and clinical studies have shown that venetoclax and BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors have synergistic effects on Philadelphia chromosome–positive (Ph +) leukemias.

title: The role of phages for microdiverse bacterial communities in proglacial stream biofilms
creator: Hannes Peter, Grégoire Michoud, Susheel Bhanu Busi, Tom J. Battin
description: Viruses modulate the diversity and activity of microbial communities. However, little is known about their role for the structure of stream bacterial biofilm communities. Here, we present insights into the diversity and composition of viral communities in various streams draining three proglacial floodplains in Switzerland. Proglacial streams are characterized by extreme environmental conditions, including near-freezing temperatures and ultra-oligotrophy.

title: ADHD help-seeking attitudes of Asian Americans
creator: Monisha Chawla, Jennalyn Vandenheuvel, Shannon L. Sibbald
description: ADHD diagnosis and treatment for Hispanic and African American populations, there is a notable gap in understanding the experiences of Asian populations. One review found that Asian children had the lowest incidence of ADHD across ethnic groups, but this may be due to differences in symptom presentation and cultural practices (2).

title: Light as a master switch: a critical review of photonanozymes from design to applications
creator: Faria Fatima, Syed Saqib Ali Zaidi, Yang Guang, He Huang, Xiao-Man Sun
description: Despite the widespread industrial applications of nanozymes, their usage is often limited by mechanistic factors. They lack reaction control with catalyst fouling, which limits catalytic turnover and makes nanozyme recovery an energy-intensive process at large scale. These mechanistic challenges have been addressed by the evolution of photoresponsiveness into nanozymes called as photonanozymes (PNZs).

title: Myeloid neoplasm with PDGFRA rearrangement presenting in blast-phase with basophilia
creator: Anne-Cecilia van Marle, Evan Bowen
description: An adult man, from Southern Africa, presented to a public health centre with symptoms of progressive fatigue. Peripheral blood morphology showed marked basophilia and 21% myeloblasts, confirmed by flow cytometry, suggesting acute myeloid leukaemia with basophilia. Bone marrow biopsy revealed increased mast cells, raising systemic mastocytosis as a differential.

title: Soil microbial community and influencing factors of different vegetation restoration types in a typical agricultural pastoral ecotone
creator: Pei Huang, Hanyu Shi, Lina Jiang, Duoping Zhu, Zefeng Zhou, Zhenhong Hou, Xingyu Ma
description: Microbial network complexity is an important indicator for assessing the effectiveness of vegetation restoration. However, the response of the microbial network complexity of bacteria and fungi to different vegetation restoration types is unclear. Therefore, in this study, we selected four vegetation restoration types (Pinus sylvestris var.

title: APOE-ε4 allele[s]-associated adverse events reported from placebo arm in clinical trials for Alzheimer's disease: implications for anti-amyloid beta therapy
creator: Kenichiro Sato, Yoshiki Niimi, Ryoko Ihara, Kazushi Suzuki, Atsushi Iwata, Takeshi Iwatsubo
description: APOE-ε4 allele[s] is a risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA) in anti-amyloid beta therapy, and is also associated with cerebrovascular risk factors such as hyperlipidemia or atherosclerosis. During AD clinical trials, APOE-ε4 carriers may experience neuropsychiatric adverse events (AEs) related to these risks, complicating the differentiation of ARIA from cerebrovascular events based on symptoms.

title: Erythema nodosum as the initial presentation of leprosy in a 15-year-old boy: a case report on Ethiopia’s persistent elimination challenges
creator: Kedir Negesso Tukeni, Tadele Molla Aga, Elias Ababulgu Abadiko, Idosa Taso Mamo, Tamirat Godebo Woyimo, Eyob Tarekegn Biru, Abdo Kedir Abafogi, Esayas Kebede Gudina
description: Leprosy remains a significant public health concern in Ethiopia, with challenges in timely diagnosis and management contributing to disabilities. This case report details a 15-year-old boy who presented with diffuse nodular and bullous skin lesions, peripheral neuropathy, and systemic symptoms, ultimately diagnosed with multibacillary leprosy confirmed by a positive skin smear for acid-fast bacilli.

title: Feasibility and Safety of a Novel Pig‐tail Inside Stent for Unresectable Malignant Hilar Biliary Obstruction: A Single‐center Case Series (With Video)
creator: Motoyasu Kan, Daiki Takahashi, Sodai Uchida, Taiga Sudo, Kouki Yokozuka, Yoshiki Nakaya, Akinori Abe, Hiroki Kurosaki, Yoshiki Ogane, Kazuki Watabe, Miho Sakai, Yu Sekine, Mayu Ouchi, Hiroshi Ohyama, Izumi Ohno, Jun Kato
description: Background and AimsInside stents are increasingly used for malignant hilar biliary obstruction because of their prolonged patency and removability. Although reported migration rates vary, migration remains a clinical concern, and deployment in angulated bile ducts can be technically challenging. We evaluated a novel pig‐tail type inside stent (X‐FLEX ARC type) in unresectable malignant hilar biliary obstruction.

title: Research on the healthy life expectancy of older adult individuals in China based on intrinsic capacity health standards and social stratification analysis
creator: Mengya Liu, Meng Zhang, Jinglei Zhou, Nannan Song, Li Zhang
description: BackgroundBased on the health standard of intrinsic capacity, this paper conducts an empirical study on the healthy life expectancy of older adult individuals aged 60 and older in China and analyzes the health inequities associated with different social characteristics to provide a reference for improving care for the older adult in China.

title: Fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations during music-evoked autobiographical memories in neurotypical older adults
creator: Teresa Lesiuk, Kaitlyn Dillon, Giulia Ripani, Ioannis Iliadis, Gabriel Perez, Bonnie Levin, Xiaoyan Sun, Roger McIntosh
description: IntroductionResearchers have shown that music-evoked autobiographical memories (MEAMs) can stimulate long-term memory mechanisms while requiring little retrieval effort and may therefore be used in promising non-pharmacological interventions to mitigate memory deficits. Despite an increasing number of studies on MEAMs, few researchers have explored how MEAMs are bound in the brain.

title: Gastrointestinal Parasites in Himalayan Musk Deer (Moschus leucogaster Hodgson, 1839) and Sympatric Livestock in Gaurishankar Conservation Area, Nepal
creator: Rabin Sharma, Narayan Prasad Koju, Aakriti Adhikari, Mahendra Maharjan, Rashila Deshar
description: BackgroundParasite infections threaten both domesticated and wildlife populations. Shared resources between wildlife and domesticated ruminants increase the risk of cross‐transmission, underscoring the need for infection research. This study aimed to determine the composition, prevalence, and habitat‐dependent patterns of gastrointestinal parasites in endangered Himalayan musk deer (Moschus leucogaster) and sympatric livestock (chauri and horses) in Lapchi Valley of Gaurishankar Conservation Area.

title: Assessing the impact of waterfront trail aesthetics on psychological restoration in urban environments: a deep learning and random forest approach
creator: Yongshu Wu, Yuhan Wang, Juan Wang, Junyi Li, Yinghong Ding, Yaqin Ding, Yuxuan Wu, Zhipeng Zhu, Xiaoling Xu
description: Urban waterfront trails can promote psychological restoration, yet how specific landscape attributes shape scenic beauty and multidimensional restorative perception across different revetment types remains unclear. This study quantified 15 landscape variables (F1–F15) across 30 urban waterfront trail sites and examined their associations with scenic beauty estimation (SBE) and four restorative dimensions (emotional, cognitive, physiological, and behavioral).

title: Mitochondrial Supercomplex‐Associated Proximity Increases in Malignant Glioma Tissue
creator: Minou Tsujishita, Haesoo Bae, Anwaar Ali, Shanmuganathan Balakrishnan, Amina Abulimiti, Nelofer Syed, Kambiz N Alavian
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
