However, the contribution of family-related variables remains insufficiently understood, particularly in non-Western contexts.Methods:This cross-sectional study included 78 children and adolescents with psychiatric disorders and their primary caregivers.

title: Distinct sex differences in ethanol consumption and operant self-administration in C57BL/6J mice with uniform regulation by glutamate AMPAR activity
creator: Sara Faccidomo, Vallari R. Eastman, Taruni S. Santanam, Katarina S. Swaim, Seth M. Taylor, Clyde W. Hodge
description: IntroductionConsidering sex as a biological variable (SABV) in preclinical research can enhance understanding of the neurobiology of alcohol use disorder (AUD). However, the behavioral and neural mechanisms underlying sex-specific differences remain unclear. This study aims to elucidate SABV in ethanol (EtOH) consumption by evaluating its reinforcing effects and regulation by glutamate AMPA receptor activity in male and female mice.

title: Changes in Dietary Behavior, Physical Activity, and Mental Health During a Lifestyle-Based Wellness Program for Women Re-Entering the Community After Incarceration: A Single-Arm Pre-Post Program Evaluation
creator: Sarah Rashdan, Sarah-Ann Keyes
description: BackgroundWomen re-entering the community after incarceration experience substantial chronic disease and mental health burdens. Evidence regarding lifestyle medicine programming in transitional housing settings remains limited. This study evaluated changes in dietary behavior, physical activity, and mental health symptoms during a wellness program.

title: Does COVID‐19 Vaccination Protect Against Post‐COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?
creator: Lidian Franci Batalha Santa Maria, Márcio Coutinho Xavier Naves, Elisabeth Carmen Duarte, Isis Polianna Silva Ferreira de Carvalho, Henry Maia Peixoto
description: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS‐CoV‐2 infection, representing an important cause of long‐term morbidity and mortality. In addition to preventing primary infection, COVID‐19 vaccination has emerged as a protective factor against post‐COVID cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Transcriptomic and photosynthetic analyses of Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 and Chlorogloeopsis fritschii sp. PCC6912 exposed to an M-dwarf spectrum under an anoxic atmosphere
creator: Mariano Battistuzzi, Maria Silvia Morlino, Lorenzo Cocola, Livio Trainotti, Laura Treu, Stefano Campanaro, Riccardo Claudi, Luca Poletto, Nicoletta La Rocca
description: IntroductionCyanobacteria appeared in the anoxic Archean Earth, evolving for the first time oxygenic photosynthesis and deeply changing the atmosphere by introducing oxygen. Starting possibly from UV-protected environments, characterized by low visible and far-red enriched light spectra, cyanobacteria spread everywhere on Earth thanks to their adaptation capabilities in light harvesting.

title: Health Inequalities, Intersectionality, and Justice
creator: ERIKA BLACKSHER
description: Policy PointsPopulation health science that uses large data sets to study health inequalities increasingly draws on intersectionality, the idea that overlapping forms of disadvantage shape health inequalities. This approach is essential to the pursuit of health equity because it provides a more complete and sound evidence base for population health policy.

title: Liver regeneration governed by zonated PIEZO1 mechanotransduction
creator: Lin Xie, Chen Zhang, Yonglong Wei, Wenxiu Ning
description: Mechanical forces are recognized as regulators of organ development, homeostasis, and regeneration, yet how physical cues are sensed in a region-specific manner within the liver remains unclear. In a Science article, Zhang and colleagues identify DPP4-positive zone 2 hepatocytes as a mechanosensory population, demonstrating that mechanical stress triggers the regenerative response through PIEZO1-mediated mechanotransduction.

title: Stellate ganglion block for ventricular arrhythmia disease states: Emerging treatment options
creator: Ahmed I. Anwar, Fatima Iqbal, Walid K. Mohammed, Alexander S. Harris, Emily A. Francis, Aishwarya Reddy, Henry Liu, Alan D. Kaye
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Autonomic modulation has emerged as an effective therapeutic target in the management of ventricular arrhythmias and electrical storm (e.g., refractory ventricular arrhythmias), in a background of growing evidence of the link between the autonomic nervous system and arrhythmias. Stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) is a minimally invasive procedure targeting the stellate ganglion with an anesthetic agent that has emerged as a temporizing treatment option for management of refractory and hemodynamically unstable ventricular arrhythmias and electrical storm (ES).

title: Early harmonies, enduring echoes—how early life experiences and personality traits shape music performance anxiety
creator: Ludivine Aubry, Mats B. Küssner
description: Music performance anxiety (MPA) is a deeply personal and often debilitating experience, causing talented musicians to dread the very stages upon which they showcase their art. An increasing number of studies have addressed this anxiety phenomenon, however, definitions vary and the underlying causes remain unclear.

title: Chromosomal and genetic causes of primary ovarian insufficiency in the Utah population
creator: Samantha Fukutomi, Edgar Javier Hernandez, Kristina Allen-Brady, Marco Marchetti, Erica B Johnstone, Lauren E Verrilli, Joseph Letourneau, Barry Moore, Mark Yandell, Corrine K Welt
description: BackgroundPrimary ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a heterogeneous disorder, with the relative frequency of known etiologies incompletely defined at a population level.ObjectivesWe used chart review and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to determine known diagnoses, pathogenic variants, and common polygenic risk.MethodsWomen with POI were identified using International Classification of Diseases codes. Established clinical etiologies were documented.

title: Effect of different postures and loads on joint motion and muscle activity in older adults during overhead retrieval
creator: Chengmin Zhou, Xue Xu, Ting Huang, Jake Kaner
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Pain is a common health problem among older adults worldwide. Older adults tend to suffer from arm, lumbar, and back pain when using hanging cabinets. Methods: This study used surface electromyography to record muscle activity and a motion capture system to record joint motion to research effects of different loads and retrieval postures on muscle activity and joint range of motion when older adults retrieve objects from a high place, to provide optimised feedback for the design of hanging cabinet furniture.

title: Inhibition of anti-tumor immunity by melanoma cell-derived Activin-A depends on STING
creator: Katarina Pinjusic, Giovanna Ambrosini, Joao Lourenco, Nadine Fournier, Christian Iseli, Nicolas Guex, Olga Egorova, Sina Nassiri, Daniel B. Constam
description: The transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) family member activin A (hereafter Activin-A) is overexpressed in many cancer types, often correlating with cancer-associated cachexia and poor prognosis. Activin-A secretion by melanoma cells indirectly impedes CD8+ T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity and promotes resistance to immunotherapies, even though Activin-A can be proinflammatory in other contexts.

title: A mature tertiary lymphoid structure-associated spatial niche is inversely associated with ACC1-related lipid metabolism in neoadjuvant-treated hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Ronghua Wang, Biao Shen, Yanan Wu, Shuai Zhao, Wenhao Xu, Wangrui Liu, Jian Wang
description: Highlights•Spatial multi-omics identifies a mature TLS-associated niche in HCC.•Niche5 is more spatially organized in pathological responders.•TLS chemokine signaling accompanies antigen presentation and CD8 immunity.•ACC1-related lipid metabolism is inversely associated with mature TLS.•Pathology validates spatial separation of TLS and lipid-metabolic regions.

title: Cerebral cavernous malformations: epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis and therapy
creator: Suyun Yu, Weiwei Zheng, Yanhong Pan, Liwenyu Chen, Jing Ma, Mengyuan Gao, Wei Zou, Yin Lu, Yang Zhao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are cerebrovascular diseases characterized by vascular lesions of the central nervous system (CNS) that can result in epileptic seizures, headaches, focal neurologic deficits (FNDs), and hemorrhagic stroke. Germline and somatic loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in one of the three established CCM-associated genes, namely CCM1 (or krev interaction trapped protein 1, KRIT1), CCM2, and CCM3 (or programmed cell death 10, PDCD10), which have been validated as core drivers of CCM pathogenesis and progression.

title: Tolerance to heavy metals of bacteria from Brazilian deep aquatic environments
creator: Agatha do Canto Shubeita, Caroline Menegotto-Silva, Rafela Wong Davi, Audrey Menegaz Proença, Cássio Stein Moura, Renata Medina-Silva
description: Bacterial tolerance to heavy metals (HM) poses a significant risk to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated tolerance to HM of 24 bacterial isolates from two deep aquatic environments in southern Brazil: the Guarani Aquifer System (GAS) and the Rio Grande Cone (RGC).

title: Managing growth and puberty concerns in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Updated guidance and future directions
creator: Meilan M Rutter, Janet L Crane, Funmbi Babalola, Robert W Benjamin, Carol Lam, Laura McAdam, Stefan Nicolau, Anne Marie Sbrocchi, Mena Scavina, Julia Sorbara, Alexandra Ahmet, Susan Apkon, Chiara Arpaia, Tommaso Aversa, Shipra Bansal, Luca Bello, Diana X Bharucha-Goebel, Sabrina Corbetta, Natascia D
description: Long-term glucocorticoid therapy is standard of care for individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) but often results in impaired growth and delayed or incomplete puberty, impacting their physical and psychosocial health. Although DMD endocrine care has evolved, leading to inclusion in the 2018 Care Considerations, these issues remain prevalent and concerning, and gaps in care persist.

title: Somatosensory processing is altered in people with hip osteoarthritis compared to controls: A cross-sectional study
creator: Andrea B Mosler, Ebonie K Rio, Benedict M Wand, Molly E Coventry, Gordon S Waddington, Myles C Murphy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWith knee osteoarthritis (OA), measures of mechanical and thermal pain sensitivity relate to both pain severity and treatment outcomes, and lower limb left/right judgement is impaired. However, little is known about these somatosensory variables in people with hip OA.ObjectivesOur cross-sectional study aimed to explore the differences in sensitivity to noxious mechanical and thermal stimuli, and lower limb left/right judgement, in people with hip OA compared to matched controls without hip OA.MethodsDemographic variables and self-reported hip-related disability were collected using an online survey,

title: Sea of plastic: representations of the sea and pro-environmental attitudes and behaviors regarding marine plastic pollution in Peru and Chile
creator: Fernanda Saavedra, Marisol Mego, Sofia Ticona, Martin Thiel, Jostein Baeza, Agustín Espinosa
description: Marine plastic pollution remains one of the greatest problems worldwide. Hence, this study explores the attitudes and pro-environmental behaviors of Peruvian and Chilean citizens regarding marine pollution, with an emphasis on plastic pollution. For this, forty-four semi-structured interviews were conducted with Peruvian (n = 24) and Chilean (n = 20) citizens, of which, through thematic analysis, semantic patterns were identified.

title: Changes in gut microbiota after gastric cancer surgery: a prospective longitudinal study
creator: Yuhua He, Shilin Gao, Lili Jiang, Jie Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThis study was designed to characterize gut microbiota changes of the patients with gastric cancer before and after the gastrectomy during their hospital staying periods.Methods16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing was used to evaluate differences in gut microbiota among patients with gastric cancer before and after the gastrectomy by comparing gut microbiota α diversity, β diversity, and structure composition at different taxonomic levels.ResultsA total of 120 fecal specimens were collected from 60 patients.

title: Mitochondrial DNA D-loop variants correlate with a primary open-angle glaucoma subgroup
creator: Antoni Vallbona-Garcia, Patrick J. Lindsey, Rick Kamps, Alphons P. M. Stassen, Nhan Nguyen, Florence H. J. van Tienen, Ilse H. J. Hamers, Rianne Hardij, Marike W. van Gisbergen, Birke J. Benedikter, Irenaeus F. M. de Coo, Carroll A. B. Webers, Theo G. M. F. Gorgels, Hubert J. M. Smeets
description: IntroductionPrimary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a characteristic optic neuropathy, caused by degeneration of the optic nerve-forming neurons, the retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). High intraocular pressure (IOP) and aging have been identified as major risk factors; yet the POAG pathophysiology is not fully understood. Since RGCs have high energy requirements, mitochondrial dysfunction may put the survivability of RGCs at risk.

title: Focusing on VaIN2+: Development and validation of a prediction nomogram based on a large colposcopy population
creator: Quanlong Lu, Yao Liu, Jing Li, Chenyao Guo, Ruifang Li, Bo Feng, Xun Gao, Lifang Gao, Zhilian Wang
description: IntroductionVaginal intraepithelial neoplasia 2 or worse (VaIN2+) has long remained in a largely passive diagnostic pattern due to the lack of specific clinical manifestations and routine screening strategies. This study aimed to explore its clinical characteristics and develop a prediction model for individualized risk assessment.

title: Exploring smallholder farmers’ access and participation in the Home Grown School Feeding Programme in selected counties of Kenya
creator: Joyce Kamau, Collins Okoyo, Tabitha Kanyui, Charles Mwandawiro, Samrat Singh, Lesley Drake
description: IntroductionSmallholder farmers (SHFs) produce 80% of the total agricultural output in Kenya. The Home Grown School Feeding Programme (HGSFP) was designed to address short-term hunger among primary school children from food-insecure households, enhancing access to primary education while providing a market to SHFs through local procurement of food for schools.

title: Disability, Fatigue and Mental Health in Acute Versus Chronic Spinal Pain in the Gaza Strip: A Comparative Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Marwa Salama, Ahmed A. Najim, Magdy Shabana, Reham Almukbel, Kinan Mokbel
description: BackgroundSpinal pain is a major contributor to disability, but evidence comparing multidomain outcomes across acute and chronic stages remains limited in conflict‐affected settings. This study aimed to compare disability, fatigue, psychological distress and sleep disturbance among patients with acute and chronic neck pain and low back pain (LBP) in the Gaza Strip.

title: CYP4B1 inhibits lung adenocarcinoma progression via PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway: mechanistic insights and development of a CYP4B1-related prognostic signature
creator: Guoyin Li, Jing Kang, Xiaoyan Li, Liping Zhao, Yuhang Chen, Chenlu Gong, Zhiqiang Liu, Bi Zhang
description: BackgroundLung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) has a poor 5-year survival rate due to delayed diagnosis and drug resistance. Cytochrome P450 4B1 (CYP4B1), a lung-predominant enzyme, is linked to cancer susceptibility, but its role and regulation in LUAD remain unclear.MethodsMulti-omics analyses of public datasets (TCGA_LUAD, GSE series) and clinical specimens assessed CYP4B1 expression. Functional experiments (cell lines, xenografts) explored its effects.

title: Occupational physicians’ perceptions of professional role change following health policy reform in France: A qualitative study
creator: Babacarsy Diop, Etienne Fourreau, Bénédicte Clin, Mathilde Boulanger
description: ObjectivesTo explore occupational physicians’ perceptions of the 2 August 2021 reform and changes in their professional role, identify reported barriers and perceived facilitators to practice change, and describe reported health promotion practices.Study designQualitative study using semi-structured interviews.MethodsTen occupational physicians practising in Normandy, France, were interviewed between November 2024 and March 2025.

title: Rapid Clearance of microRNA-371a-3p: A Longitudinal Study of Serum Levels in Patients with Localized Testicular Germ Cell Tumors
creator: Klaus-Peter Dieckmann, Tabea Niemzok, Jan Diesend, Mattis Franke, Markus Klemke, Alexander Harms, Christian Wülfing, Nina Wagener, Gazanfer Belge
description: Take Home MessageSerum levels of microRNA-371a-3p drop very rapidly with a half-life of 3.8 h after treatment. A few cases require a longer time to normalize. The kinetic profile of this biomarker allows rapid recognition of treatment response and offers prospects for future therapeutic strategies. ADVANCING PRACTICE What does this study add?

title: Readily available drugs and other interventions to potentially improve the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade in cancer
creator: Merissa Coleman, Sophia J. Mascialino, Anusha Panjwani, Emily Edwards, Vidula V. Sukhatme, Christina Gavegnano, Vikas P. Sukhatme
description: To improve the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) for cancer treatment, various strategies, including combination therapies with repurposed drugs, are being explored. Several readily available interventions with potential to enhance programmed death 1 (PD-1) blockade have been identified. However, these interventions often remain overlooked due to the lack of financial incentives for their development, making them financial orphans.

title: Effectiveness of antimicrobial agent combinations against carbapenem-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae with KPC variants in China
creator: Congcong Liu, Yuchen Wu, Yanyan Zhang, Zelin Yan, Danxia Gu, Hongwei Zhou, Ning Dong, Chang Cai, Gongxiang Chen, Rong Zhang
description: PurposeCarbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) producing carbapenemases poses a global threat to public health. Antimicrobial agent combinations have been promoted as a potential therapeutic strategy for infections. The most effective antimicrobial combinations against CRKP strains producing different carbapenemases are currently unclear, particularly those producing the KPC variant carbapenemases.

title: Effects of melatonin alone or in combination with Bio-Oss® on early osteoblastic activity: An in vitro study
creator: Christiane Colombo dos Santos, Daiane Cristina Peruzzo, Juliana Ramacciato, Ana Cláudia Garcia Rosa
description: BackgroundMelatonin modulates bone metabolism and enhances osteogenic activity; however, whether these effects are maintained when combined with xenogeneic bone substitutes during early osteoblastic responses remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of melatonin alone and combined with the xenogeneic bone substitute Bio-Oss® on early osteoblastic activity in vitro.MethodsHuman osteoblast-like cells (SaOS-2) were allocated to four groups: control, melatonin (0.

title: Case Report: Budd–Chiari-like syndrome in a cat with polycystic kidney and liver disease
creator: Eun-Soo Lee, Yoon-Seok Jang, Jae-Il Han, Tae-Rin Kim, Jae-Hwan Kim, Jae-Eun Hyun
description: A 9-year-old spayed female Persian Chinchilla cat presented with progressive lethargy and acute right hindlimb pain and lameness. Diagnostic imaging revealed diffuse renal and hepatic cysts, resulting in marked hepatomegaly. Computed tomography (CT) further identified a localized narrowing of the intrahepatic caudal vena cava (CVC), likely due to extrinsic compression by the enlarged liver.

title: Padlet: a tool for fostering collaborative learning and feedback literacy in dental education
creator: Avita Rath
description: BackgroundWhile health professions education has embraced collaborative and co-creative learning approaches, the integration of digital technologies into feedback practices remains limited, especially in undergraduate dental education. This study investigated the impact of Padlet, a digital pinboard, on collaborative learning and feedback literacy among undergraduate dental students during a formative assessment activity guided by Nicol and MacFarlane's feedback principles.

title: Arterial tortuosity syndrome with coronary artery involvement in a middle-aged female: A case report
creator: Prinsa Shrestha, Amin Shah, Saroj GC, Niraj Kumar Sharma, Aditya Mahaseth, Sanjaya Kumar Shrestha
description: Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective-tissue arteriopathy characterized by diffuse elongation and tortuosity of large and medium-sized arteries. Although it is typically diagnosed during childhood, adult presentation may occur and can be overlooked when overt connective-tissue manifestations are absent; coronary involvement is uncommon but clinically important.

title: Primary healthcare providers’ strategies of handling patients presenting with potential cancer symptoms following the introduction of standardized cancer patient pathways in Sweden
creator: Petter Fjällström, Anna-Britt Coe, Mikael Lilja, Senada Hajdarevic
description: BackgroundEarly cancer diagnosis is a healthcare priority, but identifying patients who may have cancer remains challenging because alarm symptoms are often non-specific and may also indicate other conditions. To facilitate timely cancer diagnosis, standardized cancer patient pathways (CPP) have been introduced in several health systems, including Sweden.

title: Structural basis for cysteine-linked redox-state plasticity in mammalian methionine sulfoxide reductase A
creator: Byeongmin Shin, Hye-Jin Kim Hawkes, Seonha Park, Hosam Ki, Sulhee Kim, Fenil Shah, Giovanna Di Trapani, Kathryn F. Tonissen, Kwang Yeon Hwang
description: Methionine sulfoxide reductase A (MsrA) protects proteins from oxidative damage through cysteine-based redox cycling, but how mammalian MsrA is structurally regulated during oxidation and reductive recycling has remained unclear. We report three crystal structures of mouse MsrA (mMsrA) that capture distinct redox states — reduced (3.0 Å), BME-trapped intermediate-like (BTIL; 1.6 Å), and oxidized (1.

title: A combined model of shoot phosphorus uptake based on sparse data and active learning algorithm
creator: Tianli Wang, Yi Zhang, Haiyan Liu, Fei Li, Dayong Guo, Ning Cao, Yubin Zhang
description: The soil ecosystem has been severely damaged because of the increasingly severe environmental problems caused by excessive application of phosphorus (P) fertilizer, which seriously hinders soil fertility restoration and sustainable farmland development. Shoot P uptake (SPU) is an important parameter for monitoring crop growth and health and for improving field nutrition management and fertilization strategies.

title: Exploring the potential benefits of Shirodhara as an add-on therapy for alleviating post-COVID anxiety and depression: A case study
creator: Manoj Shamkuwar, Anandaraman PV, Dinesh Kataria, Santosh Bhatted, Bhavna Bhatia
description: In this case study, we present a 31-year-old female, a homemaker, who developed persistent symptoms of anxiousness, fatigue, weakness, irritation, anger issues, and difficulty concentrating for nearly 12 months following recovery from COVID-19. She was diagnosed by a consulting psychiatrist with post-COVID anxiety with depression, and had been on anxiolytic and antidepressant medications for the past ten months.

title: First report of natural parasitism by Telenomus remus Nixon, 1937 on Spodoptera latifascia Walker, 1856 eggs in Puerto Rico: insights into spatial-temporal dynamics in a semiarid tropical region
creator: Daiane Dalla Nora, Ricardo Rubin Balardin, Ana Paula G. S. Wengrat, Wesley Augusto C. Godoy, Jose Carlos Verle Rodrigues
description: Telenomus remus is one of the most effective parasitoids of eggs used to control key pests in agricultural systems. This wasp can parasitize many species within the genus Spodoptera, including Spodoptera latifascia. The abundance and effectiveness of T. remus are influenced by landscape composition, climatic factors, and host availability, which need to be better characterized.

title: Spatial multi-omics uncovers an invasive-desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
creator: Chang-Hao Liang, Hua Ye, Hui Xu, Chen Fang, Jian-Ping Lian, Yue-Qin Chen, Wen-Tao Wang, Bo He
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and profound spatial heterogeneity, yet the multicellular organizational principles governing its tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; n = 9) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 4), integrating 61,234 single cells and 30,430 spots to identify an invasive-frontier myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast (IF-myCAF), which is characterized by elevated expression of ACTA2, TAGLN, COL11A1, THBS2, CTHRC1, and POSTN.

title: Insulin-like growth factor 2 (IGF-2) rescues social deficits in NLG3–/y mouse model of ASDs
creator: Rocco Pizzarelli, Domenico Pimpinella, Christian Jacobs, Alice Tartacca, Uarda Kullolli, Hannah Monyer, Cristina M. Alberini, Marilena Griguoli
description: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) comprise developmental disabilities characterized by impairments of social interaction and repetitive behavior, often associated with cognitive deficits. There is no current treatment that can ameliorate most of the ASDs symptomatology; thus, identifying novel therapies is urgently needed.

title: Frontal cortical neuroinflammation and circulating biomarkers following cardiopulmonary bypass in sheep
creator: Taku Furukawa, Alemayehu H. Jufar, Anton L. Trask-Marino, Clive N. May, Roger G. Evans, Andrew D. Cochrane, Bruno Marino, Peter R. McCall, Sally G. Hood, Jaishankar Raman, Connie Pei Chen Ow, Lars I. P. Snel, Scott Ayton, Ashenafi Betrie, Linda Cornthwaite, Munenori Kusunoki, Angela Connelly Huf, Da
description: BackgroundCerebral hypoxia and neuroinflammation have been implicated in neurocognitive disorders following cardiac surgery, but their postoperative trajectory and relationship with circulating biomarkers are poorly defined. We investigated cerebral tissue oxygenation, neuroinflammation, and plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration over 4 weeks after cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in sheep.

title: Targeting angiogenesis in endometriosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of VEGF-directed pharmacotherapies
creator: O. Hammond, O. El-Sheikh, R. M. Saad, P. Shetty, E. Papakonstantinou, S. L. Kastora
description: BackgroundAberrant vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)–driven angiogenesis is central to the establishment and persistence of endometriosis. Although numerous anti-angiogenic compounds have been tested, evidence remains fragmented, and no comparative framework guides the selection of agents compatible with fertility preservation.ObjectiveTo identify and rank vascular-targeted pharmacotherapies that most effectively regress endometriotic lesions and could be prioritised for fertility-sparing clinical translation.

title: Nanoparticles containing intracellular proteins modulate neutrophil functional and phenotypic heterogeneity
creator: Leonore Raudszus, Farbod Bahreini, Susanne Allan, Kai-Uwe Kalies, Charles C. Caldwell, Kathrin Kalies
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Neutrophils are rapidly recruited to sites of infection, injury, or to immune complexes. Upon arrival, they initiate degranulation, release reactive oxygen species (ROS), and/or nuclear extracellular traps (NETs) to eliminate invading microorganisms, clear debris, or remove abnormal immunoglobulins. While these processes ideally trigger healing and a return to balance, overshooting neutrophil function can lead to life-threatening infections such as sepsis or persistent inflammation observed in various autoimmune diseases.

title: Recent advances in antituberculosis drugs and therapeutics: from mechanistic breakthroughs to clinical translation
creator: Zhixiang Pan, Guan Liu, Yuehua Li, Hegui Yan, Yu Peng, Yiyi Wang, Hongri Gong, Juan Du, Shuang Wei
description: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, reclaimed its status as the deadliest single-pathogen infectious disease globally in 2023, accounting for 10.8 million new cases and 1.25 million deaths in 2023. The escalating crisis of drug-resistant TB, suboptimal BCG vaccine efficacy in adults, and persistent treatment gaps for vulnerable populations collectively drive an urgent shift toward mechanism-driven, precision-oriented therapeutic strategies.

title: Cerebral Hemodynamic Changes in Older Adults With Cognitive Complaints According to the Presence of Peripheral Artery Disease
creator: SangMi Noh, Hae‐Eun Shin, YongSoo Shim
description: ObjectiveAs a systemic expression of atherosclerosis, peripheral artery disease (PAD) has the potential to alter cerebral hemodynamics in elderly individuals presenting with cognitive concerns. However, how PAD status shapes the longitudinal trajectory of cerebral hemodynamics has not been well characterized.MethodsWe conducted a single‐center longitudinal observational study enrolling 132 participants (21 controls, 39 mild cognitive impairment, 72 mild Alzheimer's disease).

title: Encapsulation of Porphyrins in Polymer Microgels and Microbeads for Heterogeneous Photooxidation
creator: Imogen Smith, Natthakarn Olanchantarothai, Martin R. Johnston, Zhongfan Jia
description: Using porphyrin‐mediated photocatalytic energy transfer to generate singlet oxygen is a premier strategy for green, selective chemical synthesis. However, such catalytic systems are mostly conducted in organic solvents. This work aims to explore the generation and utilization of singlet oxygen for photochemical oxidation in aqueous media.

title: Epidemiology and diagnostic of MASLD in Latin America: a yet to be met challenge
creator: Carolina Elizabeth Olaez-Ramos, Karla Lizette Mojica-Zamudio, Ana Sandoval-Rodríguez, Juan Armendáriz-Borunda
description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a major global health concern, affecting more than one-third of the adult population worldwide. Notably, Latin America exhibits the highest regional prevalence, with recent estimates of 44.4%. This elevated burden is attributed to the convergence of risk factors that render the population particularly vulnerable.

title: Health poverty alleviation in China from the perspective of historical institutionalism: policy changes and driving factors
creator: Li Xu, Xiaojian You, Yinan Cui, Jiali You
description: Health poverty alleviation is an effective tool for improving the living quality and developmental conditions of impoverished populations. Since 1978, China has been actively implementing health poverty alleviation projects, resulting in a more robust rural healthcare service network and increased convenience for the local population to access medical treatment.

title: GLP-1R agonism in breast cancer: a metabolic–oncogenic switch?
creator: Angeliki Margoni, Kostas A. Papavassiliou, Athanasios G. Papavassiliou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). or agonists (GLP-1RAs) have emerged as potential modulators of the metabolic–oncogenic interface. Obesity may promote breast cancer through interconnected insulin/insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R), adipokine, inflammatory, and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)–AKT (PKB)–mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathways, reinforced by leptin–Janus kinase 2 (JAK2)–signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), nuclear factor kappaB (NF-κB) potentiation, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2/3 (HER2/HER3) crosstalk, and reduced adiponectin-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activity, favoring tumor cell proliferation, survival, invasion, and angiogenesis [1].

title: Case report: IL12RB1 deficiency in an infant with disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin disease
creator: Xiao Ma, Juping Chen, Junqiao Cheng, Jingbo Wang
description: Disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) disease is a rare adverse reaction to BCG vaccination. We report a neonate presenting with a progressive left axillary mass 3 months post-vaccination. High-throughput sequencing confirmed Mycobacterium bovis (BCG strain) infection. Genetic testing confirmed inborn errors of immunity (IEI) caused by interleukin (IL) 12 receptor β1 deficiency.

title: Targeting ferroptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms and emerging therapeutic strategies
creator: Mansoor Khaledi, Hasti Ahani, Faezeh Rezaei Tohid, Fatemeh Kazemi, Elham Amirkhani, Zeynab Daliri, Sahar Yadegari, Kosar Moarefvand, Behnam Poureslamfar, Fatemeh Sameni, Sajjad Yazdansetad
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by the lethal accumulation of lipid peroxides, has emerged as a pivotal pathway in cancer biology and a promising therapeutic target. This review synthesizes the core molecular machinery governing ferroptosis, detailing the critical roles of iron metabolism through systems like transferrin/transferrin receptor 1 and ferritinophagy, the cystine/glutamate antiporter system (Xc−)/glutathione/GPX4 axis, and the recently discovered FSP1/CoQ10 pathway.

title: Olfactory dysfunction among gas station employees exposed to fuel vapors using digital odor identification testing
creator: José Maria Viana dos Santos, Márcio Nakanishi
description: SummaryGas station employees are chronically exposed to fuel vapors containing benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), raising occupational concerns about olfactory function. In this cross-sectional study, 116 Brazilian gas station employees (86 men and 30 women; median age, 37.

title: Oxidation-regulated wide-temperature tribological behavior and mechanism of a Mo/Mo tribopair lubricated by Ga-based liquid metal
creator: Qiaona Wang, Hongji Liu, Guohua Zhang, Tongyang Li, Hailong Cui, Xing Feng, Yuan Yu, Zhengfeng Ma, Xiaoling Wang, Zhuhui Qiao, Huaguo Tang
description: SummaryGallium-based liquid metals combine fluidity with high thermal and electrical conductivity, making them attractive for lubrication in demanding environments. We investigated the tribological behavior of a Mo/Mo self-mated pair lubricated with Ga-In-Sn (GIS) from room temperature to 300°C in air and argon.

title: Plant-based dietary patterns, micronutrient status and breast cancer outcomes: a joint analysis of UK Biobank and Chinese longitudinal healthy longevity survey
creator: Weizhe Xu, Wen Gu, Yanqiu Huang, Shuli Li, Honglin Liu, Xun Zhu
description: BackgroundPlant-based diets may lower breast cancer risk, but their impact on breast cancer-related mortality is unclear. We explored associations of plant-based dietary patterns (Healthful Plant-Based Diet Index [HPDI/PDI]) and micronutrient intake with breast cancer incidence and all-cause mortality in patients.

title: Polymerase iota coordinates adaptation to replication stress in BRCA2-deficient mammary epithelial cells
creator: Kavya Vipparthi, Ariana Bellare, Resul Ozbilgic, Peter Bazeley, Nishtha Khanna, Fangfang Wang, Anand Bhushan, Liangqi Xie, Zahraa Al-Hilli, You-Wei Zhang, Mihriban Karaayvaz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBRCA2 deficiency induces chronic replication stress, yet how human mammary epithelial cells adapt before malignant transformation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify polymerase iota (Pol ι) as a context-dependent regulator of replication stress responses in BRCA2-deficient mammary epithelium. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of preneoplastic breast epithelium from BRCA2 mutation carriers revealed enrichment of POLI-positive hormone-sensing cells, while BRCA2 depletion increased nuclear Pol ι in mammary epithelial models. Functionally, Pol ι promoted post-S-phase DNA synthesis specifically in BRCA2-deficient cells.

title: Dietary diversity and its associations with sleep quality and chronotype in young and middle-aged adults
creator: Anda Zhao, Yiting Chen, Zhen Li, Qing Fan, Jiang Wu
description: BackgroundWhile sleep quality and chronotype are critical to wellbeing, the role of dietary diversity remains scarcely investigated, particularly among young and middle-aged adults. This study aimed to examine the associations of dietary diversity with sleep quality and chronotype, and to explore whether depression mediates these relationships.

title: Functional disability, diabetes and hypertension among adults in the United States, August 2021–August 2023
creator: Ying Liu, Piaopiao Chen, Yanmei Su, Juan Xie, Weiquan Zeng, Chun Pan
description: ObjectiveTo describe diabetes and hypertension prevalence, diagnosis status and measured-threshold outcomes by functional disability.MethodsWe analyzed the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted in the United States during August 2021–August 2023. Adults aged 18 years or older were classified using six Washington Group functioning domains. Outcome-specific weights and direct age standardization were used.

title: Oral Candida colonisation and cariogenic bacteria in children and adolescents with cleft lip and/or palate: A systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Muhammad Irpan Hendrawan, Elsa Ayu Amanda, Ita Purnama Alwi, Husni Mubarak, Irham Taufiqurrahman, Andi Tajrin
description: PurposeChildren with cleft lip and/or palate (CL/P) face a disproportionate cariogenic burden, yet the role of oral Candida and its partnership with cariogenic bacteria remains poorly quantified. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised observational evidence on oral Candida colonisation, cariogenic bacterial carriage, and clinical caries outcomes in non-syndromic CL/P, with GRADE-rated certainty.

title: Broad-spectrum antifungal activity of C12/C14 alkyl triphenylphosphonium salts (TPP-C12 and TPP-C14) against clinically relevant pathogens
creator: Yuanyuan Geng, Xiaohui Wang, Shu Zhang, Xuelian Liu, Huihui Liu, Xiaonan Guo, Yangzhen Lu, Jie Gong, Zhaohai Qin
description: IntroductionHuman fungal infections affect billions of people and result in more than 2 million deaths every year, however, they have historically been neglected as a cause of infectious disease-related deaths worldwide. Fungal drug resistance has become an increasingly serious problem with the wide use of antifungal drugs and the adaptive evolution of fungi.

title: From passive fillers to active implants: A 3D-printed trilayer piezoelectric scaffold recapitulating native bone hierarchy
creator: Yanbo Shan, Suyun Li, Yixuan Wang, Ye Lei, Gang Wang, Qing Zhou, Yuzheng Lu, Yanbin Wu, Hongyu Jiang, Zhengrui Zhou, Cheng Huang, Shaoyang Xu, Ning Wen, Yu Wei, Rujie He, Lisheng Zhao
description: Critical-sized alveolar bone defects affect over 10 million patients annually, yet current synthetic bone substitutes act as passive osteoconductive fillers with unpredictable outcomes. Native bone, by contrast, achieves robust regeneration through a trilayered hierarchy of cancellous, cortical, and metabolically active periosteal tissues, with intrinsic piezoelectricity converting mechanical loading into endogenous electrical cues.

title: Long-Term Trends and Regional Heterogeneity in Overweight and Obesity Among Adults — 11 Intermittent Surveys in China, 1991–2024
creator: Jiale Li, Xiaofan Zhang, Ziyu Zhang, Li Li, Chengdong Xu
description: What is already known about this topic?Overweight and obesity have increased in China. Evidence integrating long-term trends, regional heterogeneity, and multilevel factors remains limited.What is added by this report?From 1991 to 2024, age-standardized combined prevalence of overweight and obesity rose from 20.20% (1,567/8,445) to 53.10% (7,286/13,112) and obesity from 3.70% (259/8,445) to 18.10% (2,303/13,112).

title: Deciphering the profiles of grapevine microbiomes from rhizosphere-to-leaf compartments using multi-omic analysis
creator: Bo Wang, Zhuangwei Wang, Zhenxiao Chen, Jing Zhang, Xicheng Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionRoot- and leaf-associated microbiomes are crucial for plant health and influence the yield and quality of the products. The composition of microbes and their association with the host depend on different factors that must be continuously investigated.ResultsWe examined the composition and structure of bacterial and fungal communities in four compartments (root, rhizoplane, rhizosphere, and leaf endosphere) of two grapevine varieties (‘Alachua’ and ‘Noble’) targeting the 16S rRNA V5–V7 and ITS regions.Results and discussionA comparison of the effects of the varieties and compartments

title: Characterization of the glucosylated anthocyanin profile of 27 red grape (Vitis vinifera L.) varieties grown in Portugal: insights for climate change adaptation
creator: Miguel Baltazar, Eliana Monteiro, Sandra Pereira, Márcia Carvalho, Elisete Correia, Helena Ferreira, Vânia Silva, Joana Valente, Fernando Alves, Isaura Castro, Berta Gonçalves
description: IntroductionClimate change poses significant challenges to viticulture, increasing the need for sustainable adaptation strategies such as the identification of resilient Vitis vinifera L. varieties.MethodsThis study characterized the anthocyanin content, profile, and color parameters of 27 red grape varieties cultivated under the same terroir in the Douro Demarcated Region over two consecutive years.

title: Pain characterization in osteosarcopenia: an exploratory study
creator: Antimo Moretti, Marco Paoletta, Francesco P. Fabrazzo, Sara Liguori, Mariangela Airoma, Michele Tardugno, Francesca Gimigliano, Giovanni Iolascon
description: ObjectiveTo characterize pain in terms of frequency, intensity, and correlation with nutritional status, muscle mass, and physical performance in osteosarcopenic patients.MethodWe included patients affected by osteosarcopenia (OSP), according to WHO criteria and EWGSOP2 guidelines. Assessments included Bone Mineral Density, Trabecular Bone Score and Appendicular Lean Mass, Handgrip Strength, Short Physical Performance Battery, and SARC-F.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Hypertension–Diabetes–Dyslipidemia Clustering Among Adults — Hainan Province, China, 2023
creator: Juan Jiang, Tingting Ou, Ying Liu, Yang Cheng, Xingren Wang, Lu Zhong, Xiaohuan Wang, Saiku Chen, Bin He
description: What is already known about this topic?Hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia are metabolically interconnected. Although each may arise independently, shared pathophysiology commonly drives synergistic co-occurrence.What is added by this report?In Hainan, China's tropical island province, the weighted prevalence of hypertension–dyslipidemia comorbidity exceeded that of diabetes–dyslipidemia and hypertension–diabetes, as well as their triple comorbidity.

title: The degree of polymerization influences the effects of pectic oligosaccharide on intestinal histomorphology, barrier function and microbial community structure in broilers
creator: Chong Ling, Jiarong Fang, Songtao Liu, Shitang Zhang, Furui Liang, Hui Ye, Qingyun Cao, Jianjun Zuo, Weiwei Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to investigate whether the degree of polymerization (DP) influences intestinal health benefits of pectic oligosaccharide (POS) in broilers. A total of 360 one-day-old female Huanghua yellow-feathered broilers were randomly allocated into 3 groups (10 replicates/group), which received a basal diet alone or supplemented with 600 mg/kg low‑DP (DP = 10) POS (LPOS) or 600 mg/kg high‑DP (DP = 17) POS (HPOS) over a 21‑day experimental period.

title: A double-edged sword: interactions of CX3CL1/CX3CR1 and gut microbiota in systemic lupus erythematosus
creator: Rana A. Estaleen, Christopher M. Reilly, Xin M. Luo
description: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a systemic chronic disease initiated by an abnormal immune response to self and can affect multiple organs. SLE is characterized by the production of autoantibodies and the deposition of immune complexes. In regard to the clinical observations assessed by rheumatologists, several chemokines and cytokines also contribute to disease progression.

title: Ion-specific effects on the sonochemical degradation of Naphthol Blue Black: from inorganic salts to natural water matrices
creator: Hamza Ferkous, Muthupandian Ashokkumar, Oualid Hamdaoui
description: This study investigates the effects of inorganic salts and natural water matrices on the high-frequency sonochemical degradation of Naphthol Blue Black (NBB). Experiments were conducted at 585 kHz and 3.58 W/cm2 using initial NBB concentrations of 5 mg/L (8.11 × 10−6 M) and 30 mg/L (4.87 × 10−5 M).

title: Age-related changes of the tibial nerve cross-sectional area in the disabled elderly
creator: Kholoud J. Sandougah, Mohamed A. Bedewi, Saeed M. Alamri, Nawaf A. Alzain, Abdulrahman A. Alharthi, Mohammed Ayesh Zayed, Mohamed Sherif El-Sharkawy, Saleh M. Alfawaz, Husain Alturkistani, Elsayed Abbas Beheri, Rasha Ali, Muneerah Al-Aqeel, Sitah F. Alanazi, Mohammad W. Marashdeh
description: ObjectiveThis study aims to assess changes in the cross-sectional area of the tibial nerve in the disabled elderly.Materials and methodsThe study sample included 124 tibial nerves in 62 participants; 16 of which were disabled elderly patients (13 males, 3 females), with a mean age of 66.6, a mean height of 167.1 cm, a mean weight of 83.

title: Identifying Cardiac Autoantibody Biomarkers that Predict the Severity of Chagas Cardiomyopathy
creator: Heriks Ribeiro, Anton Dmitriev, Antonia Pereira Rosa Neta, Meena Fatah, Diptendu Chatterjee, Lea Campos de Oliveira, Fabiano Castro Albrecht, Hui Tzu Lin Wang, Juliana de Assis S. Gomes, Olgierd Woźniak, Karolina Borowiec, Elżbieta Katarzyna Biernacka, Antonia Claudia Jácome da Câmara, Luciana Sacil
description: Visual Abstract Chagas disease (ChD) is a tropical disease caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi. Endemic to Latin America, it results in more than 8,000 deaths annually.1 Recently, human migration and climate-driven changes in vector distribution have spread ChD to an additional 23 countries, including the United States, where endemic, local transmission has been documented.

title: Quantification of AMPA receptor subunits and RNA editing-related proteins in the J20 mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease by capillary western blotting
creator: Luke T. Milham, Gary P. Morris, Lyndsey M. Konen, Peggy Rentsch, Nesli Avgan, Bryce Vissel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionAccurate modelling of molecular changes in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia is crucial for understanding the mechanisms driving neuronal pathology and for developing treatments. Synaptic dysfunction has long been implicated as a mechanism underpinning memory dysfunction in AD and may result in part from changes in adenosine deaminase acting on RNA (ADAR) mediated RNA editing of the GluA2 subunit of AMPA receptors and changes in AMPA receptor function at the post synaptic cleft.

title: Left Ventricular Structural, Physiological, and Transcriptomic Abnormalities in a Novel Porcine Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Model
creator: Eric M Green, Carlos del Rio, Kamel Shibbani, David K Meyerholz, Joshua Gorham, Seong Kim, Daniel M DeLaughter, Marcus P Henze, Christopher S Rogers, Lindsey M Gifford, Melissa Kafa, Frank Rohret, J Adam Goeken, Jared M McLendon, Ryan L Boudreau, Christine E Seidman, Jessica C Sieren, Robert M Weiss
description: Visual AbstractKey words: cardiac myosin inhibitor, hemodynamics, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pig, transcriptome Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is the most common autosomal dominant cardiovascular disease, with a prevalence of up to 1 in 200.1 HCM is characterized by ventricular hypertrophy in the absence of exogenous stimuli such as hypertension, along with enhanced contractility.

title: An intron retention-derived secreted Endoglin Isoform as a circulating biomarker in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
creator: Hannah R Ortiz, Julia Podgorski, Monique R Archuleta, Atsushi Ishii, Aaron Ramonett, Christopher Cartmell, Nathan A Ellis, Paul R Langlais, Karthikeyan Mythreye, Nadine Hempel, Nam Y Lee
description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal malignancy with few effective strategies for early detection or prognostic assessment. Endoglin (CD105) is an endothelial receptor best known for its roles in vascular development and tumor angiogenesis, and its only recognized circulating form arises through proteolytic shedding of the full-length receptor.

title: The prevalence of off-label use and supratherapeutic blood levels of outpatient psychotropic medication in suicidal adolescents
creator: Isabel Hach, Thomas Bertsch, Patrick Nonell
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionAdolescents with mental disorders show an increased risk of suicidal phenomena. Vice versa, suicidality is a serious adverse event of psychotropic drug therapy in adolescents. There are only a few new psychotropic agents approved for this young age group.

title: Correlation between sagittal and inclined angles of cervical facet joints and cervical disc herniation: a radiological observational study
creator: Rui Weng, Hao Liu, Dongxin Lin, Haiwei Guo, Ling Mo, Hongjiang Liu, Genfu Zhu, Yikai Li, Caijun Liu, Xuecheng Huang, Zhensong Yao
description: BackgroundPrevious studies have found that asymmetry of cervical facet joints is associated with cervical disc herniation. However, the effect of facet joint angle on disc herniation is inconclusive. Further identification of the pathological anatomic features of cervical disc herniation is helpful for the prevention and treatment of the disease.

title: Inpatient burden of lung cancer and changes after a hospital performance reform: a real-world study
creator: Binbin Han, Xiaofang Chen
description: BackgroundLung cancer places a substantial burden on hospital inpatient care, particularly in tertiary cancer centers. Evidence remains limited on how hospital performance-based management reforms are associated with inpatient efficiency and costs among patients with lung cancer.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective, real-world study using inpatient administrative data from a tertiary cancer hospital in China between 2016 and 2020.

title: Age-associated trajectories of body composition at high altitude
creator: Martin Burtscher, Hannes Gatterer, Johannes Burtscher
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). social and historical determinants such as migration, socioeconomic conditions, conflict, and colonization. However, the relative contribution of these factors remains incompletely understood, and their interactions make it difficult to disentangle their individual effects [1,2]. Despite this substantial heterogeneity, aging is generally associated with progressive changes in body composition, including declines in skeletal muscle and fat-free mass and alterations in adipose tissue distribution, with trajectories that differ between men and women [3].

title: Disease Activity During Pregnancy and Postpartum in Women With Multiple Sclerosis Treated With Ocrelizumab or Rituximab Before Pregnancy
creator: Nadine Bast, Karen Dost-Kovalsky, Sabrina Haben, Laura Witt, Ralf Gold, Sandra Thiel, Kerstin Hellwig
description: Background and ObjectivesPreliminary data suggest sustained disease control with ocrelizumab (OCR) or rituximab (RTX) in women with multiple sclerosis (MS) after pregnancy suspension; however, the influence of washout duration and cumulative dosing remains unknown. This study investigates disease activity during and after pregnancy in women with relapsing-remitting MS treated with OCR/RTX before pregnancy.

title: Phosphate accumulation in rice leaves promotes fungal pathogenicity and represses host immune responses during pathogen infection
creator: Héctor Martín-Cardoso, Mireia Bundó, Beatriz Val-Torregrosa, Blanca San Segundo
description: Rice is one of the most important crops in the world and a staple food for more than half of the world’s population. At present, the blast disease caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae poses a severe threat to food security through reduction of rice yields worldwide. High phosphate fertilization has previously been shown to increase blast susceptibility.

title: Management strategies for isolated premature thelarche: a risk-stratified clinical pathway favoring “watchful waiting”
creator: Yan Xu, Hongtao Cui, Xinna Wang, Fang Liu
description: Isolated Premature Thelarche (PT) is a common clinical issue in pediatric endocrinology. Because its early presentation resembles that of Central Precocious Puberty (CPP), which requires intervention, its management is highly controversial, caught between “active intervention” and “watchful waiting.” This leads to inconsistent clinical practices and significant anxiety for affected families.

title: Advancing genetic pathogenicity prediction with three-dimensional proteoform-phenotype analysis
creator: Young Joo Sun, Gabriel Velez, Angela Li, Aarushi Kumar, Jennifer T Vu, Claudia Phillips, Ditte K Rasmussen, Jin Kyun Oh, Mauricio G S Costa, Stephen H Tsang, Yang Sun, Alexander G Bassuk, Vinit B Mahajan
description: Ascertaining the pathogenicity and clinical relevance of genetic mutations is a longstanding challenge across human disease. This is particularly relevant for genes with many variants of unknown significance (VUS), such as PRPH2-retinopathy, where complex variable phenotype patterns and limited genotype correlations hinder application of precision-medicine therapies.

title: Effect of swelling agent treatment on grape fruit quality and the application of electronic nose identification detection
creator: Jianlei Qiao, Guoqiang Su, Liang Yuan, Lin Wu, Xiaohui Weng, Shuang Liu, Yucai Feng, Dan Jiang, Yuxuan Chen, Yuan Ma
description: The swelling agent is a plant growth regulator that alters the composition and content of nutrients and volatile gases in the fruit. To identify whether grape fruit had been treated with swelling agent, the odor information and quality indexes of grape berries treated with different concentrations of swelling agent were examined by using electronic nose technology and traditional methods.

title: Interactive effects of dietary protein and fiber levels on total tract and apparent ileal nutrient digestibility, microbiota profiling, and fermentation products in pigs fed a blend of branched-chain volatile fatty acids
creator: Angie P. Benavides-Infante, Anlly M. Fresno-Rueda, Lucas Alves Rodrigues, Michael T. Socha, Tatiane Fernandes, Benoit St-Pierre, Jorge Y. Perez-Palencia, Crystal L. Levesque
description: IntroductionThe experiment investigated the interactions between diet protein and fiber and branched-chain volatile fatty acids (BCVFA) on nutrient digestion, fermentation products, and microbiome modulation in pigs.MethodsFourteen cannulated pigs (body weight 20.4 ± 1.4 kg) were used in a replicated 6 × 5 Youden square design with 6 diets and 5 periods for at least 11 observations per dietary treatment.

title: Heavy metal exposures and constipation among United States adults
creator: Huanhuan Lin, Shijian Wang
description: Constipation is a common gastrointestinal disorder that can substantially impair quality of life. Environmental exposure to heavy metals has been implicated in gastrointestinal dysfunction; however, population-based evidence regarding their associations with constipation remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of blood lead, mercury, and cadmium levels with constipation among US adults.

title: Outcomes of sequential keratoplasty for bilateral gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy
creator: Mohammed M. Abusayf, Rana Alhumaemydi, Abeer Alkhodier, Majed AlKharashi
description: Rationale:Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy (GDLD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by subepithelial amyloid deposition, progressive corneal opacification, and recurrent erosions. GDLD may present during the first decade of life and interfere with visual development. It may recur after keratoplasty, complicating surgical management.

title: Current situation and factors influencing elderly care in community day care centers: a cross-sectional study
creator: Junyu Chen, Yuan Zhu, Yulei Song, Yongqi Liang, Lulu Wang, Weitong Li, Huimei Wang, Guihua Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe latest census data show that people over 60 years of age account for about 18.7% of the total population in China, and the aging of the population has become an irreversible trend in the 21st century.

title: Patterns and associated factors of health literacy among residents aged 15–69 in Zhejiang, China: a latent profile analysis
creator: Shuiyang Xu, Yunfang Zhou, Mingyu Huang, Xinyu Wen, Xuehai Zhang, Yue Xu, Dingming Yao, Xiujing Hu, Heni Chen, Chun Chen, Xiangyang Zhang
description: BackgroundHealth literacy plays an important role in disease prevention and control. The aim of this study is to explore the health literacy patterns and associated factors among residents in Zhejiang Province.MethodsThis study included 56,863 residents aged 15–69 years from the 2024 Zhejiang Province Health Literacy Survey.

title: Analysis of a case of immune-related pancreatitis induced by anti-PD-1 antibody therapy for gastric cancer
creator: Fengyun Zhang, Wenhua Xiao
description: Background:Immune-related pancreatitis is a rare but clinically significant adverse event associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Early recognition and appropriate management are essential to prevent potentially serious outcomes. Herein, we report a case of suspected immune-related pancreatitis during nivolumab-based immunotherapy for metastatic gastric cancer.

title: The role of probiotics in modulation of the gut-brain axis: a prospective therapy for depression and mood disorders
creator: Hui Wang, Yining Chen, Allen Zhao, Zhongxia Shen, Yu Zhang
description: The gut-brain axis is a bidirectional pathway linking the gastrointestinal microbiota to neurological functions. While its significance in the pathogenesis of gastrointestinal conditions is well-documented, emerging evidence indicates that dysbiosis of the gut microbiota could also be implicated in various neuropsychiatric disorders, specifically major depressive disorder (MDD).

title: Benefit finding in adults living with somatic non-communicable chronic disease: a systematic review on the mean level and the prevalence
creator: Zhunzhun Liu, Xiang Hu, Volker Arndt, Melissa S. Y. Thong
description: IntroductionBenefit finding (BF) refers to the phenomenon of identifying positive changes from challenging circumstances. This review aimed to comprehensively assess the BF prevalence in persons with somatic non-communicable chronic diseases (pSNCDs).Materials and methodsElectronic databases were systematically searched using the concept “benefit finding”.

title: Dietary vitamin B1 intake and stroke risk in U.S. adults
creator: Zhi Li, Min Fu, Li Wang, Qiong Chen, Guang Yao, Qianhua Dai, Lili Jiang, Yangzhou Xu
description: Stroke imposes a substantial global burden of mortality and long-term disability, and its occurrence is driven by diverse vascular risk factors. As an essential micronutrient, vitamin B1 (thiamin) has been implicated in cardiovascular protection, yet whether habitual dietary intake of this vitamin relates to stroke occurrence remains incompletely understood.

title: Association of NK cells with a shift in tryptophan catabolism in patients with heart failure after a single exercise exertion
creator: Krithika Swaminathan, Bita Astan, Sabine Kaczmarek, Kristin Lehnert, Anke Hannemann, Aycen Koc, Nele Friedrich, Kathrin Budde, Ann-Kristin Henning, Grażyna Domańska, Ulf Landmesser, Christian Templin, Marcus Dörr, Martin Bahls, Nicolle Kränkel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTryptophan (TRP) metabolism via the kynurenine (KYN) pathway links immune function, energy metabolism, and redox homeostasis. Dysregulation of this pathway has been implicated in inflammatory conditions and heart failure. Here, we investigated the acute effects of exercise on TRP-KYN metabolism and its relationship with natural killer (NK) cell function in controls and patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).MethodsControl (n=13) and HFrEF (n=16) groups had comparable composition regarding age and sex.

title: Risk factors for post-PCI restenosis in patients with coronary heart disease and the development and validation of a nomogram prediction model
creator: Xin Jin, Zhengliang Dong, Dongsheng Chai
description: This study aimed to analyze risk factors for in-stent restenosis (ISR) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with coronary heart disease and develop and validate a nomogram prediction model. Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 1135 patients with coronary heart disease who underwent PCI at our hospital between January 2015 and December 2024.

title: Mechanistic and therapeutic dimensions of DcR3-mediated immunomodulation in sepsis
creator: Bilal Abbas, Xinrui Lin, Chen Xu, Qi Chen, Jingqian Su
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by dysregulated host-immune responses, progressing through hyperinflammatory and immunosuppressive stages. Decoy receptor 3 (DcR3), a soluble member of the TNF receptor superfamily, serves as an immunomodulator in sepsis. Beyond neutralizing FasL, LIGHT, and TL1A to block apoptosis and inflammatory signaling, DcR3 regulates macrophage polarization, dendritic cell maturation, and immune cell survival through its heparan sulfate proteoglycan-binding domain.

title: Associated factors and a prognostic model for 28-day mortality in Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection
creator: Zhanpeng Yu, Zeyun Lin, Xiaoyan Tian, Zhenle Zhang, Chuyue Zhou, Yuntao He, Huiyan Wu, Yanling Zhang, Liang Peng
description: This study aimed to identify factors associated with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection (S aureus BSI), compare 28-day survival after propensity score matching (PSM), and develop a prognostic model for 28-day mortality. Adult intensive care unit patients with culture-confirmed BSI were identified in Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV.

title: Global scientific trends on thyroid disease in early 21st century: a bibliometric and visualized analysis
creator: Mingyuan Song, Wei Sun, Qi Liu, Zhongqing Wang, Hao Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundBibliometrics has been used to analyze the literature in the field of thyroid disease studies in the early 21st century, indicating the changes in current international study trends.MethodsIn this study, a bibliometric analysis of data retrieved from the Web of Science (WoS) database was conducted, and the publication trends and thematic evolution in the field of thyroid disease research from January 1, 2000, to November 16, 2022, were analyzed.

title: Maternal undernutrition results in transcript changes in male offspring that may promote resistance to high fat diet induced weight gain
creator: Tiffany K. Miles, Melody L. Allensworth-James, Angela K. Odle, Ana Rita Silva Moreira, Anessa C. Haney, Alex N. LaGasse, Allen J. Gies, Stephanie D. Byrum, Angelica M. Riojas, Melanie C. MacNicol, Angus M. MacNicol, Gwen V. Childs
description: Maternal nutrition during embryonic development and lactation influences multiple aspects of offspring health. Using mice, this study investigates the effects of maternal caloric restriction (CR) during mid-gestation and lactation on offspring neonatal development and on adult metabolic function when challenged by a high fat diet (HFD).

title: Exploring the nano-wonders: unveiling the role of Nanoparticles in enhancing salinity and drought tolerance in plants
creator: Abdul Rehman, Sana Khan, Fenlei Sun, Zhen Peng, Keyun Feng, Ning Wang, Yinhua Jia, Zhaoe Pan, Shoupu He, Lidong Wang, Abdul Qayyum, Xiongming Du, Hongge Li
description: Plants experience diverse abiotic stresses, encompassing low or high temperature, drought, water logging and salinity. The challenge of maintaining worldwide crop cultivation and food sustenance becomes particularly serious due to drought and salinity stress. Sustainable agriculture has significant promise with the use of nano-biotechnology.

title: Mycoplasma infection aggravates cardiac involvements in Kawasaki diseases: a retrospective study
creator: Guoyan Lu, Xing Li, Jie Tang, Yuxi Jin, Yang Wang, Kaiyu Zhou, Yifei Li
description: Background Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) infection serves as a substantial cofactor in Kawasaki disease (KD) among patients. Although the dominant issue triggering KD has recently focused on MP infection, the complete demonstration of the relationship between MP infection and KD remains elusive. This study endeavors to scrutinize and compare the clinical manifestations and cardiac involvement between MP-triggered KD and non-infection–associated KD.

title: Tobacco-attributable burden of alzheimer’s disease and other dementias in China and ASEAN
creator: Piaoyun Wen, Wenwen Liu, Yanjiang Li, Mengmeng Liao, Haofeng Qin, Jiaxi Ye, Ziyong Deng, Shuqi Cui, Yongli Zhao, Xiaowen Wang, Yingzi Huang, Huamin Tang, Hui Qin, Kaihua Wang, Qijing Qin
description: This study aimed to systematically analyze the disease burden of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias (ADOD) attributed to tobacco in China and ASEAN countries from 1990 to 2021, and predict the disease burden in the next ten years to characterize the disparities in disease burden between the 2 sides, and to conduct a preliminary exploration of factors that may be

title: Rapid authentication of endangered Cistanche Herba (Rou Cong Rong) using a high-throughput multi-SNP panel and MALDI-TOF MS platform
creator: Rong Lei, Yixia Cao, Yifen Yang, Haolong Cong, Limei Li, Xin Li, Junxia Shi
description: Cistanche Herba (Rou Cong Rong), a critically endangered edible tonic and medicinal plant, is traditionally valued for its nephroprotective and kidney-yang tonifying properties. However, wild populations are declining due to habitat loss, overharvesting, and increasing market demand, leading to widespread adulteration in commercial supplies.

title: The effects of intermittent fasting for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS): a systematic review
creator: Xiaoxiao Lin, Shuai Wang, Yue Gao
description: Some studies have investigated the impact of intermittent fasting (IF) for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). We aimed to conduct a comprehensive systematic review to analyze and summarize all clinical studies concerning the effects of IF on patients with MS. We conducted an exhaustive review of information available in the Embase, Cochrane, and PubMed databases up until 1 September 2023.

title: Potato and warm moist compresses to accelerate healing of limb swelling and bruising after venous stent placement
creator: Qin Zhang, Zhuoyin Wang, Hongqun Zhang, Xiaojuan Han, Jiani Bao, Yaru Yang, Qi Chen
description: Rationale:Hemodialysis is an essential renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease, and an autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is preferred because of its durability and low complication rate. Maintaining AVF patency is critical for effective dialysis. AVF stenosis may reduce blood flow, impair dialysis adequacy, and compromise vascular access function.

title: Computational reconstruction of evolutionary selection in human brain networks
creator: Lukasz Piszczek, Clara Fazzari, Sophia Ulonska, Katja Bühler, Wulf Haubensak
description: IntroductionThe accumulation of genomic and brain data opens new opportunities for resource friendly, data driven brain exploration. A key challenge is to develop versatile and accessible strategies that integrate and mine multimodal datasets for novel neuroscientific insights. Here, we optimized an integrated workflow for mapping multigenic evolutionary traits in the human brain across cognitive, cellular, and molecular levels.

title: The Na/K-ATPase role as a signal transducer in lung inflammation
creator: Adriana Ribeiro Silva, Kauê Franscisco Correa de Souza e Souza, Thamires Bandeira De Souza, Mauricio Younes-Ibrahim, Patrícia Burth, Hugo Caire de Castro Faria Neto, Cassiano Felippe Gonçalves-de-Albuquerque
description: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is marked by damage to the capillary endothelium and alveolar epithelium following edema formation and cell infiltration. Currently, there are no effective treatments for severe ARDS. Pathologies such as sepsis, pneumonia, fat embolism, and severe trauma may cause ARDS with respiratory failure. The primary mechanism of edema clearance is the epithelial cells’ Na/K-ATPase (NKA) activity.

title: Physics informed neural network framework for non-similar nano-heat and solutal transport in a rheological fluid over a stretching cylinder
creator: Muhammad Naveed Khan, Hameed Ullah Khan, N. Ameer Ahammad, Nurul Amira Zainal, Nadia Ayari
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Accurate prediction of non-similar momentum, thermal and solutal transport phenomena in rheological fluids is crucial for the design and optimization of advanced thermal management systems, heat exchangers, polymer processing, chemical reactors, energy conversion devices and biomedical transport processes. Motivated by these engineering applications, this study presents a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for analyzing magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection flow of a Jeffrey fluid over a stretching horizontal cylinder embedded in a Darcy porous medium.

title: Combined qualitative and quantitative MRI reveals short-term progression in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy
creator: Anna-Lena Mayer, Anika Starke, Valentina Schunk, Matthias Türk, Michael Uder, Arnd Dörfler, Armin M. Nagel, Pierre-Yves Baudin, Elisabetta Gazzerro, Teresa Gerhalter
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is characterized by slowly progressive and heterogeneous muscle involvement; therefore, clinical measures show limited sensitivity to short-term change. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides useful biomarkers of muscle degeneration and disease activity. To investigate one-year longitudinal changes in lower leg muscles of patients with FSHD using qualitative (T1-weighted [T1w], STIR) and quantitative MRI (fat fraction [FF], water T2), and to assess their relationship with clinical function.

title: Prevalence and correlates of severe anxiety in patients with first hospitalization for major depressive disorder combined with dyslipidemia: a large sample cross-sectional study
creator: Huimin Yin, Qi Zhang, Yi Li, Jun Ma
description: BackgroundAnxiety symptoms and dyslipidemia are common co-morbidities in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), and there are complex pathophysiologic as well as clinical mechanisms underlying the association between the three. In this study, we investigated the prevalence and associated factors of severe anxiety in first-time hospitalized patients with MDD with dyslipidemia.

title: Proton-density fat-saturated non-contrast MR imaging is comparable to post-contrast MR imaging for revealing wrist synovitis
creator: Su Wu, James Francis Griffith, João Dourado, Lai Shan Tam
description: ObjectivesStandard MR imaging (MRI) for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients comprises a post-contrast T1-fat-saturated (T1FS + C) sequence to detect wrist synovitis and tenosynovitis. This study investigates whether non-contrast sequences can provide similar information to post-contrast imaging.Materials and methodsSeventy-seven RA patients (F/M: 64/13; age: 61 ± 12 years) underwent MRI examination of the most symptomatic wrist on a 3.0-T system.

title: Recurrent CIC-rearranged sarcoma of central nervous system: a clinicopathological case report
creator: Shan Jiang, Kay Ka-Wai Li, Jingqi Hu, Yun Guan, Rui-Ze Zhu, Hou-Shi Xu, Mao-Yuan Sun, Bei-Ning Liu, Hui-Hui Chai, Yue Wang, Qi-Sheng Tang, Ho-Keung Ng, Zhi-Feng Shi
description: CIC-rearranged sarcoma (CRS) is a subgroup of small round blue cell tumors similar to Ewing’s sarcoma but lacking the EWSR1 gene translocation. It is characterized by a CIC gene rearrangement on chromosome 19q13, with the most common partner gene being DUX4.

title: Imaging in localized intrahepatic bile duct dilatation: a pictorial review of diagnostic and differential approaches
creator: Yongyi Cen, Xiaoqi Zhou, Mimi Tang, Yanjin Qin, Chenyu Song, Jifei Wang, Yanji Luo, Zhi Dong, Hongyan Dai, Zhibing Ruan, Zhenpeng Peng, Shi-Ting Feng
description: Localized intrahepatic bile duct dilatation (LIBD) is a prevalent radiological finding characterized by a variety of etiologies, including congenital anomalies, inflammatory conditions, hepatolithiasis, and neoplastic lesions. Accurate differential diagnosis of diseases associated with LIBD is crucial for formulating appropriate treatment strategies and improving patient prognosis.

title: Exploring Family Interactions: Heterogeneity in Family Specific Network Models
creator: Lea Schumacher, Daniela Hartmann, Felix Vogel
description: Daily family interactions have a profound impact on children's emotional and behavioral development. While extensive research highlights the detrimental effects of negative parenting practices and the benefits of positive parenting programs, less is known about the complex within‐family interactions that occur on a day‐to‐day basis.

title: The diagnostic value of high-resolution 3D T2-weighted MRI in preoperative evaluation and classification of Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: a prospective study
creator: Yafei Qi, Shuang Song, Xin Gao, Shu Wang, Yiwei Zhang, Yonglan He, Peng Zhang, Menglin Huang, Huadan Xue, Lan Zhu
description: ObjectiveHerlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome (HWWS) is a rare female reproductive tract malformation. Accurate preoperative diagnosis and classification are vital for surgical planning. This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic value of high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) T2-weighted MRI in the preoperative assessment and classification of HWWS.Materials and methodsThe study prospectively enrolled 84 patients clinically diagnosed with HWWS between May 2020 and January 2025.

title: Molecular mechanisms of corpus callosum development: a four-step journey
creator: Maria Gavrish, Angelina Kustova, Juan C. Celis Suescún, Paraskevi Bessa, Natalia Mitina, Victor Tarabykin
description: The Corpus Callosum (CC) is a bundle of axons connecting the cerebral hemispheres. It is the most recent structure to have appeared during evolution of placental mammals. Its development is controlled by a very complex interplay of many molecules. In humans it contains almost 80% of all commissural axons in the brain.

title: The role of satisfaction with care among factors affecting health-related quality of life in people with cancer: a cross-sectional study
creator: Federica Sancassiani, Goce Kalcev, Mirian Agus, Olga Mulas, Elena Massa, Diego Primavera, Giulia Origa, Mariarita Monni, Veronica Vacca, Francesca Pibiri, Antonio Egidio Nardi, Clelia Madeddu, Giovanni Caocci, Mario Scartozzi, Marco Cruciata, Rosangela Caruso, Maria Giulia Nanni, Martino Belvederi M
description: BackgroundDespite advances in therapies that have increased the duration of post-diagnosis survival, living with long-term adverse effects of cancer and its treatment is common. This study aims to evaluate satisfaction with care (SC) as a dimension affecting Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) among people with cancer, considering other sociodemographic and clinical variables supposedly impacting HRQoL.

title: Assessment of Compliance With Infection Prevention Guidelines/Standard Precautions Among Healthcare Workers of Debark and Metema General Hospitals, Northwest Ethiopia
creator: Mequanente Dagnaw, Meera Indracti, Dinesh Govindraj
description: IntroductionHealthcare‐associated infections remain a major public health problem, especially in low‐resource settings. Adherence to infection prevention (IP) guidelines reduces infection transmission and improves patient safety, yet poor compliance remains common in developing countries, including Ethiopia. Evidence from Debark and Metema General Hospitals is limited.

title: DSCA-PSPNet: Dynamic spatial-channel attention pyramid scene parsing network for sugarcane field segmentation in satellite imagery
creator: Yujian Yuan, Lina Yang, Kan Chang, Youju Huang, Haoyan Yang, Jiale Wang
description: Sugarcane plays a vital role in many global economies, and its efficient cultivation is critical for sustainable development. A central challenge in sugarcane yield prediction and cultivation management is the precise segmentation of sugarcane fields from satellite imagery. This task is complicated by numerous factors, including varying environmental conditions, scale variability, and spectral similarities between crops and non-crop elements.

title: Case Report: A case of myocardial calcification combined with abnormal Q waves on electrocardiogram
creator: Dan Li, Qixiang Huang, Xiaoxian Situ, Weidong Gao, Dong Li
description: BackgroundMyocardial infarction is the most common cause of pathological Q waves on electrocardiogram (ECG), but other conditions that cause myocardial injury or abnormal conduction (such as cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, cardiac tumors or amyloidosis, WPW, etc.) can also produce pathological Q waves. Whether myocardial calcification can lead to pathological Q waves remains uncertain.

title: An inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL)-based peptide therapy for proteinuric kidney diseases targeting αvβ3 integrin
creator: Alexis P Jimenez-Uribe, Yan Xu, Yanxia Cao, Ryan Spear, Kwi Hye Koh, Adrian P Mansini, Ariana G Alcantar, Felix Kliewe, Nicole Endlich, Jochen Reiser, Steve Mangos, Eunsil Hahm
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dysregulated αvβ3 integrin activation in podocytes contributes to proteinuric kidney disease by disrupting podocyte architecture and the glomerular filtration barrier. However, no treatments currently exist that therapeutically target this integrin. We previously identified inducible co-stimulator ligand (ICOSL) as an endogenous antagonist of αvβ3 integrin that protects kidney function through its arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) motif, independent of its canonical role in immunity.
