creator: Remedios Aguilar-Moya, Raquel Ibáñez-Martínez, David Melero-Fuentes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In recent years, there has been considerable concern about the deterioration of mental health in children and adolescents, and there is a coincidence between mental disorders and addictive disorders. In view of this situation, it is important to review preventive interventions from the educational field, since it is considered an area of socialization par excellence of the subjects that can avoid or reduce exposure to adversities at an early age. For this purpose, a narrative review was carried out.

title: Pediatric-adult split liver transplantation: an ethical imperative and systems-based roadmap for global expansion
creator: Tran Cong Duy Long, Huynh Tran Bao Chau, Dat Tien Le, Thi Tran Nguyen Minh, Bui Cong Minh, Anh Le Thien Diep, Hoang Bao Tran Van, Truc Thi Thu Huynh, Nguyen Tien Huy
description: This paradox emphasizes the urgent need to re-engineer transplant systems around pediatric-adult split liver transplantation (SLT). Despite being as effective as whole-liver transplants, SLT remains underutilized due to logistical and policy barriers. We believe that expanding SLT is not only clinically acceptable but a just and effective moral necessity.

title: Detect de novo expressed ORFs in transcriptomes with DESwoMAN
creator: Anna Grandchamp, Marie Lebherz, Elias Dohmen
description: De novo gene emergence refers to the process by which new genes arise from mutations in previously non-coding genomic regions. Investigating early stages of de novo gene emergence is essential for understanding the mechanisms that enable gene formation from scratch. Several workflows have been developed to detect and study the early stage of de novo gene emergence in specific species.

title: Whole genome sequencing and annotation of Daedaleopsis sinensis, a wood-decaying fungus significantly degrading lignocellulose
creator: Jin-Xin Ma, Hao Wang, Can Jin, Yi-Fan Ye, Lu-Xin Tang, Jing Si, Jie Song
description: Daedaleopsis sinensis is a fungus that grows on wood and secretes a series of enzymes to degrade cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin and cause wood rot decay. Wood-decaying fungi have ecological, economic, edible, and medicinal functions. Furthermore, the use of microorganisms to biodegrade lignocellulose has high application value.

title: Parathyroid carcinoma as an overlooked etiology of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women: a case report
creator: Jing Su, Shiqiong Lei, Meiyuan Jin, Hongzhi Hu, Wenshan He
description: Parathyroid carcinoma (PC), an extremely rare endocrine malignancy, disrupts calciumphosphorus homeostasis and lead to musculoskeletal system disorders including osteoporosis, bone pain and pathological fractures. For postmenopausal women, osteoporosis is a common disease. Therefore, secondary osteoporosis is often overlooked in this demographic. We report a 54-year-old woman presenting to Orthopedics Department due to arthralgia diagnosed with severe postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO).

title: Biallelic loss-of-function PTPN6 variants lead to inflammatory lung disease and hemolytic anemia
creator: S. Farshid Moussavi-Harami, Matt S. Zinter, Marialetizia Motta, Luca Pannone, Paolo Calligari, Luca Mignini, Anne Slavotinek, Pierre-Marie Martin, Henry Sanchez, Lauren Sanchez, Iman Ragab, Clare L. Abram, Martin Broly, Yasmina Abi Ayad, Amina Serradj, Guilaine Boursier, Aida M. Bertoli-Avella, Muku
description: Moussavi-Harami et al. report that biallelic loss-of-function variants in PTPN6, encoding the immune-regulatory phosphatase SHP1, cause anemia and fatal lung hyperinflammation in families from diverse ethnic backgrounds. Introduction Severe inflammatory lung diseases, such as acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), contribute significantly to morbidity and mortality.

title: The physiological function of squalene and its application prospects in animal husbandry
creator: Xin Du, Xue Ma, Yang Gao
description: Squalene, which is a natural triterpenoid unsaturated hydrocarbon, is abundant in shark liver and plant seeds. Squalene has various physiological functions such as being anti-inflammatory and antioxidant. This paper reviews the physiological functions of squalene and its application prospects in livestock and poultry production, with a view to providing a theoretical basis for its in-depth application in animal husbandry.

title: An intronic micro-deletion impacts the transcription and translation of PKD1 gene
creator: Wei Zheng, Xinli Xing, Xuejing Sun, Na Wei
description: Polycystin-1 (PC1), encoded by the PKD1 gene, forms a complex with polycystin-2 (PKD2; 173910) that regulates multiple signaling pathways to maintain normal renal tubular structure and function. Mutations in the PKD1 gene are the primary cause of type 1 PKD (polycystic kidney disease), accounting for 78%–85% of all PKD cases.

title: A dynamically frustrated allosteric checkpoint consistent with conformational proofreading in CRISPR–Cas9
creator: Jianxiang Huang, Jiacheng Wei, Huazhang Chen, Xin Qiao, Ning Liu, Shaoyong Lu
description: CRISPR–Cas9 DNA cleavage requires R-loop extension to activate the histidine–asparagine–histidine (HNH) nuclease domain, yet how heteroduplex maturation gates catalytic commitment remains unclear. Using extensive molecular dynamics simulations across seven experimentally trapped heteroduplex states (6–18 nt), we define a three-stage activation pathway: unlocking, preorganization, and precatalytic gating.

title: Future impact of thymoquinone-loaded nanoemulsion in rabbits: prospects for enhancing growth, immunity, antioxidant potential and resistance against Pasteurella multocida
creator: Marwa I. Abd El-Hamid, Mona M. El-Azzouny, Rania M. S. El-Malt, Mona E. Elkenawy, Abdelwahab A. Abdelwarith, Elsayed M. Younis, Wessam Youssef, Rehab E. Dawod, Dalia W. A. H. Elged, Manal A. M. Habaka, Amal S. A. El Oksh, Soad Mekawy, Simon J. Davies, Doaa Ibrahim
description: Phytochemical nanoemulsions, such as thymoquinone nanoemulsions (TQN), are regarded as innovative alternatives to antimicrobials that significantly improve the performance, digestion, antioxidant potential and immunity of rabbits. Thus, the potential effects of TQN on growth, digestibility, antioxidant potential, immunity and resistance against Pasteurella multocida (P. multocida) in rabbits were assessed.

title: High prevalence of intestinal protozoan infections among asymptomatic individuals in rural and urban communities in conflict-affected Northwest Cameroon
creator: Calvin B. Ebai, Irene U. Ajonina-Ekoti, Joyceline B. Ndonwi, Nicoline F. Tanih, Flore N. Ngoufo, Marcelus U. Ajonina
description: BackgroundIntestinal protozoan infections remain an important public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa. In Cameroon, there is limited evidence comparing the epidemiology of intestinal protozoan infections in rural and urban settings. This study determined the prevalence of intestinal protozoan infections, identified associated factors, and compared selected diagnostic techniques among asymptomatic individuals in rural and urban communities of Northwest Cameroon.

title: Malignant transformation of endometriosis into endometrioid ovarian carcinoma with a contralateral borderline seromucinous tumour: A rare case report
creator: T Kiruthika, Damodar R Rao, Asha Rao, G Padmashri
description: BackgroundEndometriosis-associated ovarian cancer is uncommon and is most often represented by endometrioid and clear cell carcinomas. Synchronous contralateral borderline ovarian tumours are uncommon and may be missed when gross intraoperative assessment is reassuring.CaseA 43-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of endometriosis for approximately 5 years presented with worsening pelvic pain and menstrual symptoms. A left ovarian endometrioma increased from 6.

title: Photovoice, emotional health, and structural inequalities: adolescent voices from an intercultural neighborhood in the global south
creator: Matías Araya-Tessini, María Sol Anigstein Vidal, Alicia Arias-Schreiber Muñoz, Constanza Jacques-Aviñó
description: IntroductionThe research is framed within the Latin American collective health perspective, which understands emotional well-being as a relational and situated phenomenon shaped by social determinants. We aimed explores how a group of cisgender and non-binary adolescent girls from Global South construct and give meaning to their emotional well-being in a context marked by structural inequalities, migration, and cultural diversity.

title: FACS-based isolation and recovery of physiologically distinct bacterial subpopulations from infected insect hosts
creator: Hasna Toukabri, Christophe Buisson, Yves Le Vern, Alix Sausset, Mickaël Bourge, Leyla Slamti
description: Phenotypic heterogeneity is often encountered during infection but remains challenging to investigate in vivo. Here, using the entomopathogenic spore-former Bacillus thuringiensis with the Galleria mellonella insect larva infection model and Fluorescence-Activated Cell Sorting (FACS), we present a workflow that enables the isolation of bacterial subpopulations in distinct physiological states, directly from infected hosts, for downstream characterization.

title: Efficacy of immune-oncology combinations versus sunitinib in patients with bone metastases from renal cell carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of phase III trials with long-term follow-up
creator: Clara Fish Araujo de Albuquerque, Leila Caroline Souza Reis, Eliza Del Fiol Manna, Ana Elisa Saragossa Zafalon, Angela Theresa Zuffo Yabrude, Camillo Porta
description: BackgroundBone metastases occur in approximately one-third of patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and are associated with poor prognosis. Although immune-oncology (IO)-based combinations are the standard first-line treatment, the relative efficacy of IO plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor (IO+TKI) versus dual immunotherapy (IO+IO) in this subgroup remains uncertain.

title: Vigorous physical activity is associated with mental well-being: indirect associations via resilience and physical self-esteem in university students
creator: Manman Shi, Xia (Sebastiane) Chen, Binfeng Yuan
description: This cross-sectional study examined whether resilience and physical self-esteem statistically account for the association between vigorous physical activity (VPA) and mental well-being among university students. A total of 2,432 undergraduates from three universities in Guangdong, China completed validated measures of VPA (IPAQ-SF), resilience (CD-RISC-10), physical self-esteem (PSPP–Physical Self-Worth), and mental well-being (WHO-5).

title: New Delhi Metallo-β-Lactamase Plasmidomes of Intensive Care Unit Clinical and Environmental Enterobacterales Isolates
creator: Florencia Martino, Denise De Belder, Renata Monge, Agustina Forastiero, Molly Patrick, Kara A Moser, Alejandra Corso, Fernando Pasteran, Matthew Robinson, Valeria Fabre
description: BackgroundThere are limited data on the molecular epidemiology of New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)–producing carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) in Latin America, despite the high burden of NDM-CRE in the region. This study characterized blaNDM-harboring plasmids from CRE from patients and the environment of an Argentine hospital.

title: Plant mediated synthesis of flower-like Cu2O microbeads from Artimisia campestris L. extract for the catalyzed synthesis of 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole derivatives
creator: Halla Abdelbaki, Amar Djemoui, Lahcene Souli, Ahmed Souadia, Mohammed Ridha Ouahrani, Brahim Djemoui, Mokhtar Boualem Lahrech, Mohammed Messaoudi, Ilham Ben Amor, Adel Benarfa, Ali Alsalme, Mikhael Bechelany, Ahmed Barhoum
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study presents a novel method for synthesizing 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazole derivatives through a one-pot, multi-component addition reaction using flower-like Cu2O microbeads as a catalyst. The flower-like Cu2O microbeads were synthesized using an aqueous extract of Artimisia Campestris L. This extract demonstrated the capability to reduce and stabilize Cu2O particles during their initial formation, resulting in the formation of a porous flower-like morphology.

title: Temporal interpretation of right ventricular strain after pulmonary embolism
creator: Hasan Burak Isleyen, Sercan Bulut
description: % confidence interval 1.01–1.21).1 The timing of outcome onset relative to the 3-month scan determines the clinical interpretation of this association. In the parent FOCUS study, PPEI was a combination of persistent or worsening clinical, functional, biochemical, and imaging abnormalities assessed during follow-up.2 Some participants may therefore have met PPEI criteria by the time of the three-month echocardiogram.

title: Tislelizumab plus nimotuzumab is effective against recurrent or metastatic oral squamous cell carcinoma among patients with a performance status score ≥ 2: a retrospective study
creator: Wen-Jie Wu, Pu-Gen An, Yi-Wei Zhong, Xiao Hu, Lin Wang, Jie Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesThe efficacy of treatments targeting recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma are unsatisfactory in practice for patients with a ECOG PS score ≥ 2. Thus, this study retrospectively evaluated the safety and efficacy of a programmed cell death 1 inhibitor (tislelizumab) combined with an epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor (nimotuzumab) in treating patients with a PS score ≥ 2 who suffer from recurrent or metastatic oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC).Materials and methodsFifteen patients were treated with tislelizumab (200 mg

title: Proteomic markers associated with blood pressure, hypertension, and treatment-resistant hypertension
creator: Anna Dieden, Olle Melander, Manan Pareek, Lennart Råstam, Ulf Lindblad, Petri Gudmundsson, Bledar Daka, Margrét Leósdóttir, Peter M. Nilsson, Michael H. Olsen, Amra Jujic, Martin Magnusson
description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to investigate associations between 92 proteins and blood pressure (BP), prevalent hypertension (HT) and apparent treatment-resistant HT (aTRH) in a population-derived sub cohort.MethodsExcluding subjects with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) (n = 189), linear regression models assessed associations between proteins and systolic BP.

title: AI trust and protean career among university students: the mediating role of intrinsic motivation and the moderating role of job insecurity
creator: Juan Jiang, Jiachun Chen
description: Amid the growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the labor market, university students have to develop career orientation that aligns with the constant state of technological change. Drawing on self-determination theory and conservation of resources theory, we examine how AI trust influences university students' protean careers, while also considering the roles of intrinsic motivation and job insecurity.

title: Selection of relevant domains and instruments for the ASAS core set to assess axial spondyloarthritis in clinical practice: a Delphi survey of stakeholders
creator: Marius L Smits, Victoria Navarro-Compán, Xenofon Baraliakos, Anna Moltó, Elena Nikiphorou, Wilson Bautista-Molano, Philippe Carron, Adrian Ciurea, Jo Davies, Warren Fong, Rodrigo García-Salinas, Laure Gossec, Désirée van der Heijde, David Kiefer, Uta Kiltz, Yu Heng Kwan, Jo Lowe, Marina Magrey, Deni
description: ObjectivesThe Assessment of SpondyloArthritis international Society (ASAS) aims to develop a core set for the assessment of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) in clinical practice to improve standardisation. The first step is to explore stakeholder preferences regarding candidate domains and instruments used for their assessment.

title: Veno-venous ECMO-assisted orthopedic stabilization for polytrauma with severe ARDS and refractory hypoxemia: a case report
creator: Lin Liu, Kaiji Deng, Haifeng Tang, Yanjun Wang
description: This case report describes the successful integration of veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) with physiologically optimized fracture fixation in a critically ill polytrauma patient who presented with life-threatening acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). A 23-year-old male with bilateral femoral fractures, Gustilo IIIB open tibiofibular injury, left radius-ulna fractures, and refractory hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 40.

title: PFKFB3 inhibition dictates the adaptive responses and cell fates in tumor cells
creator: Dianpeng Zheng, Yaowen Mao, Zhipeng Ai, Yue Song, Xiaoyu Liu, Ruoqing Xu, Chenyang Ma, Weikang Meng, Feng He, Hongqing Liang, Jun Ma
description: Summary6-Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3), a key regulator of glycolysis highly expressed in many tumor cells, has a critical role in promoting glycolysis and tumor progression. Consequently, anti-cancer strategies have sought to inhibit PFKFB3 to exploit this metabolic dependency of tumor cells.

title: Intraparotid lipoma in a 15-year-old girl: MRI-based diagnosis of a rare parotid lesion
creator: Chakir Mahfoud, Hamza Bouayad, Abdelqader Sqalli Houssaini, Retal Hamza, Kettani Najwa, Fikri Meriem, Touarsa Firdaous
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Intraparotid lipoma is a rare benign tumor of the parotid gland, accounting for less than 1% of all parotid tumors. Its slow growth and typically painless presentation often lead to delayed diagnosis, which relies primarily on imaging findings.We report the case of a 15-year-old girl presenting with a painless left cheek swelling, evolving since the age of five and causing progressive discomfort, without any associated clinical signs.

title: Deep learning software and revised 2D model to segment bone in micro-CT scans
creator: Andrew H. Lee, Ganesh Talluri, Manan Damani, Brandon Vera Covarrubias, Helena Hanna, Jeremy Chavez, Julian M. Moore, Jacob Baradarian, Michael Molgaard, Beau Nielson, Kalah Walden, Thomas L. Broderick, Layla Al-Nakkash
description: Deep learning (DL) enables automated bone segmentation in micro-CT datasets but can struggle to generalize across developmental stages, anatomical regions, and imaging conditions. We present BP-2D-03, which is a revised 2D Bone-Pores segmentation model. It was fitted to a dataset comprising 20 micro-CT scans spanning five mammalian species and 142,960 image patches.

title: Harnessing hydrogel technology for advanced periodontitis therapy: A multifunctional approach to oral health restoration
creator: Xiaoqing Zhuo, Shaoqiang Wang, Li-Yuan Liu, Minmin Zhu, Zhenjiang Zhang, Yuqi Zhou, Maoshan Wang, Xudong Deng, Yanxia Miao, Niannian Li, Xue-Ting Wang, Hongguang Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPeriodontitis is a bacterially driven inflammatory disease that can lead to tooth mobility and tooth loss. Conventional non-surgical therapy, antibiotics, and surgery may be limited by residual subgingival biofilms, antimicrobial resistance, and variable clinical outcomes. This review synthesizes recent studies of hydrogel-based systems for local periodontal therapy, focusing on stimuli-responsive release mechanisms, cargo-loading approaches, and regenerative outcomes in relevant animal models.

title: Speed-driven transitions between discrete and rhythmic dynamics in walking revealed by kinematic smoothness and muscle synergies
creator: Giulia Panconi, Diego Minciacchi, Riccardo Bravi, Nadia Dominici
description: SummaryHumans control movement through motor primitives that generate discrete and rhythmic actions. We investigated whether and how speed may drive a transition between discrete and rhythmic organization in walking, and whether muscle synergy changes are associated with kinematic shifts. Eighteen healthy adults walked on a treadmill during incremental and decremental trials (0.5–5 km/h in 0.5 km/h steps).

title: Genetic gains in early maturing maize hybrids developed by the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center in Southern Africa during 2000–2018
creator: Amsal Tarekegne, Dagne Wegary, Jill E. Cairns, Mainassara Zaman-Allah, Yoseph Beyene, Demewoz Negera, Adefris Teklewold, Kindie Tesfaye, MacDonald B. Jumbo, Biswanath Das, Egas J. Nhamucho, Kelvin Simpasa, Kesbell K. E. Kaonga, Kingstone Mashingaidze, Ndhlela Thokozile, Xavier Mhike, Boddupalli M. P
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Genetic gain estimation in a breeding program provides an opportunity to monitor breeding efficiency and genetic progress over a specific period. The present study was conducted to (i) assess the genetic gains in grain yield of the early maturing maize hybrids developed by the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT) Southern African breeding program during the period 2000–2018 and (ii) identify key agronomic traits contributing to the yield gains under various management conditions.

title: Delivering the message: mRNA replacement reaches the liver in Niemann-Pick type C1 disease
creator: Laura Lentini, Emanuele Vitale
description: er and central nervous system. Although the conditions can be severe, available therapeutic options remain limited. In this issue of Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids, Koufer and colleagues reported results from an in vivo evaluation of an mRNA-based NPC1 replacement therapy.

title: Alcohol-Related Emergency Department Visits of Young Adults in a University City in the Netherlands
creator: Thirza Arentje Helena Noordermeer, Louise Elisabeth Maria Pigeaud, Loes de Veld, Nico van der Lely
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the incidence and characteristics of alcohol-related emergency department (ED) visits in young adults compared with older age groups.MethodsA retrospective electronic health record study of patients aged ≥18 years with an alcohol-related ED visit, including acute alcohol intoxication (AAI) and alcohol-related injuries, was conducted at Reinier de Graaf Gasthuis (RdGG) from January 1, 2022 to January 1, 2024.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of the appendicitis inflammatory response (AIR) score for acute appendicitis during pregnancy: A systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis
creator: Yasaman Tavakoli, Behdad Ghanami, Azad Alimohammadi, Arefeh Motaharnia
description: Highlights•The Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) score demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy for detecting acute appendicitis during pregnancy (AUC = 0.752).•Pooled analysis showed a sensitivity of 69% and specificity of 76%, supporting the AIR score as an adjunct rather than a standalone diagnostic tool.

title: Consensus scoring-guided virtual screening identifies potent anti-saprolegniasis compounds targeting a P450 fusion protein
creator: Muhammad Akhtar Ali, Anum Javaid, Charuvaka Muvva, Natarajan Arul Murugan, Vaibhav Srivastava
description: Saprolegniasis, predominantly caused by Saprolegnia spp., particularly Saprolegnia parasitica, has reemerged as a major threat in aquaculture, resulting in substantial economic losses of millions of dollars annually. Historically, malachite green was highly effective against this disease; however, its use was banned in aquaculture due to its carcinogenic nature.

title: Integrated Optimization of Opuntia stricta Extracts Coupled with HPLC-Based Phenolic Profiling: Linking Phytochemical Composition to Molecular Docking Simulation
creator: Moufida Chaari, Sarra Akermi, Khaoula Elhadef, Walid Elfalleh, Hassan Ahmed Rudayni, Slim Smaoui
description: This study intended to simultaneously model and optimize aqueous extracts obtained from whole Opuntia stricta fruits (OSE) to maximize the overall response profile, namely total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), antioxidant activity and antibacterial efficacy. For this purpose, the Response Surface Methodology was used to evaluate the influence of three extraction parameters: temperature, sample-to-solvent ratio, and time.

title: ROS-dependent catalytic mechanism of melatonin metabolism and its application in the measurement of reactive oxygen
creator: Xiangge Tian, Xiaohui Kang, Fei Yan, Lei Feng, Xiaokui Huo, Houli Zhang, Yan Wang, Xia Lv, Xiaochi Ma, Jinsong Yuan, Jiao Peng, Li Dai
description: Melatonin (Mel) is an endogenous active molecule whose metabolism progress significantly influences its bioactivity. However, the detailed metabolic pathway of Mel in the pathological state has not yet been fully illustrated. In this study, 16 metabolites of Mel in cancer cells and human liver microsomes were identified, of which seven novel metabolites were newly discovered.

title: Water Temperature and Practical Feeding Regimes Interact to Affect Growth, Enzyme Activities, and Histological Characteristics in Juvenile and Sub-Adult Chinese Mitten Crab (Eriocheir sinensis)
creator: Min Wei, Yuyan Sun, Xinran Yin, Yijin Zhu, Yansong Zhang, Yi Xu, Zhongwei Li, Chao Guo
description: Simple SummaryChinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis) is widely farmed using either commercial pellets or iced fresh fish, but the effectiveness of these feeding practices may vary with water temperature and developmental stage. We conducted a 28-day indoor experiment to examine the responses of juvenile and sub-adult crabs to the two feeding regimes at 20, 24, 28, and 32 °C.

title: Geochemical variability and microbial metabolic functions in oligotrophic sediments exposed to minor seepage
creator: Ellen Schnabel, Aurèle Vuillemin, Sarah Esser, Lea Griesdorn, André R. Soares, Pål Tore Mørkved, Steffen L. Jørgensen, Alexander J. Probst, Jens Kallmeyer, the PROSPECTOMICS Consortium
description: Low primary productivity in Barents Sea surface waters and limited nutrient flux to the seafloor favor nitrification and nitrogen fixation in deep waters, resulting in a dearth of organic substrates in local sediments. The addition of labile hydrocarbons naturally occurring through seepage from subsurface reservoirs could promote microbial activity in organic-lean sediments, notably by denitrifying and sulfate-reducing microbes.

title: Trends in utilization of imaging among ophthalmic-related emergency department visits in the United States
creator: Brandon Chou, Serena M. Shah, Meghana Kalavar, Jayanth Sridhar, Peter MacIntosh, Andrew G. Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAdvanced neuroimaging use has increased in U.S. emergency departments (EDs), including for neuro-ophthalmic conditions requiring computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and their use has shifted in recent years amid changing care patterns and the COVID-19 pandemic. To evaluate these changes, this study examined national trends of CT and MRI use for eye-related ED visits from 2016 to 2022.Materials and methodsA retrospective trend study was conducted using 2016–2022 National Hospital Ambulatory Medical Care Survey (NHAMCS) data.

title: Soil microbial geolocation in forensic casework: a mini-review of methods, evidentiary strength, and admissibility
creator: Abdulla Albastaki, Judith Smith
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Soil is among the most frequently transferred trace materials in violent crime, and its examination draws on an established suite of physical, chemical and biological methods whose resolution at fine spatial scales is nonetheless limited. Over the past decade, advances in high-throughput sequencing of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene, paired with supervised machine-learning classifiers, have been proposed as a means of discriminating soils that these methods cannot readily separate.

title: Machine learning prediction of ARDS after heart valve surgery: development and validation in Northwest China
creator: Xuhua Li, Hao Chen, Aoxiang Chen, Wenhao Zhan, Hengxi Zhang, Qiyuan Bai, Yalan Zhang, Bing Song
description: ObjectiveTo develop an AI-based predictive model for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB)-assisted heart valve replacement (HVR) to enable early identification of high-risk patients.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 400 patients who underwent CPB-assisted HVR between January 2023 and February 2025.

title: Characterization and genomic analysis of a jumbo Aeromonas hydrophila phage BMBAH1, representing a candidate novel viral genus
creator: Shitian Huo, Pengfei Zhu, Jikai Xu, Kai Wang, Ming Sun, Donghai Peng
description: Highlights•A novel jumbo phage, BMBAH1, infecting Aeromonas hydrophila was isolated and characterized.•Phage BMBAH1 exhibited broad temperature and pH stability, a large burst size, and sustained antibacterial activity.•Phage BMBAH1 possesses a 237 kb genome encoding 241 predicted ORFs, many of which remain functionally uncharacterized.•Comparative genomic and phylogenetic analyses assigned phage BMBAH1 to the family Chimalliviridae.

title: Bodies at play: the role of intercorporeality and bodily affordances in coordinating social play in chimpanzees in the wild
creator: Bas van Boekholt, Ray Wilkinson, Simone Pika
description: The comparative approach is a crucial method to gain a better understanding of the behavior of living human and nonhuman animals to then draw informed inferences about the behavior of extinct ancestors. One focus has been on disentangling the puzzle of language evolution. Traditionally, studies have predominantly focused on intentionally produced signals in communicative interactions.

title: Projected Impact of LDL-C and HbA1c Control on Cardiovascular Outcomes in ASCVD and Diabetes
creator: Hridhay Karthikeyan, Wenjun Fan, Ran Jin, Nafeesa Dhalwani, Lisa Head, Nathan D. Wong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). population estimates of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk reduction from comprehensive cardiometabolic risk factor control remain limited among patients with ASCVD and diabetes mellitus (DM).ObjectivesThe objective of the study was to predict 3-year reduction in composite ASCVD event risk and number of preventable events associated with achieving guideline-based targets for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and/or hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) in adults with ASCVD and DM.

title: Clinical Context in Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiographic Risk Stratification for Atrial Fibrillation
creator: Hiroki Sato, Naohiko Takahashi
description: hort, 50 of 137 patients with documented AF (36.5%) were assigned to the high AF-likelihood category. In our cohort, 46 of 104 patients with documented AF (44.2%) were assigned to the high AF-likelihood category using the same system.2 Similar proportions were observed in these 2 distinct clinical cohorts.

title: Current situation and trend of non-coding RNA in rheumatoid arthritis: a review and bibliometric analysis
creator: Zehong Wei, Huaiyu Li, Senhao Lv, Junping Yang
description: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, systemic autoimmune disease that affects multiple joints and has adverse effects on various organs throughout the body, often leading to a poor prognosis. Recent studies have shown significant progress in the research of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) in RA.

title: Genomic Analysis Using Liquid Biopsy: Considerations for Pretest Counseling in UK Practice
creator: David John McMahon, Elizabeth Bancroft, George J Burghel, Ellen Copson, Michael Hubank, Jennifer Wiggins, Katie Snape, Natalie Cook, Ian Frayling, Matthew J Murray, Alastair Greystoke, Matthew G Krebs, Sanjay Popat, Terri Patricia McVeigh, On behalf of UK Circulating Biomarkers Network of Excellence
description: Modern cancer diagnostics is heavily reliant on molecular data. Next-generation sequencing using liquid biopsy (LB) is primarily focused on identifying predictive and prognostic biomarkers to guide systemic therapy decision making. However, additional findings including genomic variants of possible or probable germline origin are detected in a significant minority of patients (3%-18%), with significant implications for patients and their families.

title: Propofol-related biological alterations and incidence of propofol infusion syndrome in status epilepticus: a 10-year cohort study
creator: Chanez Djahel, Clémence Marois, Léa Cosme, Zineb Hayatou, Nesrine Braham Ghedira, Quentin Calonge, Vincent Navarro, Adam Celier, Dominique Bonnefont-Rousselot, Randa Bittar, Sophie Demeret, Aurélie Hanin
description: IntroductionContinuous anesthetics are often required for the management of refractory status epilepticus. While essential to achieving seizure control, these agents carry significant adverse effects. In particular, propofol may induce hypotension, respiratory depression, metabolic acidosis, or pancreatitis, with the most feared complication being propofol infusion syndrome (PRIS).

title: Safety and efficacy of COVID-19 vaccine immunization during pregnancy in 1024 pregnant women infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron virus in Shanghai, China
creator: Hongmei Deng, Yinpeng Jin, Minmin Sheng, Min Liu, Jie Shen, Wei Qian, Gang Zou, Yixin Liao, Tiefu Liu, Yun Ling, Xiaohong Fan
description: BackgroundLarge sample of pregnant women vaccinated with COVID-19 vaccine has not been carried out in China. The objective of this study was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of COVID-19 inactivated vaccine in pregnant women infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant.MethodsA total of 1,024 pregnant women and 120 newborns were enrolled in this study.

title: Results of the inoperable and operable with aortic valve endocarditis
creator: Jing-bin Huang, Chang-chao Lu, Zhen-zong Du, Jian-rong Yang, Jun-jun Li
description: ObjectivesTo evaluate the results of the inoperable and operable with aortic valve endocarditis, focus on risk factors, significance, and management of destruction of the aortic annulus in aortic valve endocarditis.MethodsThe retrospective study was completed to investigate patients with aortic valve endocarditis undergoing cardiac surgery between January 2006 and November 2022 at our hospital.

title: KSHV K15 genetic heterogeneity is associated with Kaposi sarcoma aggressiveness through modulation of the host inflammatory microenvironment
creator: Yu Zhang, Peng Wang, Jingzhan Zhang, Yunying Wang, Tingting Li, Yuan Ding, Xiaojing Kang
description: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) exhibits profound clinical heterogeneity, yet current risk assessment remains constrained by anatomical staging systems that lack universality across diverse KS variants. This study characterized the functional impact of Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) K15 genotypes (M or P) on clinical aggressiveness in a retrospective cohort of 156 patients from Xinjiang, China.

title: A study on the impact of mental health problems on the academic buoyancy of medical students and the mechanisms
creator: Bin Hu, Yue Wang, Hai Tao Zhou, Min Li, Li Zheng
description: ObjectiveTo analyze the effects of different family environmental backgrounds and mental health problems on academic buoyancy and to explore the potential mechanisms of their effects, using a sample of 2085 medical students in Jiangsu province.MethodsUsing the multiple linear regression to analyze the impact of mental health problems on academic buoyancy in different family environment contexts.

title: DyME: An MD-based engine exploiting HTP mutagenesis for protein engineering and recognition mimicry
creator: Pedro M. Guillem-Gloria, Gloria Ruiz-Gómez, M. Teresa Pisabarro
description: Protein recognition mimicry (PRM) is of great interest in the field of molecular bioengineering and rational design, with mutagenesis frequently employed to analyze the effects of altering amino acids involved in molecular recognition. The conformational and energetic effects of such alterations can be investigated in detail with the help of molecular dynamics (MD) methodologies.

title: Effects of a stepwise alveolar recruitment maneuver on lung volume distribution in dogs assessed by computed tomography
creator: Ana Flávia Sanchez, Aline Magalhães Ambrósio, Ana Carolina B. C. Fonseca Pinto, Marco Aurélio Amador Pereira, Felipe Silveira Rego Monteiro Andrade, Renata Ramos Rodrigues, Alessandro Rodrigues de Carvalho Martins, Carina Outi Baroni, Bruno Ferrante, Denise Tabacchi Fantoni
description: BackgroundPulmonary atelectasis is a commonly occurs during anesthesia. In these cases, mechanical ventilation (MV) associated with alveolar recruitment maneuvers (ARMs) and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is indicated to reverse the condition, ensure adequate gas exchange and improve oxygenation. ARMs can trigger volutrauma, barotrauma, and atelectrauma. Therefore, computed tomography (CT) is the gold-standard method for monitoring lung aeration after ARM.

title: Serum GFAP, NfL, and tau concentrations are associated with worse neurobehavioral functioning following mild, moderate, and severe TBI: a cross-sectional multiple-cohort study
creator: Katie A. Edwards, Rael T. Lange, Sara M. Lippa, Tracey A. Brickell, Jessica M. Gill, Louis M. French
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe purpose of this study was to examine whether blood-based biomarkers associate with neurobehavioral functioning at three time points following traumatic brain injury (TBI).Materials and methodsParticipants were 328 United States service members and veterans (SMVs) prospectively enrolled in the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center-Traumatic Brain Injury Center of Excellence (DVBIC-TBICoE) 15-Year Longitudinal TBI Study, recruited into three groups: uncomplicated mild TBI (MTBI, n = 155); complicated mild, moderate, severe TBI combined (STBI, n = 97); non-injured controls (NIC, n = 76).

title: Protocol for quantifying chromatin DNA replication by multiplex labeling and single-molecule localization microscopy
creator: Zhiguang Xiao, Xiaodong Guan, Yujie Sun, Mengling Zhang, Qian Peter Su
description: SummaryWe present a protocol for imaging and quantifying chromatin DNA replication-associated signals in synchronized mammalian cells. We describe steps for cell-cycle enrichment, nucleoside analog-based metabolic labeling, and fluorescence detection. We then detail the procedure for dual-color STORM imaging and SR-Tesseler-based cluster analysis.

title: Veterinarians' attitudes, knowledge, and practices about antibiotic use in animals: questionnaire design and reliability
creator: Ana Filipa Pereira, Leonardo de Rago, Jacinta Oliveira Pinho, Ana Isabel Plácido, Adolfo Figueiras, Fátima Roque, Maria Teresa Herdeiro, Ana Cláudia Coelho, Paula Alexandra Oliveira
description: IntroductionAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health concern that requires a One Health approach. The role of veterinarians in promoting antimicrobial stewardship is essential for successful mitigation of AMR.ObjectiveThis study aimed to design a self-administered questionnaire and evaluate its reliability as a tool to assess veterinarians' knowledge, perceptions, and attitudes regarding AMR and antibiotic prescription and use in animals.

title: The impact of parental overprotection on the emotions and behaviors of pediatric hematologic cancer patients: a multicenter cross-sectional study
creator: Yahui Yu, Xiaofeng Zheng, Wenjing Xu, Yuru Huang, Xulu Wang, Wanting Hong, Runping Wang, Xiaojing Ye, Chunmei Zhang
description: BackgroundParental overprotection may have an impact on children’s emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs). As pediatric hematologic cancer patients have compromised immune systems, parents of such children often worry excessively, interfering with their daily lives. Therefore, avoiding overprotection is crucial for the overall physical and mental health of pediatric hematologic cancer patients.

title: Bridging the intention‒behavior gap in herpes zoster vaccination: A nationwide survey in a self-payment setting
creator: Fang-Yu Liou, Chang-Ying Chen, Yin-Fan Chang, Ru-Hsueh Wang, Wei-Chen Shen, Cheng-Kuo Huang, Chin-Sung Chang, Chih-Hsing Wu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Herpes zoster (HZ) causes substantial morbidity, yet global uptake remains suboptimal where the vaccine is excluded from universal coverage. Taiwan exemplifies such a self-payment setting, with the HZ vaccine self-financed and local government subsidies restricted to limited eligible groups. This study analyzed data from a nationwide, web-based cross-sectional survey of adults aged ≥18y fielded in 2025, examining factors associated with HZ vaccination behavior, intention, and willingness to pay (WTP).

title: Gastrointestinal symptom profiles after resection of esophageal or gastric cancer
creator: Yipei Lee, Dimitris Katsimpokis, Felice N. van Erning, Grard A. P. Nieuwenhuijzen, Hanneke W. M. van Laarhoven, Suzanne S. Gisbertz, Bastiaan R. Klarenbeek, Paul M. Jeene, Roos E. Pouw, Loes Noteboom, Rob H. A. Verhoeven, Pauline A. J. Vissers
description: PurposePersistent gastrointestinal symptoms are common after esophagectomy or gastrectomy, which frequently co-occur and significantly decrease quality of life. This study aimed to identify gastrointestinal symptom profiles over the first-year post-surgery and to explore changes over time.MethodsPatients diagnosed between 2013 and 2024 who underwent esophagectomy or gastrectomy for nonmetastatic esophageal or gastric cancer were selected.

title: Enhanced cattle identification using Siamese network and MobileViT with EMA attention
creator: Mingshuo Han, Baoshan Li, Qi Li, Yueming Wang, Mei Yang, Chang Gao
description: Accurate identification of individual cattle is paramount in livestock insurance to combat fraud. However, the performance of existing muzzle recognition methods degrades in complex scenarios involving occlusion or multi-angle views. This study addresses this limitation by first constructing a comprehensive cattle muzzle image dataset encompassing frontal, multi-angle, and occluded conditions.

title: Evolution and phylogenetic characteristics of the first Brucella canis strain isolated from a human patient in Yunnan Province, China
creator: Qiuju Yang, Peng Wang, Xiangdong Yang, Su Zhao, Qing Zhang, Fuping Yang, Zhiguo Liu, Binbin Yu
description: IntroductionBrucella canis is a zoonotic pathogen that infects both dogs and humans, yet its evolutionary and phylogenetic characteristics are poorly understood.MethodsHere, we comprehensively characterized an isolated strain of B. canis through integrated bacteriological, comparative genomic, and whole-genome sequencing-based core genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (WGS-cgSNP) analyses.ResultsB. canis YN20042 was isolated from a febrile patient (38 °C) with sweating and fatigue.

title: Scaffold Hopping Provides Liver X Receptor Agonist With Preference for the β Subtype
creator: Annette Kärcher, Fiona L Motel, Felix F Lillich, Astrid Kaiser, Ewgenij Proschak, Pascal Heitel
description: The liver X receptor is a promising target for diseases with dysregulated cholesterol levels. In addition to enhanced reverse cholesterol transport, however, LXR activation induces hepatic lipogenesis. Since the subtype LXRα is dominant in the liver, one strategy to overcome this is the development of LXRβ‐selective agonists.

title: Topical drug delivery strategies for enhancing drug effectiveness by skin barriers, drug delivery systems and individualized dosing
creator: Lin Zhao, Jiamei Chen, Bai Bai, Guili Song, Jingwen Zhang, Han Yu, Shiwei Huang, Zhang Wang, Guanghua Lu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Topical drug delivery is widely used in various diseases because of the advantages of not passing through the gastrointestinal tract, avoiding gastrointestinal irritation and hepatic first-pass effect, and reaching the lesion directly to reduce unnecessary adverse reactions. The skin helps the organism to defend itself against a huge majority of external aggressions and is one of the most important lines of defense of the body. However, the skin’s strong barrier ability is also a huge obstacle to the effectiveness of topical medications.

title: Effect of liraglutide on depressive symptoms in overweight or obese patients with type 2 diabetes: protocol for a pilot randomized controlled trial
creator: Wei Fang, Zinan Li, Jie Xu, Jing Zhao, Hongxia Zhu, Huanping Wang
description: IntroductionPatients with concurrent obesity, type 2 diabetes, and depression experience high disease severity and prevalence. This triad of conditions compromises quality of life and treatment adherence, further exacerbating disease progression. Therapeutic strategies for such patients must address both glycemic control and psychological well-being.

title: Overall survival of Black patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma in the era of triplet and quadruplet therapies
creator: Hamlet Gasoyan, Shahzad Raza, Michael B. Rothberg, Jeffrey D. Kovach, Nicholas J. Casacchia, Jason Valent, Faiz Anwer
description: ve treatment utilization [2–4], given that Black patients generally exhibit equal or better survival than White patients after adjustment for key treatment-access barriers [2, 5]. Recent evidence also indicates that genomic features do not account for differences in MM risk across genetic ancestry groups [3].

title: Case Report: effect of lumasiran treatment in a late preterm baby with antenatal diagnosis of primary hyperoxaluria type 1
creator: Francesca Taroni, Alfredo Berrettini, Michele Gnech, Francesca Rella, Gian Antonio Manzoni, Giovanni Montini
description: BackgroundPrimary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) is a rare disease with autosomal recessive transmission, characterized by increased urinary excretion of oxalate, resulting in chronic kidney disease secondary to recurrent urolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, and accumulation of oxalate in various organs and tissues (systemic oxalosis). Since 2020, an innovative pharmacological approach, namely, lumasiran, has been added to the therapeutic armamentarium (dialysis and liver-kidney transplantation).

title: Contralateral-controlled thigh muscle biomarkers on CT angiography for prediction of 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy for unilateral peripheral artery disease
creator: Shuangxiang Lin, Xinhong Wang, Yifeng Pan, Libing Zhang, Jianzhong Sun, Bing Chen
description: ObjectiveTo develop and internally validate a model using contralateral-controlled thigh muscle biomarkers, measured on routine computed tomography angiography (CTA), to predict clinically driven, DSA-confirmed 1-year restenosis after endovascular therapy for unilateral peripheral artery disease (PAD).Materials and methodsIn this retrospective cohort study, 378 patients with unilateral PAD undergoing endovascular therapy and having baseline and 1-year follow-up CTA were included.

title: Prevalence of Hallux Valgus in Patients With Femoral Neck Fracture and Its Association With Postoperative Functional Outcomes
creator: Kazuki Kanazawa, Shunsuke Akiho, Masahiko Sakai, Ken Ichikawa, Soshiro Goshima, Ryohei Haraguchi, Takuaki Yamamoto
description: BackgroundHallux valgus is a frequent forefoot deformity in older adults and has been linked to impaired balance, gait dysfunction, and increased fall risk. However, its prevalence among patients with femoral neck fracture and its association with postoperative functional outcomes remain unclear.

title: Effect of light intensity on celery growth and flavonoid synthesis
creator: Yanmei Qin, Xuanxuan Liu, Chunyan Li, Qianwen Chu, Shaobo Cheng, Lihong Su, Dalong Shao, Xin Guo, Zhongqun He, Xiaoting Zhou
description: Light is one of the important environmental factors affecting the growth and development of facility vegetables. In this experiment, we investigated the effects of different light intensities on the growth, nutritional quality and flavonoid accumulation of celery under hydroponic and full LED light conditions.

title: Mendelian randomization studies on the causal relationship between insomnia and disease
creator: Xuan Hou, Yingjun Wei, Yongfeng Wang, Lijun Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Insomnia, a prevalent sleep disorder, poses significant threats to both physical and mental health. Traditional studies suggest multiple factors are associated with insomnia, yet the causal direction often remains unclear and susceptible to confounding biases. Mendelian randomization, a cutting-edge method leveraging genetic instrumental variables for causal inference, effectively overcomes these limitations by providing high-quality evidence to clarify causal relationships between insomnia and various diseases. This review systematically integrates 105 recent Mendelian randomization studies on insomnia.

title: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Special Statement: Guidance to reduce racial disparities in substance use screening and biological testing in pregnancy at the delivery admission
creator: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM), Jennifer J. M. Cate, Samuel T. Bauer, Niraj R. Chavan, Marc Parrish, Jessica Peterson, Dena Goffman, Christina Davidson, SMFM Patient Safety and Quality Committee
description: Substance use complicates upward of 10% of US pregnancies. The Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the American Society of Addiction Medicine have jointly recommended universal screening for substance use during pregnancy using a validated tool, without recommending universal biological testing.

title: Insights into group-specific pattern of secondary metabolite gene cluster in Burkholderia genus
creator: Byeollee Kim, So-Ra Han, Hyun Lee, Tae-Jin Oh
description: Burkholderia is a versatile strain that has expanded into several genera. It has been steadily reported that the genome features of Burkholderia exhibit activities ranging from plant growth promotion to pathogenicity across various isolation areas. The objective of this study was to investigate the secondary metabolite patterns of 366 Burkholderia species through comparative genomics.

title: Ophthalmic implications of biological threat agents according to the chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosives framework
creator: Emma H. Curran, Max D. Devine, Caleb D. Hartley, Ye Huang, Christopher D. Conrady, Matthew R. Debiec, Grant A. Justin, Joanne Thomas, Steven Yeh
description: As technology continues to evolve, the possibility for a wide range of dangers to people, organizations, and countries escalate globally. The United States federal government classifies types of threats with the capability of inflicting mass casualties and societal disruption as Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Energetics/Explosives (CBRNE).

title: Liver fibrosis in biliary atresia: identification of the key gene EDIL3 via integrated bioinformatics
creator: Meng Kong, Jinhua Jia, Chuanyang Liu, Hongzhen Liu, Shisong Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBiliary atresia (BA) is one of the most destructive liver and biliary diseases in neonates and is characterized by progressive fibrous inflammatory obstruction of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, ultimately leading to liver fibrosis and liver failure.

title: Mechanisms and determinants of mRNA Lipid Nanoparticle biodistribution: From pharmacokinetics to clinical translation
creator: Zakia Alhareth, César López‐Camacho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics formulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed the field of nucleic acid medicine by enabling transient, programmable protein expression for vaccination, protein replacement, immunotherapy, and genome engineering. Extending their clinical success beyond vaccines requires a mechanistic understanding of where LNP components and mRNA travel, which cells they enter, where cargo is translated, and how each component is cleared.

title: Optimization of PET acquisition time for thoracic lesions in 18F-FDG PET/MRI: a retrospective analysis
creator: Haifeng Gu, Yue Jiang, Jun Cai, Gang Yang, Jianrui Li, Sui Chen, Song Luo, Longjiang Zhang
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to define the minimum positron emission tomography (PET) acquisition time for chest PET/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), providing image quality and lesion detectability comparable to a 20-min reference.Materials and methodsIn this retrospective study, list-mode data from 101 patients undergoing chest 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/MRI on a 3-T PET/MRI system were reconstructed to simulate 10 acquisition times (0.5–20 min).

title: Synergy between immune system and antibiotics drives infection control in mice
creator: Rajalekshmy G. Padmakumari, Ruchi Roy, Foyez Mahmud, Deepa Dehari, Getnet Tesfaw, Christi Thomas, Athena M. Soulika, Roslyn Rivkah Isseroff, Sasha H. Shafikhani
description: BackgroundAntibiotics and host immunity are traditionally viewed as independent defenses, with antibiotics reducing bacterial load to levels manageable by the immune system. Modeling studies, however, predict that synergy between these defenses is critical for infection control, but this has not been experimentally verified.

title: Bridging radiomics and histopathology: cross-modality consistency of radiomic features from CT to micro-CT in NSCLC
creator: Leonardo Brizzi, Chandra Bortolotto, Raffaella Fiamma Cabini, Francesca Brero, Silvia Megalizzi, Gioacchino D’Ambrosio, Marta Filibian, Roberta Gioia, Paola Falvo, Giulia Maria Stella, Olivia Maria Bottinelli, Alessandro Lascialfari, Lorenzo Preda
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveRadiomics extracts quantitative features from medical images that may provide non-invasive biomarkers of tumor biology and heterogeneity. However, few studies have explored radiomics on micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) or its transferability to clinical CT. This study investigates the reproducibility and the potential biological correlation of radiomic features across in vivo CT, ex vivo CT, and ex vivo micro-CT in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).Materials and methodsA retrospective cohort of 60 NSCLC patients with preoperative CT scans and surgical specimens was analyzed.

title: Fragmented Data, Fragmented Care: Strengthening Health Information Systems for Universal Health Coverage in Somalia
creator: Ilyas Abdullahi khalif, Aniso Mohamed Abdi, Yusuf Abdullahi Hubow, Ahmed Mohamed Omar, Nour Ahmed Dahir, Abas Nor Abdi, Sharmake Gaiye Bashir, Nuradin Abdullahi Sheikh Rashid
description: Health information systems (HISs) are essential for achieving universal health coverage (UHC), yet Somalia's health sector remains constrained by fragmented data systems, weak interoperability, limited infrastructure, workforce shortages, and poor governance. This commentary examines the challenges undermining Somalia's digital health transformation and argues that fragmented information systems perpetuate fragmented healthcare delivery.

title: Mendelian randomization study highlights hypothyroidism as a causal determinant of alopecia areata
creator: Xue-Yong Zheng, Yan-Ping Ma, Bo Zhang, Yan-Xin Chen, Lei Tang, Xiao-Hua Tai, Jia-Hao Cao
description: BackgroundAlthough observational studies have found an association between hypothyroidism and alopecia areata, the causality of this relationship remains unclear.ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate the genetic variants associated with hypothyroidism and their potential impact on the risk of developing alopecia areata.

title: Durable treatment response to Trastuzumab deruxtecan in two patients with recurrent grade III anaplastic ependymoma
creator: Dietmar Krex, Irina A. Kerle, Arne Grey, Stephanie Pleißner, Stephan Richter, Christoph Heining, Stefan Fröhling, Hanno Glimm, Martin Bornhäuser, Gunnar Folprecht, Andy Göbel, Cornelia S. Link-Rachner
description: BackgroundAnaplastic ependymoma is a rare and aggressive central nervous system malignancy for which effective systemic treatment options are limited. Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), an antibody–drug conjugate targeting human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), has demonstrated intracranial activity in patients with HER2-positive solid tumors.

title: Advances in the application of tumor vaccines and combination strategies: new perspectives in lung cancer treatment
creator: Lei Sun, Qi Zhao, Liyun Miao
description: Lung cancer remains one of the most prevalent and lethal malignancies globally and its treatment has consistently been a focal point of research in the medical field. The emergence of immunotherapies such as immune checkpoint inhibitors has brought about a new understanding of vaccine treatment for tumors. Tumor vaccines induce anti-tumor immune responses by targeting tumor-associated antigens or specific neoantigens.

title: Investigating the Relationship Between Estrogen Replacement Therapy and Postoperative Complications Following Single-Level Lumbar Fusion: A Propensity Matched Analysis
creator: Kyle B. Stump, Alec M. Giakas, Gregorio Baek, Mitchell K. Ng, Andrew P. Alvarez, Alan S. Hilibrand, Alexander R. Vaccaro, Gregory D. Schroeder, Christopher K. Kepler
description: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort.ObjectivesThe objective of this study was to investigate the relationship between preoperative estrogen replacement therapy and postoperative complications following single level lumbar fusion.MethodsThe TriNetX Research Network was queried for menopausal patients aged ≥ 50 years who underwent single level lumbar fusion. Patients issued ERT within the 12-month preoperative period were separated from patients with no documented ERT use.

title: Editorial: From causal circuit mapping to clinical translation: Prefronto‐thalamic hypoconnectivity in schizophrenia
creator: Norio Yasui‐Furukori
description: ather than starting with a human imaging association and seeking a mechanistic explanation retrospectively, Yahata et al. begin with a pathway whose function was established by selective manipulation in nonhuman primates (NHPs), then ask whether the homologous circuit is altered in people with psychiatric disorders. That foundation was a chemogenetic study in macaques by Oyama et al.

title: Assessing the nutritional quality of Pleurotus ostreatus (oyster mushroom)
creator: Magdalene Eno Effiong, Chidinma Precious Umeokwochi, Israel Sunmola Afolabi, Shalom Nwodo Chinedu
description: There is a huge gap between food production and the exploding population demands in various parts of the world, especially developing countries. This increases the chances of malnutrition, leading to increased disease incidence and the need for functional foods to reduce mortality.

title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes mellitus by birth order: A descriptive study across lifetime reproductive history
creator: Sage Wyatt, Linn Marie Sørbye, Liv Grimstvedt Kvalvik, Aditi Singh, Rolv Skjærven
description: IntroductionHypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes mellitus are known to be strongly related, and underlying maternal cardiometabolic dysfunction has been proposed as a mechanism for both complications. A comparison of the trends by birth order for the two complications may reveal insights into their shared or different causes.

title: Basic psychological needs and parental bonding in Italian adults at high risk of hikikomori (extreme social withdrawal): the distinctive association of Competence Frustration with symptom severity
creator: Virginia Pupi, Cinzia Bressi, Paolo Brambilla, Maria Gloria Rossetti, Cinzia Perlini, Francesca Girelli, Maria Diletta Buio, Niccolò Zovetti, Isabella Fanizza, Antonio Trabacca, Fabrizia Claudia Guarnieri, Roberto Sassi, Marcella Bellani, Antonella Delle Fave
description: This brief research report explored the relationships between hikikomori symptom severity (extreme social withdrawal), basic psychological needs of Competence, Autonomy, and Relatedness, and perceived parental bonding in Italian adults experiencing social isolation. Participants (N = 33; Mage = 27.83, SD = 7.46; 42.

title: XPA lactylation is required for UV-induced DNA damage repair
creator: Jie Yang, Xin Ding, Zhikai Zeng, Hui Yin, Yiming He, Mingpeng Jin, Bingsong Huang, Zhe Wang, Xiaoning Yang, Rui Li, Qianwen Wang, Xuan Zhou, Yifei Song, Yu Li, Xuanhe Wang, Wen Zheng, Lu Lu, Qian Zhu, Jiaqi Liu, Zhihua Kang, Lei Li, Yunhui Li, Chengyuan Wang, Jian Yuan, Yuping Chen, Jinhuan Wu, Bent
description: Xeroderma pigmentosum group A (XPA) serves as a core nucleotide excision repair (NER) factor essential for the repair process triggered by UV irradiation. Lactylation, a newly identified post-translational modification, plays a key role in tumorigenesis and cancer progression. Herein, we discovered that XPA was lactylated in the DNA-binding domain by the acyl-transferase KAT5.

title: Train to sustain: a randomised controlled trial evaluation of a vitality training employing behaviour-change techniques
creator: Bernice R. C. Plant, Mattheis L. Van Leeuwen, Pascale Peters, Beatrice I. J. M. Van der Heijden
description: IntroductionThis paper reports on the effects of a 9-week vitality training that employed behaviour-change techniques and was evaluated using a randomised controlled trial (RCT) in three large companies based in the Netherlands.MethodsA total of 84 adult employees from three participating organisations in the Netherlands were enrolled in the study.

title: Acetylation-independent mechanism for binding of ENL to intrinsically disordered regions in TAF2/6 and SNF5
creator: Zohreh Tavaf, Moustafa Khalil, Minh Chau Nguyen, Hong Wen, Aniruddha J Deshpande, El Bachir Affar, M Andres Blanco, Tatiana G Kutateladze
description: Eleven-nineteen-leukemia (ENL) is a well-established epigenetic regulator essential for transcription in development and implicated in cancer. Here, we report the molecular mechanisms and functional consequences of the ENL association with components of transcriptional and chromatin remodeling complexes, TAF2, TAF6, and SNF5, and describe ENL intramolecular contacts and autoregulation.

title: Multimodal learning for scalable representation of high-dimensional medical data
creator: Areej Alsaafin, Abubakr Shafique, Saghir Alfasly, Krishna R. Kalari, H. R. Tizhoosh
description: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with healthcare data is rapidly transforming medical diagnostics and driving progress toward precision medicine. However, effectively leveraging multimodal data, particularly digital pathology whole slide images (WSIs) and genomic sequencing, remains a significant challenge due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of these modalities and the need for scalable and interpretable frameworks.

title: RNA therapeutics in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and systemic sclerosis: a compartment-aware translational framework
creator: Yusif Afandizada, Hikmet Memmedov, Mushfig Orujov, Shahla Eyvazova, Shirkhan Amikishiyev
description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis (SLE/LN), and systemic sclerosis (SSc) remain major causes of chronic inflammation, disability, organ damage, and treatment burden despite therapeutic advances. RNA therapeutics offer programmable transcript suppression, network-level microRNA modulation, transient restoration of protective proteins, and targeting-ligand functions.

title: Unraveling the invasiveness of Prosopis juliflora (Neltuma juliflora): seed traits and ecological implications
creator: Kamel Chibani, Mengjie Fan, Hamada E. Ali, Laya Al-Kharusi
description: Prosopis juliflora (Neltuma juliflora) is a globally invasive tree species threatening arid ecosystems. Its invasion success is driven by specific seed traits that function as an adaptive bet-hedging strategy. The impermeable seed coat enforces physical dormancy and enables the formation of a persistent soil seed bank that buffers against environmental stochasticity (population insurance).

title: Applications of AI to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics: current state-of-the-art and challenges
creator: Boris Tchatchoua Ngassam, Huilin Niu, Sunny Pang, Valeryia Shydlouskaya, Tallulah S. Andrews
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a common tool for bioinformatics, with hundreds of methods published in recent years. Due to the training data demands of deep-learning algorithms, high-throughput single-cell and spatial transcriptomics is one of the most popular areas for these applications.

title: Potential risk of occupational exposure to respirable crystalline silica in Saudi Arabia: a comprehensive review of the current status and future challenges
creator: Salman Alquwayi
description: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing.

title: Time-lapse imaging of identified granule cells in the mouse dentate gyrus after entorhinal lesion in vitro reveals heterogeneous cellular responses to denervation
creator: Davide Greco, Alexander Drakew, Nina Rößler, Tassilo Jungenitz, Peter Jedlicka, Thomas Deller
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Denervation of neurons is a network consequence of brain injury. The effects of denervation on neurons can be readily studied in vitro using organotypic slice cultures of entorhinal cortex and hippocampus. Following transection of the entorhino-dentate projection, granule cells (GCs) are denervated and show on average a transient loss of spines on their denervated distal dendrites but not on their non-denervated proximal dendrites.

title: Novel pyroptosis-immune-related lncRNA signature exhibits a distinct immune cell infiltration landscape in breast cancer
creator: Dedi Kong, Hongju Cheng, Meihong Wang
description: IntroductionThis study investigated pyroptosis- and immunity-related long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to identify promising therapeutic targets for breast cancer (BC), and constructed lncRNA signatures to determine the prognosis and immunotherapy responses of BC patients.MethodsPearson’s correlation coefficient was used to identify pyroptosis- and immune-related differentially expressed lncRNAs (DE-pyrolncRNAs and DE-ImmlncRNAs, respectively).

title: Investigating the potential immunomodulatory effects of commercial oral probiotic supplements on equine gastrointestinal tract barrier function
creator: Agnieszka Żak-Bochenek, Paulina Żebrowska-Różańska, Joanna Bajzert, Łukasz Łaczmański, Bogumiła Szponar, Natalia Siwińska, Klaudia Gładysz, Katarzyna Sikorska, Anna Chełmońska-Soyta
description: BackgroundOral probiotic dietary supplements are widely used in veterinary medicine, including in horses. It is hypothesized that the presence of probiotic strains can both modulate the intestinal microbiota and affect mucosal immunity parameters. Such a study has not yet been conducted in horses.

title: Insights into self-reported food allergies in Romanian schoolchildren
creator: Claudia Felicia Pop, Daniela Rajka, Ioana Corina Bocsan, Petronela Alina Coblisan, Gabriela Edita Ichim, Anna Lazar, Paraschiva Chereches-Panta
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The prevalence of food allergy (FA) varies worldwide with an increasing rate in the last decades. Data of self-reported FA have been recorded by most European countries, the US, Canada and Australia, but not Romania.

title: Corticosteroids, serum proteins, and the next phase of precision medicine in IgA nephropathy
creator: Carmine Zoccali, Jürgen Floege
description: Systemic glucocorticoids remain an important but problematic treatment option in high-risk IgA nephropathy, offering kidney protection at the cost of clinically relevant toxicity. Recent serum proteomic analyses embedded within the randomized TESTING trial provide a new framework for identifying patients most likely to benefit from methylprednisolone.

title: The m6A regulatory network in plant stress adaptation: from mechanisms to breeding potential
creator: Jun Zhang, Sainan Jiang, Jie Yang, Jingjing Zou, Wen Xing, Zeqing Li
description: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant internal modification of eukaryotic mRNA and is dynamically regulated by three classes of proteins: writers, erasers, and readers. Writers deposit methylation marks, erasers confer reversibility, and readers translate these signals into specific regulatory outcomes, collectively modulating mRNA stability, translation efficiency, splicing, and polyadenylation, thereby influencing plant stress adaptation.

title: Endocrine determinants of MASLD: mechanisms and therapeutic targets
creator: Richa Chaturvedi, Anu Mathew, Aprajita Pradhan, Monika Goyal, Monika Sharma, Varsha Kachroo, Chhavi Agrawal, Aishwarya Krishnamurthy, Surabhi Atreja, Ashish Atreja
description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of adults worldwide, yet is still framed largely as a hepatological disorder despite being driven substantially by endocrine and metabolic dysfunction. This review proposes a unified endocrine framework organised around seven hormonal axes, presenting each in terms of molecular pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and therapeutic implications.

title: Reversing NK cell exhaustion: a novel strategy combining immune checkpoint blockade with drug sensitivity enhancement in the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Yuxiang Huang, Hengjian Liao, Jiefu Luo, Huaning Wei, Anling Li, Yujie Lu, Bangde Xiang
description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common lethal cancers worldwide. Natural killer cells (NK cells) play a key role in liver immunosurveillance, but in the tumor microenvironment, NK cells are readily depleted, as evidenced by down-regulation of activating receptors, reduced cytokine secretion, and attenuated killing function.

title: Mapping risk of gambling disorder in older adults: a neural network approach
creator: Roser Granero, Fernando Fernández-Aranda, Isabel Baenas, Lucero Munguía, Anahí Gaspar-Pérez, Mónica Gómez-Peña, Jeffrey Derevensky, Sally Gainsbury, Rebeca Rodríguez-García, Susana Jiménez-Murcia
description: Background and objectivesGambling disorder (GD) in older adults remains insufficiently understood, despite growing concerns about gambling-related harm in older adulthood. Risk profiles and clinical presentations in this age group may differ from those typically described in younger or mixed-age samples, reflecting age-specific psychosocial contexts, health conditions, and life transitions.

title: Advances and applications of engineered protein therapeutics and their role in precision medicine
creator: Wadha Aldossary, Nada Alqahtani, Layla Asiri, Noora Alkhurayef, Samar Alagl, Sana Alturki, Duha Saad, Mashael Al Yahya, Samah Al-Harthi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Proteins are a vital class of biomolecules. They play essential roles in biological processes, including building cellular structures, forming cellular channels and receptors, catalyzing biological reactions, transporting molecules, and contributing to immune defense mechanisms. Advances in protein engineering have enabled the genetic modification of naturally occurring proteins, using recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology, leading to the development of therapeutic proteins with enhanced specificity, stability, and clinical performance.

title: Diagnostic efficiency of exome-based sequencing in pediatric patients with epilepsy
creator: Huafang Zou, Qian Zhang, Jianxiang Liao, Dongfang Zou, Zhanqi Hu, Bing Li, Li Chen, Jialun Wen, Xia Zhao, Victor Wei Zhang, Dezhi Cao
description: ObjectiveEpilepsy, a prevalent neurological disorder, has multifaceted etiologies. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) has emerged as a robust diagnostic tool for this condition. This study aims to evaluate the detection efficiencies of different exome-based sequencing techniques.MethodsExome-based epilepsy panel tests, clinical exome sequencing (CES), and whole exome sequencing (WES) were conducted on 259 pediatric patients diagnosed with epilepsy.

title: The multiple sclerosis exposome: environmental determinants, immunological convergence, and the Gulf Region as a natural test case
creator: Eslam Shosha, Najeeb Qadi
description: BackgroundThe multiple sclerosis (MS) exposome is widely invoked but rarely measured; grouping environmental exposures together obscures large differences in evidence quality. Much of the existing gene–environment evidence originates from genetically and environmentally homogeneous northern European cohorts, leaving open whether it generalizes elsewhere.

title: Characterization of Listeria monocytogenes strains isolated from soil under organic carrot farming
creator: Maciej Nowak, Zbigniew Paluszak, Natalia Wiktorczyk-Kapischke, Katarzyna Grudlewska-Buda, Anna Budzyńska, Joanna Skonieczna-Kurpiel, Ewa Wałecka-Zacharska, Monika Huse-Kutowska, Krzysztof Skowron
description: IntroductionListeria monocytogenes are Gram-positive, non-spore-producing rods that are the etiological agent of listeriosis. L. monocytogenes is isolated from soil, water, sewage, rotting vegetation, and the main source of these rods for humans is food (fish, unpasteurized dairy products, or raw fruits and vegetables). In recent years, there has been an increase in consumer interest in healthy food, especially organically grown.

title: Early recognition of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis in outpatient settings: musculoskeletal and gastrointestinal clues beyond respiratory disease
creator: Ernesto Aitella, Massimo De Martinis, Lia Ginaldi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a multisystem immune-mediated disease characterized by adult-onset asthma, eosinophilic inflammation, and necrotizing vasculitis of small-to-medium-sized vessels. Diagnosis is frequently prompted by clinically overt neurological, cardiac, renal, cutaneous, or gastrointestinal involvement. However, potentially informative manifestations may already be recognizable earlier, particularly when asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and blood eosinophilia coexist with otherwise nonspecific extrapulmonary findings.

title: Clinical correlates for fluconazole resistance in Candida bloodstream infections
creator: Zihuan Li, Tian Wang, Mengdie Zhang, Shu Cao, Baohong Liu, Cuiqiong Fan, Guanwen Lin, Yanfen Ming
description: BackgroundCandidemia poses a growing global health threat, with rising fluconazole resistance complicating clinical management. This study aimed to investigate the species distribution and fluconazole resistance profiles of Candida bloodstream infections and identify risk factors associated with fluconazole resistance.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Guangzhou, China, from 2023 to 2025.

title: The global burden of otitis media in 204 countries and territories from 1992 to 2021: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease study 2021
creator: Guan-Jiang Huang, Bao-Rui Lin, Pei-Shan Li, Na Tang, Zhi-Jun Fan, Biao-Qing Lu
description: ObjectivesThis study aims to analyze the global burden of otitis media and predict future trends using data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 (GBD 2021).Study designA cross-sectional analysis of GBD 2021 results was conducted.MethodsAge-standardized incidence rates (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR), and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) rates (ASDR) were calculated.

title: Shenshuaikang enema restores the intestinal barrier and microbiota-gut-kidney axis balance to alleviate chronic kidney disease via NF-κB pathway
creator: Yan Ye, Xiaopeng Huang, Xueying Li, Fei Gao, Wenzhen Zhong, Anqi Tang, Liangbin Zhao, Dengpiao Xie, Naijing Ye
description: IntroductionChronic kidney disease (CKD) is a chronic progressive disease characterized by abnormalities in kidney structure or function caused by variousfactors. It has become a significant public health problem, posing a threat to human health worldwide. Shenshuaikang enema (SSKE) has demonstrated notable efficacy and safety in treating CKD, although its mechanism of action remains unclear.

title: Assessment of hypoxia status in a rat chronic liver disease model using IVIM and T1 mapping
creator: Wenlu Dong, Longyang Xiao, Ziwei Luo, Haiyang Yu, Lili Wang, Yuanxiang Gao, Zhiming Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesThis study was aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and T1 mapping in detecting hypoxia status of chronic liver disease using a carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced rat model.Materials and methodsThe hypoxia group of chronic liver disease consisted of eight rats induced by injection of CCl4 and the control group consisted of nine rats injected with pure olive oil. All 17 rats underwent MRI examination at week 13 after injection, using T1 mapping and IVIM.

title: Use of amantadine in traumatic brain injury: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: João Félix, Luísa Araújo, Antônio Henriques, Ana Pereira, Saul Carneiro
description: IntroductionAmantadine has been shown to accelerate cognitive and functional brain recovery after cerebrovascular accidents. However, the efficacy of this drug in TBI patients remains poorly defined.MethodsWe performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of amantadine in TBI patients.

title: Integrating cotyledon-based virus-induced gene silencing with visual marker promises a rapid, highly effective validation of gene functions in Nepeta cataria
creator: Zongxia Yu, Ruo Lv, Bo Hong, Lei Yang
description: Nepeta spp. generate volatile nepetalactone iridoids that have cat-attractant and insect-repellent activities. They differ from typical mint family (Lamiaceae) iridoids, which are non-volatile glucosides, and also vary from other species in the Nepetoideae sub-family, which do not generate iridoids. The chemistry and evolution of Nepeta make it suitable for further investigation.

title: Incidence and Predictors of QTC Prolongation Among Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Patients Receiving Bedaquiline-Based TB Regimens in Uganda: A Countrywide Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Marble Nasasira, Kevin Ouma Ojiambo, Daniel Iraguha, Joseph Baruch Baluku
description: BackgroundBedaquiline improves culture conversion in drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment; its main safety concern is QTc prolongation, particularly when combined with other anti-TB drugs. This study assessed the incidence and predictors of QTc prolongation among DR-TB patients receiving bedaquiline under programmatic conditions in Uganda.

title: Associations between subjective and objective measures of stress and load: an insight from 45-week prospective study in 189 elite athletes
